— *Rejected:* the key of the service account of `api`; the module author's own key. — *Does not cover* children's samples in the measurement of stage 2: they lie outside the repositories and go to the provider only with the platform's key under an agreement that admits children (П-3, П-10). While П-3 has not given such an agreement, children's samples do not go to AI. — *Consequence:* the provider's terms for this key are checked as in privacy 5.3, and the price of a run is named before the first launch (rule 4 of RUN.md). — *Open:* where the key lies — a repository secret or the Secret Manager of `infra` with Workload Identity Federation (architecture 3.11) —, and how eval runs on a pull request from a fork. Decide in T15 together with the shared workflows. — architecture 3.6, 3.10; R15.

— *Amendment 2026-10-20:* how a job with a secret meets a pull request from a fork was decided by `.github` (R05 .github). The rule concerns every such job in all the repositories, not only eval:
- the shared workflows take no secrets: a shared workflow without secrets has nothing to leak;
- `pull_request_target` is used nowhere: "Workflows triggered by `pull_request_target` run with elevated trust: the job receives the base repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` and access to repository and organization secrets" ([GitHub Docs, Securely using pull_request_target](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target)), and the code of a pull request from a fork is someone else's;
- a job with a secret does its work only on a push to `main` and on a pull request from a branch of the repository itself. Without the secret it is not skipped but fails at once and names the reason. This happens on a pull request from a fork: "With the exception of `GITHUB_TOKEN`, secrets are not passed to the runner when a workflow is triggered from a forked repository" ([GitHub Docs, Using secrets in GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)). And a job must not be skipped: "A job that is skipped will report its status as "Success". It will not prevent a pull request from merging, even if it is a required check" ([GitHub Docs, Status checks](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/status-checks)). A failed job holds the merge until a maintainer reads the code of the change and carries it into a branch of the repository: until then someone else's code is given no secrets.

All three places were read 2026-10-20. Rejected: `pull_request_target` for eval on a pull request from a fork, and skipping the job on a fork.

A Dependabot pull request comes from a branch of the repository, but gets no Actions secrets: "Secrets are populated from Dependabot secrets. GitHub Actions secrets are not available" ([GitHub Docs, Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-on-actions), read 2026-10-20). Whether a job with a secret fails on it or takes a Dependabot secret is decided together with the job itself. For eval it is decided together with the key's place: this part of "Open" moves from T15 to Т-28.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the "Open" about the key's place and about a Dependabot pull request for eval was settled by R120: the keys are in the Secret Manager of `infra`, a secret per provider, the CI of `modules` and `tutor` reads them through Workload Identity Federation, with a pool of its own `github-eval`, from the GitHub environment `eval`, and on a Dependabot pull request the eval job fails, and the change is carried into a branch of one's own.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to Т-28 (RUN.md, T106). — R120; Т-28.

## Checks

**R30. The CI checks are the same for all NovaTrail repositories. The merge into `main` is held by all the checks but Scorecard, the quality gate of SonarCloud included. Which of them become shared workflows, `.github` itself decides.**
- **Each repository has:**
  - its own checks — what only it knows. In `spec` these are `docs-check`, the tests of `tools/` and the license check of `tools/`: only it has this lock file. Repositories with code have the language checks, with the first code (repositories 6), and with them the shared license check of Go and TypeScript (architecture 3.11);
  - a secret search — with the gitleaks binary;
  - CodeQL — for the workflows, the language `actions`, and for the repository's languages;
  - OpenSSF Scorecard;
  - a DCO check: each commit of a pull request, but merge commits, has a `Signed-off-by` of its author (R22). It is a job of its own, without a third-party app;
  - SonarQube Cloud (SonarCloud) on the OSS plan, with Automatic Analysis;
  - GitHub's own means: secret scanning and push protection, private vulnerability reports (R22), Dependabot.
- **What holds the merge.** Each repository has its own ruleset of the branch `main`:
  - only through a pull request, without approvals: there is one author;
  - all the checks above but Scorecard are required, and the quality gate of SonarCloud too;
  - the branch is up to date before the merge;
  - no force push and no deletion of the branch; the bypass list is empty.
- **Where.** Which checks become shared workflows in `.github`, what their inputs are and how their SHAs are updated, T01 `.github` decides in its own container (architecture 3.11); `spec` and the component repositories connect them (RUN.md, T17 and T16). The CI files of the component repositories are written by the session of `spec` through `.repos/<name>`, as when they were set up.
- **The image.** The own checks run in the `toolchain` stage of the repository's devcontainer — with the same Node and just as locally. The image is built on each run and published nowhere.
- **Versions.** Dependabot updates what it sees: actions together with the version comment, the base image, the languages' packages. It does not see the `ARG`s in the Dockerfile, the VS Code extensions in `devcontainer.json` and in `repo-template/kinds.json`. The executor checks them against the latest releases before each new tag of `spec`: every new repository copies this devcontainer.
- **SHA.** The author enables in the organization "Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA": GitHub checks the pinning, not review.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-19 in planning T15: SonarCloud holds the merge and analyses by itself, the image is built on each run, versions outside Dependabot are checked by hand, the DCO is checked, `.github` decides the shared workflows (question В5). The list of checks, the details of the ruleset, Scorecard not holding the merge, and pinning by SHA for the whole organization are the proposal of the plan the author approved on 2026-10-19. Scorecard runs only on `main` and on a schedule: "The following GitHub triggers are supported: `push`, `schedule` (default branch only). The `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers are experimental" ([ossf/scorecard-action, README](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard-action), read 2026-10-19). A pull request has no result of it. The other arguments are from the documentation, read 2026-10-19:
- **A ruleset in each repository.** "Rulesets are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations" ([GitHub Docs, About rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)). Rules for the whole organization are not: "For customers on GitHub Team or GitHub Enterprise plans you can create rulesets in your organization" ([GitHub Docs, Creating rulesets for repositories in your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/creating-rulesets-for-repositories-in-your-organization)). The organization is on the Free plan (RUN.md, T03).
- **Shared workflows.** A workflow from another repository can be called if "The called workflow is stored in a public repository, and your organization allows you to use public reusable workflows" ([GitHub Docs, Reusing workflow configurations](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations)). Pin by SHA: "Using the commit SHA is the safest option for stability and security" ([GitHub Docs, Reuse workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows)). A required check from it is named "`<job name> / <reusable job name>`" ([GitHub Docs, Troubleshooting rules](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/troubleshooting-rules)).
- **It costs no money.** The repositories are public (R18):
  - "GitHub Actions usage is **free** for **self-hosted runners** and for **public repositories** that use standard GitHub-hosted runners" ([GitHub Docs, GitHub Actions billing](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions));
  - "Code scanning is available for the following repository types: Public repositories on GitHub.com" ([GitHub Docs, Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/code-scanning));
  - for public repositories "Secret scanning runs automatically for free" ([GitHub Docs, About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/about-secret-scanning));
  - "Public, OSI-licensed repos get SonarQube for OSS and Gitar AI Code Review for OSS, with the same features as the paid Pro plan" ([SonarQube Cloud, Plans and pricing](https://www.sonarsource.com/plans-and-pricing/sonarcloud/)).
- **SonarCloud.**
  - It holds the merge by its own check: "SonarQube Cloud adds the quality gate status as a GitHub check" ([SonarQube Cloud, GitHub integration](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-cloud/managing-your-projects/administering-your-projects/devops-platform-integration/github)).
  - Automatic analysis and analysis in CI do not work together: "Automatic analysis is not intended to be used in conjunction with CI-based analysis". It accepts no coverage: "Code coverage information is not supported" ([SonarQube Cloud, Automatic analysis](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-cloud/analyzing-source-code/automatic-analysis)).
  - Analysis in CI needs a token, and a pull request from a fork will not get it: "With the exception of `GITHUB_TOKEN`, secrets are not passed to the runner when a workflow is triggered from a forked repository" ([GitHub Docs, Using secrets in GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)). The required check of such a pull request would not come at all.
- **DCO.** GitHub does not check the sign-off of commits from the command line (R22), so a contribution without it could be merged unnoticed (RUN.md, Д5).
- **Versions.** The Dependabot ecosystem for devcontainers is only Features: "to update Features in your `devcontainer.json` configuration files" ([GitHub Docs, Dependabot supported ecosystems and repositories](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/ecosystems-supported-by-dependabot/supported-ecosystems-and-repositories)). And actions pinned by SHA it keeps together with the comment: "Dependabot updates the version documentation of GitHub Actions when the comment is on the same line" (ibid.).
- **SHA.** "When you enable **Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA**, all actions must be pinned to a full-length commit SHA to be used" ([GitHub Docs, Disabling or limiting GitHub Actions for your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization)).

And an organization needs a key: "Clicking "Sign Up" will take you to a google form where you will need to supply name, email, and company" ([gitleaks-action, README](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks-action), read 2026-10-19). gitleaks itself is under MIT;
- SonarCloud that only reports, as in MathTrail (R50 canvas-api, R31 standalone): the author decided that its quality gate holds the merge;
- SonarCloud analysis in CI now: a token in the secrets and pull requests from forks without a check, and its action under LGPL-3.0 would have to be named an exception of R12. Return to it when the quality gate needs code coverage;
- Renovate: it does not see VS Code extensions either — its devcontainer manager "Extracts all Docker images from the image and features properties" ([Renovate, devcontainer manager](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/devcontainer/), read 2026-10-19). It would raise the `ARG`s, but at the cost of a second update bot beside Dependabot and a third-party app with write access;

- the DCO app — a third party with its own terms;
- organization rulesets — they do not exist on the Free plan.

— *Amendment 2026-10-23:* the test coverage of `spec` and what holds the merge by it (R48; RUN.md, T40). Read 2026-10-23.
- **The tests of `tools/`** run in one run, with coverage: the recipe `just coverage`. In the job "Documents and tools", the six steps "Tests of …" became one — "Tests of tools/": the run names each failed test anyway. The lcov report, `coverage/lcov.info`, goes as an artifact to the job "Coverage", and that job sends it to Codecov by OIDC; it alone has the permission `id-token: write` (R48). A module of `tools/` that no test loads fails the recipe: Node puts no such file in the report, and `codecov/patch` would not see its lines. Node measures only JavaScript: `toolchain.sh` and the bash recipes of the `justfile` have tests, but no coverage.
- **What holds the merge** is `codecov/patch`. In the ruleset of `main` of `spec` (25424994), it is added bound to the Codecov app, `integration_id` 254, as in the ruleset of `main` of standalone (23788682). On a pull request, Codecov sets it as a check (check run) of that app — so on pull request #144 of standalone (the GitHub API). The app the check is bound to must already be sending it: "The app must be installed in the repository with the `statuses:write` permission, must have recently submitted a check run, and must be associated with a pre-existing required status check in the ruleset" ([GitHub Docs, Available rules for rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#require-status-checks-to-pass-before-merging)).
- **When.** The check becomes required when the first pull request of Dependabot shows that it gets OIDC and that `codecov/patch` arrives on it (RUN.md, Д10). Until then it only reports. This is the author's decision in planning T40: GitHub's documentation says two things about the permissions of Dependabot's runs (the amendment of the same day to R48), and without OIDC a required check would hold every pull request of Dependabot.
- **The job "Coverage"** is not in the ruleset: without the upload, `codecov/patch` does not arrive, and the merge waits anyway. Any failure of it fails the run of the pull request, so that a missing `codecov/patch` has a visible cause. It does not fail the run of `main`: the job there has `continue-on-error`, which "Prevents a workflow run from failing when a job fails" ([GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idcontinue-on-error)). The release waits for green CI (R31), and a failure of Codecov must not hold it. The report is kept for a week: after a failure, the job can be rerun.
- **`codecov/project`** does not arrive at all (the amendment of the same day to R48), and it is not in the ruleset.

A module is each `go.mod` that git knows, outside any `testdata/`, and a new module is checked with no change to the recipes:
  - `ci-lint` — `gofmt -l` over the Go files that git knows, and `go vet`;
  - `ci-test` — `go test -race`, with a coverage profile in `coverage/go.out` (the amendment of the same day to R48);

So the recipe skips such a module's own packages (`--ignore`), and checks the packages it is built from: for `tools/gomod` — `golang.org/x/mod`, BSD-3-Clause, for `tools/types/roundtrip` — `spec` itself, Apache-2.0.

- **`go-check`** checks what only it knows: that the module requires nothing, and the zip of `HEAD` (R64). Vet and the tests of all modules are with `ci-lint` and `ci-test`, and `just coverage` runs the Go tests through `ci-test`. The step "Go module" of the job "Documents and tools" stays, and its former part is now held by the checks "Go / …".

So it is in `module-kit` and `tutor` too: a check that passes with a known vulnerability would not hold it. On 2026-11-01, govulncheck found nothing in any of the three modules.
- **Named by R12.** govulncheck is BSD-3-Clause, go-licenses is Apache-2.0, and each package they are built from is under a license of category A. For govulncheck these are `golang.org/x/vuln`, `x/tools`, `x/mod`, `x/sync` and `x/telemetry`, all BSD-3-Clause; for go-licenses — Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, ISC and MIT (`go-licenses report` on each, 2026-11-01). Both are CI tools and ship nowhere, and they need no exception. The Go telemetry of govulncheck is in its default mode: "When `mode` is `local`, telemetry data is collected and stored on the local computer, but never uploaded to remote servers" ([Go Telemetry](https://go.dev/doc/telemetry), read 2026-11-01), and nobody calls `go telemetry on`.

Rejected:

- a copy of `LICENSE` in each module of `tools/`: a file that has to be kept the same as the root's, for a check that the code of `spec` is under the license of `spec`;
- Go coverage as a separate recipe: the Go tests would run two ways, and the contract of `ci-test` from Д29 already tells the recipe to write the report;

## Releases

**R31. A release of `spec` comes out by itself: after green CI on `main`, the next patch of the line, the tag together with the release; nobody sets tags by hand. The release is immutable and has no files, and GitHub's attestation signs it.**
- **The workflow** is the own `.github/workflows/release.yml` of `spec`, after the pattern of canvas-api: its `release.yml` and the recipe `release-version`, commit 0901af0 (R52 canvas-api). It starts after a run of CI on `main` — only a successful one, only from a push and only from the repository itself. The button releases the tip of `main` that has no release yet, and works only on `main` after green CI of that commit. The button sets no numbers. The release runs go in a queue, `queue: max`: "Up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be `pending` in the concurrency group" ([GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax), read 2026-10-19), so every commit gets a release, not only the last.
- **The number** is the next patch of the line `RELEASE_LINE` in `release.yml`. The first line is `0.2`, the first release `v0.2.0`. A new line comes by a change of `RELEASE_LINE` in the pull request that deserves it; a line below the newest release is an error. The number is computed by `just release-version`: `tools/release/version.mjs`, with tests. A commit is released once. The number only goes forward along the history of `main`: a commit whose history does not hold the newest release — an old commit whose CI passed late or again — gets no release. Tags not of the form `vX.Y.Z` do not count as releases — for `just new-repo` either, which takes the newest release by the same function. The rules of format versions are still for Т-11 to settle.
- **The release** has no files: the other repositories take the tag itself, as a submodule (R21). The releases of `spec` are immutable, and the tag is locked on its commit: "its associated Git tag is locked to a specific commit, cannot be changed, and cannot be deleted while the release exists". The signature is the attestation that GitHub creates itself: "a cryptographically verifiable record of a release containing the release tag, commit SHA, and release assets" ([GitHub Docs, Immutable releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/immutable-releases), read 2026-10-19). The check is `gh release verify <tag> -R altnovatrail/spec`, and the workflow runs it itself too. Files and their signature come when the schemas and the packages enter the release (Т-7).
- **The tags `v*`** are protected by the ruleset "v-tags": moving, deleting and force push are forbidden, and nobody has a bypass. It does not restrict creation: GitHub does not accept a bypass for GitHub Actions — "Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization" (the API's answer, 2026-10-19). So the rule "only the release workflow sets tags" is held by this decision, not by a setting. A tag without a release — on the commit itself, or a newest "release" outside the history of `main` — the workflow takes as set by hand and fails on it: otherwise such a tag would silently stop all releases.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-19: «релиз должен быть автоматическим», as in canvas-api. A workflow of its own, a release on every green `main`, an immutable release with no files, and protection of the tags without forbidding their creation are the author's decisions in planning T20. The submodules of all repositories and `just new-repo` depend on the tag of `spec` (R21), and a manual tag can be forgotten, set on the wrong commit, or on a commit with red CI. In canvas-api: "Nobody tags anything by hand: the version is the next patch of the line the releases are numbered in, and the tag is created with the release" (`release.yml` of canvas-api, commit 0901af0). A release on every `main` does not hurry the other repositories: each moves to a new tag in a task of its own (RULES.md, Across repositories). A release created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no other workflows: "events triggered by the `GITHUB_TOKEN` will not create a new workflow run" ([GitHub Docs, GITHUB_TOKEN](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token), read 2026-10-19).

— *Rejected:*
- manual tags, as it was with `v0.1.0`;
- a release only by the button: it would again depend on whether someone forgot to release it;
- a shared "signed release" from `.github` now (architecture 3.11): `spec` has no code, and `.github` itself needs the first tag with R30;
- cosign and release files now, as R52 canvas-api: there is nothing to sign but the tag, and the attestation signs the tag. GitHub builds the "Source code" archives on download, and the attestation does not cover them;
- a GitHub App of our own, the only one allowed to create the tags `v*`: one more secret and one more actor with write permission;
- a number set by the button: a new number comes only with `RELEASE_LINE`.

— *Consequence:* R21 gets an amendment. `tools/new-repo` takes the same `RELEASE_TAG`. CI gets the steps "Release version" and "Tests of release-version". Д6 begins with the first release. — RUN.md, T20; repositories 2.2, 5; `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

— *Amendment 2026-10-20:* on the questions В8–В10 of `.github` (RUN.md, T17).
- **Checkout without the event's commit.** `release.yml` takes `main` as it is, and names the commit on which CI passed only by its SHA: the recipe `release-version` gets it as an argument and reads `RELEASE_LINE` from the `release.yml` of that commit. That commit is in the history of `main`, which the ruleset of `main` does not let anyone rewrite. A checkout of the event's commit is exactly what Scorecard marks as Dangerous-Workflow: the trigger `workflow_run` "in conjunction with an explicit pull request checkout", and "This check does not detect whether untrusted code checkouts are used safely" ([Scorecard, docs/checks.md](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/6d4113e/docs/checks.md), read 2026-10-20), so a condition of the job that lets in only a push from the repository itself does not save the score. The price: the image and the recipe are the tip's.
- **The publishing step** runs with `pipefail`: an empty tip of `main` is an error, not "not the tip". After a refusal of the Releases API, `main` is fetched again, and the refusal is skipped only when the commit is no longer the tip and its files `.github/workflows/` differ from the tip's: that is the cause the documentation names. Both 404 and 403 are skipped: "Otherwise, this endpoint returns 404 Not Found; some authentication paths surface 403 Resource not accessible by integration instead" ([GitHub Docs, REST API endpoints for releases](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases), read 2026-10-20). In `self-release.yml` of `.github` it is the same, but without comparing the files.
- **The number for another repository.** `version.mjs` takes the line from the environment variable `RELEASE_LINE`, if it is set, and otherwise from the `release.yml` of `spec`. The recipe `release-version` counts the tags of the repository it is called from: `just -f spec/justfile release-version` in `.github` counts the tags of `.github`. Without `RELEASE_LINE`, the recipe does not work outside `spec`: another repository has a line of its own. Then `self-release.yml` calls the recipe of `spec` as it is, with no second copy of the wrapping.

Rejected: closing Dangerous-Workflow as false, with a reason, as R51 canvas-api, — the Scorecard score for the check would stay 0, and the pattern would go into the next releases; the release as a job in CI, without `workflow_run`, — a file of another kind, a job with `contents: write` in CI, and a skipped check "Release" on every pull request. The author's decisions of 2026-10-20 follow the recommendations of `.github`, within T17.

— *Amendment 2026-10-20:* `spec` has a release interface for the other repositories, the author's answer to В16 of `.github`. The wrappings around the recipe are no longer copied into their workflows.
- **The line.** `just -f spec/justfile release-version <commit> <workflow>` outside `spec` reads `RELEASE_LINE` from the named workflow on this commit — whatever the environment sets, where the `env` is the tip workflow's — and the commit counts in the line in which it was made, as in `spec`. A commit older than the workflow itself takes the line from its copy in the checkout, and the variable from the environment is used only when no workflow is named. The caller no longer needs the internal script of `spec`, `tools/release/line.mjs`, and it can be renamed without breaking another repository's release. In `spec`, the recipe rejects a second argument: its line is always its own.
- **A refusal of the Releases API.** The rule of when a refusal is skipped is the recipe `release-refusal <commit> <tip> <error file>`, in one copy: the commit is no longer the tip of `main` but is in its history — only then does the release of the tip cover it —, it adds or changes files `.github/workflows/` relative to the tip, and the answer is 404 or "403 Resource not accessible by integration". The recipe exits with 0 when the refusal is that one, and with 1 and a reason in every other case, so an unclear refusal still fails the run. It is called by the own `release.yml` of `spec` — in the stage `toolchain`, with the runner's temporary directory mounted read-only — and a release of another repository can call it the same way.

The price is the tests of both in `tools/release` and one more start of the stage `toolchain` in the publishing step, only after a refusal. Rejected: leaving the wrappings with the callers and comparing them at each move to a tag of `spec` — the rule would live in two copies, and a change of `spec` would not reach them by itself, with the tag.

— *Amendment 2026-10-21:* to the release interface for the other repositories — a script that runs recipes in the stage `toolchain` on the runner. The author's answer to В18 of `.github`, by its recommendation.
- **The script** is `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh`, one copy for everyone. The runner runs it with its own shell from the repository's root: CI and the release of `spec` from `tools/`, the release of another repository from its submodule `spec/`, at the tag it is on.
  - `build` builds the stage `toolchain` from the repository's `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`;
  - `run` runs a command in it: as the runner's user, with the home in `/tmp`, with the repository in `/work` and the runner's temporary directory mounted read-only;
  - `spec` runs in the same way a recipe from the justfile of `spec`, wherever it lies: `release-version`, `release-refusal`, and with them `docs-check-repo` and the license recipes (R39).

  How the stage is built and how a command runs in it is written once and reaches the callers with the tag. The script cannot be a `just` recipe: just is in the stage itself, and to call a recipe you need the `docker run` that the script does.
- **The probe.** Before the number, the caller calls `spec --dry-run release-refusal` with the arguments that the publishing step will give. A dry run of just parses the call and runs nothing. A tag of `spec` in which the recipe disappeared or takes another number of arguments then stops the run that moved to that tag, not the run of a refusal. The probe does not see arguments swapped. There is none in `spec`: the script, the recipes and their tests are one commit here.
- **Quoting.** Paths go to docker as arguments, not as the text of a script, which `printf` wrote before. The characters `$`, the backquote, `"` and `\` in `$PWD` or `$RUNNER_TEMP` no longer break anything. There will be no colon in the path: docker itself splits `--volume` on it, and the script rejects such a path. The tests of the script with a fake docker check this — the recipe `just toolchain-test`.

*Why:* `self-release.yml` and the shared `release.yml` of `.github` repeat the script and the probe after the `release.yml` of `spec` (RUN.md of `.github`, commit b3ee1a8), and the note in the `ci.yml` of `spec` — "a change here goes there" — linked only two copies within `spec` itself. «Если новый рецепт потребует другого запуска — тома, переменной, флага, — до `.github` правка дойдёт не с тегом, а руками, и сломаться может как раз путь отказа» (В18 `.github`). One copy — as with the rule of refusal above. *Rejected:* keeping the copies and extending the note of `spec` to the copies outside it; leaving it as it is. *Consequence:* the `ci.yml` and `release.yml` of `spec` call the script. `.github` moves to it in `self-release.yml` and the shared `release.yml` with its move to the tag (RUN.md, Д15). — repositories 5; architecture 3.11.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* which pull request deserves a new line — R44, the author's answer to Т-11.
- The one that gives the module format a new version: it raises `RELEASE_LINE` in the same change, so that within one line the format is one. A major version of the format raises the major version of `spec` too.
- While the format is v0, `spec` stays 0.x, and format v1 comes out with `spec` v1.0.0.
- Whether the versions of the contracts and protocols raise the line, epics E3 and E5 will decide.
- "The rules of format versions are still for Т-11 to settle" in the item "Number" now refers to R44.

The link of the line with the format's version will be checked by CI from the first release where the schemas are files (RUN.md, T35). `tools/release/version.mjs` needs no change: it already starts a line above the newest release from `.0`, and rejects a line below.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* the release of `spec` runs recipes in copies of the checkout, as the releases of `.github` do since T28 (the amendments to R10 and R18 .github). The author's answer to В25 of `.github`, by its recommendation.
- **What was.** Each container of the script `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` gets write access to the folder the script was started from, and to the `.git` in it too (the 2026-10-21 amendment above). The release of `spec` ran `release-version` in the checkout itself. After that container, the runner itself worked in the same checkout, and the steps had `GH_TOKEN` with `contents: write`:
  - the publishing step did `git fetch` by `.git/config` on every release;
  - after a refusal of the Releases API, it called the script from the same checkout, and nobody compared the script's checksum;
  - the post step of `actions/checkout` at the end of the job runs `git config` and `git submodule foreach` in the checkout (architecture 4 .github).
- **Now:**
  - the number step, before the first container, takes a copy of the checkout — `cp -a` into `RUNNER_TEMP`, with all the history and tags — and runs the script from it;
  - after a refusal, `release-refusal` runs in a new copy, taken after `git fetch`: the first copy does not have the new tip, and its container could have changed it;
  - the runner's `git` reads only the checkout itself, and no container mounts it.

  Like `.github`, `spec` does not compare the script's checksum: the script no longer runs from a copy after its container, and no container has seen the new copy. The script's contract does not change: `run` still mounts the folder it is called from. The price is a copy of the checkout on the runner's disk: the `.git` of `spec` weighs 15 MB.
- **Checked** on 2026-10-22 locally: the number and publishing steps were taken out of `release.yml` word for word. docker was faked: it runs the recipe in the mounted folder, and then appends a line to `.git/config` and to the script of that copy. `gh` was faked too: it refuses the release with 404. After both steps, the script and `.git/config` of the checkout are the same as before them. `release-refusal` in the new copy sees the tip that came after the refusal, and skips the refusal. actionlint 1.7.12 with shellcheck 0.11.0 — the versions and checksums of `self-ci.yml` of `.github` — found no remarks. The real run is the first release after the merge.

*Why:* the recommendation of `.github` in В25 (RUN.md of `.github`, commit 9b1ea42). This is the change that passed the trial #54 in `.github`: one file of `spec`, the script's contract as before. Only the release has a write token, and the CI of `spec` runs with read permission only, `contents: read` (`ci.yml`).

*Rejected:*
- the script's own mode `spec` runs the recipe in a copy of the folder it is called from. This would close the path for everyone who calls the recipes of `spec`, and `.github` would drop its own copy. But the recipes with `_tools` would install the npm packages anew in each copy. And the checkout cannot be mounted read-only: `_tools` writes `tools/node_modules`;
- accepting it: the containers of the release of `spec` run the same commit of `spec` as `release.yml` itself, and the image's tools are pinned by digest and checksum (R34). The protection costs one `cp -a`, and without it the release of `spec` would remain the only one in NovaTrail where the runner reads `.git` after a container;
- a copy with hard links, `git worktree add` and `git clone` from the checkout — by the arguments of the amendment to R18 .github: a file that the container changes in place would change in the checkout too, and the working copy of `git worktree` shares `.git` with it.

*Consequence:* `ci.yml` needs no change. `.github` closes В25 with its move to the tag (RUN.md, Д24). — `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* a release of another repository is given only by the files its output is built from. The pattern `paths` of the calling `release.yml` is their list, by the kind of the repository, not everything but exceptions. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `module-kit` В6 (RUN.md of `module-kit`, commit 1a54028), by its recommendation.
- **What was.** The pattern `paths` in architecture 3.3 .github is `.` with exceptions: `docs/**`, `*.md`, `.github/**` and the submodule `spec`. A release was given also by changes that do not change the output: Claude Code, gh or just-lsp in the stage `devcontainer` of the Dockerfile, `devcontainer.json`, `.claude/`, `.gitignore`, a test. Dependabot would offer each such tag to the consumers — for `module-kit` these are `api` and `tutor` —, and this is what R18 .github wanted to avoid. A change of `RELEASE_LINE` lies in `.github/` and gave no release by itself: the new line began with the next change in `paths`.
- **Now** it is a list. For the kind `go`: `**/*.go` without `*_test.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `justfile`, `LICENSE`, `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` — whole, since Go is pinned in it —, and `.github/workflows/release.yml`, so that a change of the line gives a release. The list of the kind `typescript` is written by `.github` with the first release in TypeScript, in `canvas`, by the same rule: the list holds what the consumer will get.
- **The price.** A release is still given by two changes that do not change the output: the tools of the stage `devcontainer` in the Dockerfile and raising the reference to the shared `release.yml` of `.github`. The second comes as a pull request of Dependabot, which for the callers runs once a week (architecture 3.3 .github).

*Why:* the recommendation of `module-kit` in В6: a release of a library is when what its consumers get changes. The pattern is held by `.github` in architecture 3.3 .github, and the caller takes it in a task of its own, like everything the repository's code adds to its CI files (the 2026-10-21 amendment to R30). `spec` decides: the rule is one for all repositories with releases, and `.github` itself gave this choice to the row В6 of `module-kit`.

*Rejected:*
- keeping the exceptions: any test and any tool of the devcontainer would give a release;
- keeping the exceptions, and changing the line together with a change of code: the noise from tests and tools would remain.

*Consequence:* `.github` changes the pattern in architecture 3.3 .github, and `module-kit` its own `release.yml`, and closes В6; both with their move to the tag (RUN.md, Д27). `spec` has no `paths` of its own: its release comes out after every green CI on `main`.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **a release of `spec` carries files** (R64). The author's answers in planning T35.
- **From line 0.3**, `RELEASE_LINE` is `0.3`, and the first release of the line, v0.3.0, releases format version 0.1 (R44). The items "The release has no files" and "Files and their signature come when the schemas and the packages enter the release" above are fulfilled by this. A release of line 0.3 and newer carries `format-<version>.tar.gz` and its cosign bundle `<file>.sigstore.json`. A release of a line before 0.3 — and the release of its commit whose CI finished late — carries no files: the recipe `release-files` reads the line of the commit itself.
- **The rejected "cosign and release files now: there is nothing to sign but the tag"** is no longer true, and the cosign signature stands on top of the attestation: Scorecard Signed-Releases looks for signatures among the files and does not read the attestation (R64). These are new facts, not a revision without them.
- **The files are built from the event's commit, not from the tip.** The tip's recipe — a price this item has already accepted — reads only the objects of the commit, `git archive`, in a new copy of the checkout. The copy of the number step has already had a container, and the script does not run from a copy after its container (the 2026-10-22 amendment above).
- **A draft** with files, left by an interrupted run, is deleted by the publishing before the release is created and after a refusal. The rule of refusal is the same `release-refusal`: a refusal of the Releases API can come both on creating the draft and on publishing it, and the text of gh's error names HTTP 404 or 403 in both cases.
- **The release check** downloads its files, compares them with the list of those built, and checks each with `gh release verify-asset`. The Go module of the release is checked by the step "Verify the Go module" — through the Go proxy (R64).
- **The number** is computed by the same `version.mjs`, and `release-version` in `spec` also refuses a commit that gives the format a new version in the line of the previous release. This is the "link of the line with the format's version" promised above from the first release where the schemas are files (the 2026-10-22 amendment above) — `tools/release/format-line.mjs`.

— R44; R64; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; RUN.md, T35.

— *Amendment 2026-11-01:* the list `paths` of each kind is held by the pattern in architecture 3.3 .github, and the 2026-10-22 amendment above gives the rule by which it is made. The author's answer to the second part of the row «в реестр spec» `.github` В28 (RUN.md of `.github`, commit 6ffbe10), by its recommendation; the price of a new base image is by the executor's recommendation, on the question the row left to `spec`.
- **An error in the list.** The item "Now" of the 2026-10-22 amendment writes the Go code of the kind `go` as `**/*.go`. But the `paths` of the shared `release.yml` are a git pathspec: `git diff --quiet "$previous" "$TARGET" -- "${paths[@]}"` (`.github/workflows/release.yml` of `.github`, commit 6ffbe10). Without the magic `glob`, `*` in a pathspec matches `/` too, and `**/` requires a slash. So `**/*.go` misses the Go files in the root — `main.go`, `doc.go` —, and a change of them would give no release. A trial on 2026-11-01, git 2.56.0, in a temporary repository with `main.go`, `main_test.go`, `cmd/x/a.go`, `cmd/x/a_test.go` and `testdata/t.go`: `git diff --name-only` with `'*.go' ':(exclude)*_test.go'` found `main.go`, `cmd/x/a.go` and `testdata/t.go`, and with `'**/*.go' ':(exclude)**/*_test.go'` only `cmd/x/a.go` and `testdata/t.go`. The pattern of `.github` writes `*.go` and `:(exclude)*_test.go` — by the same trial (the 2026-11-01 amendment to R18 .github; architecture 4 .github).
- **Now** the list is taken from the pattern of architecture 3.3 .github, not from this decision. Here is only the rule: the list holds what the output is built from and what the consumer will get. The list of the kind `go` in "Now" above is the first record of the rule, not a pattern: where it differs from the pattern, the pattern is right. How the rule applies to files that code embeds through `//go:embed`, and to code in `testdata/`, is also written by the pattern.
- **The price** is one more change that may not change the output while a release comes out: a new base image in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`. The stage `toolchain` is built in it, the Dockerfile is in the list whole, and Dependabot offers the image once a week, and the pause `cooldown` does not hold it: Microsoft's registry does not report the release date of the image (architecture 3.3 and 3.5 .github). The item "The price" of the 2026-10-22 amendment names only the tools of the stage `devcontainer` and raising the reference to the shared `release.yml`.

*Why:* a list written in two places diverges, and this has already happened: the pattern was corrected, and the decision was not. The pattern is held by `.github` — so the 2026-10-22 amendment said too —, and the caller takes it in a task of its own (the 2026-10-21 amendment to R30). The decision names the price in full, so that a new image is not taken for an error in `paths`.

*Rejected:*
- correcting the list here — "`*.go` without `*_test.go`" and the rest: two places that have to be kept the same;
- leaving it: whoever reads R31 and not the pattern — for example, `module-kit` by Д27 — would write `**/*.go`, and a change of Go code in the root would give no release;
- writing here the rules of `//go:embed` and `testdata/` too: it is the same rule, and how it applies to Go is a detail of the pattern.

*Consequence:* `module-kit` takes the list of its `release.yml` from the pattern of architecture 3.3 .github, not from "Now" of the 2026-10-22 amendment. Its `release.yml` on `main` (commit 1a54028) is still on exceptions, and there is no `**/*.go` there (RUN.md, Д27). `.github` closes the second part of В28 with its move to the tag with this amendment (RUN.md, Д52).

— RUN.md, Д27, Д52; R18 .github; architecture 3.3, 3.5 and 4 .github.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **from line 0.7, the release sets a second tag — `contracts/<tag>` on the same commit, the version of the Go module of the contracts — once the release is out and checked; the ruleset "v-tags" holds `refs/tags/contracts/v*` too.** A tag `contracts/<tag>` on another commit the workflow takes as set by hand and fails on it, as on a tag `v*` without a release. The line is also raised by a change that brings a new kind of file into the release, so that a rerun of an old release builds the files it got. — the fourth 2026-11-02 amendment to R83; RUN.md, T57.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **CI takes the image of the stage `toolchain` from the GitHub Actions cache, as R57 canvas does: a file of `docker save` by the key `toolchain-<OS>-<architecture>-<sha256 .devcontainer/Dockerfile>`; `actions/cache` restores it before the build and saves it right after the build, only on a miss, and the scope of `main` is filled by the run of CI on a push to `main`. Where `toolchain.sh build` builds the image, it loads and writes the file itself, and deletes a file that did not load and builds the image; the `go.yml` and `typescript.yml` of `.github`, which build the image without the submodule `spec`, do the same in their own steps by the same key. The releases — the `release.yml` of `spec` and the shared one of `.github` — take no cache: the image of the job that signs the files is built from the Dockerfile.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В65 (RUN.md of `canvas`, `main` 0e1c99a) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, by the row's recommendation. — *Why:* the Dockerfile pins everything by exact versions and checksums (R34, R40), so the image from the cache is the one it would have built, and on a hit the Dockerfile does not run, and no network to nodejs.org, GitHub and the snapshot of the Ubuntu archive is needed. On 2026-11-09 the build of the stage failed in `canvas` on nodejs.org (R57 canvas) and in `spec` on the archive of just from github.com: `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 504` after three retries, in three attempts of the four of the CI run 42569536919. Only runs on `main` write to the scope of `main`: "When a cache is created by a workflow run triggered on a pull request, the cache is created for the merge ref (`refs/pull/.../merge`). Because of this, the cache will have a limited scope and can only be restored by re-runs of the pull request"; the limit is "10 GB per repository" ([GitHub Docs, Dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching), read 2026-11-09), and the entry of the image of `canvas` is about 575 MB. — *Rejected:* buildx with the cache `type=gha` — two actions `docker/*` instead of one, as R57 canvas rejected too; only retries of downloads — longer, each job still downloads everything, and a long failure brings the check down; the cache for the release too — the image of the job with the signing permission would be held by a cache entry and not by the Dockerfile, and a failed release is rerun; not caching. — *Consequence:* `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` and its tests, the `ci.yml` of `spec` — task T104; the shared workflows of `.github` — RUN.md, Д146; rows 1.13 and 2.4 of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md). — R30, R34, R40; R57 canvas; R03–R05 .github.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-09:* **`toolchain.sh build` takes the image file from the environment variable `TOOLCHAIN_IMAGE_FILE` — a full path that the caller sets — not from an argument; empty or unset means building the stage, as before, and the releases do not set it. With the variable: the file is there — `docker load --quiet --input <file>` and `docker image inspect novatrail-toolchain`, and if both succeed, the file is deleted and there is no build; the file did not load or gave no image — it is deleted, `::warning::`, the stage is built, and the file is not written; there is no file — the build and `docker save --output <file> novatrail-toolchain`, and a failed save gives `::warning::`, the unfinished file deleted, code 0; a failed build gives its code. The warning is a workflow command without the path, and the path is a line in stderr; it tells to delete a broken cache entry: the entry is immutable, and otherwise the hit would repeat. The script takes the cache from the release tag of the end of E4, `v0.13.0` (RUN.md, T102). The job "Go" of `spec` runs by the shared `go.yml` of `.github` and will get the cache with its release of epic E17.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 in planning T104 (RUN.md), by the recommendations, — and the request of `.github` (E17, pull request 109). — *Why:* the `documents.yml` of `.github` calls the script of the caller's submodule at any tag since `v0.2.17`, and the former `build` refuses any argument: the variable it can always set — the old script will not notice it and will build the image, the new one will take the cache, and the tag need not be checked. The check `image inspect` after `load` is needed because a file with another image would load "successfully", and the next `docker run novatrail-toolchain` would go for the image to Docker Hub. A file that was there is a hit, and no save follows it: a cache entry is immutable. — *Rejected:* an argument `build <file>`; an explicit `env -u` in the release — nobody sets the variable there. — R31; RUN.md, T104, Д146; rows 1.13 and 2.4 of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md).

— *Third amendment 2026-11-09:* **`v0.13.0` comes out now, not with T102: the second branch `e4` merges into `main` before the end of the epic.** The author's decision of 2026-11-09 is the third amendment of that day to answer 5 of epic E4 (RUN.md): `.github` needs the cache for T53.

## The documents check

**R32. The documents of a component repository are checked by the `docs-check` of the `spec` its submodule is on. Citations of `spec` are checked against that submodule, and examples of citations are written in inline code.**
- **Running** — from the repository's root: `just -f spec/justfile docs-check-repo`. The dependencies of `tools/` are installed by the recipe `_tools` — into `spec/tools/node_modules` of the submodule, where they are in `.gitignore`. The repository needs no justfile of its own: it comes with code (repositories 1). The root is the folder above the submodule in which the script itself lies: the path is taken neither from the arguments nor from the working folder.
- **What is checked** — the repository's files, without `spec/`:
  - links and anchors, including in `spec/`;
  - its own sections — "architecture 2" without a suffix — and the sections of the documents of `spec` — "architecture 3.8 spec", "concepts 9, 10 spec";
  - its own log of R: while there are no decisions, it is empty, and the next is R01;
  - the numbers of `spec`: "R18 spec" — by the log of `spec`, О-, П-, Т- — always by the registers of `spec`;
  - the tables «В» and «Д» in RUN.md;
  - Mermaid diagrams.
- **How citations are read:**
  - «раздел N» without a link, in a document without sections of its own — RUN.md — is a section of `docs/architecture.md`;
  - «раздел N» right after an external link, after the name of a MathTrail repository — "`docs/spec.md` canvas-api, section 4.2" — or in a nested item under an item whose last link is external, is a section of another text, and it is not checked;
  - a document of `spec` without a suffix is an error, with a hint on how to cite it.

  Errors in `spec` itself are not its business: `spec` checks itself.
- **The tables «В» and «Д»** are checked both in the repositories and in `spec`: a number does not repeat in the table, and «следующий — В…» is greater than each number in it. Gaps are allowed — an answered row leaves —, so citations of «В» and «Д» are not checked.
- **An example of a citation** — `R03`, `R19` — is written in inline code: `docs-check` does not read numbers in code (RULES.md, Citations). The template writes so. The repositories already set up fix their five examples in the task of moving to the new tag.
- **`just new-repo-check`** runs the same mode on the copy. Links to `spec` are checked by its submodule, and for a draft, by the working tree of `spec`.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-19 in planning T18: running from the submodule, examples in code, the tables «В» and «Д» in `spec` too. The parsing of citations, the root above the submodule and the reading of «раздела N» are the plan's proposal. Until now the documents of the component repositories were checked by hand (rule 6 of their RUN.md), and the one-off script of T05–T14 was lost with the session's folder (RUN.md, Д2). The current `docs-check` on the root of `.repos/module-kit` gave 434 errors: it read the submodule itself as well, and took "architecture 3.8 spec" for its own architecture.

— *Rejected:*
- a justfile of its own in the template — before code, against repositories 1;
- not checking the numbers in guillemets — the check would then be blind to real citations in quotes too, and `spec` has many of them;
- the tables «В» and «Д» only in the component repositories — one tool would hold two rules for identical tables;
- the path to the repository from the command line.

— *Consequence:* Д2 closes when the repositories move to the tag with this check — each in a task of its own (Д6). In CI it is connected by T17 and T16; whether it is a shared workflow or an own one is decided by T01 `.github`. — RUN.md, T18; repositories 2.2, 5; RULES.md, Citations.

— *Amendment 2026-10-19:* Д2 is merged with Д6. They have one deadline — the repository's move to the tag with this check —, and they close together.

— *Amendment 2026-10-20:* Д6, and with it Д2, is closed in T21. All eleven component repositories are on `spec` `v0.2.9`, and in each this check is the required CI check "Documents / docs-check-repo". In CI it was connected by T17, T16 and T21 (RUN.md).

— *Amendment 2026-10-21:* which name of a NovaTrail repository is a citation's suffix. The author's answer to В22 of `.github`, by its recommendation.
- A name that can be a word of prose — `modules`, `engine`, `sim`, `tutor`, `api`, `canvas`, `app`, `infra`, `site` — is still a suffix only where the sentence ends with it: in `R99 modules are data` the citation is the repository's own.
- `.github` and the hyphenated names — `module-kit`, `learner-model`, `skill-map`, `module-registry`, `module-pipeline`, `widget-template` — are never words of prose. After a number or a section, like the names of MathTrail, they are a suffix wherever a word boundary follows them: "R19 .github and its citations" and "R03 module-kit and its recipes" are citations of other logs. A list of the form "canvas-api: R37, R38" still knows only the names of MathTrail: that is how their logs are cited (RULES.md, Citations).

Which name is which, `tools/docs-check/citations.mjs` decides by the name itself: letters only means a word. *Why:* the restriction caught a natural sentence in every repository that cites these names, and the session of `canvas` rewrote a sentence because of it in its T27 (В22 `.github`). In `spec` itself, several citations of `.github` and `module-kit` were read so as its own — in the 2026-10-21 amendment to R30, in R37 and in the archive of E1 —, and the check compared them with the log and sections of `spec`. *Rejected:* writing a citation so that a sign follows the name — every author would have to remember this; a list of exceptions in the check's `config.mjs` — a second rule beside the first. — `tools/docs-check/citations.mjs` and its tests; RULES.md, Citations.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* **in a repository the check reads only the files that git tracks or does not ignore.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В29 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its first option.
- **What was.** The check walked the whole tree of the root and skipped only `.git`, `node_modules` and `spec/` (`tools/docs-check/config.mjs`). In `tutor`, the measurement reports that `tutor-eval report` writes are files `.md` in `samples/runs`, outside git (architecture 3.1 tutor), and the check read them. There is no handwriting in the reports, and in CI this folder does not exist at all. But the rule of the CLAUDE.md of `tutor` keeps agents out of `samples/`, and only the command `go` has an exception from it (R14 tutor).
- **Now.** In a root with its own `.git` — in a repository, in the submodule `spec/`, in a copy that `just new-repo` built — the check reads the files `.md` by the list `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-per-directory=.gitignore`: the tracked ones that are in the working tree, and the new ones that the repository's own `.gitignore` files do not keep outside git. It sees a document not yet committed, and does not see `samples/` of `tutor`.
  - git does not enter a folder it ignores at all. The trial of 2026-10-26 on git 2.56.0 showed it: a folder without read permission under the rule `/samples/` gave not a word, and without the rule — "could not open directory".
  - The rules come only from the repository's `.gitignore`. `--exclude-standard`, which `tutor` named, adds to them also ".git/info/exclude … and the user's global exclusion file" ([git-ls-files](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/Documentation/git-ls-files.adoc), v2.56.0, read 2026-10-26), and the list would depend on the machine.
  - If git gives no list — for example, `.git` points to a folder that does not exist —, the check says so, in one line.
  - The check takes the root only by itself: `spec`, where the script lies, or with `--component` the repository around the submodule. It accepts no path from the command line: having become git's working folder, the path would let whoever writes the command run git in any folder. And git runs commands from the settings of its `.git/config`: the trial of 2026-10-26 on git 2.56.0 showed that `git ls-files` runs the hook `core.fsmonitor`. So git also runs with `-c core.fsmonitor=false`. A path on the command line was needed only by the tests, and SonarCloud found this on pull request #47 (jssecurity:S8705 and S8707).
  - A root without `.git` — the draft of `just new-repo` from the item above and the tests' copies — the check still walks whole. The skips of `config.mjs` apply in both cases.

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`: so the check sees exactly the repository's documents, in any component, and the components need to change nothing on their side. The rule is one — for `spec` and for the components. In `spec` itself the check reads the same files as before: git ignores `.repos/`, `coverage/` and `tools/node_modules/`, and it skipped `.repos/` and `node_modules` anyway. Rules only from `.gitignore` are the executor's proposal after the review.

*Rejected:* `--exclude-standard` — the list would depend on the rules of the machine and of the clone; skipping the paths from the component's `.gitignore` by our own parsing — a second rule beside git's rule, and they could diverge; the report of `tutor` not in `.md` — a change in `tutor` only, and another component with an ignored `.md` would meet the same; refusing in a root without `.git` — `just new-repo-check` checks the draft too, which has no `.git`.

*Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/main.mjs` and its tests. The components get the change with their move to the tag, and `tutor` closes В29 with it (RUN.md, Д33).

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **the name of a NovaTrail repository after a number or a section is a citation's suffix wherever a word boundary follows it, and so is a name that can be a word of prose: `R03 modules сравнивает граф` is a citation of R03 modules, and `R10 engine решил` of R10 engine. An own citation does not put the name of a repository after it as a word of prose. After О-, П- and Т-, a NovaTrail name is a word of the sentence, not a suffix: these registers are `spec`'s, and no other NovaTrail repository keeps them. The first item of the 2026-10-21 amendment is replaced by this.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `sim` В5 (RUN.md of `sim`, `main` 6887f07) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, not by the row's recommendation: its second option, with the triage's refinement about О-, П- and Т-.

In the middle of a sentence the citation was read as its own: `R10 engine решил` in `sim` went red, and `R03 modules сравнивает граф` passed, checked against its own R03.
- **What the trial of 2026-11-08 showed.** The rule of the row's first option on the `main` of `spec` and of the eleven repositories with documents found 113 such places. In `spec` there are 74 of them, with 105 errors — 24 in `docs/decisions.md` and 16 in the epic archives `docs/plan/` —, and in the others 39: in `tutor` 14, `app` 8, `canvas` 5, `.github` 5, `learner-model` 3, `api` 2, `module-kit` 1, `sim` 1; in `engine`, `modules`, `skill-map` and `infra` — none. *Why:* the first option requires rewriting 113 places, among them entries of decision logs, which are not rewritten, and the bodies of done tasks in the archives. The argument by which the 2026-10-21 amendment made `.github` and the hyphenated names a suffix everywhere now holds the name-words too.

*Rejected:* the row's first option — an error with a hint at each ambiguous place: 74 places in `spec` and 39 in other repositories, logs and archives among them; the same, where «и» or "and" after the name ends the sentence — still 48 places in `spec`, 11 of them in the log; the second option without the refinement — `П-15 app показывает` would become another repository's citation and would not be checked, although NovaTrail has no other registers О-, П- and Т-; leaving it as it is — 112 places where a citation of another log is checked against one's own.

## Analyzer findings

**R33. An analyzer's finding that a change cannot close stays open, and its reason is recorded here.** As R51 canvas-api. The findings of CodeQL and Scorecard come to the Security tab, those of SonarCloud to its project, and rule 12 of RUN.md closes them before a new task. The answer is given once, not on each scan, and the next reader tells an answered finding from a new one. The list was compared with the first runs of CodeQL and Scorecard on `main` on 2026-10-20: `spec` — commit f2769e1, Scorecard score 6.6; `module-kit` — 254452e, 6.3 (RUN.md, T17). It is shared by all repositories with the shared checks (R30): their template, devcontainer and author are the same.
- **Scorecard `Code-Review` and `Branch-Protection`** want approvals by a second person. The project has one author, and the ruleset of `main` does without approvals on purpose (R30). Setting up a second account for the sake of the score is worse than the score itself (R51 canvas-api).
- **Scorecard `Pinned-Dependencies`** is about the `npm install -g` of Claude Code in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`. The installation goes by exact version, and npm checks the archive against the hash that the registry publishes: that is the check available to a global installation (R51 canvas-api).
- **CodeQL in `draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`** — `js/xss-through-dom` (high) and four `js/cross-window-information-leak` (medium). This is the loader of a single-file prototype that a design tool built, not the platform's code. The prototype does not ship, and the documents override it ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)); SonarCloud no longer reads it. CodeQL will stop reading it when the shared `codeql.yml` gets an input for exclusions (Д8).
- **Pass with time or with tasks:**
  - `Maintained` — the repositories are younger than 90 days;
  - `SAST` — in `spec`, some of the commits were made before CodeQL;
  - `CI-Tests` — some pull requests were merged before CI: in `spec`, CI checked 11 of 13;
  - `CII-Best-Practices` — there is no OpenSSF Best Practices badge. The author gets it on bestpractices.dev, as canvas-api got it (R51 canvas-api), if the author finds it needed;
  - `Fuzzing` — there is no code yet that parses outside input: `docs-check` reads the documents of the repository itself. Fuzz tests come with such code.

`Signed-Releases` and `Packaging` (−1) and `Contributors` (3 — one organization) give no alerts.

— *Why:* rule 12 of RUN.md and the author's decision of 2026-10-20 to exclude `draft/` from CodeQL, as it is already excluded from SonarCloud. A check that will be red for the whole life of a one-person project is not a defect (R51 canvas-api).

— *Rejected:* closing such findings with the mark "false positive" or "won't fix" — then a new finding of the same rule would disappear silently; leaving the prototype's findings forever, or fixing the generated code — a new prototype would bring them again.

— *Consequence:* a finding not on this list is new, and it is closed by a change (rule 12 of RUN.md). Excluding `draft/` from CodeQL is Д8. — RUN.md, T17; R30.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* CodeQL no longer reads `draft/`, and Д8 is closed. The shared `codeql.yml` of `.github` got the input `paths-ignore` as early as v0.1.1 ("Paths CodeQL leaves out of the analysis of javascript-typescript — draft/**, say", the input's description at v0.1.10, read 2026-10-22), and the `codeql.yml` of `spec` is on v0.1.10 from this day and passes `draft/**`. The analysis of `actions` still reads all workflows. The item about the findings of CodeQL in `draft/NovaTrail Widget.html` above is now about the past: the five alerts are closed by the first analysis of `main` without `draft/`, and a new prototype will not bring them. The references to `.github` in the other shared checks — secrets, DCO and Scorecard — will be raised by Dependabot (RUN.md, Д10).
