## The module format: JSON Schema and conventions

**R45. The module format is JSON Schema 2020-12, and the author writes a module in YAML 1.2.2 with restrictions. The format text, the schemas, the examples and the test vectors lie in `format/` and are written by one set of conventions.** Т-7 is closed. Normatively the conventions are written in English in the format text, [format/README.md](../format/README.md), and here is what is decided, why, and what is rejected.
- **The schemas** are JSON Schema 2020-12, JSON files `format/schemas/<term>.schema.json`. The term is the English term of the part from concepts 15, in kebab-case; the common definitions of the parts lie in `common.schema.json`.
  - `$id` is `https://altnovatrail.github.io/spec/format/`, the number from `format/VERSION`, a slash and the file name. References between schemas are relative. An absolute reference to this prefix is forbidden: it would silently tie the schema to one version.
  - The root of a schema has `title` and `description`, each property has `description`, there too where it has only `$ref`; all in English (R42).
  - An object is closed by `unevaluatedProperties: false` in the schema that describes it whole in its place. A schema that another takes and extends — through `allOf` or through `$ref` beside its own `properties` — is open: closed, it would reject the fields of the extension. `additionalProperties: false` is not used: it does not see properties declared through `$ref` and `allOf`. A dictionary whose keys are data is set by `additionalProperties` with a schema and `propertyNames`.
  - A module is checked by the schemas of exactly its MAJOR.MINOR (R44). So an unknown field is an error, and a module does not take a field of a version newer than its own.
  - The check does not rest on `format`. A `pattern` is written only from the tokens that 2020-12 advises, without `\d`, `\w` and `\s`. The subschema `false` stands only at `unevaluatedProperties`.
  - Marks of our own carry the prefix `x-`, and the format text lists them. For now there is one mark — `x-open`.
- **The names** of fields and of the values of enumerations are the English terms of concepts 15 in snake_case: `answer_slots`, `trap_advice`. A field without a term — `id`, `title`, `version` — is a plain English word, an array is in the plural. A new term first enters concepts 15 (R42). A module writes the format version number as a string: `"0.1"`.
- **The author's YAML** is YAML 1.2.2 with the Core schema, and rules beyond it, each with an ID `yaml.<name>`:
  - UTF-8 without BOM; one document, `---` allowed at the start; without directives, anchors, aliases `*` and tags;
  - keys are strings: quoted or plain by the rule below, but not `null`, `true`, `false` and not a number. After escapes are processed they do not repeat;
  - the plain scalars `null`, `true`, `false` and JSON numbers are these values. A number fits in a double, an integer lies within ±(2^53−1), and `-0` is an error;
  - any other plain scalar is a string. It is not empty, does not start with a digit, `+`, `-`, `.`, `~`, `<` or `=`, and is not equal, case-insensitively, to `y`, `n`, `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `true`, `false` or `null`. Such a string is quoted;
  - strings hold no surrogates and no Unicode noncharacters, and no escape `\/`.

  Comments, block strings and flow collections are allowed. The order of keys carries no meaning, and the reader does not normalize Unicode. A file in JSON syntax is read by the same rules.
- **An open field** is marked by `x-open: true` in the subschema of a property under `properties`, `patternProperties` or `additionalProperties`, beside `$ref` if there is one.
  - A place in a module is open when its parent is open and it itself is an element of an array or is marked; the root of a part is open.
  - A mark counts only if its subschema applies and passes, in the branches of `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `if`/`then`/`else` and `dependentSchemas` too.
  - The field by which an open object chooses a branch of `oneOf` is open.
  - Without the mark a field is closed, so a new field is closed until it is opened explicitly (architecture 1). The key or the predicate, the solution, the traps and the leak phrases are never opened (R05).
  - Opening a closed field is a major format version, and a new field open at once is a minor one (R44).
- **A format rule** is what a schema does not express: a graph without cycles, references, keys (architecture 3.7), and also the rules of YAML.
  - A rule has an ID `<part>.<name>` in kebab-case, where the part is the one in which the violation is reported, and a statement with the word MUST. The ID is not reused.
  - The rule is checked by `module-kit`, and its refusal names the ID. A new rule or one stricter than before is a major version (R44).
- **The test vectors** are normative (R42).
  - The vectors of a rule lie in `format/vectors/rules/<ID>/`. A case is a file, and if the rule links several files, a folder laid out as a module (RUN.md, T26). It passes the schema of its part and breaks only this rule; a vector of a YAML rule breaks only its YAML rule. CI of `spec` checks both, and CI of `module-kit` that the case is rejected with the rule's ID.
  - The valid examples meet the format rules that are checked within a part too, and CI of `module-kit` runs them as well. So each rule also has cases that it lets pass. A rule between parts is checked on examples laid out as a whole module (RUN.md, T26).
  - The vectors of the open view are in `format/vectors/open-view/` (RUN.md, T28); the verdict vectors — T29, of the open view of a template — T33, of the generator — T32, if it puts them in `format/`.
- **The examples** are `format/examples/<term>/valid/<case>.yaml` and `…/invalid/<case>.yaml`. A valid one passes its schema. An invalid one breaks one thing and names in its first line the error it must give: `# error: <keyword> at <place>`.
  - The place is a JSON Pointer in a URI fragment: `#` is the whole file, `#/answer_slots/0` an element. It is the place where the schema with this keyword applies. For `required`, `additionalProperties`, `unevaluatedProperties` and other keywords about an object the place is the object, for keywords about an array the array, for `type`, `enum`, `const`, `pattern` and other keywords about a value the value.
  - `$ref`, `allOf`, `properties`, `items` and `if`/`then`/`else` are not named: the keyword that failed inside is named. `oneOf` and `anyOf` are named when no branch passed.
  - The check looks for this pair among all errors of the validator, not for the text of the message: validators have different texts.
  - The examples show the format and check the schemas, but add no rules (R42).
- **The folder `format/`:**
  - `README.md` — the format text, in English, with normative words by BCP 14 and numbered sections;
  - `VERSION` — the version number, now `0.1` (R44);
  - `vectors/` will be started by RUN.md, T25: it writes the vectors of the YAML rules together with their check. `schemas/` and `examples/` will come with T26 and the following tasks.

  The folder and the number appeared in this task, before the first schema — amendments to R42 and R44.
- **What R45 does not decide.** The packages for code from the releases of `spec` are still R21, and how they come out, RUN.md, T35, decides. How the open view goes into the contract `app` ↔ `api` on protobuf, epic E3 will decide.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-22 in the planning of T24, by the plan's recommendations: Т-7, the version of JSON Schema, `$id`, the mark of an open field, the error of an example, YAML and the style of names. The rest — the rules for `$ref`, the closing of objects, `pattern`, the format rules and the vectors — is the plan's proposal after an independent review of the draft. All sources were read 2026-10-22.
- **JSON Schema 2020-12.** "The current version is 2020-12!" ([JSON Schema, Specification](https://json-schema.org/specification)). It is implemented by validators in both languages of the platform — `spec`, `canvas` and `app` are written in TypeScript, `module-kit` in Go:
  - ajv 8.20.0 under MIT: "Supports JSON Schema draft-04/06/07/2019-09/2020-12" ([ajv-validator/ajv](https://github.com/ajv-validator/ajv), README);
  - santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema 6.0.3 under Apache-2.0, whose README marks 2020-12 with a Bowtie badge ([santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema](https://github.com/santhosh-tekuri/jsonschema)).

  In draft-07 a mark beside `$ref` would be lost: "All other properties in a "$ref" object MUST be ignored" ([JSON Schema draft-07 core](https://json-schema.org/draft-07/draft-handrews-json-schema-01), §8.3). The author writes data, not API messages: JSON Schema checks the author's YAML directly and expresses enumerations, string patterns and conditions.
- **`$id`.** "Note that this URI is an identifier and not necessarily a network locator" ([JSON Schema 2020-12 core](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core), §8.2.1). The address of a project on GitHub Pages is "http(s)://<owner>.github.io/<repositoryname>" ([GitHub Docs, About GitHub Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/about-github-pages)): this is the organization's space, nobody else will take it. The address is hierarchical, so the references between schemas are relative, and the version number stands only in `$id`.
- **`x-open`.** "Unknown keywords SHOULD be treated as annotations, where the value of the keyword is the value of the annotation" (2020-12 core, §4.3.1). The next version of JSON Schema will not allow unknown keywords, and for user marks "the prefix `x-` has been selected" ([json-schema-spec, ADR 2023-04-sva-prefix](https://github.com/json-schema-org/json-schema-spec/blob/main/adr/2023-04-sva-prefix.md), accepted 2023-04-04). A mark in the schema itself will not diverge from the schema, as a separate list would.
- **The error of an example.** The output unit of 2020-12 names the keyword and the place: "The JSON key for this information is `keywordLocation`" and likewise "`instanceLocation`" (2020-12 core, §12.3). So the comparison does not depend on the texts of messages. The whole document in a URI fragment is `#` ([RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901), §6).
- **YAML.**
  - YAML 1.2 was conceived as a superset of JSON: "Its primary focus was making YAML a strict superset of JSON" ([YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/), §1.2). Keys in it are unique: "each of the keys is unique" (ibid., §3.2.1.1). The Core schema is "the recommended default schema": a plain scalar that resembles nothing it reads as a string, while the JSON schema counts such a scalar an error, and then the whole text would have to be quoted (ibid., chapter 10).
  - Parsers read the same thing differently. `go-yaml`, which the YAML organization maintains, "Supports octals encoded and decoded as `0777` per YAML 1.1, rather than `0o777` as specified in YAML 1.2" and "Supports YAML 1.1 bools (`yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`) as long as they are being decoded into a typed bool value" ([yaml/go-yaml](https://github.com/yaml/go-yaml), README, commit 32734c3), while the Core schema reads `0777` as 777. So the format leaves plain only the scalars that all read alike, and the others are quoted.
  - Characters, numbers and repeated keys follow I-JSON ([RFC 7493](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7493), §2.1–2.3):
    - strings "MUST NOT include code points that identify Surrogates or Noncharacters";
    - numbers no larger than a double allows, and integers in "[-(2**53)+1, (2**53)-1]";
    - repeated names are counted "after processing any escaped characters".

    Then Go and TypeScript get the same JSON value from a file.
- **snake_case** — as the content of standalone, which is carried over into `modules`, writes: `grade_level`, `correct_answer`, `builds_on` (mathtrail-standalone, commit c6cbeb2). And as the fields of protobuf: "Use snake_case for field names, including extensions. Use pluralized names for repeated fields" ([Protocol Buffers Style Guide](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/style/)).
- **The normative words** follow BCP 14: they are normative "when, and only when, they appear in all capitals" ([RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174)).

— *Rejected:*
- protobuf for the modules too — one format for everything, the second option of Т-7: the author would write the text format of protobuf or its JSON, and protobuf does not itself express enumerations, string patterns and conditions;
- draft-07: without `unevaluatedProperties` and `$defs`, and keys beside `$ref` do not act in it;
- `$id` on a domain of our own: there is no domain, and the purchase waits for О-16. If a domain appears before v1, `$id` moves to it with the next 0.y;
- `$id` as a URN: there are no relative references, and the version number would stand in every reference;
- a separate list of open fields — it is edited apart from the schema and can diverge from it;
- a JSON Schema vocabulary of our own with its own metaschema — it would have to be written and released together with the format;
- a file of expectations at the invalid examples — a second place that can diverge from the example;
- one keyword without the place — an example could fail not where it was meant to;
- YAML 1.2.2 Core without restrictions: numbers and booleans would depend on the parser, and anchors and aliases make a file not a tree;
- JSON only: without comments and multiline strings it is harder for authors to write, and `modules` already plans to write YAML;
- camelCase: standalone and `tutor` write in snake_case, and carrying the tasks over would rename every field;
- `additionalProperties: false` for closing an object — it does not see properties declared through `$ref` and `allOf`.

— *Consequence:*
- Т-7 is closed (repositories 8); amendments to R11, R42 and R44.
- CLAUDE.md, README.md and repositories 5 name the format text and the version number.
- concepts 1 and 15 — snake_case in the schemas; the terms "open field", "format example", "test vector" and "format rule", and with them "solution" and "leak phrase", which the format text names; "open view" — at any part of a module. architecture 1 and 3.7 — the open view by `x-open`, YAML with restrictions and the format rules by ID. repositories 3 — the vectors of the rules.
- What R45 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-22, T24)» at table 1 of RUN.md. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д21.

— concepts 1, 15; architecture 1, 3.7; repositories 3, 5, 8; RUN.md, T24.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* what the format check `just format-check` made precise (RUN.md, T25). The author's answer in its planning: where the check needs an exact reading, the format text gives it, together with the limits of Go for `pattern`. Version 0.1 is a draft until T35, and the number does not change (R44). Normatively the refinements are written in English in [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 4, 5 and 7.
- **The keywords of a schema** are only the list of the [format text](../format/README.md), section 5: the keywords of 2020-12 and `x-open`, and `$schema` and `$id` only at the root. The strict mode of `ajv` does not hold this: it lets through `nullable`, `definitions` and `dependencies`, which 2020-12 does not have. Of 2020-12, the list leaves out:
  - `$anchor`, `$dynamicRef`, `$dynamicAnchor` and `$vocabulary` — a reference names only `$defs`;
  - `minContains` and `maxContains` — `ajv` names their error `contains` (`dist/vocabularies/applicator/contains.js`, 8.20.0), and an invalid example would name a keyword the specification does not name;
  - `unevaluatedItems` — the test runner of `ajv` skips the cases of the JSON Schema suite where it meets `contains` (`spec/json-schema.spec.ts`, v8.20.0), and an array has enough with `items` and `maxItems`;
  - the content vocabulary — the format does not need it.
- **`$ref`** is one of three forms: `#/$defs/<name>`, `<file>.schema.json` or `<file>.schema.json#/$defs/<name>`. A ban on the prefix of `$id` is not enough: `../0.1/common.schema.json` would also tie the schema to a version, and `ajv` allows it.
- **`description`** is at the subschema of each field: under `properties` and `patternProperties` and at the schema of the values of a dictionary. A condition — what `if` and `not` hold — does not need it.
- **Closing is by place**, as the text said: "Only the schema at the object's place closes it".
  - A place is the root of a schema or a subschema directly under `properties`, `patternProperties`, `additionalProperties`, `items`, `prefixItems` or `contains`, outside a condition. The entries of `$defs`, the targets of `$ref` and the branches of `allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `not` and `dependentSchemas` are parts of the place.
  - If the parts of a place describe an object, the place has `unevaluatedProperties: false`. `unevaluatedProperties` stands only at a place and only as `false`, and beside a `$ref` to an object there is the line `"unevaluatedProperties": false`. A dictionary is closed by `additionalProperties` with a schema and `propertyNames`.
- **A name from `if` or `not`** is declared also by a part of the place that always applies: the place itself or where its `$ref` and `allOf` lead. By 2020-12 a subschema that failed gives no annotations, while `ajv` counts a field of a failed `if` as evaluated when there is an `else`. The test runner of `ajv` skips this case of the suite: "unevaluatedProperties with if/then/else, then not defined" — "when if is false and has unevaluated properties" (`spec/json-schema.spec.ts`, v8.20.0). Without the rule, `spec` would let through a value that the validator of `module-kit` rejects by 2020-12.
- **`pattern`** — and the keys of `patternProperties`. Beyond the tokens of 2020-12 — so that Go and JavaScript, into which `ajv` compiles a pattern in mode `u`, read alike:
  - in a class `[` and `]` are escaped, `-` is first, last or between the ends of a range, a range is ascending, there is no empty class. Go reads `[]a]` as a class of `]` and `a` — "] and - are okay as first char in class" (`parseClass`) — and rejects `[^]`, while JavaScript rejects `[]a]` and accepts `[^]`;
  - outside a class `{`, `}` and `]` only in a quantifier or escaped: Go reads them as letters, while JavaScript rejects them;
  - a count has no leading zeros — "Disallow leading zeros" (`parseInt`): `a{01}` in Go is letters, and in JavaScript `a{1}`;
  - neither a count nor the product of nested counts is greater than 1000, and Go counts them so: `{x}` and `{x,y}` by the largest, `{x,}` by `x`, and `{0,}` as 1: "Implementation restriction: The counting forms x{n,m}, x{n,}, and x{n} reject forms that create a minimum or maximum repetition count above 1000" (`doc.go`; `repeatIsValid` in `parse.go`).

  Go — `src/regexp/syntax`, commit fb3c20e; JavaScript — `new RegExp(pattern, "u")` in Node 24 of the devcontainer.
- **`yaml.json-scalars`**: an integer is a number written without a fraction and an exponent, as go-yaml divides int and float. Any number is finite as a double, and precision is not a criterion: otherwise `0.1` would be a violation too. There is no negative zero in any notation, as there is no negative number that a double rounds to zero, such as `-1e-400`: it reads as the same −0.
- **`yaml.characters`**: an escaped surrogate is forbidden both in a pair and in the form `\U`. `yaml` joins a pair into one character, while go-yaml rejects any such escape: "found invalid Unicode character escape code" (`internal/libyaml/scanner.go`, commit 32734c3). Escapes are read from left to right, and `\\/` is a backslash and a slash.
- **Not YAML** — also a character outside the printable set of [YAML 1.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/), section 5.1, even in a comment. `yaml` lets through the C0 control characters and U+FFFE, while go-yaml rejects them: "control characters are not allowed" (`internal/libyaml/reader.go`, commit 32734c3). This is YAML itself, not a rule `yaml.*`.
- **The rules of a part** are listed in the [format text](../format/README.md) as a table whose first column is the ID, like the YAML rules in section 4. By the tables, `just format-check` matches the rules with their vectors.

*Why:* the author's answer in the planning of T25 and the review of the plan's draft by an independent agent: it found where the draft diverged from 2020-12, from `ajv` and from Go, and this was checked against the primary sources. All was read 2026-10-22.

*Rejected:*
- the rule of "extensible" subschemas from the draft: the branches of `allOf`, the targets of `$ref` beside their own fields and the branches at a schema with its own fields are open, and the other objects closed. It let through an open object — `if`, `then` and `else` without fields of their own — and rejected a lawful one — a common base with `oneOf` —, and an edit of the base in one file pulled edits of places in others;
- a dynamic probe — an unknown field in each object of the valid examples: it sees only what is in the examples;
- the strict mode of `ajv` instead of the list of keywords;
- an integer by value: then `1e300` too would be an integer out of bounds;
- snake_case for the values of `enum` too: they hold `"0.1"`, SPDX identifiers and BCP 47 tags;
- to leave the text as it is and put what is disputed into an open question: the check and the text would say different things.

*Consequence:* `just format-check` checks all this, and T26–T34 write the schemas so. The components get the amendment together with R45 (RUN.md, Д21). — [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 4, 5, 7; RUN.md, T25.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* the layout of a folder vector and of the examples of a whole module, which R45 left to RUN.md, T26, was decided by R46. An example of a whole module is a folder `format/examples/module/valid/<case>/`, and a vector of a rule that links files is a folder laid out as a module. The rules of the whole module `module.*` and `manifest.format-version` are checked by `just format-check` itself, like the YAML rules.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* a field that names by a verb how its element is linked with others is an array even without the plural: `replaced_by` of a retired skill is the skills that replaced it (R49). So the name reads as a link, not as an object. The other arrays are in the plural. This is the plan's proposal in the planning of RUN.md, T27; normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), section 5.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* `format/schemas/` also holds a schema that describes no part of a module — the vocabulary of the shared taxonomy, `shared-taxonomy.schema.json` (R50). Its name is a term of concepts 15 too, "shared taxonomy"; the parts reference it, as they do `common.schema.json`, and it has no examples of its own. `teaches` of a skill is a link named by a verb, like `replaced_by`, and so an array without the plural. Normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 3 and 5.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* what the task brought (R51; RUN.md, T28).
- **The vectors of the open view** are folders `format/vectors/open-view/<part>/<case>/`: `part.yaml` — a part that passes its schema, and `open-view.yaml` — its open view. This is a kind of folder of its own, not laid out as a module. `format-check` itself builds the open view too — by a second implementation beside `module-kit`, like the YAML rules and the rules of the whole module —, and compares it with the vector without regard to the order of keys.
- **The mark `x-open` counts** only where its subschema applies and passes: JSON Schema 2020-12 collects an annotation only at a subschema that passes — "Schema objects that produce a false assertion result MUST NOT produce any annotation results" ([2020-12 core](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core), §7.7.1.2, read 2026-10-26). Under `if`, `not`, `contains` and `propertyNames` the mark opens nothing, and `format-check` does not let it through there. The field by which an open object chooses a branch of `if`/`then` is open, as is the field that chooses a branch of `oneOf`.
- **The placeholder `<id>`** in the layout is a name in the form of a local ID before the extension of the last name: `tasks/<id>.yaml`. `format-check` checks the form of the name by the definition `local_id` from `common.schema.json`, not by a copy of its pattern.

Normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 6, 9 and 10.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the verdict vectors (R56). They lie in `format/vectors/verdicts/<kind>/<case>.yaml`, and their schema `verdict-vector.schema.json` is the third schema that describes no part of a module: it describes vectors and references the schema of a task. `format-check` computes their verdicts by a second implementation, `tools/format-check/verdicts.mjs`, as it builds the open view; for a predicate only "blank" and "not in notation", since `spec` has no Starlark. The item "the verdict vectors — T29" is done by this.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the leak vectors (R57). They lie in `format/vectors/leaks/<case>.yaml`, and their schema `leak-vector.schema.json` is the fourth schema that describes no part of a module: it describes vectors and references the schema of a task. `format-check` computes them by a second implementation, `tools/format-check/leaks.mjs`. Among what is never opened are now named the trap values, the trap catalog and the traps of a task too. The new fields — `trap_advice`, `trap_values`, `rung_templates`, `simpler_case`, `leak_phrases`, `givens`, `unknown`, `exit_condition` — are terms of concepts 15.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the rule `lesson.no-leaks` (R58). `format-check` computes it itself, together with the leak check: on its vectors, on the valid modules and on the module vectors of other rules. Its vectors are only module folders: the rule covers a lesson and its tasks. The parts of the task statement, the canvas and the rectangle of the sheet now lie in `common.schema.json`. The schema of a lesson references them, and the schema of a part does not reference the schema of another part ([format text](../format/README.md), section 3). The new fields of a lesson — `segments`, `explanation`, `worked_example`, `demo` and `area` — are terms of concepts 15.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the generator vectors (R59). They lie in `format/vectors/random/<case>.yaml`, and their schema `random-vector.schema.json` is the fifth schema that describes no part of a module, and the only one of them that references no other. The 64-bit integers in them are strings of decimal digits: a YAML number holds an integer of no more than 53 bits. `format-check` computes them by a second implementation, `tools/format-check/random.mjs`, and it is checked against the references of Go and RFC 9923. The item "of the generator — T32, if it puts them in `format/`" is done by this.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* the template vectors (R60) — `format/vectors/templates/<case>.yaml` by the schema `template-vector.schema.json`, the sixth schema without a part: a template, the number of its instances, and attempts — the seed, the numbers of the instance and the instance itself. `format-check` computes them by a second implementation — `expressions.mjs` and `templates.mjs` —, and checks the rules of a task and `lesson.no-leaks`, which it implements, on each instance. Leak vectors do not hold templates: a leak of a template is looked for by its instances.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* four more schemas without a part — `canonical-view.schema.json` and `inventory.schema.json` of the package, each by its term of concepts 15, and `tier-vector.schema.json` and `package-vector.schema.json` of the vectors; there are now ten schemas without a part, and of them only the inventory has examples. The schema of the canonical view references the schemas of the parts: the rule that the schema of a part does not reference the schema of another part does not concern it. The integers `from` and `to` of a template's range and the width and height of a picture got the bounds ±(2^53−1): an integer written with an exponent, `1e20`, passed `type: integer` and `yaml.json-scalars`. — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* two more schemas without a part: `module-index.schema.json` of the module index, by its term of concepts 15 and with examples of its own, and `index-vector.schema.json` of its vectors. There are now twelve schemas without a part, and of them the inventory and the index have examples of their own. The rules of the index, `module-index.<name>`, reject the build of an index, not a module, and their vectors are refusals among the index vectors, `format/vectors/indexes/`, not folders of `vectors/rules/`. `teaches` of an index record is a string in the form of an anchor skill's ID, not a `$ref` to the vocabulary: the record lives longer than the version of the vocabulary. — R63; RUN.md, T44.

— *Amendment 2026-11-04:* **a schema of the format does not take `dependentSchemas` and does not put `$ref` beside `oneOf` or `anyOf` in one subschema, and `format-check` rejects both forms and names the cause.** The author's answer of 2026-11-04 to question В25 of RUN.md — option (a), by its recommendation; the errors of `ajv` 8.20.0 themselves were recorded by R51. Beside `unevaluatedProperties: false`, by which each object is closed at its place, `ajv` counts the fields of the place as unevaluated when the object lacks the key of `dependentSchemas` or when, at `$ref` together with `oneOf` or `anyOf`, a branch other than the first passes, and it rejects a value valid by 2020-12, and its error names `unevaluatedProperties`, not the cause. There is no release of `ajv` newer than 8.20.0 (npm, read 2026-11-04). Both forms have a workaround, and the refusal names it: `allOf` with `if: {required: [<key>]}` and `then` instead of `dependentSchemas`, and `$ref` or the branches in `allOf` — these `ajv` checks correctly, and the test of `format-check` that pins both errors checks the workarounds too. No schema of format 0.3 and of the admission table takes either form, so there is no new version: neither a module, nor a package, nor an index changes by this, only how `spec` writes its schemas changes. The trial schema of the tests of `format-check` held `$ref` beside `oneOf` and now puts it in `allOf`. The check of the conventions and the open view still go through the branches of `dependentSchemas`, so what stands in them is checked too, and a new amendment will lift the ban when `ajv` fixes the errors and the test says so. Rejected: to report the errors to `ajv` — not now, it is an action outside the repository (rule 4 of RUN.md); another validator of 2020-12 — a new dependency by R12, and the headers of the errors of the invalid examples would have to be checked again; to do nothing — the author of a schema would learn of the form only when their valid example failed, and not for that reason.

## Module manifest and layout

**R46. A module is a folder: the manifest `manifest.yaml`, the files of its parts, `media/`, `eval/` and an optional `NOTICE`. The module ID is `<publisher>/<name>`, skills, tasks, traps, techniques and lessons have a local ID, and the module version is semver `X.Y.Z`. A module has one explanation language.** The author's answers when planning RUN.md, T26. Normatively it is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 10 and 11, and in the schemas `common.schema.json` and `manifest.schema.json`; here is what was decided, why, and what was rejected.
- **Identifiers.**
  - The module ID is `<publisher>/<name>`, both in kebab-case starting with a letter: `novatrail/olympiad-math`. A publisher owns the namespace of its modules, so the module IDs of two authors will not coincide (concepts 3).
  - A skill, a task, a trap, a technique and a lesson have a local ID: kebab-case starting with a letter, no longer than 64 characters, unique within its kind inside the module. The module's files name its parts only so.
  - The full ID is the module, the kind and the local ID joined by `/`: `novatrail/olympiad-math/skill/counting-gaps`. The kinds are `skill`, `task`, `trap`, `technique` and `lesson`. The learner model, the engine and progress know a part of a module by its full ID, and the module's files do not hold it.
  - Neither the publisher and the name in the module ID nor a local ID is ever the name of a Windows device — `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`–`com9`, `lpt1`–`lpt9`: a local ID becomes a file name, and a module ID may become a folder path.
- **The module version** is semver `X.Y.Z`, as a quoted string, with no pre-releases and no build metadata. To allow them later is to widen the pattern, and that is a minor format version (R44).
- **The layout.** A module is a folder, and what lies in it is set by the table of the format text: the path, the part the schema checks, and what is in the file.
  - `manifest.yaml` is the manifest; `media/` holds pictures and sound; `eval/` is the eval set, and its format will come with the eval protocol (epic E3); `NOTICE` holds the license notices and is optional.
  - A part of which a module has one is a file in the root, named by its term: `skill-graph.yaml`. Parts of which a module has many — tasks and lessons — lie in a folder, a file for each: the file is named by its local ID and carries it in the field `id`. So the open view and the canonical view get the ID from the part itself. The rows of the layout come with the tasks of their parts, T27–T33, and the rule "a file's name is its `id`" with the first such part, T28.
  - Names are compared exactly as the folder lists them, case-sensitive. Files and folders starting with `.` are not part of the module, a folder without files holds nothing, there are no symbolic links, and the order of files carries no meaning.
  - Where the module's folder lies and what it is called, the format does not say: `modules` decides that (architecture 3.10).
- **The manifest** is `manifest.yaml` by the schema `manifest.schema.json`, and all its fields are open:
  - `module_format_version` — the format version, as a string: `"0.1"`. It stands in the root of the manifest in every format version (R44), and the schema gives it the pattern MAJOR.MINOR, not a single value. A version the reader does not read is rejected by the rule `manifest.format-version`;
  - `id` and `version`; `title` — in the explanation language;
  - `subject` — the subject code: `mathematics`, `physics` or `writing`. `physics` is for the manifest of a third-party module, as in concepts 16.3. A new code is a new value of the list, that is, a minor version (R44), and v1 will hold only the codes of the modules of the first slice;
  - `audience.age_categories` — a non-empty list without repeats of the age category codes of concepts 13: `under_13`, `from_13_to_consent`, `from_consent_to_18` and `adult`. The platform offers the module only to learners of these categories (privacy 3.2);
  - `languages.explanation` — the explanation language, and `languages.target` — the target language, only in a language module. A language is a BCP 47 tag of the language, the script and the region, and the script and the region are optional. The case of letters is as in the registry: `en`, `zh-Hans`, `pt-BR`, `es-419`. The schema checks the form of the tag, but not that it is in the registry;
  - `authors` — a non-empty list of `{ name }`;
  - `license` — an SPDX identifier: letters, digits, `.` and `-`; the official modules have `Apache-2.0` (R20). Whether it is in the SPDX list, the schema does not check.
- **One explanation language per module** in v0. All the module's texts are in it, except the material of a language module: that is in the target language. There are no translations in format v0, and the same content in another explanation language is another module, with its own ID and its own progress. Translations later are most likely files by language on top of the module's texts. That is an addition, a minor version, and earlier modules do not change.
- **Media files** are PNG, JPEG, WebP and MP3, with one extension for each format: `.png`, `.jpg`, `.webp` and `.mp3`. A part refers to a file by its path from `media/`: names in kebab-case joined by `/` and an extension, no longer than 128 characters — `pictures/ladder.png` (`media_path` in `common.schema.json`).
- **Rules.** The rules of the whole module have the part `module`, and it has no schema of its own:
  - `module.manifest` — the module's folder has `manifest.yaml`;
  - `module.layout` — every file stands at a path of the layout table, and the module holds nothing but files and folders.

  A module may break both rules — for example, with `Manifest.yaml` instead of `manifest.yaml` — but each vector breaks exactly one. What lies in `media/` the rule `module.media` will say (T28). The rules `module.manifest` and `module.layout` and the manifest's rule `manifest.format-version` `just format-check` checks itself, like the YAML rules, and it reads the layout table from the format text.
- **Examples and vectors.**
  - An example of a whole module is a folder `format/examples/module/valid/<case>/`, laid out as a module: the files with a part pass their schemas, and the module breaks no rule. There are no invalid examples of a whole module: a module that breaks a rule is a vector of that rule.
  - A vector of a rule that links files is a folder laid out as a module. A vector of a rule of the whole module breaks only that rule, and a vector of a part's rule passes the rules of the whole module and holds the file of its part.
  - The manifest in an example and a vector names the version from `format/VERSION`, except the vectors of `manifest.format-version`: they name a version outside the window of the reader of this version (R44). One names `"0.0"`, which the format never had, the other the next minor version.
- **Common definitions** are `common.schema.json`: the format version, the module ID and version, the local ID and, on it, the ID of a skill, a task, a trap, a technique and a lesson, the language tag, the license, the age category, the subject, the media file path, and text — a non-empty string. The patterns are of the subset of R45: with classes, without `\d` and `(?:`.
- **What R46 does not decide:**
  - translations — and what they will have to cover: leak phrases, the keys of text answers, the open view, the types of `app` and `canvas`;
  - the presentation style — О-23;
  - the field `dependencies` and the grade as a label of the module and a starting point — RUN.md, T27, together with the form of the ID of the taxonomy's dictionary. This departs from «Сделать» of T26: «зависимости от общей таксономии — поле»;
  - the rule `module.media` with file signatures and binary vectors, the rule of the file name of a part, and standalone's description pictures — T28;
  - what goes into the module package — `NOTICE` and the license text — T34;
  - who may publish under which publisher — the publication rules (О-9) — and which licenses third-party modules carry (О-10);
  - SPDX expressions such as `MIT OR Apache-2.0` and BCP 47 tags with variants and extensions: to widen the pattern later is a minor version.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-22 when planning T26, by the plan's recommendations: the form of the ID, a module as a folder, one explanation language, the presentation style outside the manifest, `dependencies` with T27 and `module.media` with T28. The rest — the manifest's fields, the rules and the layout of the vectors — is the plan's proposal after an independent check of the draft. All sources were read 2026-10-22.
- **A local ID, and the full ID outside the module.** A module's file does not repeat its module's ID in every reference, and renaming the module does not touch its files. The full ID is needed where parts of different modules lie side by side: in the learner model, the engine and progress.
- **A folder, not one file.** The olympiad maths module has 603 tasks (product 10). In one file an edit of a task is an edit of the whole module, and in a folder of one file, and a pull request of `modules` shows it separately. A file per task, not per topic as in standalone (c6cbeb2): a topic is a label of the task, and a task that changes its topic does not move.
- **The format version as a pattern.** A single value, `const`, would reject the manifests of the earlier version already in the schema of the next minor version, though a minor version only adds (R44). A refusal by version is a rule with its own vectors, and the reader names its ID.
- **The case of language tags.** BCP 47 compares tags without case: "language tags and their subtags, including private use and extensions, are to be treated as case insensitive", but "The format of subtags in the registry is RECOMMENDED as the form to use in language tags" ([RFC 5646](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5646), §2.1.1). The format takes the registry's form, and one tag is always written as one string.
- **semver:** "A normal version number MUST take the form X.Y.Z where X, Y, and Z are non-negative integers, and MUST NOT contain leading zeroes" ([Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html), item 2). The regular expression of its FAQ writes `\d` and `(?:`, which the `pattern` subset of R45 lacks, so the pattern is written with classes.
- **SPDX.** An identifier is "idstring = 1*(ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." )" ([SPDX License Expressions](https://spdx.github.io/spdx-spec/v3.0.1/annexes/spdx-license-expressions/)); the list is SPDX License List 3.29.0 of 2026-09-16 ([spdx.org/licenses](https://spdx.org/licenses/)).
- **The media formats** are those every browser shows ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/), mdn/content, `main` 8bc3252):
  - PNG, JPEG and WebP — "All versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera, and Safari" ([Image file type and format guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Formats/Image_types));
  - MP3 — "MP3 (MPEG-1 Audio Layer III) is supported by all major browsers" ([Web audio codec guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Formats/Audio_codecs)).
- **The names of Windows devices** — "Do not use the following reserved names for the name of a file: CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1, …, LPT9 … Also avoid these names followed immediately by an extension; for example, NUL.txt and NUL.tar.gz are both equivalent to NUL", and also "Do not assume case sensitivity" ([Microsoft, Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/naming-a-file), revision of 2024-08-28). Hence IDs and names in lowercase only, and names compared by the folder's listing.
- **`NOTICE`** is for the notices that licenses require to be kept. Apache-2.0: "If the Work includes a "NOTICE" text file as part of its distribution, then any Derivative Works that You distribute must include a readable copy of the attribution notices contained within such NOTICE file" ([Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), section 4(d)), and the recipient gets a copy of the license too: "You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License" ([Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), section 4(a)). MIT: "The above copyright notice and this permission notice shall be included in all copies or substantial portions of the Software" ([MIT License](https://opensource.org/license/mit)). standalone's tasks are under MIT, and whether to keep their notice or to re-release the content under Apache-2.0, `modules` decides (RUN.md `modules`, T03).

— *Rejected:*
- full IDs in the module's files, as in the illustrations of concepts 16: every reference would repeat the module's ID;
- IDs in standalone's styles — `logic.knights_liars`, `off_by_one`, `cal-12-d1-1` (c6cbeb2): an ID becomes a file name, and one style is needed. Carrying over standalone's IDs — `.` and `_` into `-`, with a check for collisions — is the work of `modules` (RUN.md, Д22);
- a module as one file and tasks in groups by topic, as in standalone;
- translations in the module at once: what they are to cover is not decided, and to add them later is a minor version;
- the presentation style in the manifest: there is no list of styles either in the documents or in the components, and a field without a list would fix only a name (О-23);
- `dependencies` in a temporary form now: T27 decides the form of the ID of the taxonomy's dictionary, and an edit of the temporary form would be breaking;
- `const` for the format version — the argument above;
- SVG: it is code that the browser draws, and the ban on scripts in it is "For security purposes, some browsers place restrictions on SVG content when it's being used as an image. Specifically, the following limitations may apply: JavaScript is disabled" ([MDN, SVG as an image](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Guides/SVG_as_an_image)): "some" and "may" are no promise;
- AVIF: "As support is not yet comprehensive (and has little historical depth) you should provide a fallback in WebP, JPEG or PNG format" (MDN, Image file type and format guide);
- Opus and Vorbis in Ogg: "Safari 18.4+ (on macOS 15.4+, iOS 18.4+, iPadOS 18.4+, and visionOS 2.4+) added support for Opus and Vorbis codecs in Ogg containers" ([MDN, Media container formats](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Media/Guides/Formats/Containers)) — devices older than that will not play them;
- `.jpeg` beside `.jpg`: two extensions of one format would give one file two names;
- SPDX expressions now: О-10 is open, and one license is enough for the official modules.

— *Consequence:*
- concepts 3, 13 and 15 — the module ID, the local ID, the full ID, the module layout, the subject, the audience, the explanation language, the target language, the license notices, the age category codes and the field `module_format_version`. О-23 is in product 13.2; architecture 3.10 — what is inside the module's folder.
- Amendments to R41, R44 and R45: translations, the place of the format version in the manifest and the layout of folder vectors were decided by R46.
- What R46 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-22, T26)» at table 1 of RUN.md. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д22.

— concepts 3, 13, 15; product 13.2; architecture 3.10; [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 10, 11; RUN.md, T26.

The field `dependencies` and the form of the ID of the taxonomy's dictionary are decided by RUN.md, T42: when planning T27 the author split the shared taxonomy off into that task.

The ID of an anchor skill is `core.<name>`. An anchor skill is not part of a module and has no full ID: outside a module the same ID names it. The rule `module.media`: a file in `media/` stands at a path of the form `media_path` and begins with the signature of its format. Both, like `module.manifest` and `module.layout`, `format-check` checks itself.

These are parts of which a module has one each — files in the root: the solving steps are named by their term, and a catalog by the entries it holds, in the plural. A published ID of a trap, like that of a skill, never names another trap: the learner's progress counts traps by their full IDs. The eval set is not part of the package. So the item "what goes into the module package — `NOTICE` and the license text" of "What R46 does not decide" is answered. — R62; RUN.md, T34.

## AI providers and age

**R47. Google's generative AI is closed on the platform — both the Gemini API and Vertex AI: for all learners on both AI routes and for the other parts of the platform — until a lawyer answers otherwise.** The author's answer to the `tutor` row В5 «в реестр spec» (RUN.md `tutor`, commit 3029dfb), by its recommendation.
- **What the terms say.** Google Cloud's Service Specific Terms, section "20. Generative AI Services", item "d. Age Restrictions": "Customer will not, and will not allow End Users to, use a Generative AI Service as part of a website, Customer Application, or other online service that is directed towards or is likely to be accessed by individuals under the age of 18". Item "f. Suspected Violations": "Google may immediately suspend or terminate Customer's use of a Generative AI Service based on any suspected violation of … subsection (d) above" — a reference to another item of the same terms is left out ([Google Cloud Service Specific Terms](https://cloud.google.com/terms/service-terms), "Last modified October 12, 2026").
- **Vertex AI is generative AI of these terms.** Among the Generative AI Services is "Generative AI on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Generative AI on Vertex AI)", and also "Generative AI Services also includes any generative AI features or functionality of a Service" ([Google Cloud Platform Services Summary](https://cloud.google.com/terms/services), "Last modified October 21, 2026"). Both pages were read 2026-10-22.
- **What follows from it** is our conclusion, not a legal one, as in privacy 5.3. The condition concerns the service as a whole, as for the Gemini API in the AI Studio variant, and NovaTrail is open to children (R06). So Google's models are closed for all learners, adults too — both through platform AI and with an own key: with an own key the key's owner accepts the terms, but the service in which the call runs is still NovaTrail.
- **Not only learners.** The condition speaks of the service, not of who calls the model. So a part of the platform that serves not learners — for example, the authors' pipeline of stage 4 — takes no Google models either: it goes to AI providers through `tutor` (architecture 3.13).
- **What is open** is for a lawyer, together with П-3: whether Google's models are allowed in a separate deployment or service for adults only. Until the answer the route is closed.

— *Why:* the recommendation of `tutor` in В5. privacy 5.3, checked 2026-10-18, wrote of Vertex AI: «В Service Specific Terms такой фразы не нашлось». But item (d) is there, and with the same text it stood already in the revision of 2024-07-18: `tutor` checked it by the archive of the terms 2026-10-21 (architecture 4 tutor). The study "A child's handwriting on the canvas and the AI tutor" («Рукопись ребёнка на канве и ИИ-наставник»), by its own reading, also not a legal one, comes to the same (ibid.). And item (f) lets Google stop the service on a mere suspicion: a platform that kept learners on Google's models would risk this AI route as a whole. The item "Not only learners" is the executor's proposal, by the same reading of the condition.

— *Rejected:*
- Google's models in a separate deployment for adults — now: by the study's reading the ban concerns a platform open to children as a whole, and that is a question for a lawyer (П-3);
- asking Google for an exception, and leaving the route open until the answer: the answer would come when learners' data had already gone;
- closing Google only to learners and leaving it to the other parts of the platform: the condition is about the service, and they are parts of the same NovaTrail.

— *Consequence:*
- privacy 2, 5.3 and 10, П-3, Т-20, product 6 and architecture 3.6 speak of Google by R47. Without Google the platform keeps OpenAI and Anthropic: privacy 5.3 has not checked other providers yet.
- R07 does not change: "The providers' rules about age are kept" — R47 applies it.
- `tutor` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д26. The measurement is not affected: Google was removed from it already on 2026-10-21 (R06 tutor).

— privacy 2, 5.3, 9, 10; product 6; repositories 8; architecture 3.6, 3.13; RUN.md, Д26.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **the Prompt API in Chrome — Google's generative AI on the device, Gemini Nano — is closed too, by this decision.** The author's answer to the `tutor` row В27 «в реестр spec» (RUN.md `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), by the recommendation of `tutor`; reading on the device is R66.
- On Chrome's pages about this API `tutor` found no age terms, and it did not read Google's general terms, to which their footer refers. For the same model on Android, the [ML Kit GenAI terms](https://developers.google.com/ml-kit/genai-terms) say: "You must be 18 years of age or older to use the APIs" (architecture 2.6 and 4 tutor, T44; read by `tutor` 2026-10-25).
- Until a lawyer's answer (П-3) the route is closed, like Google's models in the cloud. Besides, this API has no tablets and no Russian (ibid.).

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. This is Google's generative AI in a service open to children, and the terms of the same model require 18 years. *Rejected:* leaving the route open until Chrome's terms are checked: the terms of the same model on Android require 18 years, and the route would open to children at once.

*Consequence:* privacy 5.3; `tutor` closes В27 — RUN.md, Д47.

Return if a product for adults only appears. The part of П-3 about Google is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 when planning T94 (RUN.md), by the analysis's recommendation (R112). Generative AI Services": "d. Age Restrictions" is the same, and "f. Suspected Violations" is "Google may immediately suspend or terminate Customer's use of a Generative AI Service based on any suspected violation of `Section 17(b)` or subsection (d) above"; [Google Cloud Platform Terms of Service](https://cloud.google.com/terms), "Last modified October 12, 2026": ""Customer Application" means a software program that Customer creates or hosts using the GCP Services", and para. 3.3(d)(iii) forbids "creating multiple Customer Applications, Accounts, or Projects to simulate or act as a single Customer Application, Account, or Project". Each text judges a separate site, application or service, and "likely to be accessed" is defined nowhere. — *Rejected:* allowing Google's models in a deployment for adults on conditions — its own project, domain, accounts and build — and with a second admission table for it: a deployment with shared code, content and modules is easily held to be one service, and a suspension on suspicion would close it too. — privacy 5.3; П-3.

## Status badges

**R48. The README of every repository carries MathTrail's status badges — up to 14 in two rows, and a badge stands only when what it speaks of exists. Coverage goes to Codecov by OIDC, without a secret, and `codecov/patch` ≥ 90 % holds the merge; OpenSSF Best Practices comes first at `spec`.** The author's answer to Т-34 when planning T39 (RUN.md), 2026-10-23.
- **The set** is as at mathtrail-standalone (`main` c6cbeb2) and canvas-api (0901af0). The first row is CI, Release, CodeQL, the release number, the language, coverage, OpenSSF Best Practices, OpenSSF Scorecard and the license; the second is the five measures of SonarCloud: code smells, reliability, security, maintainability and vulnerabilities. The addresses, the captions and when which badge appears are in repositories 2.3.
- **A badge stands only when what it speaks of exists**: no "no releases", no "not found", no "unknown".
  - From day one, from the template: CI, CodeQL, Scorecard, the license and SonarCloud's measures. In all 13 repositories they work already now. A new repository gets their answers when it is set up to the end: with the shared checks (repositories 2.2), a SonarCloud project (R30) and the first run of Scorecard.
  - Release and the release number come with the first release, the language with the first code, coverage with the first upload to Codecov, Best Practices with the passing level.
  - These badges are put up by the repository's own session, as is what code adds to the CI files (the 2026-10-21 amendment to R30).
- **Coverage goes to Codecov by OIDC, without a secret:** "Any token supplied will be ignored, as Codecov will default to the OIDC token for verification. Note that the codecov action must have write permission for `id-token` for this to work" ([codecov/codecov-action, README](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/blob/v7.1.1/README.md), tag v7.1.1). Only the upload job gets the permission `id-token: write`.
  - A pull request from a fork does not get this permission, and Codecov accepts its upload even without a token: "Codecov should work smoothly on pull requests from forks out of the box" ([Codecov Tokens](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/codecov-tokens)).
  - An upload for `main` without OIDC Codecov will not accept if the organization's settings turn on the token requirement: "For public repositories, a token is required if the upload is for a commit on a protected branch and the repository owner has not disabled token authentication for public repositories". The author turns it on: a new organization by default has "new organizations will start with tokens Not required" (ibid.).
- **`codecov/patch` holds the merge:** the changed lines are covered at least 90 %, as in R38 standalone. It is a required check of the ruleset of every repository whose coverage goes to Codecov, and `codecov/project` only reports. The amendment to R30 is given by T40, when the check appears at `spec`.
  - The cost: no upload means no status, and the merge waits. This happens when Codecov fails, and for a Dependabot pull request if GitHub does not give it OIDC; whether it does is not checked yet. How such a pull request does not get stuck, T40 decides.
- **OpenSSF Best Practices.** The project on bestpractices.dev is set up by the author, signing in through GitHub (rule 4 of RUN.md). First `spec` (T41), then every repository with code and automated tests: without them the passing level cannot be had.
  - The criterion `test` — "The project MUST use at least one automated test suite that is publicly released as FLOSS", of the category MUST and without "N/A" ([best-practices-badge](https://github.com/ossf/best-practices-badge), `criteria/criteria.yml` and `config/locales/en.yml`, `main` e4c99b5).
  - The badge is by the project's ID: "We recommend individual projects use the id-based interface listed above" (ibid., `docs/api.md`).
- **The services** are in architecture 3.12.
  - shields.io draws the release number, the language and the license, and through it the Scorecard badge too. "Shields.io is non-tracking and privacy-respecting", "We do not store any logs of your visits, requests, or other activities on our site" ([Privacy Policy](https://shields.io/privacy)). It requires nothing of the repository's owner.
  - Codecov: "Codecov will always be free for open source projects" ([Codecov for open source](https://about.codecov.io/for/open-source/)), and "If you are a GitHub user you MUST install the Codecov GitHub app for your organization - Codecov can't function without it" ([Quick Start](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/quick-start)). An upload carries the report and the paths of all the repository's files: its CLI takes them from `git ls-files` (codecov-cli v11.3.1). There are no learners' data in the repositories (RULES.md), and all NovaTrail repositories are public.
  - The reader's browser takes the badge's picture not from the service but from GitHub's proxy: "Camo generates an anonymous URL proxy for each file which hides your browser details and related information from other users" ([GitHub Docs, About anonymized URLs](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/about-anonymized-urls)).
- **Named by R12** are the CI tools that ship nowhere:
  - `codecov/codecov-action` — MIT;
  - the CLI that the action downloads and verifies by GPG and SHA256, `codecov/codecov-cli` — Apache-2.0 (GitHub's API, the repositories' licenses);
  - Codecov itself — a service on terms that are free for open source.

  NovaTrail does not distribute them, and is built, run and deployed without them (the 2026-10-22 amendment to R12). The CLI's telemetry is turned off by the action's input `disable_telem`.

All was read 2026-10-23.

— *Why:* the author's answers when planning T39. The set — «меня устраивают значки там», of the README of mathtrail-standalone. OIDC, the 90 % threshold, Best Practices at `spec` now and the split of T39 into three tasks are options of the plan the author chose. OIDC because the shared workflows take no secrets (R05 .github), and OIDC has no token that would be stored and could leak. A badge of what does not exist yet would show an error.

— *Rejected:*
- a row only of the services that exist already — option 1 of Т-34 and the recommendation of `.github`; a README without badges — option 3;
- the secret `CODECOV_TOKEN`, as at standalone and canvas-api: a shared workflow would take a secret against R05 .github, and a copy of the token would live in the secrets of every repository and of Dependabot;
- an upload without a token for all: no permissions need changing, but anyone could send a report for `main`;
- `codecov/patch` for information only — the author chose standalone's threshold;
- Best Practices at all 13 at once — at repositories without code the badge would not appear while there are no tests — or at none yet;
- SonarCloud from CI for the sake of coverage, as at standalone (R31 standalone): it needs `SONAR_TOKEN`, and the automatic analysis is enough for the five measures of the set (R30).

— *Consequence:*
- repositories 2.3 — the badges, their addresses and when which stands; repositories 2.2 — a copy's README begins with them. The template's README carries the badges of day one, and `spec`'s README carries them, Release and the release number. architecture 3.12 — shields.io, Codecov and OpenSSF Best Practices, and with them SonarQube Cloud and OpenSSF Scorecard. Т-34 is closed.
- T40 — coverage of `spec`, the amendment to R30 and the rule for the wrappers of `.github`; T41 — Best Practices at `spec`; R33 — the amendment on `CII-Best-Practices`.
- The other repositories put up badges with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д28.

- **`codecov/project` does not come.** The item "`codecov/project` only reports" in fact means that it does not exist. On the plan that Codecov gives a public repository there is no coverage status of the whole project: "The Team Plan shows Patch ONLY coverage" ([Codecov, Pricing](https://about.codecov.io/pricing/)), and the free plan `users-developer` in the plan data of Codecov's server is of the same tier, `team` ([codecov/umbrella](https://github.com/codecov/umbrella), `main` c6a2a28, `apps/codecov-api/core/management/commands/codecovPlans-Jan25.csv` and `codecovTiers-Jan25.csv`). standalone's `codecov.yml` sets it, but neither pull request #144 nor `main` c6cbeb2 has it (GitHub's API). `spec`'s `codecov.yml` still makes it informational only — in case Codecov sets it. The coverage of all the code is shown by the badge.
- **Without changed lines** in the report, `codecov/patch` is success "Coverage not affected". So Codecov's server sets it (ibid., `apps/worker/services/notification/notifiers/mixins/status.py`), and so it came for standalone's pull request #144, where only `.md` files changed. A pull request of `spec` with documents alone passes.
- **The cost "no upload means no status"**, case by case.
  - **Dependabot.** GitHub writes both that its runs "are treated as if they were opened from a repository fork" and get a read-only token, and that "You can use the `permissions` key in your workflow to increase the access for the token" ([GitHub Docs, Troubleshooting Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/troubleshoot-dependabot/dependabot-on-actions)). The changelog of 2021-10-06 says that such runs "will begin to respect the permissions specified in your workflows" ([GitHub Changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2021-10-06-github-actions-workflows-triggered-by-dependabot-prs-will-respect-permissions-key-in-workflows/)). And the page of the workflow syntax does not name this exception: "Workflow runs triggered by Dependabot pull requests run as if they are from a forked repository, and therefore use a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`" ([GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#permissions-for-workflow-runs-triggered-by-dependabot)). Of `id-token` nothing is said anywhere. So `codecov/patch` becomes required after the first Dependabot pull request (the same day's amendment to R30; RUN.md, Д10). If it does not get OIDC, the action's step that asks for the token fails, and the author chooses between a Dependabot secret at `spec` only and a check of its own of the changed lines in CI.
  - **A Codecov failure.** The job "Coverage" on the pull request is red, and it is rerun.
  - **A pull request from a fork** does not ask for OIDC. Action v7.1.1 recognizes a fork by `head.repo.full_name` and sends the report without a token from the branch `owner:branch` (`action.yml`, the steps "Set fork" and "Override branch for forks"). Such a branch Codecov accepts without a token for a public repository: "the repository is public **and** the upload is for a commit that is on an "unprotected" branch (like `forkname:main`)" ([Codecov Tokens](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/codecov-tokens)). The author decided not to make a trial from a fork: the first such pull request will show the route.
- **The CLI by its own sum, as R34.** The action would verify the CLI with a GPG key that it takes from Keybase during the run and whose fingerprint it does not check (`dist/codecov.sh` v7.1.1, lines 128–161). A substitution on both cli.codecov.io and the Keybase account at once such a check would not catch.
  - The job "Coverage" downloads CLI v11.3.1 itself and checks the sha256 pinned in `ci.yml`. The action gets the ready file through the input `binary` and downloads nothing.
  - The executor checked the sum once: the file of sums is signed by a key with the fingerprint `2703 4E7F DB85 0E0B BC2C 62FF 806B B28A ED77 9869` — the one the page [Codecov Uploader](https://docs.codecov.com/docs/codecov-uploader) names: "Key Fingerprint: `2703 4E7F DB85 0E0B BC2C 62FF 806B B28A ED77 9869`".
  - The version and the sum are raised by hand, together: Dependabot moves only the action's SHA.

  This is the author's decision when planning T40; the action's own check is rejected. The item "Named by R12" reads so: the job downloads the CLI itself and checks it by the pinned sha256.
- **The CLI's plugins are off**, the input `plugins: noop`. By default the CLI runs `xcode`, `gcov` and `pycoverage` (`codecov_cli/commands/upload.py`, v11.3.1), and the upload job runs nothing but the upload.
- **A module that no test loads** does not get into Node's report, and `codecov/patch` does not see its lines. The recipe `just coverage` fails on such a module of `tools/` (the same day's amendment to R30).

## Skill graph

**R49. The skill graph is the file `skill-graph.yaml`: the module's skills are a dictionary by local ID, with a title, a description, prerequisites and assessability. The tier is computed from the graph, and the author gives the tiers names. The mapping table is `retired_skills`, and the grade is the label `audience.grades` in the manifest.** The author's answers when planning RUN.md, T27; О-18 is decided. Normatively it is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 11 and 12, and in the schemas `skill-graph.schema.json` and `manifest.schema.json`; here is what was decided, why, and what was rejected.
- **The skill graph** is `skill-graph.yaml` by the schema `skill-graph.schema.json`.
  - `skills` — the module's skills under their local IDs: `title`, an optional `description`, `prerequisites` and `assessability`. Prerequisites are skills of the module, and all are needed: "to take on B, you need A". Skills outside the module — the anchor skills of the shared taxonomy — come with RUN.md, T42.
  - A module has one graph or none, and a module without a graph is without skills.
  - Rules: `skill-graph.acyclic` — prerequisites make no cycle, and a skill that names itself as a prerequisite is a cycle too; `skill-graph.known-skills` — a prerequisite and a skill in `replaced_by` are skills of the module; `skill-graph.retired-ids` — the ID of a retired skill does not name a skill of the module. `module-kit` checks them, and `spec`'s CI checks the YAML and the schema of their vectors ([format text](../format/README.md), section 9).
  - `tiers` and `skills` with all the skill's fields are open: by them the app draws the skill map. `retired_skills` is closed: the server transfers progress.
- **The tier (О-18)** is computed from the graph and is not written in the module. A skill without prerequisites among the module's skills has tier 1, the others 1 above the highest tier of their prerequisites in the module. So the tier is the number of skills in the longest chain of prerequisites that ends in the skill, and a prerequisite always stands a tier lower. There is no limit on the number of tiers. `module-kit` computes the tiers when it builds the package (architecture 3.7).
  - Names for the tiers are an optional list `tiers` in the explanation language: the first name is tier 1's. A tier without a name is shown by its number, and a name past the last tier names nothing.
- **A skill's assessability** is one of three: `verdict` — the skill's tasks are checked by a key or a predicate, and their verdicts are evidence for the learner model; `rubric` — on the skill the learner gets feedback by a rubric, without a verdict; `none` — the skill is trained but not assessed. The engine adapts to the learner only for a skill with `verdict` (concepts 4).
- **Retired skills are a mapping table.** A published ID of a skill does not name another skill, and a skill whose meaning changed gets a new ID: a change of meaning cannot be seen from the module. `retired_skills` are the skills of earlier versions that the module no longer has, under their earlier IDs, and each has `replaced_by`, the skills of this version that replaced it:
  - a renamed one has one skill, a split one several, and merged ones each name the same one;
  - `[]` — nobody replaced it, and the progress in it passes to no skill;
  - if a skill from `replaced_by` is later retired itself, the record names its replacement instead;
  - the evidence of a retired skill goes to each skill that replaced it, and with what weight `learner-model` decides (architecture 3.8);
  - the record stays in all the following versions, so that progress of any age passes over. To retire a skill is a major change of the module (concepts 3).

  That each skill of the earlier version stayed in the module or was retired, and that no entry has gone, is seen only by comparing two versions. They are compared by `diff` of `module-kit` (T04 module-kit), and its rules will come to the format text as a row «в реестр spec».
- **The grade** is the module's label `audience.grades`: school grades from 1 to 12, as the module's author counts them; the platform does not convert one country's grades into another's. A module with grades asks the learner's grade, and the answer may be outside the list. Unlike the age categories, the grade closes nothing: a skill opens by its prerequisites (concepts 4). The starting point by grade — a point of the scale of task difficulty — comes with that scale (RUN.md, T28). There is no grade 0 and no grades above 12 in version 0.1: to add them later is a minor version (R44).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-26 when planning T27, by the plan's recommendations: the tier is computed, and the author gives the names; the table is `retired_skills`; the grade is a label now, and the starting point comes with T28; three values of assessability; the MIT notice in the example; the shared taxonomy as a separate task T42. The rest — a dictionary of skills instead of a list with `id`, the rule `retired-ids`, a name past the last tier, an optional graph, `minItems` and `minProperties` — is the plan's proposal after an independent agent checked the draft. All was read 2026-10-26.
- **The tier is computed** — as in standalone: "a topic's layer is the longest chain of bases below it — 0 the foundations, 1 the rules, 2 the hard problems — computed rather than drawn" ([SPEC.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/SPEC.md), section 8.12.2, line 1706; commit c6cbeb2). Tiers that the author types R164 standalone rejected: "layers typed by hand, which drift from the links" ([docs/decisions.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/docs/decisions.md), ibid.). A computed tier will not drift from the graph.
- **There is no depth limit.** standalone's map draws three layers, the catalog's test keeps chains within three, and for that one edge is not drawn: "a link from divisibility would make a fourth layer through calendar and divisibility, and the map draws three" (R164 standalone). And an edge is a teacher's judgement: "which topic is a good base for another is a teacher's judgement the data only supports" (ibid.). The format should not fit the graph to the map's drawing, and the map can fold the far tiers into a row, as the prototype does ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)).
- **The author gives the tiers names** — as in the prototype: the module Goroutines has its own steps — Basics, Waiting, Many goroutines and Review — and the caption is "Step N · name" or, without a name, "Step N" (`draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`). The olympiad module has standalone's names: Foundations, Rules, Hard problems.
- **Three values of assessability.** A key and a predicate both give a verdict, and the engine and the learner model behave the same with either. And for a skill that is trained by tasks both with a key and with a predicate, none of the four values of the table of concepts 4 would be right.
- **A dictionary of skills by local ID.** The uniqueness of IDs is held by the rule `yaml.unique-keys`, not by a rule of its own, and the order of skills carries no meaning, like the order of keys (R45).
- **The table is in the graph, with skills without replacement too.** A skill retired without replacement is recorded in the same place as the others, and its ID is protected from reuse too. standalone has no mapping table.
- **The grade is a point on the ladder of tasks, not at the skills.** In standalone the grade decides one thing: "Start is where a child of this grade begins: the shift of the level the grade falls into. It is the one thing the grade decides" ([`internal/domain/rating/ladder.go`](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/internal/domain/rating/ladder.go), commit c6cbeb2), and a task's level is "the band of grades it is written for" (SPEC 1.1 standalone). So the starting point is given by the scale of task difficulty (T28), and the label is needed already now: by it the app asks the grade (privacy 4).
- **The MIT notice** on the example of the olympiad graph is by R12: "MathTrail's code under MIT carries over freely: MIT is compatible with Apache-2.0, and the MIT notice is kept". standalone's topics and their links are under MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 MathTrail" ([LICENSE](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/LICENSE), commit c6cbeb2). A file `NOTICE` beside the example `format-check` would not accept, so the notice stands in the example's opening comment.

— *Rejected:*
- the author sets the tier: it would drift from the graph, which is what R164 standalone warns against;
- computing the tier, but no deeper than three, as standalone's map: the graph would be fitted to the drawing;
- tiers without names: the steps that the module names itself would be lost;
- four values of assessability — key, predicate, rubric and none;
- skills as a list with a field `id`, as in the illustration of concepts 16.3: the uniqueness of IDs would be held by a rule of its own;
- `formerly` — a list of earlier IDs on the new skill: a skill retired without replacement is recorded nowhere, and its ID has nothing to protect it;
- the table as a separate file `skill-mapping.yaml`: a layout row of its own, and the references to skills a rule between two files;
- everything about the grade in T28; grades on skills, like the `grade_levels` of standalone's topics: there the starting point was given by the level of tasks, not by the grades of topics;
- an example without standalone's topics, and their re-release by the author under Apache-2.0;
- the graph and the shared taxonomy as one task — by rule 11 of RUN.md.

— *Consequence:*
- О-18 is closed (product 13.1). Amendments to R44 — T42 decides the taxonomy's dictionary —, to R45 — a link field named by a verb —, and to R46 — the grade, the starting point and `dependencies`.
- concepts 3, 4, 13 and 15 — the graph, the tier, a skill's assessability, a retired skill, the rubric and the grade; architecture 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.7 and 3.8; repositories 5. The [format text](../format/README.md), section 9, now says what `spec`'s CI checks and what `module-kit`'s CI checks: the graph's rules are the first that `format-check` does not check itself.
- What R49 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-26, T27)» at table 1 of RUN.md, and the shared taxonomy by RUN.md, T42. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д30.
