## The generator of randomness

**R59. The platform's generator is PCG, as in Go's `math/rand/v2`, and the stream of a place of randomness is derived as in standalone's simulator: FNV-1a 64 of the seed and the place's names, and the seed itself. Over the stream five Go functions are normative. The text is the [format text](../format/README.md), section 22, and the vectors are `format/vectors/random/`, and `spec` computes them itself. Т-18 is closed.**
- **The generator** is PCG with 128 bits of state, exactly the `PCG` of Go's package `math/rand/v2`:
  - the state is two words, the high and the low, taken from the words of the seed as they are;
  - the step is `state · M + C mod 2^128`, with Go's constants;
  - the output is DXSM after the step.

  This is not numpy's PCG64DXSM and not a cryptographically secure generator. The algorithm is set by the format itself, not by a library.
- **A place of randomness** is a seed, an unsigned 64-bit integer, and a non-empty list of names. A name is a non-empty string without "|", and names are compared as written.
  - The stream of a place is a generator with the words: FNV-1a 64 (RFC 9923) of the UTF-8 text "the seed in decimal digits, and then '|' and the name, for each name" and the seed itself.
  - A new place is new names, and it does not shift the numbers of the earlier places. `seeded` of standalone's simulator is a place of the main seed with the names "experiment, unit, assignment".
  - For reference: the places of one seed share the low word of the state, and FNV-1a is not resistant to collisions. For the places of a module and of a run this does not matter.
- **The functions**, as Go's methods, and how many integers each takes: an integer (`Uint64`), a number below a bound (`Uint64N`: a power of two by a mask, otherwise Lemire's method with rejection), a number in a range (`a + Int64N(c − a + 1)`), a fraction of 53 bits (`Float64`) and the Fisher–Yates permutation (`Perm` and `Shuffle`). The format has no normal and no exponential distributions.
- **The platform's seeds:**
  - `api` takes the seed of an attempt from a cryptographically secure source and keeps it with the attempt. Neither it nor the state of its places goes to the device: the state of a place shows its seed;
  - the places of a module are places of the seed of its attempt, and the first name says whose place it is: `template` — a task template's, the other names are decided by T33;
  - a widget has its own seed, and how it gets it is decided by the widget protocol (Т-24);
  - `engine`, if it needs randomness, and `sim` have their own seeds, of the choice and of the run, and their own names.
- **The vectors** are `format/vectors/random/<case>.yaml` by the schema `random-vector.schema.json`: the start of the stream — the words and, if the stream is a place, its seed and names — and the calls of the functions in order, each with its value. `format-check` derives each state and computes each value with a second implementation, `random.mjs`. And `random.mjs` repeats the golden outputs of Go and RFC 9923 in its tests.
- **Versions** are as the amendment to R44 says: the generator has no version of its own.

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 22, and edits of sections 1, 2, 3 and 9.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T32 — five, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T32, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Not waiting for T02 `module-kit` and T03 `engine`:** neither is started, nor are the tasks before them (`module-kit`, commit 1a54028; `engine`, commit 08bc48a; read 2026-10-27). Т-18 is a question of the register of `spec`, and T33 and T38 would wait together with T32.
- **PCG from Go** is the generator that standalone's simulator and `tutor` already take. Go promises the streams not by the package's documentation but thus:
  - the blog post "Evolving the Go Standard Library with math/rand/v2" (go.dev/blog/randv2, 2024-05-01): "Go 1 compatibility included the specific random outputs for a given seed", and "The concrete rand.Rand API is now locked in to that value stream";
  - and `regress_test.go`: "Do NOT make changes to the golden outputs" (Go, commit b98d22c1, read 2026-10-27).

  So the format sets the algorithm itself, and the vectors will catch a divergence. A port on BigInt repeated Go's golden outputs exactly.
- **The derivation as in the simulator** — R27 required taking the simulator's scheme into account, and with it `sim` will repeat its streams. The simulator keeps the same promise: "a generator added leaves every child of the others as they were" (docs/learners.md standalone, commit 4dece74). FNV-1a 64 is RFC 9923, February 2026 (read 2026-10-27). There is nowhere to take a synchronous SHA-256 in the browser from: `crypto.subtle.digest` returns a Promise (W3C Web Cryptography Level 2, draft 2025-04-22, read 2026-10-27).
- **Go's functions, without the normal and the exponential distributions:** otherwise two consumers would make a range differently. And `Math.exp` and `Math.log` in JS give implementation-approximated values (ECMA-262, draft 2026-10-23, read 2026-10-27), and Go on arm64 fuses a multiplication with an addition: "On arm64 the last digits may differ, since Go fuses a multiplication and an addition there" (docs/learners.md standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-27).
- **The seed of an attempt does not go to the device:** the state of a place contains the seed itself, and the generator is not cryptographically secure. The seed carries nothing about the learner, so this does not change privacy.

— *Rejected:*
- waiting for the recommendations of T02 `module-kit` and T03 `engine`;
- SplitMix64 — it does not repeat the simulator's numbers — and ChaCha8, complex in JS;
- a derivation where the second word is SplitMix64 of the first;
- only a stream of integers, without functions over it;
- a document and a version of its own for the generator; vectors that only `module-kit` computes;
- Go in the container of `spec` for the sake of the vectors: Go's golden outputs in the tests of `random.mjs` and CI of `module-kit` check the same without it;
- the vector fields `n`, `pcg` and `uint64`: `n` is rejected by the rule `yaml.plain-strings`, and the others are not words.

— *Consequence:*

- the schema `random-vector` and 12 vectors in `format/vectors/random/`;
- `format-check` — `random.mjs`;

## Task templates

**R60. A module's tasks are a pool and templates with parameters, and О-12 is decided. A template is a task with the field `template`: parameters with domains, derived numbers and a constraint, and the expressions are a narrow subset of Starlark. The key of each instance is known already at the module's check: `module-kit` enumerates all combinations, no more than 10,000, and checks each instance by all the rules of a task, and an attempt gets an instance by its seed. The text is the [format text](../format/README.md), section 23, and the vectors are `format/vectors/templates/`, and `spec` computes them itself.** The author's answers in the planning of T33 (RUN.md), 2026-10-27.
- **О-12:** a published pool and templates with parameters. Tasks with the help of AI only in the preparation of a module, and the author checks them; there is no generation on the fly.
- **A template** is a task of R51 in `tasks/<id>.yaml` with the field `template`, closed whole:
  - `parameters` — a name and a domain, integers from `from` to `to`;
  - `derived` — derived numbers, each an expression of the parameters;
  - `constraint` — a constraint, a boolean expression of the parameters and derived numbers.

  A name is lowercase letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter, no longer than 14 characters, and not a keyword or a reserved word of Starlark. A lesson names a template as a task, and the learner model and the engine see one task.
- **Expressions** are a narrow subset of Starlark: integers and names, `+`, `-`, `*`, `//`, `%`, comparisons without chains, `and`, `or` and `not`. Types are checked: arithmetic and comparisons are of integers, logic of `bool`. The meaning is Starlark's: integers without a bound, division rounding down, an error at division by zero, and `and` and `or` evaluate the right operand only when the left does not decide. An expression is up to 1000 characters, without a step limit.
- **Instances:** combinations in counter order — names by code units, the first changes slowest of all —, and on each first the derived numbers, then the constraint. The product of the domains is no more than 10,000, the derived numbers are within ±(2^53−1), and there is at least one instance.
- **An attempt's instance** is the number `below(count)` of the place of its seed with the names `template`, the task's ID and `instance` (R59). The same package and the same seed give the same instance (R03).
- **Placeholders** are `{name}` in each string of the task outside `template`; `{{` and `}}` are a curly brace of the text; substitution goes in one pass. In the key and the trap value of `number` and `fraction` a placeholder stands in the place of the integer, the numerator or the denominator: `"{second}"`, `"{part}/{whole}"`; a decimal fraction has no placeholders.
- **The key in advance:** the rules of a task and `lesson.no-leaks` are applied to each instance at the module's check. At an attempt Starlark is not run, and what the package carries about a template is decided by T34.
- **To the device** goes the open view of the instance — without `template`, without the seed and without numbers that are not in its open fields.
- **Five rules:** `task.template-names`, `task.template-expressions`, `task.placeholders`, `task.template-instances` and `task.instances`. `format-check` checks them itself, with the earlier rules of a task on the instances.
- **The vectors** are `format/vectors/templates/<case>.yaml` by the schema `template-vector.schema.json`: the template, the number of its instances and attempts — the seed, the numbers of the instance and the instance itself. `format-check` computes them with a second implementation, `expressions.mjs` and `templates.mjs`, and its tests compare the expressions with the examples of the Starlark specification.
- **The solver** — a Starlark program that computes the key by enumeration when there is no formula — is separated into RUN.md, T43.

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 23, and edits of sections 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 14, 15, 20, 21 and 22.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T33 — four, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T33, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **A pool and templates, without generation on the fly:** a module is data (R02), and a program gives the verdict (R03). A text that a model writes at an attempt passes no rule of the format. In standalone such a task was checked by a solver written by the same model: "the program is written by the same model that wrote the task, so if the model misread its own wording, the program will confirm the misreading" (SPEC 6.1 standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-27). standalone has no parametric templates. Closest to them is GSM-Symbolic, which the simulator's review retells: "Templates name variables, their domains and conditions that keep answers whole" (`research/literature/generation-verification.md` standalone, the same commit).
- **The key in advance:** T03 `module-kit` is not started (commit 1a54028, read 2026-10-27), and its В1 — where to compute a template's key — waits for the cost of running a solver. All 2^64 seeds cannot be enumerated, but a seed only chooses the number of an instance, and there are no more than 10,000 instances. Then each instance passes all the rules of a task, the leak too, before the first attempt, and an attempt has neither the solver's clock nor its refusal. As T32 decided without T02 `module-kit`, so T33 without T03.
- **A subset of Starlark:** the language is the same as the check's predicate (R56), and `module-kit` computes the expressions with the same go.starlark.net. And a narrow subset `spec` computes itself too, so its template vectors are checked not by the schema alone. The Starlark specification (bazelbuild/starlark, commit c0af0ea03d, read 2026-10-27): "The `//` and `%` operations on integers compute floored division and remainder of floored division", and "Comparison operators, `in`, and `not in` are non-associative, so the parser will not accept `0 <= i < n`". `x or y` there "yields the value of `x` if its truth value is `True`", so `and` and `or` in the subset take only `bool`. The parser of go.starlark.net puts unary minus above `*`, `//` and `%`: "Unary MINUS, unary PLUS, and TILDE have higher precedence so are handled in parsePrimary" (`syntax/parse.go`, google/starlark-go, commit 4f4267fb14, read 2026-10-27).
- **The fields `derived` and `constraint`:** "values" would be confused with the value of an answer slot and with `trap_values`, and "condition" in Russian is «условие», which is both the check kind `predicate` and the task statement.
- **A derived number is only of the parameters:** the order of keys carries no meaning ([format text](../format/README.md), section 4), and a chain of derived numbers would have to set an order of evaluation.
- **One call of `below`:** the choice is uniform over the instances, takes one integer — or slightly more at Lemire's rejection —, and `spec` computes it itself. Parameters one at a time with rejection by the constraint take an unknown number of integers, and a limit of tries would make some seeds a refusal that nobody will check.
- **Splitting the task:** about 3000 lines is more than one check (rule 11 of RUN.md). The cut is clean: in T33 everything that `spec` computes itself, in T43 only the solver's Starlark.

— *Rejected:*
- only a pool in v0; AI generation on the fly, with a solver or without;
- the key at each attempt, with parameters one at a time and rejection; waiting for T03 `module-kit`;
- everything, the numbers of the task statement too, by a solver: then `spec` would check the template vectors only by the schema;
- the format's own language of expressions beside Starlark;
- `abs`, `min`, `max`, a conditional expression and derived numbers of derived numbers in v0: no example asks for them, and each will come as a minor version;
- parameters as a list, not a dictionary: names without repeats are given by `yaml.unique-keys` anyway;
- a template as a part of its own, `templates/<id>.yaml`: a lesson names a task, and the learner model sees one;
- one task together with the solver.

A template may have the field `solver` — a Starlark program and the names of its results, and the results are more names of placeholders, but only in the key and the trap value of `number` and `fraction`, in the solution and in the leak phrases. `task.template-names` and `task.placeholders` know them too. A template's key is now computed by an expression or by the solver, and `spec` checks the instances without the solver's results and takes them only from the template vectors.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* what the package carries about a template was decided by R62: the template itself is in `tasks`, and the numbers of each of its instances, in order, are in `instances`. The server takes number `below(count)` and substitutes the numbers without executing expressions. The `from` and `to` of a range got the bounds ±(2^53−1). — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **template expressions run in the dialect of all of the format's Starlark — go.starlark.net `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d` (R88).** The meaning and the subset do not change. "It takes no more steps than it has tokens" of the format text is wrong on both of go.starlark.net's counts: on the new one any expression takes 10 steps on entering the function. The conclusion is the same — an expression calls no functions and holds no loops, and it has no step limit; format 0.3 will say so, RUN.md, T69. — R88.

**R61. A template may carry a solver — the field `solver` with a program in Starlark and the names of its results. `solve` gets the numbers of an instance's open fields and returns a dictionary of results, and the results stand only in the key and in the trap value of `number` and `fraction`, in the solution and in leak phrases. The dialect is that of standalone's solvers, the budget is 100,000,000 steps for all the template's instances together. Only `module-kit` runs the solver, and in template vectors its results are data. Text — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 24.** The author's answers in planning T43 (RUN.md), 2026-10-28.
- **The field** `template.solver`, closed, like all of `template`:
  - `program` — the program, no longer than 8192 characters, most conveniently as a block scalar;
  - `results` — the names of the results, at least one and without repeats. A name is like a parameter's, and a parameter, a derived number and a result never share a name (`task.template-names`).
- **The input of `solve`** is a frozen dictionary of the numbers that the template's open fields show: each parameter and each derived number whose placeholder stands in the statement, the data, the unknown, an item's text, a piece of a line or an option of a slot with the binding `choice`. The names are inserted in the order of code units. The numbers of only closed fields — the key, the trap value, the solution — do not go into the dictionary.
- **The output** is a dictionary with exactly the names of `results`, and each value is an `int` in ±(2^53−1). A result is a number of the instance, like a derived one, and its placeholders are replaced by it.
- **Where the results stand** — only in the key and in the trap value of `number` and `fraction`, in the solution and in leak phrases. Everything the learner sees before solving, `spec` builds without the solver, and a placeholder of a result anywhere else breaks `task.placeholders`.
- **The dialect** is go.starlark.net with the `syntax.FileOptions` options of standalone's solvers: `Set`, `While`, `TopLevelControl` and `GlobalReassign` on, `Recursion` off, `load` forbidden. Only Starlark's own names are built in: none of the modules `math`, `json`, `time`, nor the 13 helpers of standalone's sandbox. `print` writes nothing, and the dialect has no randomness and no clock.
- **The run:** the program is executed once, on one thread, and `solve` is called on each instance in the order of instances (R60), on the same thread. The top level and all the calls together take no more than 100,000,000 steps in go.starlark.net's count. The budget is the template's, not the instance's, and it is in the format, like a predicate's step limit (R56); the clock and concurrent runs are `module-kit`'s.
- **The rule** `task.template-solver`: the solver gives its results on each instance — the program parses and executes in the dialect, `solve` is a function of one parameter, and on each instance, within the budget, without an error, it returns exactly its results as integers within the bounds. Only `module-kit` checks it. The rule's vectors are checked by `spec`'s CI as it checks the vectors of `task.predicate-expression`: by the schema, the YAML rules and by their not breaking the rules it checks itself.
- **What `spec` does:** on an instance without results it checks the task's rules on whatever has no results, and skips the key, the trap value and the leak phrase with a result. A template vector with a solver names `inputs` — the names that `solve` gets — and the results at each attempt: `spec` compares `inputs` with the template's open view and checks the task's rules on the instance with these results, and `module-kit`'s CI runs the solver and compares.
- **Provenance:** a key that the solver computes is "checked by a solver", like a key from a template expression (concepts 9.4).

Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 24, and the edits to sections 1, 2, 9, 14, 15, 20 and 23.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-28 in planning T43 — four, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T43, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Only the numbers of open fields:** the solver solves the task that the learner sees. If it got all the numbers, it could return a closed parameter, and "checked by a solver" would check nothing. standalone's solver, too, gets only what the learner sees — the texts of the options: "`options: {"A": "4", "B": "5", "C": "6", "D": "8", "E": "12"} — the task's own option texts`" (SPEC 6.2 standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-28). The order of the names is fixed, because a Starlark dictionary is iterated in insertion order, and the result must not depend on it.
- **Results only in closed fields:** `spec` does not run Starlark (R56), and it must build an instance's open view itself: its vectors of the open view and of templates are then checked by more than the schema (R60).
- **standalone's dialect:** its solvers already run in it — "`Set: true, While: true, TopLevelControl: true, GlobalReassign: true, Recursion: false, LoadBindsGlobally: false`" (`internal/infra/starlark/dialect.go`, lines 29–36 of standalone, the same commit). On recursion, SPEC 6.4 standalone: "A recursive Starlark function recurses on the **Go** stack, and a stack overflow in Go cannot be recovered". standalone rejects `load` at compilation: `if program.NumLoads() > 0` (`internal/infra/starlark/starlark.go`, line 214). No helpers — because each would become a normative contract that `module-kit` implements and holds with test vectors. The format example needs only `range`, `len` and `fail`, and a helper will come in a minor version when a module asks for it.
- **A budget per template:** 100,000,000 is the recommendation of the plan of T33. In standalone it is 25,000,000 steps per run: "`thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps`; the interpreter tests the counter on every instruction", and the heaviest of the 705 solvers takes 2,413,617 steps (SPEC 6.6 standalone). A budget per instance at 10,000 instances would give up to 250 billion steps for one template when a module is checked. One budget for all the instances bounds the cost of checking a module, and a template with a search for each instance searches only what is open, like standalone's solver templates: "A solver template searches only what the question leaves open, and every program runs under the one step budget" (R72 standalone).
- **The program in the task:** the template stays one file, closed as a whole, like a check's predicate, for which R56 rejected the file `predicates/<id>.star`. The limit of 8192 characters is like standalone's "`MaxSource = 8 * 1024`" (`internal/infra/starlark/starlark.go`, line 36), only in characters: the schema measures a string's length in characters.
- **One thread and the order of instances:** a thread's steps accumulate, and the template's budget is simply the thread's limit. Starlark's global variables are frozen after the top level, so the calls do not affect one another.

— *Rejected:*
- `solve` gets all the numbers of the instance; the numbers as capitalized constants without an argument, like standalone's solver templates (R64 standalone);
- 25,000,000 steps for each instance, without a shared budget; the helpers of standalone's sandbox in format v0;
- results also in trap texts, simpler cases and hints; a result only in the key;
- the program as a file `solvers/<id>.star` in the module layout.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **the dialect is go.starlark.net `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d` with the same options, one for all of the format's Starlark, and the built-in names are the list of the 33 names of its `starlark.Universe`; the budget is 100,000,000 steps in this version's count, and the run stops when the count reaches the budget (R88).** The budget does not change: the heaviest solver of standalone on this version takes 2,725,355 steps (R11 module-kit). ## Module package

**R62. A module package is two parts and an inventory. The server part is the canonical view: the module as one JSON object, with the tier of each skill and the numbers of each instance of a template. The device part is `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and the media files. The package inventory names the module and both parts by digests; the canonical text is RFC 8785, the digest is SHA-256, and the package digest is the digest of the inventory. The open views are built by `module-kit` on the server, and they reach the app from `api`. `LICENSE` is a mandatory file of a module's folder, and the eval set does not go into the package. Text — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 25.** The author's answers in planning T34 (RUN.md), 2026-10-28. Т-15 is closed.
- **Without T01 of `module-kit`:** its recommendation on Т-15 is an input of T34, but T01 has not started (RUN.md of `module-kit`, `main` 1a54028, read 2026-10-28). As T32 decided without T02 of `module-kit` and T33 without T03 (the amendment to R27; R60), `spec` decides itself, and T01 narrows to checking the build against R62. The module index is split off into task T44 (RUN.md): what it names, who teaches each anchor skill (R50), what is signed and the withdrawal mark (Т-30).
- **The canonical view** is an object of `canonical-view.schema.json`:
  - each part is under its own member: a part that a module has one of is under its term in snake_case, `manifest`, `skill_graph`, `traps`, `techniques`, `solving_steps`, and parts that there are many of are under the name of their folder, `tasks` and `lessons`, as an object by local ID. The value of a part is the JSON value of its file as it is: a template as written, with no default values;
  - `skill_tiers` — the tier of each skill of the graph (R49);
  - `instances` — by template ID, the numbers of each of its instances in the order of R60: parameters, derived numbers and the solver's results (R61).

  A member whose part the module lacks is absent from the view too. The canonical view has no open fields: the app gets a part's open view, not it.
- **Not in the package:** `eval/`, files starting with `.`, comments of the module's files and everything that is not in the module's files — the version of `module-kit`, the time, paths. So the canonical view and the digest depend only on the module's files and the format version of its manifest (R44).
- **The canonical text** is the RFC 8785 serialization: keys by UTF-16 code units, without whitespace, strings escaped as ECMAScript's `JSON.stringify` escapes them, UTF-8 without a BOM and without a newline at the end. A number of the format is an integer in ±(2^53−1) (R45), and it is written in decimal digits: `5e1` is `50`. The format text sets the serialization itself, as it set the generator (R59), so that an implementation does not depend on a library.
- **The digest** is `sha256:` and the SHA-256 in 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, and the size is a number of bytes. The server part is named by the canonical text of the canonical view, and the device part by the canonical text of the list of its files: `license`, `notice` and `media` by path from `media/`. How the files travel — in an archive or one by one, compressed or not — does not change the digest.
- **The package inventory** is the term of concepts 15 for the part that names the digests of both parts (В8). The schema is `inventory.schema.json`: `module_format_version` at the root, in one place in all versions, `id`, `version`, and `server_part` and `device_part` — with a digest and a size. The package digest is the digest of its canonical text, and the attempt stores it (architecture 1).
- **The package as files** — `inventory.json`, `server.json`, `device.json` and `device/` with the files of the device part. In which archive the packages lie in a release of `modules` is for `modules` to decide.
- **Who reads what:**
  - `api` and the eval runner of `tutor` — through `module-kit`, and `canvas`'s CI — through its CLI (R25);
  - `sim` — `server.json` by the types of the canonical view from `spec`'s releases (RUN.md, T35), without `module-kit`;
  - `app` does not read the package. The open views of the manifest, the skill graph, the technique catalog and the solving steps are given by `api` by the package digest of the attempt, and `app` caches them by it, and the manifest goes to the canvas as the property `manifest` (R36). A lesson's open view comes whole when the lesson suits the learner (R58), the open view of a task or an instance with each attempt, the tiers with the data of the skill map (architecture 3.3), and the files of the device part are served by `api`. How this fits into messages is decided by the contract `app` ↔ `api` (RUN.md, epic E3).
- **A template at an attempt:** the server takes instance number `below(count)` from `instances`, where count is their number, and substitutes its numbers (R60). It executes neither expressions nor the solver at an attempt.
- **`LICENSE`** is a mandatory file of a module's folder: the text of the license that the manifest names — the rule `module.license`. `LICENSE` and `NOTICE` are UTF-8 without a BOM, and lines end with one LF — the rule `module.plain-text`, since the device part carries them byte for byte. License notices are only in `NOTICE`: comments do not go into the package.
- **A gap of T33:** an integer written with an exponent, `1e20`, passes `type: integer` and the rule `yaml.json-scalars`, and the canonical view writes only integers up to 2^53−1. So the `from` and `to` of a template's range and the width and height of a picture of a statement and of a demo got the bounds ±(2^53−1).
- **Vectors** — of tiers, `format/vectors/tiers/` with the schema `tier-vector.schema.json`, and of packages, `format/vectors/packages/` with the schema `package-vector.schema.json`. `spec` computes them itself, and the solver's results are the vector's data, as in template vectors (R61).

Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 25, and the edits to sections 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 12, 21, 23 and 24.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-28 in planning T34 — seven, all by the plan's recommendations. Two of them — how the open views reach the device and where the license text comes from — the author gave again: an independent review of the draft plan found that the first answers collide with R58 and R20 (RUN.md, T34, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **A compiled view, not the YAML as it is** — the recommendation of Т-15. A reader without `module-kit`, `sim`, needs neither parsing YAML by the rules of R45, nor enumerating instances, nor computing tiers: all of this is already in the package.
- **One JSON, not a file per part:** the module of olympiad maths has 603 tasks (product 10), and a reader would assemble the module from hundreds of files, and a part's digest would become one more list. An edit to one task is shown by a pull request of `modules` anyway.
- **RFC 8785:** "JSON object properties MUST be sorted recursively", the comparison is "code units are treated as unsigned integers", and "Whitespace between JSON tokens MUST NOT be emitted" ([RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785), sections 3.2.3 and 3.2.1, Informational; read 2026-10-28). On the format's data — ASCII keys, integers, no surrogates (`yaml.characters`) — it comes down to sorting the keys and `JSON.stringify`. Only the object must be written by hand: JavaScript puts an integer key like `"1"` first in an object, and the sorting example of [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785), section 3.2.3, does not pass through `JSON.stringify` (checked in Node 2026-10-28). There is no ready canonical text in Go:
  - `Value.Canonicalize` of the package `encoding/json/jsontext` "canonicalizes the raw JSON value according to the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) as defined by RFC 8785", but the package's files in go1.27.3 begin with `//go:build goexperiment.jsonv2` (`src/encoding/json/jsontext/value.go` and `doc.go`, tag go1.27.3, read 2026-10-28);
  - `encoding/json` escapes a string otherwise: "the string is encoded using HTMLEscape, which replaces "<", ">", "&", U+2028, and U+2029", and U+2028 and U+2029 "unconditionally" (`src/encoding/json/encode.go`, the same tag).

  So the format text sets the serialization itself, and the package vector `strings` holds these characters.
- **SHA-256 and the notation `sha256:`** — as in an OCI descriptor: "digest ::= algorithm ":" encoded", and "Implementations MUST implement SHA-256 digest verification for use in descriptors" ([OCI Image Spec, descriptor.md](https://github.com/opencontainers/image-spec/blob/main/descriptor.md), read 2026-10-28). The same algorithm is held by the Dockerfile's sums (R34) and the releases' `SHA256SUMS` (R37).
- **The device part — by the list of files**, like the h1 hash of Go modules: "the go command computes the hash from the names and contents of files within the archive in a deterministic order. The hash is not affected by file order, compression, alignment, and other metadata" ([Go Modules Reference](https://go.dev/ref/mod), "Authenticating modules", read 2026-10-28). Hash1 is the SHA-256 of a list of lines "the file's hash, two spaces, the name" (`golang.org/x/mod/sumdb/dirhash`, `hash.go`, read 2026-10-28). So neither an archive's timestamps nor compression change the digest.
- **The open views — from `api`, not in the device part:** a lesson is given only to a learner whom the lesson and each of its tasks suit (R58), and the device part is one for all the learners of a module, and a lesson only for adults would land on a child's device. A withdrawn version (Т-30) the device would then hold in its cache with all its texts. And `api` already gives a task's open view (R05) and serves the media (architecture 3.10).
- **The numbers of instances, not expanded instances:** a template has up to 10,000 instances (R60), and an expanded package would hold up to 10,000 copies of a task. The numbers are the same as the "numbers of an attempt" of template vectors, and substitution is a replacement of strings, not Starlark.
- **`LICENSE` in the module's folder:** Apache-2.0 requires giving the recipient a copy — "You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License" ([Apache License 2.0](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0), section 4(a), read 2026-10-28) — and the package travels to the learner's device too. A text from the module's folder keeps the package dependent only on that folder (R44), suits any license of a third-party module and does not require of the format a list of licenses, which is still open (О-10). Go, for a module in a subfolder, takes `LICENSE` from the root — "the go command will copy the file named LICENSE from the repository root directory" — and itself writes that "this cannot be extended without breaking cryptographic sums of existing modules" ([Go Modules Reference](https://go.dev/ref/mod), "Special case for LICENSE files", read 2026-10-28).
- **The eval set outside the package:** there is no format of samples yet (the eval protocol is epic E3 in RUN.md), the samples are needed neither by `api` nor by the device, and a new sample changes neither a verdict nor the digest. The eval runner takes the samples from the module's folder in `modules`'s CI. The recommendation of Т-15 "the server part is all the content" is thus narrowed to the content that the platform executes.

— *Rejected:*
- waiting for T01 of `module-kit`; one task together with the index;
- the author's YAML as it is; the canonical view as a file for each part;
- the module's open view in the device part — with lessons or without them. Return to it with storage and a CDN (Т-17);
- expanded instances of a template in the package;

## Module index

**R63. The module index is the file `module-index.json` in each release of `modules`: the canonical text of an object by the schema `module-index.schema.json`. The index is cumulative: it names each published version of each module by the digest of its package, with the tag of the release of `modules` in whose files the package lies, with the anchor skills that the version teaches, and with the withdrawal mark and its reason. A release builds the index from the index of the previous release and its own packages, and the index's three rules reject the build. A withdrawn version remains only for repeating a verdict. Т-30 is closed. Text — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 26.** The author's answers in planning T44 (RUN.md), 2026-10-28.
- **What the index names.** At the root — `module_format_version`, the version by which the index is built, and `modules`: by module ID and by its version — a record. In the record:
  - `module_format_version` — the format version of the package, from its inventory;
  - `package_digest` — the package digest, that is, the digest of the inventory (R62);
  - `release` — the tag of the release of `modules` in whose files the package lies: `vX.Y.Z`, as any NovaTrail repository numbers its releases (R31). How the files lie in the release is for `modules` to decide. The place requires no trust: the package is checked by its digest;
  - `teaches` — the anchor skills that the skills of the version's graph teach, each once, in the order of code units (R50). Its element is a string in the form of an anchor skill's ID, not a reference to the vocabulary: the record stays valid even when the next format version removes the anchor skill;
  - `withdrawn` — for a withdrawn version: the withdrawal reason, `wrong_key`, `answer_leak` or `unsuitable_content`.
- **One index for all the modules, cumulative.** A release's index names each version that any release of `modules` published, not only the versions of its own release. It is built by the CLI of `module-kit` in `modules`'s CI at a release (R17), inside the shared release: after the number, since a new record names the tag of its release, and before publication. At the input — the index of the previous release, the release's packages, its tag and the withdrawals:
  - the first release has no previous index, and the build is told so explicitly. If the previous index cannot be read, it is a refusal, not a new index;
  - a record of the previous index stands in the new one as it was;
  - a package whose version is already in the index does not change the record, nor the tag: the same module gives the same package (R62). So a release may build all the modules or only the changed ones — this is for `modules` to decide;
  - the other packages get new records;
  - withdrawals are marked last. A repeated withdrawal with the same reason changes nothing, so the list of withdrawals in `modules` can grow from release to release. A version that comes out in this same release can be withdrawn too.

  Until T37, the previous index is taken from the previous release of the same repository, without checking the signature: releases are immutable.
- **The index's rules** reject the build of the index, not a module: `module-index.entries-kept` — a record of the previous index stands in the new one as it was, `module-index.one-package` — a version of a module has one package, `module-index.known-withdrawals` — a withdrawal names a version that is in the index. Their vectors are refusals among the index vectors, not folders of `vectors/rules/`.
- **The signature.** The index is a file of a release of `modules`, and it is signed by the shared release workflow of `.github` together with the other files (R17). What checks the signature is T37. Whoever checked the index trusts the packages by the chain of digests: the index names the inventory, the inventory the parts, and the list of the device part the files (R62).
- **Withdrawal** is the second option of Т-30. Releases are immutable, so a version is withdrawn by the next release of `modules`: its index marks the version's record. A withdrawal is not undone: the fix is a new version of the module. What a withdrawn version means for the platform:
  - it remains only for repeating a verdict. New attempts do not take it, and the device does not load its device part and does not hold its open views. From stage 4 its widget bundles are not loaded either, and a reason for a dangerous bundle will come in a minor version with epic E5 (RUN.md, table 2);
  - an attempt started on it is closed "unchecked", `unchecked`, with a neutral phrase: this is not the learner's mistake (R04);
  - finished attempts remain in the history. With the reason `wrong_key` their evidence no longer goes into the learner model, and it is recomputed from the evidence log (Т-22);
  - `api`: a pull request pins in the configuration the release of `modules` and its index, and this is the anchor of trust (architecture 3.10). `api` gives a new attempt only on a version that this index does not mark withdrawn, and the marks are not carried over by hand. A withdrawal takes effect with the pull request that moves `api` to the release with the mark, and with the build of the image. The form of the configuration is decided by the detailing of `api` (T03 api);
  - `canvas`'s CI, before building the samples page, reads `withdrawn` in the index of the newest release of `modules` — only it knows of all the withdrawals — and does not build the page from a withdrawn version. A child sample session is run with the build of the latest release of `canvas`, and the page tells the adult this in the steps of the session — the second option of `canvas` in Т-30;
  - from stage 4 the index is written by the registry service (architecture 3.13), and it puts the mark: only whoever signs the index can remove or forge it.

  How each component does this is for it to decide.
- **Who teaches an anchor skill** (R50). The modules that teach an anchor skill are those whose record names it in `teaches`. For each module what counts is the newest by semver non-withdrawn version whose format version the reader reads. A module is offered to the learner by `api` — only from those it holds itself and that suit the learner: the audience and the language (R46, R51).
- **Versions** — an amendment to R44. The index stores the records of all format versions, so its members keep their place and meaning in all versions, and while the format is v0 too, like `module_format_version` in the manifest: `module_format_version` and `modules` at the root and `module_format_version`, `package_digest`, `release`, `teaches` and `withdrawn` in a record. A new version may add only an optional member and a withdrawal reason, and both are minor. A reader reads these members of an index of any version by their places, not by the schema of its own version, which would reject what the next one added. A record whose format version it does not read, it skips, rather than rejecting the index, and a version with any `withdrawn` it considers withdrawn, even if it does not know its reason. How a record is derived from a package is part of the format version.
- **Vectors** — `format/vectors/indexes/<case>/`: the release's modules in `modules/` and `index.yaml` by the schema `index-vector.schema.json` — the previous index, the tag, the withdrawals and either the index or a refusal by a rule. `spec` computes them itself, `tools/format-check/index.mjs`, and the vectors' digests are checked by an independent computation in Python. The modules of the index vectors are without a solver: `spec` does not run Starlark.

Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md), section 26, and the edits to sections 1, 2, 3, 7, 9, 13 and 25.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-28 in planning T44 — six, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T44, «Решено автором»). The rest is the plan's proposal, which the author approved. Before the work, an independent agent reviewed the plan, and its findings are taken into account (the same place, «Выяснилось при планировании»).
- **The mark in the index already in v0.** The recommendation of Т-30 was to withdraw a version before stage 4 by a pull request to the configuration of `api`, and to put a signed mark in the index from stage 4. The author chose the mark at once. `canvas`'s CI does not know the configuration of `api` (architecture 3.2) and otherwise would not learn of a withdrawal, while so a withdrawal has one path at all stages — the signed index, and from stage 4 only whoever writes it changes. The pull request to `api` stays the anchor of trust: the mark reaches `api` together with it.
- **The reason in the mark.** With a wrong key the evidence of finished attempts is wrong, and with a leak or unsuitable content it is right, and without the reason `learner-model` cannot tell them apart. The values of the format's lists are terms of concepts 15 (R45), and `key` there is the correct value. So the reasons are named by the words of Т-30: "wrong key", "answer leak", "unsuitable content". And `reason` in concepts 15 is already the verdict reason, and the value of `withdrawn` is the withdrawal reason itself, without a field of its own.
- **A cumulative index.** A withdrawn old version can be marked only in an index that names it, and releases are immutable. And a repetition of a verdict by the digest of an attempt finds the package's release by the index, not by going through releases.
- **A tag, not a URL.** The records stay forever, and a URL would sew GitHub's address scheme into them, while the tag and the file name give the address anyway. The place requires no trust, so there is no need to sign it separately. The form of the tag is set by R31, and `release` holds it: a tag outside the form or with the sign `-` in front the schema will not pass.
- **`teaches` in the record, not a map at the root.** It is a fact of one package, and it has no way to diverge from the packages. A map at the root would force the index to decide whose version counts — the newest, non-withdrawn, at which format version — and that is decided by the reader by its window.
- **The index's template for all versions.** In v0 only the current format version is read (R44), and without this rule each change of 0.y would break the chain of indexes: `module-kit` of the new version would not read the previous index. In the same way, the place of `module_format_version` in the manifest and in the inventory is one in all versions.
- **Refusals with vectors.** A broken build loses the history of the index or names one version with two packages, and a repetition of a verdict by the digest then finds no package. The refusal vectors bind this for both implementations, `module-kit` and `spec`.

— *Rejected:*
- an index without the mark before stage 4; a mark without a reason;
- only adding to Т-30, and leaving attempts and evidence to the detailing of `api` and `learner-model`;
- an index of its own release only;
- URLs of the package's files; one digest without a place — a reader would look for the package by going through releases;
- a map `anchor_skills` at the root of the index;
- vectors of the build only, without refusals, and no vectors at all — only the schema and examples;
- `teaches` as a reference to the taxonomy's vocabulary: the record would fail when the next version removes the anchor skill.

— *Consequence:*

- the schemas `module-index.schema.json` and `index-vector.schema.json`; two correct and four incorrect examples of the index; six index vectors — three builds and three refusals;
- `format-check` — `index.mjs`, the index vectors in `cases.mjs` and `main.mjs` and the check of the index examples; tests;

## Files of the `spec` release

**R64. Code takes `spec`'s files from its releases. From line 0.3 a release carries each normative part with a version of its own as a file `<part>-<version>.tar.gz` — now this is the module format, `format-0.1.tar.gz` — with a keyless cosign signature and under the attestation of an immutable release. Code in Go takes the same tag as the version of the Go module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec`, whose package embeds `format/`. Format version 0.1 comes out with v0.3.0, and `release-version` refuses a commit that gives the format a new version without a new line. The format's types for Go and TypeScript and the npm package are RUN.md, T45, and the types of the `canvas` element and its vectors are T46.** The author's answers in planning T35 (RUN.md), 2026-10-28.
- **The release file.** Each normative part with a version of its own comes out as a file `<part>-<version>.tar.gz` for each version that the platform reads (R44). While the format is v0, this is one file, `format-0.1.tar.gz`. It is built by the recipe `just release-files <commit> <folder>`:
  - what a release carries is decided by `tools/release/files.mjs` by the commit's line: from `FIRST_FILES_LINE`, 0.3, the files, and before it nothing;
  - the file is a `git archive` of the commit itself, not of the working tree: in it is the folder `<part>-<version>/`, and in that `LICENSE` and the part's folder, as in the commit. The recipe checks the archive against `git ls-tree`;
  - the archive's bytes depend on gzip in git, so reproducibility is not promised: the check is the signature.
- **The signature** is double:
  - keyless cosign puts `<file>.sigstore.json` beside each file. The shared release of `.github` signs files this way too (R08 .github), and cosign of the same version, 3.1.4, is pinned by its sum. The certificate names `https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`, and it is issued by `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`;
  - the attestation of the immutable release names both the files and their signatures.

  A consumer checks a file with the command `gh release verify-asset <tag> <file> -R altnovatrail/spec` or `cosign verify-blob` with the bundle, this identity and this issuer. What else the signature check compares is decided by T37 together with the signatures of the shared release (Т-27).
- **The Go module.**
  - `go.mod` lies at the root of `spec`: the module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec`, `go 1.27.0`, without `require`. From v2 the path ends in `/v2`, as Go requires.
  - The package `spec` is `spec.go`, and `spec.Format` in it is an `fs.FS` rooted at `format/`. The directive `//go:embed all:format` takes the files starting with `.` and `_` too: a package vector holds `.editor-notes` on purpose.
  - The module's version is the release's tag, and it has no other tag. The Go proxy builds the module's zip from the tag, and the checksum database sum.golang.org records its hash forever. After that a version can only be retracted with the directive `retract`, not removed.
  - Code in Go takes the format so: `go get github.com/altnovatrail/spec@<tag>`, and then `spec.Format`.
  - The module's zip carries the whole repository except nested modules, the documents too; code imports only the package `spec`. The zip is checked by the nested module `tools/gomod`: with the same code as the proxy, `golang.org/x/mod/zip`, it builds the commit's zip, reads it back and checks that it holds `LICENSE` and each file of `format/`, byte for byte. `tools/gomod` itself is not in `spec`'s zip, and the module `spec` has no `golang.org/x/mod` among its dependencies.
- **The steps of `release.yml`:**
  - the number — as before, and the recipe `release-version` also checks the format version (below);
  - "Build the files" — the recipe `release-files` in a new copy of the checkout: the copy of the number's step has already had the container. On the runner the step checks that `dist/` holds only regular files with names by the pattern;
  - "Sign the files" — cosign on the runner, without the container: the OIDC token does not go into the container. The job gets `id-token: write`;
  - publication — `gh release create` with the files. A draft of this version left by an interrupted run is deleted before creation and after a refusal. The refusal path `release-refusal` is as before;
  - "Verify the release" — the files are downloaded from the release, compared with the list of those built, and checked by `gh release verify` and `gh release verify-asset`, in one loop of retries. A repeated run of a released commit checks the same way;
  - "Verify the Go module" — `go mod download -json` of the release's module in the stage `toolchain`, only through the proxy, `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org`, up to 10 attempts 30 s apart. A broken zip fails the run already after the release is out, and a repeated run asks again;
  - the job's timeout is 25 minutes.
- **The link of the line with the format** — `tools/release/format-line.mjs`, only in `spec`: through it the recipe `release-version` passes what `version.mjs` prints. The check runs only if the commit gets a release, and the previous release is of line 0.3 or newer, that is, it already carried the format as files. Then `format/VERSION` of the commit and of the previous release hold R44:
  - a different format version — only above the previous one and only in a raised line, so that a line holds one format version;
  - a new major format version — only with a new major version of `spec`;
  - while the format is v0, `spec` stays 0.x.

  The refusal is caught already by the CI step "Release version" on the pull request.

They exclude the module `spec` from Dependabot's `gomod`: a release comes out on each edit to a document, and otherwise Dependabot would propose a new tag every week.

The vectors and conformance tests of the other normative parts — the eval protocol, the widget protocol — their tasks put here too: as a file of their own if the part has a version of its own, and as an `fs.FS` of their own in the same module, without a new delivery.

  - how a release and the Go module carry the previous major format version. From v1 the window is the current major version and the previous one (R44), and `format/` holds one version. Two major versions in the window occur only from v2, and the path is decided by the pull request that opens it;

Normative — [the format text](../format/README.md), sections 2 and 3; `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `justfile`, `go.mod`, `spec.go`, `tools/release/`, `tools/gomod/`.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-28 in planning T35 — six, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T35, «Решено автором»). The rest is the plan's proposal, which the author approved. Before the work, an independent agent reviewed the plan, and its findings are taken into account (the same place, «Выяснилось при планировании»). All read 2026-10-28.
- **Three tasks instead of one.** The path, the generator of types with open views and the types of the `canvas` element are three different circles, and each is for one review (rule 11 of RUN.md). The path is one for all the files, and T45 and T46 only add files to the same release and the same module.
- **The Go module at the root.** The release tags `vX.Y.Z` are already versions of the module. A module in a subfolder would need tags of its own: "If a module is defined in a subdirectory within the repository … then each tag name must be prefixed with the module subdirectory, followed by a slash" ([Go Modules Reference](https://go.dev/ref/mod), Mapping versions to commits). That is a second kind of tags and a ruleset of its own, and `format/` would have to be copied inside: "Patterns must not match files outside the package's module" (the documentation of the package `embed`, Go 1.27.3). Only a release file for Go would mean gh with a token in the CI of each consumer, and the types of `sim` would have to be copied to it.
- **`all:` in `//go:embed`.** "If a pattern names a directory, all files in the subtree rooted at that directory are embedded (recursively), except that files with names beginning with ‘.’ or ‘_’ are excluded", and "If a pattern begins with the prefix ‘all:’, then the rule for walking directories is changed to include those files" (the same place).
- **Checking the zip before the tag.** "Module zip files do not include the contents of vendor directories or any nested modules (subdirectories that contain go.mod files)" (Go Modules Reference, Module zip files). Such a file in `format/` would vanish for consumers silently, and `go test` in `spec`, which reads the working tree, would not see it. `golang.org/x/mod/zip` is the code with which `go` and the proxy build a zip.
- **The cosign signature.** R31 rejected cosign because "there is nothing to sign but the tag" — now there is something. Scorecard's Signed-Releases looks for signatures among the files: "This check looks for the following filenames in the project's last five release assets: … *.sig, *.sign, *.sigstore, *.sigstore.json …", and "It ignores the source code-only releases that are created automatically by GitHub" ([ossf/scorecard, docs/checks.md](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/6b98ea0a6a1c017fd399e5777301263dc20badee/docs/checks.md), commit 6b98ea0). It does not read the release attestation, so it would score a file without a bundle at 0, and there would be an alert in the Security tab (rule 12 of RUN.md).
- **The attestation.** "creating an immutable release automatically generates a release attestation, which is a cryptographically verifiable record of a release containing the release tag, commit SHA, and release assets" ([GitHub Docs, Immutable releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases)), and after publication "you cannot add, replace, or delete assets" ([GitHub Docs, Managing releases in a repository](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/managing-releases-in-a-repository)). So the files are signed and checked before publication.
- **Drafts.** "When you attach assets, gh release create creates a draft release, uploads each asset, and then publishes the release. These steps use separate API requests and do not form a single atomic operation" ([gh manual, gh release create](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_create)). An interrupted run may leave a draft, and the next one deletes it.
- **The Go proxy in the release check.** "The new version should be available within one minute. Note that if someone requested the version before the tag was pushed, it may take up to 30 minutes for the mirror's cache to expire" ([proxy.golang.org](https://proxy.golang.org/), FAQ). Hence five minutes of retries and the ban on asking for the version before the tag. With the default `GOPROXY`, `go` on a 404 answer would go to GitHub directly and would hide that the proxy does not give the version.
- **The shared `go.yml` — with T45.** Now the Go code in `spec` is one package that embeds a folder, without dependencies, and a CI tool in a nested module. Four shared Go checks with their tools and the ruleset's required checks will give more when the Go types come.

- one task together with the types and `canvas`; two tasks — the path and all the types together;
- only a release file for Go; a Go module in the subfolder `go/` with tags `go/vX.Y.Z`;
- npm already in T35, when the package would carry only schemas; no npm — R37 rejected this for UI packages;
- a trial release in a separate repository; only a build in CI, without a local run of the publication steps;
- the shared `go.yml` already in T35;
- only the attestation, with the open alert Signed-Releases and the reason in R33;
- `SHA256SUMS` in `spec`'s release: the attestation already names the digest of each file, and the link of the npm package with the release will be decided by T45.

## AI providers beyond OpenAI and Anthropic

**R65. The terms of an AI provider beyond OpenAI and Anthropic are checked in full when the platform needs it — the way privacy 5.3 checked the first ones. Until then the route to it is closed. First Cerebras, then Groq.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В26 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its second option, by the recommendation of `tutor`.
- **`tutor`'s screening** (architecture 2.6 and 4 tutor, T44; the sources read by `tutor` 2026-10-25). Six providers of fast inference and Mathpix went through four questions in order: a model with images, training on the customer's data, minors, retention. The outcome is in privacy 5.3:
  - Groq, Together AI, Cerebras, SambaNova and Mathpix passed. But all of them except Groq are silent on learners, and where the terms are silent, it is "18+ only": for under 18, privacy 5.1 requires terms that expressly permit them;
  - SiliconFlow and Fireworks are stopped: their terms forbid passing on the personal data of children under 14 and under 13.
- **The order of checking.** First Cerebras: by its help pages and documentation, it stores no data, and it calls its model with images ready for production. Its DPA is needed, and a written confirmation that the line of its help pages "our products are not intended for minors" does not concern learners. Then Groq, when its model with images leaves Preview and its DPA covers it. The check is as in privacy 5.3: verbatim quotes with the date read, and whether a text permits minors is decided by a lawyer (П-3).
- **eval.** Together, Cerebras and Fireworks forbid benchmarking in their terms, and SambaNova forbids publishing its results without its consent. The check reads this too: an eval run of `tutor` at a provider and its published report go by that provider's terms (architecture 4.6).

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. Those that passed the screening suit now only adult learners, and Groq's and SambaNova's models with images are for trial only. Terms change, and a check ahead of time would be outdated by the day the provider is needed: privacy 5.3 requires checking them again "before each decision on an AI route".

*Rejected:*
- checking all who passed now;
- not checking: the route to a fast provider would be left without a rule.

*Consequence:* privacy 5.3; architecture 4.6. `tutor` closes В26 by its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

— privacy 5.3; architecture 4.6; RUN.md, Д47.

## Reading on the device

**R66. A model that would read the work on the device is code of `tutor`: its release carries it with the digest of its weights, its eval admits it, and the verdict on what was read is given by `module-kit` on the server, as for a typed answer. In the first slice there is no reading on the device.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В27 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its first option, by the recommendation of `tutor`. The boundary "not in the first slice" is the executor's proposal: R66 says whose this reading is, and does not introduce it.
- **What it is for** (architecture 2.6 tutor, T44). The answer slots of a workbook (R41) are digits. A small network of its own on the device would read them without an AI call, and the strokes would stay on the device (privacy 1). By the assessment of `tutor`, only such a network passes the 2026-10-28 amendment to R12: code, weights and data under category A. TexTeller does not pass it because of its training data, and for Pix2Text-MFR this cannot be decided: it discloses neither its data nor its initial weights.
- **Whose.** "Everything that calls a model is in `tutor`" (architecture 1), and a model on the device is a model too. Its weights and their digest, the eval set and the admission are with `tutor`, and it is admitted, like any model of an AI capability, by eval (R07; architecture 4.6). What runs it on the device — `app` or `canvas` — is decided when reading on the device comes.
- **The verdict** stays with `module-kit` on the server (R03). The server gets the read value the same way as a typed answer (architecture 4.2).
- **When it reads** — only on the learner's action, like the AI on the server (R69): on "Check" and "Step done". If the device is not sure, the work goes to the ordinary reading call.
- **The Prompt API in Chrome** — Google's generative AI on the device — is closed, like Google's models (the 2026-10-28 amendment to R47).
- **In the first slice** the answer slots of a workbook are read by an AI call (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R53). `tutor` has no digit network of its own: its eval and its cost will be shown by its task.

*Why:* the recommendation of `tutor`. So the rule of architecture 1 holds, and the server gets the value as a typed answer, and the platform needs no second path to the verdict.

*Rejected:*
- the model as a part of `canvas`: the model, its eval and its admission would end up outside `tutor`, against architecture 1;
- no reading on the device: it would close the path on which the strokes of a workbook do not leave the device.

*Consequence:* architecture 1 and 3.6. `tutor` closes В27 with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

— architecture 1, 3.6, 4.2, 4.6; RUN.md, Д47.

## Reading and analysis

**R67. Reading and analysis are two calls: reading without the key, analysis with the key and the task's solution. One call of a model is admitted only if it passed the threshold of R03 `tutor` on the handwriting of adult volunteers (П-16), by a new decision, with a change to privacy 5.1.** Т-23 is closed. The author's decision of 2026-10-28 on the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В37 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its second option, by the recommendation of `tutor` (R46 tutor).
- **The threshold** (Т-23). With the correct key, there are no more false "correct" and false alarms than without the key — a paired test by sheets, a worsening at p < 0.05 is a failure. Not one incorrect line is read as the correct key, and not one correct line as a false one.
- **The measurement of E4 `tutor`** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера чтения»; R37 tutor) applied the threshold to the observation on the test part of the synthetic data: 68 sheets — free writing, the lines of E2 and the near-key, where the key differs from the sheet by one similar digit. Opus 5.5 · `high`, Haiku 5.5 · `low` and Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking gave not one false "correct", not one false alarm and not one reading as the key, in any condition. By the threshold, one call is admissible for all three.
- **But the test has no power.** On no sheet did the reading with the key differ from the reading without it, so there was nothing to fail the paired test with:
  - the handwriting is synthetic data, and Opus without the key read 66 sheets of 68 correctly;
  - the near-key was measured at the weakest shift of a digit, 0.1. At a larger shift, Opus read fewer and fewer sheets correctly even without the key: at 0.2 — 9 of 12, at 0.3 — 7 of 12, at 0.4 — 5 of 12 (R36 tutor, the 2026-10-28 amendment);
  - the key does shift the reading of Haiku, though — toward "unreadable". On the near-key sheets with an error, Haiku · `low` gave the correct verdict in 4 calls of 15 with the key against 12 without it.
- **The data at the provider.** With two calls, the key and the task's solution go to the model only for the analysis, after "not yet" (privacy 5.1).

## Reading unfinished work

**R69. The work is read only on the learner's action: on "Check", and in the solving mode "by steps" also on "Step done". On a pause, the app only blinks a button, without an AI call, and the pause does not go to the AI. A request for a hint does not send work not submitted for reading either.** О-8 is closed, О-21 is added to. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В40 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8): for О-8 — its first option, by the recommendation of О-8 and of `tutor`; for О-21 — the executor's option.
- **What the measurement of E4 measured** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера чтения» and «Итог прогонов на листах автора»; R35 and R37 tutor). Haiku 5.5 · `low` without the key read a sheet where the device itself would read it: after a line, on a pause from 0.4 s, and before erasing.
  - "Correct" or "not yet" before the answer is written: after a line — in 94 calls of 196, on a pause — in 46 of 131, before erasing — in 11 of 22. A result that the work does not yet give — in 113, 57 and 12: the last number on the sheet is read as the answer. This is the very "read 1" of О-8.
  - The pauses were chosen, not all taken: the longest one in the answer line and in one other line. So the share on a pause is not the share over all pauses.
  - Readings per sheet beyond submission on the synthetic data: after each line — 2.9, on pauses from 0.4 s — 15.6, from 2 s — 2.9, from 6 s — 0.4. On the author's three sheets, live writing with a mouse — 15.0, 54.0, 7.7 and 1.7. A policy of pauses from 0.4 s would cost Opus about $0.15 per sheet of the synthetic data and about $0.69 per sheet of the author's.
- **A pause** is neither a reason to read nor a mark for the AI: nothing of the writing history goes to the AI (R52). The refinement of О-8 of 2026-10-22 — "a pause is only a mark in the course of solution for review" — R52 has already cancelled.
- **О-21.** Before the first submission, the request "Hint" gives what the module gives the solving steps, without AI and without reading the work (R57). Between submissions — the same: the request does not send work not submitted for reading, and the option of О-21 "the request sends the work for reading without a verdict" is rejected. What the request gives after an incorrect answer and what "explain differently" means is decided, as before, by the detailing of `api` (architecture 3.5). In this part О-21 is open: E4 did not measure it.

*Why:* the recommendation of О-8 and of `tutor`. Reading on a pause gives a verdict on unfinished work in almost half of the cases and costs up to 15.6 readings per sheet of the synthetic data and 54 on live writing, and each reading gives the provider work not submitted. The request would read unfinished work in the same way. Not closing О-21 as a whole is the executor's proposal: the 2026-10-27 amendment to О-21 gave the part after an incorrect answer to the detailing of `api`, and the data of E4 are only about reading unfinished work.

*Rejected:*
- reading on pauses — by any policy of the measurement;
- deciding later: the data that О-8 waited for are there;
- closing О-21 by its second option as a whole, as `tutor` advised: E4 did not measure the part after an incorrect answer.

*Consequence:* О-8 is closed, О-21 is added to (product 13); concepts 9.1; architecture 3.5. `tutor` closes В40 with its move to a tag, and `api` and `app` get the answer with theirs — RUN.md, Д47.
