## Checks of the tutor's words

**R70. The model's words that the learner will see are checked by a program not only for a leak. A hint — by the form check: exactly one question, no more than two sentences, the letters of the explanation language and a word limit by language — 30 in Russian, 35 in English. Feedback by a rubric — by the feedback rule: no more than three sentences and 80 words in English, and a stretch in quotation marks of four words or more is only the learner's words. The tutor's words do not give away the learner's gender.** The author's answers to the rows «в реестр spec» `tutor` В43 and В45 and to the feedback rule of В49 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8) — by the recommendations of `tutor`, with the executor's options: where the check is and how the word limit depends on the language (В43), and the rule on gender — for all of the tutor's words (В45).
- **The form of a hint.** concepts 10 prescribes: one question, no more than two short sentences. Only the prompt held this rule, and `api` checked only the leak (architecture 3.5). The measurement T76 of `tutor` checked the form the way `api` would check it (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера подсказок»; R39 tutor): exactly one sentence is a question, no more than two sentences, from 1 to 30 words, the letters of the hint's language — Cyrillic in a Russian one, where a Latin letter of the task statement, such as `x`, may stand too, and Latin in an English one.
  - The result on 34 test sheets, 204 hints per configuration: Opus 5.5 · `high` breaks the form in 25, all by the number of words, and 24 of them in English. Its English hint is 28.2 words on average, its Russian one 21.5, so the limit is by language: 30 words in Russian and 35 in English. Haiku 5.5 · `low` has 21 breaches, Haiku without thinking 65.
  - A hint that did not pass the form is the same as one that did not pass the leak: the learner reads the fallback text (concepts 10; R57).
- **The rule of feedback by a rubric.** How feedback does not write the essay for the learner (R05), architecture 3.6 left to the detailing. The measurement T84 of `tutor` checked feedback by a program (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера сочинений»; R45 tutor): no more than three sentences and 60 words, a stretch in quotation marks of four words or more stands in the essay as it is written, the letters are Latin. Not one quote of others' words, and Opus exceeded the limit of 60 words in 3 feedbacks of 45 — all about an essay where three criteria are not met. So the limit is 80 words. What the learner sees instead of feedback that did not pass the rules is decided by the detailing of `api` (architecture 3.5).
- **Where the check is and whose code.** Both checks are done by `api`, before the text goes to the device, beside the leak check (R54). The code is in `tutor`, the same with which its eval measures models: so admission measures exactly what the platform will check (R07). How words and sentences are counted is set by this code (R39 tutor). The checks do not go into the module format: they do not depend on the module's data.
- **The language.** The word limit is measured for Russian and English. An explanation language that the measurement did not measure is checked without a word limit until a measurement in that language sets it: the platform is for any language (R01), and one limit for all languages is too tight already for English. The other rules hold in any language.
- **The learner's gender.** The model does not get it (concepts 10). But in languages where the form of a word gives away gender — in Russian, the past tense and short adjectives about the learner, «ты нашёл», «ты прав» —, the tutor's words may call the child by the wrong gender.
  - The rule is for all of the tutor's words, not only for a hint: praise, an explanation and feedback give away gender the same way. The words are in forms without gender: «здесь всё верно», not «ты верно нашёл».
  - A program does not check this: by the forms of words there is no way without false alarms — «начала» is both a verb and a noun. The eval checks it: each capability that writes words to the learner has an item on gender in its eval set, and a model that gives away gender does not pass it.
  - The measurement T76, by a rough search: in the Russian hints of the test, gender is given away by Opus in 0 of 102, by Haiku · `low` in 13, by Haiku without thinking in 37.

*Why:* the recommendations of `tutor` in В43, В45 and В49. The form is a rule of concepts 10, and for a program it is as simple to check as the leak, and a hint of three sentences or in another language would otherwise reach the learner. The executor's options:
- the check does not depend on the module's data, so it is code of the platform, not a format rule;
- the word limit is by language, because modules are written in any language;
- the rule on gender is for all words, because «молодец, справился» gives away gender the same way as a hint.

*Rejected:*
- form checks in the module format: the module gives them nothing;
- one word limit for all languages: it is too tight for English;
- leaving the form to `api` without a norm, or not checking it at all;
- the rule on gender only for a hint; a programmatic check of gender by a dictionary of forms.

*Consequence:* concepts 10 and 15; architecture 3.5 and 3.6. `tutor` closes В43 and В45 with its move to a tag, and `api` gets the answer with its own — RUN.md, Д47.

— concepts 10, 15; architecture 3.5, 3.6; RUN.md, Д47.

## Assessment by a rubric

**R71. Assessment by a rubric is measured by two measures. The main one is the share of false alarms: criteria that the AI called not met, though they are met. The second is agreement with people's assessment and Cohen's kappa for each criterion. The target and the eval set are set by the measurement of `tutor` on the essays of adult volunteers (П-16).** О-22 is closed. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В49 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its first option, by the recommendations of О-22 and of `tutor`. The feedback rule from the same row is R70.
- **The measurement of E4 of `tutor`** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера сочинений»; R44 and R45 tutor): 20 synthetic essays in English and a rubric of six criteria. The truth is the plan, without disputed cases. On the test, 15 essays with three repeats each:
  - Opus 5.5 · `high` has 0 false alarms of 197 assessments of met criteria, the upper bound of 95% over essays is 0.015, κ 1.00;
  - Haiku 5.5 · `low` has 1 of 198, κ 0.99;
  - Haiku without thinking has 2 of 198, κ 0.97.

  The measure is computed by a program and separates the models.
- **Why the target is not by the synthetic data.** The synthetic data are even, and the criteria are without disputed cases, so a target by them would be too strict for live writing. Without a target there is no admission (architecture 4.6), so the target is needed before the first learner with essays.
- **The guide for authors** (epic E5 of RUN.md). A criterion about capital letters on handwriting is disputable for c, o, s, u, v, w, x and z: only height tells their capital from their lowercase. Haiku's false alarms in the measurement are by the criterion "capitals and full stops", and one of them is of this kind: in essay 11, "One" was read as lowercase, since the capital O of the synthetic data is written as the lowercase one, only larger.

*Why:* the recommendations of О-22 and of `tutor`. Feedback that does not see what was done confuses the learner just as "not yet" on a correct answer does (R04).

*Rejected:*
- leaving О-22 open until the volunteers' essays: the measure is already there and checked;
- a target now, by the synthetic data.

*Consequence:* О-22 is closed (product 13); product 10; architecture 3.6 and 4.6; epic E5 of RUN.md. `tutor` closes В49 with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

— product 10, 13; architecture 3.6, 4.6; RUN.md, table 2, Д47.

## Types of the module format

**R72. The types of the module format are given by a generator of its own from its schemas, `tools/types`. The Go module `spec` carries them in the packages `types/formatv0` — the parts, the shared definitions, the canonical view, the inventory, the part list for the device, the index and the vectors — and `types/formatv0/open` — the open view of each part, under the same names. The package is named by the major version of the format. The TypeScript types by the same generator and the npm package `@altnovatrail/spec` are RUN.md, T49, and the shared Go checks from `.github` are T50.** The author's answers in the planning of T45 (RUN.md), 2026-10-29.
- **The generator** is `tools/types/`, on Node, like the other tools of `spec`. It reads the schemas, the module layout and the version from `format/` with the same functions as `format-check`. The model, `model.mjs`, takes the shape of a value from the schema:
  - a type is at the root of each schema and at each `$defs`, in PascalCase and with `ID` instead of `id`: `task` → `Task`, `answer_slot` → `AnswerSlot`, `skill_id` → `SkillID`;
  - an object without a name of its own is named by the table `INLINE_NAMES`, in the words of concepts 15: `Audience`, `Band`, `Languages`, `CanvasSettings`, `Author`, `Skill`, `RetiredSkill`, `Technique`, `Trap`, `RandomState` and five kinds of `…Draw`. The enumeration of a field is named by the object and the field: `CanvasKind`, `AnswerSlotBinding`;
  - the fields of an object come from its `properties`, its `allOf` and the branches of `if`/`then`/`else`. A field that the object always holds is required: it is in the `required` of the object or of its `allOf`, not of a branch;
  - a `$ref` beside which the keys only narrow the value is the type it refers to. A `$defs` that narrows a structure in this way is another name of the same structure: `WrittenCheck` is `Check`;
  - `pattern`, bounds, `not`, `contains` and conditions between fields are the business of the schema, not of the type.

  A shape that the model does not know is a generation error with a pointer to the place in the schema: two places of one name, an object without a name, a field to which the branches give different shapes. The generator understands the schemas of 0.1 as they are (RUN.md, T24 and T45): the model has 101 types, and the open views are 24.
- **Go**, `go.mjs`:
  - a structure per object. A field that the object always holds is a value, and any other is a pointer, a slice or a map with `omitzero`. So absence and zero — an empty `alt`, `false`, 0 — are told apart, and a value is written back by the same JSON by which it was read;
  - `integer` is `int64`: the bounds ±(2^53 − 1) by R62 fit in it. `number` is `float64`, and `["string", "null"]` is `*string`;
  - a string, an integer, a list or a map with a name of its own is a type of its own: `type SkillID LocalID`, `type Numbers map[TemplateName]int64`. The values of an enumeration are constants: `CanvasKindHandwritingSheet`;
  - the comment of a type names its place in the schema and repeats its `description`, and that of a field also its `default`;
  - there is no code in the packages, only types and constants: what is valid is decided by the schema, and `spec` is not the platform's library (repositories 5). Whoever reads a value from outside first checks it against the schema.
- **The open view** is the package `open`: a structure for each type that the open view of a part reaches, with the fields marked `x-open`. A field is open if at least one subschema of its place marks it (R45). On 0.1 this is the same as the rule by value of `tools/format-check/openview.mjs`: a field with the mark in a branch is either marked in a subschema that always applies too, or declared only in this branch. `open.Task` has no `check`, `template` and `solver`, but has `givens` and `unknown`; `open.Traps` is an empty structure. Strings, integers and enumerations `open` takes from `formatv0`.
- **The files are in the repository:** the Go module is built from the tag (R64). `just types` writes them anew, and `just types-check` is the CI step "Types":
  - it compares them with what the generator would give, file for file;
  - it reads with its type, strictly, each value of `format/` that passes the schema, and writes it back. These are the examples, the part files of each module of the examples and vectors, the vectors themselves and the canonical view of each example of a whole module — 288 cases now. The open view of an open-view vector is read by the type `open`, and the part of the same vector with a closed field the type `open` must fail to read (`tools/types/corpus.mjs`, `tools/types/roundtrip`);
  - the nested module `tools/types/roundtrip` takes `spec` from the working tree and requires no other modules.
- **The Go module** carries `types/`, and `tools/gomod` compares its files byte for byte, like `LICENSE` and `format/`. `go-check` checks `./...`, and the module still requires nothing.
- **Versions in the window.** The package is named by the major version of the format (R44): 0.2 (RUN.md, T48) changes its types, but not its path. With v1, `formatv1` stands beside `formatv0`, and with v2 the module is `/v2`, with `formatv1` and `formatv2` in it. How the module carries the previous major version of the format is still decided by the pull request that opens it (R64).
- **The Go module gives no generator of randomness as code.** The normative functions of R59 are exactly Go's `math/rand/v2` and `hash/fnv`, and how to call them is decided by `module-kit` (architecture 3.7). For TypeScript this is decided by T49.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-29 in the planning of T45 — three, all by the recommendations of the plan (RUN.md, T45, «Решено автором»). The rest is a proposal of the plan that the author approved. All read 2026-10-29.
- **Three tasks instead of one.** The generator with the Go types, the npm package with a publication step of its own and the shared Go checks are three rounds, and each is for one check (rule 11 of RUN.md). The Go types come out at once, with the next tag, and `module-kit` and `sim` wait for them. The TypeScript types have no consumer while there is no npm package.
- **A generator of its own.** json-schema-to-typescript 16.0.0, quicktype 26.0.0 and go-jsonschema v0.24.1 do not understand `if`/`then`/`else`, `propertyNames` and `unevaluatedProperties` (RUN.md, T35, «Выяснилось при планировании»), and the schemas of 0.1 write unions through `allOf` and `if`/`then` — 24 times. A generator in Go would go into the module's zip or would be a second language of the tools, and 101 types by hand would diverge from the schemas.
- **Open views as a package.** Under the same names in `open`, the consumer gets the type of what the learner sees — `api` gives the open view of the manifest (R36) —, and a closed field cannot be read by them. The names `OpenTask` would double the length of one package.
- **Pointers with `omitzero`.** `omitempty` on writing would throw out the empty `alt` of a picture that only decorates, `false` and 0, and the consumer would not tell "not set" from zero.
- **Types of their own for IDs.** `type SkillID LocalID`, not an alias: the compiler will not let one confuse the ID of a skill with the ID of a task. Another name of a structure is an alias, since the narrowing of the schema does not change its shape.
- **Duplicates in SonarCloud.** The open view repeats the fields of the part, and the duplicates of new code would fail the quality gate, so `types/**` is in `sonar.cpd.exclusions`.

— *Rejected:*
- two tasks — the types of both languages, then npm and `go.yml`; one task, as it was;
- a third-party generator; a generator in Go; types by hand;
- the open views in the same package under the names `Open…`; the package `formatv0/` at the root of `spec`, beside `format/`; a path by the full version of the format;
- values with `omitempty`;
- the generator of randomness as code in the Go module.

— *Consequence:*
- amendments to R30, R36, R44 and R64;
- "T45" in R21, R36, R37, R44, R45 and R64 reads so: the generator and the Go types are T45 (R72), the TypeScript types and the npm package are T49, the shared Go checks are T50, and the types of the element `canvas` are T46, after T49;
- repositories 1 and 5; architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.7, 3.9 and 3.11; README.md, CLAUDE.md; CI — the step "Types";
- the components in Go take the types by the same tag as the format, with their move to a release of `spec` — RUN.md, Д46.

**R73. The TypeScript types of the module format are given by the same generator, `tools/types`, by the same model as the Go types — flat, as in Go, as the file `index.d.ts` beside the Go of each package. The npm package `@altnovatrail/spec` carries them as declarations only and exports `./formatv0` and `./formatv0/open`, and the release of `spec` from the line 0.4 on carries it as the file `altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz`, with a cosign signature and under an attestation. Packages take it as a copy of their own by exact version. The first version in npm the author publishes by hand, and publication by each release is RUN.md, T51.** The author's answers in the planning of T49 (RUN.md), 2026-10-29.
- **The TypeScript output** is `tools/types/ts.mjs`, by the model of R72 without changes to it:
  - the names are the same as in Go. A structure is an `interface`: a field that the object always holds is required, and any other is `?:`, and so is a field of the schema's branches;
  - an enumeration is a union of strings, `type CanvasKind = "handwriting_sheet" | "workbook"`. A string, an integer, an ID, another name of a structure, a list or a map with a name of its own is an alias: `type SkillID = LocalID`, `type Numbers = Readonly<Record<TemplateName, number>>`;
  - `integer` and `number` are `number`, `["string", "null"]` is `string | null`. Everything is `readonly`, and lists are `readonly T[]`: these are data read from a module;
  - an empty open view is an object each field of which is `never`: an empty interface would accept any object, closed fields too;
  - a map by an enumeration key and a description that holds the end of a comment are generation errors;
  - the comment of a type and of a field is JSDoc from `description`, and that of a field also has `@defaultValue`;
  - there is no code: neither constants nor a generator of randomness. Declarations import with `import type`.
- **The npm package** is `tools/types/npm.mjs`. `package.json` is written by code, and the archive holds `package.json`, `LICENSE`, the package's README `tools/types/npm/README.md` and two `index.d.ts`, and nothing more:
  - `exports` are `./formatv0` and `./formatv0/open` with the condition `types`, and `./package.json`; `type: module`; neither `main`, nor scripts, nor dependencies;
  - `repository` is `git+https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec.git`: npm's provenance requires it to match the repository;
  - the version is the number of the release without `v`. It comes out with each release of the line, even when the types are the same;
  - the archive is built by `npm pack` of the Node that runs the tool, without the user's and the system's settings, with a cache of its own and without scripts, and is read back by `tar`.
- **The check** is in `just types-check`, the CI step "Types":
  - the package is built from the working tree and unpacked into a project that `tools/types/typescript.mjs` writes from the corpus of R72 — a declaration per case, in one line;
  - `tsc` checks the project twice — under `nodenext` and under `bundler` —, with `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `verbatimModuleSyntax` and without `skipLibCheck`;
  - a case with a closed field stands under `@ts-expect-error`: if `tsc` accepts such a value, it fails;
  - `typescript` 7.0.2 is in `tools/package.json`.
- **The release file** (R64):
  - from `FIRST_NPM_LINE`, 0.4, `tools/release/files.mjs` also names `altnovatrail-spec-<X.Y.Z>.tgz`, and `just release-files <commit> <folder> <tag>` builds it from the objects of the commit;
  - the signature and the check of the release are the same as for `format-0.1.tar.gz`;
  - the consumer checks the archive from npm with the command `gh release verify-asset <tag> altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz -R altnovatrail/spec`.
- **The line 0.4** is opened by this change, and the format in it is still 0.1: R44 allows the same format version in a raised line.
- **How packages take the types** — as a copy of their own by exact version:
  - `canvas` — in `dependencies`, since its `.d.ts` refer to the types of `spec`;
  - `app` — in `devDependencies`.

  The version is moved together with the submodule `spec/`, in one move to a tag, and the package is excluded from Dependabot `npm`, like the Go module (R64).
- **A generator of randomness as code** the package does not give: how a widget gets the seed is decided by the widget protocol, epic E5 (R59; Т-24).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-29 in the planning of T49 — four, all by the recommendations of the plan (RUN.md, T49, «Решено автором»). The rest is a proposal of the plan that the author approved. All read 2026-10-29.
- **Two tasks.** npm sets up a trusted publisher only for a package that is already in the registry: "Package must exist: The package you're configuring must already exist on the npm registry" ([npm Docs, npm trust](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v12/commands/npm-trust)). And a setting that has published nothing expires "48 hours after creation" ([GitHub Changelog, 2026-10-02](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-02-unvalidated-npm-trusted-publishing-configurations-now-expire/)). So first the release carries the package's file and the author publishes the first version by hand, and the publication step comes as a task of its own, T51, right after the setup.
- **Flat types.** One model and one corpus for both languages: what is checked in Go is checked in TypeScript too. Exact unions would require reading the branches of the schemas — their `required` and `not` — and giving names to the variants. The consumer narrows by itself, by a field: `slot.zone !== undefined`.
- **A copy of their own.** The package is declarations only, and two copies of it in a build cost nothing. TypeScript types are structural: two versions of one shape are one type, and a shape that diverged is a compiler error at the junction of `app` and `canvas`. With `peerDependencies` by exact version, each version of `canvas` would require exactly the version of `spec` that `app` has, otherwise npm refuses the installation, and a release of `spec` comes out on each change of `main`.
- **The line 0.4.** Which files the release carries is decided by its line (`tools/release/files.mjs`), as the files themselves came — from the line 0.3 on. A rerun of a release of the line 0.3 does not expect the package's file.
- **`tsc` by the corpus.** The check of a literal's excess properties is the same strict reading as `DisallowUnknownFields` in Go, and a missing required field `tsc` catches by itself. There are two module resolutions, since under `node16`, `nodenext` and `bundler` "TypeScript always matches the "types" and "default" conditions if present" ([TypeScript, Modules — Reference](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/reference.html), updated 2026-10-28), and `canvas` resolves modules as `NodeNext`.
- **TypeScript 7.0.2** is `latest`, under Apache-2.0, "a native port of TypeScript built in Go" ([Announcing TypeScript 7.0](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-7-0/), 2026-07-08); `canvas` has the same version. Its builds are the optional packages `@typescript/typescript-<platform>` 7.0.2, under Apache-2.0 and without install scripts, and the license check skips them.
- **`readonly` and aliases** — as in the temporary types of `canvas`. Brands for IDs are rejected: each value from JSON would have to be cast.

— *Rejected:*
- one task together with the publication step;
- exact unions by a constant field and by the presence of a field;
- `peerDependencies` by exact version;
- the package in the line 0.3, by the content of the commit;
- brands for IDs; constants of enumerations and a generator of randomness as code in the package;
- a `.d.ts` file per schema: per Go package there is one file, and the `exports` point straight at it.

— *Consequence:*
- amendments to R36, R37, R64 and R72;
- architecture 3.1, 3.2 and 3.12; repositories 1 and 5; README.md, CLAUDE.md; CI — the steps "Types" and "Release files";
- `canvas` and `app` take the types with their move to a tag of the line 0.4 — RUN.md, Д49.

## Types of the element `canvas`

**R74. The types of the element `<novatrail-canvas>` — the agreement of `canvas` and `app` — `spec` writes by hand, as the file `types/canvas/index.d.ts`, and the npm package `@altnovatrail/spec` from the line 0.5 on carries them and exports them as `./canvas`. They have no version of their own and no release file of their own. Only the tutor's marks wait for the contract of epic E3, and the test vectors of `canvas` come out with the eval protocol.** The author's answers in the planning of T46 (RUN.md), 2026-11-01.
- **What is in the types** — the contents of the temporary types of `canvas` (`main` ff05c7e), except the marks:
  - `CanvasElement extends HTMLElement`:
    - the properties `tool`, `task` — the open view of the task `open.Task`, `manifest` — the open view of the manifest `open.Manifest`, `history` for reading and assignment and `filled` for reading;
    - the method `exportWork()`;
  - the events — `ToolChange` and `ToolChangeEvent`, `HistoryChange` and `HistoryChangeEvent`, and `CanvasEventMap` names them by their names;
  - the writing history — `HistoryEvent`, `Stroke` and `InkPoint` (R22 canvas): the eval protocol takes it as it is (В33 `canvas`; RUN.md, epic E3);
  - the work for checking — `ExportedWork`, `ExportedSheet`, `ExportedWorkbook` and `ExportedCell`;
  - the submission context — `Submission`, `SheetSubmission` with `CropNumbers`, `Frame`, `Group` and `Box`, `WorkbookSubmission` with `Filling`;
  - `CellPlace`, `Filled` and `Tool`.

  The unions are exact: a history event is told by `kind`, and the work and the context by a key. The rule "flat, as in Go" (R73) is a rule of the generator, and these types are written by hand, and there are none of them in Go.
- **What is not in the types:**
  - the marks — the property `marks` and the types `Marks`, `Mark` and `Anchor`. The look and the place of a mark are written by the contract of epic E3 (R53; В37 `canvas`), and until it the types of the marks at `canvas` are temporary;
  - members of the element that the agreement does not name: `media`, `undo()` and `clear()` at `canvas` (`main` ff05c7e). If they are an agreement with `app`, `canvas` brings them as a row «в реестр spec»;
  - the place of the element in the DOM maps, `HTMLElementTagNameMap` and `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`. They are augmented by the package `canvas`, which registers the element: `interface GlobalEventHandlersEventMap extends CanvasEventMap {}`.
- **The file and the check:**
  - `types/canvas/index.d.ts` lies beside the generator's output. `just types` replaces only the generator's folders, and `just types-check` refuses if there is anything else in `types/`. The Go module carries this file in its zip, like the `.d.ts` of the format;
  - the declarations take the DOM types — `Blob`, `CustomEvent`, `HTMLElement` —, so the consumer's `lib` must include `dom`. The types of the format do not take the DOM, and the corpus is still checked without it;
  - the check is `tools/types/canvas.check.ts`. It holds a class of `canvas` that keeps the agreement, a synthetic history, contexts and work, the narrowing of the work by a key, and under `@ts-expect-error` — everything the agreement does not allow. `tools/types/typescript.mjs` puts it into the project of `types-check` beside the corpus. `tsc` checks it under `nodenext` and `bundler`, with the DOM, against the package built by the line of the working tree.
- **The npm package** from the line 0.5 on also carries `canvas/index.d.ts`, and in its `exports` — `./canvas`. The contents of the package `tools/types/npm.mjs` takes by the line of its version, starting from `FIRST_CANVAS_LINE`, and the package of the line 0.4 stays as before byte for byte.
- **The version.** The types of the element have no version of their own, just as there is no file `<part>-<version>.tar.gz`: this is not a normative part with a version of its own (R64), but declarations of a package whose version is the tag of the release. `canvas` and `app` take the package as a copy of their own by exact version (R73), and a shape that diverged `tsc` catches at their junction. A change of the types of the element requires no new line, and a new file of the package enters with a new line, like this one.
- **The line 0.5** is opened by this change, the format in it is still 0.1. The format 0.2 comes out in the line 0.6 (RUN.md, T48).
- **The vectors of `canvas`** — `groups.json`, `crops.json`, `snaps.json` and `boxes.json` — come out with the eval protocol of epic E3. Its task puts them into `spec` by the route of R64: as a file of its own, if the protocol has a version of its own, and as an `fs.FS` of its own in the Go module. Until then the vectors are at `canvas`, and `pages.json` is still decided by RUN.md, T38.
- **How packages take the types** — by the same move to a tag as the types of the format (Д49):
  - `canvas` — a class with `implements CanvasElement` and the augmentation of the DOM maps;
  - `app` — the same types in `devDependencies` (RUN.md, Д50).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-01 in the planning of T46 — four, all by the recommendations of the plan (RUN.md, T46, «Решено автором»). The rest is a proposal of the plan that the author approved. All read 2026-11-01, `canvas` on GitHub, `main` ff05c7e.
- **By hand.** An event, a method and a promise are not JSON data, and a schema will not describe them. A schema of the data alone — the history and the context — would give two sources for one agreement, and the generator would need the DOM types, which it does not know.
- **The marks wait for E3.** The type of a mark comes with the contract (R53; «Вход» of T35 in RUN.md), and the contract of E3 is protobuf (R11), and a mark may lie in it differently than the temporary one at `canvas`.
  - The writing history is already decided: the eval protocol takes R22 canvas as it is (В33 `canvas`), and later only replaces these types with its own, under the same names.
  - The submission context is named by the amendments to R36. It is held by `app` — as it is, through JSON —, and it needs the type of what it stores.
- **The vectors with the protocol.** Until E3 nobody takes them from `spec`: `canvas` is their source, and the eval runner comes with E3. Without the protocol's text and without schemas they would be just a copy of the files of `canvas`. Besides, the protocol may choose the field and the threshold of snapping anew by its own data (RUN.md, epic E3).
- **Without a version of its own.** The agreement of two packages that take `spec` by exact version is held by the compiler, not by the rule of lines. A version of its own would require a `VERSION` of its own, the rule "a new version is a new line" and a check in `release-version`.
- **The line 0.5.** A rerun of the release builds the package by the list of files of the tip, from the objects of its commit (R31; `release.yml`, the step "Build the files"). The commit of the line 0.4 has no file `types/canvas/index.d.ts`, and without binding the contents to the line such a rerun would fail. Checked on a trial commit: `release-files` built `altnovatrail-spec-0.4.1.tgz` of the commit v0.4.1 byte for byte the same as the release file.
- **The DOM maps are augmented by `canvas`.** If the package itself augmented them, and two copies of it with a diverged shape ended up in a build — at `canvas` and at `app`, R73 —, `tsc` would give the error TS2717 in the package's declarations in `node_modules`, where neither of them looks. Without this, a diverged shape is an error where `app` touches it. This is checked by a trial consumer with two copies of the package, and two copies of one shape do not interfere with each other either way.

— *Rejected:*
- the data by a schema, by the generator;
- all types now, with the marks;
- one surface of the element, with the history and the context as opaque JSON;
- the vectors of `canvas` now — as they are or with schemas;
- a version of its own for the types of the element and a release file of its own;
- the types in the package 0.4.x by the content of the commit — what T49 rejected too (R73);
- the augmentation of the DOM maps in the package of `spec`;
- the types of the element in the package `canvas`, as R07 canvas and architecture 3.3 canvas write: the agreement written down in `spec` by the amendments to R36 would come out as types at only one side.

— *Consequence:*
- amendments to R36, R64 and R73;
- architecture 3.1 and 3.2; repositories 1 and 5; README.md, CLAUDE.md, `tools/types/npm/README.md`;
- RUN.md: T48 takes the line 0.6, epic E3 and Д50.

No new line is needed. — RUN.md, Д72.

— *Amendment 2026-11-03:* **the vectors of `canvas` came out with the eval protocol — `contracts/vectors/eval/v1/`, as messages of the protocol, in `contracts.Vectors` and in the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts` (R94). The types of the writing history — `HistoryEvent`, `Stroke` and `InkPoint` — remain types of the element, and the protocol does not replace them: the element's history needs pressure, to draw the width of the pen's line, and a sample has none (R93). How the element's history becomes the history of a sample is said by the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 12.** "later only replaces these types with its own, under the same names" in "Why" above is withdrawn by this: the shape of the messages of protobuf-es — `$typeName` and `case` with `value` for a `oneof` — is foreign to the element, and the replacement would break `canvas` and `app`. Only the comment of `types/canvas/index.d.ts` changes, and no new line is needed. — R94; RUN.md, T59.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-03:* **the marks are in the types of the element: the property `marks` and the types `Marks`, `Mark` and `Anchor` `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` writes by hand, in the shape of the temporary types of `canvas`, and their look and place are checked against the message `Mark` of the contract `novatrail.api.v1`** (R97; R83). "What is not in the types" above is answered by this: the mark lay in the contract by its look and place, and the name is written by `app`. A mark with a workbook cell circles the box and its strokes, and an empty box — one box: this is a change of R39 canvas. A change of the types of the element requires no new line (above). `canvas` takes the types with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д50. — R97; RUN.md, T62.

## The path of assessment by a rubric

**R75. Assessment by a rubric is two calls. The first is the reading of the essay: one reader, without the rubric, gives the text as it is written. The second is the assessment of the text read by the criteria of the rubric, without the picture: for each criterion — a justification and whether it is met, and one feedback on the whole essay. An essay that cannot be read does not reach the assessment, and the learner rewrites the sheet.** The item "To decide when detailed" of the card architecture 3.6. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В58 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 2f68b04) — all its options except "writing nothing down", by the recommendation of `tutor` (R53 tutor).
- **The path** (architecture 4.1; architecture 3.5 tutor):
  1. `app` sends the work — the crop of the handwriting sheet;
  2. `api` calls the reading of the essay. The reading gets the same as the reading of handwriting: the work, the open view of the task, the age category and the AI route. `tutor` checks the admission, and `api` gets the observation — the text read;
  3. `api` calls the assessment by the rubric with this text. `tutor` checks the admission again, and the model gives the assessments by criteria and the feedback;
  4. the feedback passes the leak check and the feedback rule (R70) and goes to the device.

  These are two calls of the library `tutor`, not one with two requests inside: between perception and the rubric stands a program (concepts 9.1). Between the calls `tutor` stores nothing: the text lives in the memory of the request of `api` (R09).
- **What the assessment gets:**
  - the text read — as data, not instructions;
  - the topic — the task statement;
  - the criteria of the rubric, in order;
  - the presentation style (О-23);
  - the module's explanation language, in which the feedback is written;
  - the age category and the AI route — for the admission.

  The picture does not go to the assessment, and a rubric has no key and no solution of the task (privacy 5.1).
- **An essay that cannot be read** does not reach the assessment, and the learner rewrites the sheet, as with "unreadable". But an item with a rubric has no verdict, and "unreadable" is a verdict (concepts 9.1). How `api` shows and records this is decided by its detailing (architecture 3.5).
- **The data** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог двух вызовов сочинений» and «Итог большого прогона»; R53 tutor). These are synthetic data and the rubric of E4 of six criteria:
  - on the 300 essays of T95, for the four configurations together, the false alarms on met criteria are 26 with two calls and 28 with one, and the missed "not met" are 13 and 11. On the 15 essays of T92, for five configurations — 3 with two calls and 5 with one;
  - a separate reading keeps the learner's errors more exactly. Of 178 words with an error, read as written: Haiku 5.5 · `low` 167 against 155, Haiku 5.5 · `medium` 164 against 161, Sonnet 177 against 175, Opus 5.5 · `high` — 178 on both paths;
  - two calls cost $13.13 against $12.61 for 300 essays for the four configurations, 4% more, and the time is longer by 0–2 s (T92).
- **The measure** is R71 along the whole path, the reading and the assessment together: a false alarm from a wrong reading enters the main measure. The measurement on the essays of adult volunteers (П-16) checks this path and measures one call beside it. If one call gives fewer false alarms, the question is returned to by a new decision.
- **One reader** — the second 2026-11-01 amendment to R68.

— *Why:* the author's answer — all options of the row except the last: a decided item must not stand open in the card, and the detailing of `api` needs the path and the data that go to the AI. The arguments of `tutor` (R53 tutor):
- on the synthetic data, two calls are no worse than one by the main measure of R71, and the cost and time are almost the same;
- the reading of handwriting is an AI capability of its own, with a prompt and an eval set of its own, as is the assessment by a rubric (concepts 10). Reading and analysis are arranged the same way (R67);
- the assessor does not see the picture: only the text read goes to it.

— *Rejected:*
- one call, as the measurement of E4 went (R45 tutor): it merges reading and assessment into one capability, and on the synthetic data it has no fewer false alarms;
- waiting for the volunteers' essays: the item of the card would stay open, and the product's code would have nothing to rest on;
- writing nothing down.

— *Consequence:*
- architecture 3.6 — the item leaves "To decide when detailed", and the assessment by two calls goes to "Does";
- architecture 4.1 — the path of a task with a rubric, and architecture 3.5 — what the learner sees when an essay cannot be read;
- privacy 5.1 — the criteria of the rubric and the text read without the picture;
- `tutor` closes В58 with its move to a tag, and `api` takes the path with its own — RUN.md, Д51.

— architecture 3.5, 3.6, 4.1; privacy 5.1; concepts 9.1, 10; R67, R68, R70, R71.

## The cross-repository plan

**R76. The work of the other repositories is coordinated by the cross-repository plan — the file `COORDINATION.md` at the root of `spec`: the order of repositories 6 and links to the tasks of their RUN.md. The first app is with handwriting, lessons and the engine, at the author's, locally.**
- **The file.** `COORDINATION.md` holds only the order: which task of which repository leads to the first app, after what it goes and what its status is. The tasks themselves are in the RUN.md of their repositories (R19), and a row of the file names them by number, as "T01 `module-kit`". A task that the repository does not have yet the row names by its goal, and the session of that repository writes it down.
  - The file is in Russian, like RUN.md (the 2026-11-01 amendment to R14).
  - It has no registers «В» and «Д» of its own: a question to the author is a row of table 3 of RUN.md, a question of several repositories goes to the registers О-, П- and Т-.
- **The coordinator** is a session of `spec` that the author starts with the phrase «Что дальше по COORDINATION.md?». It reads the RUN.md of the repositories on GitHub, by reading only, marks the done rows and names the next task with the phrase for its session. It does not run the tasks of other repositories and does not change their files (RULES.md, Across repositories). Its rules are in the file's section «Как пользоваться».
- **The order is repositories 6:** first the format and the core — `module-kit` and `modules`, then `learner-model`, `engine` and `sim` —, and only then `api`, `app` and `skill-map`. `tutor` and `canvas` go alongside, as they have gone so far (item 5 of repositories 6).
- **The first app** is the first build of `app` with `api`, on which the author personally solves tasks in the browser:
  - handwriting from the first day. An answer by hand on a sheet of `canvas` is read by `tutor` (R67, R68), and the verdict is given by `module-kit`. `canvas` comes from npm (R37), `tutor` as a library in the process of `api` (R15), and both need a first release;
  - the module is olympiad maths. The first batch is 20–30 tasks of standalone for three bands, without templates and solvers, and the pictures as files of `media/` (R51). The rest of the port of 603 tasks goes after it. The contents of the batch and the bindings of its tasks are decided by `modules`;
  - the module manifest names `adult` in the audience too. The platform offers a module only to learners of its age categories ([format text](../format/README.md), section 11), and an adult tests it;
  - tasks come in lessons (R58): `modules` has the lessons of the first batch, `app` the lesson player. The next lesson or task is chosen by `engine` (architecture 3.8);
  - sign-in at once, by T01 `api`, and the dependencies in RUN.md of `api` do not change;
  - only the author tests, locally, in the devcontainer. The author's work is read by Claude models, and the key lies in an environment variable, as for the review board of `tutor` (R43). There are no children and no deployment: `infra`, П-1, П-3, П-10 and П-11 wait, and the database of `api` lies outside the repository.
- **E3 without the children's parts.** The age of digital consent by country and the export format (R09) move to epic E4 «Приватность до первого ребёнка»: the first app does not need them. The admission table for AI (Т-20) stays in E3: without it `tutor` does not call AI for an adult either.
- **`module-kit` is the whole format.** The first release of `module-kit` with code passes all test vectors of the format 0.2, the Starlark predicates, templates and solvers too ([format text](../format/README.md), section 1). There are no departures from the format, and the rest of the port waits for nothing from `module-kit`.
- **CI of `modules` before `sim`.** By repositories 6, the first releases of `modules` come out earlier than the simulator:
  - until the first tag of `sim` there is no graph gate in CI of `modules`, and the first tag of `sim` runs the graphs already published;
  - the eval runner of `tutor` comes into CI of `modules` from stage 2 (R24);
  - how a release of `modules` gets the index of the previous release, from which the new one is built (R63), is Т-35.

- **The format 0.2 first.** T48 goes first of the open tasks of `spec`. Each repository then moves to a tag of the line 0.6 once, as the first task of its turn. With the same move it fixes the tasks that became outdated: T01 and T02 `module-kit` narrow (RUN.md, Д40 and Д44), and T02 and T04 `skill-map` go away — О-18 was decided by R49, Т-26 was closed by R37.

## The check of a release's signature

**R77. The signature of a NovaTrail release file is checked by one recipe of `spec`, `release-verify`, where the file enters NovaTrail, and it checks everything the certificate names: who signed, by whose call, on what branch and from what commit. A file of a shared release is signed by the shared `release.yml` of `.github` at the SHA of its release no lower than v0.1.7, on the history of its `main`, and a file of `spec` is bound to its tag by its content. The library `module-kit` does not check signatures: it trusts a package by the chain of digests from a pinned index. Т-27 is closed.** The author's answers in the planning of T37 (RUN.md), 2026-11-01.
- **A file of a shared release** is a release file of any NovaTrail repository except `spec`, with the tag T. The check passes only if everything matches:
  - the bundle `<file>.sigstore.json` is a Sigstore v0.3 bundle with one Fulcio certificate. The signature matches the bytes of the file, the certificate the Fulcio chain, and the transparency log entry and the timestamp the Sigstore root of trust;
  - the issuer, Issuer (`1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.8`), is `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`;
  - who signed. The SAN and the Build Signer URI (`…1.9`) are `https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/.github/workflows/release.yml@<S>`, where S is the SHA of a commit, 40 characters, and the Build Signer Digest (`…1.10`) is the same S. S is the commit of a tag `v*` of `.github` no lower than v0.1.7, and it lies on the history of `main` of `.github`. "No lower than v0.1.7" is checked by history, not by the name of the tag: the commit of the release v0.1.7, 0acbf75, lies on the history of S. A branch or a tag instead of a SHA does not pass;
  - by whose call. The Source Repository URI (`…1.12`) is `https://github.com/altnovatrail/<repository>`, and the Source Repository Owner URI (`…1.16`) is `https://github.com/altnovatrail`. The Source Repository Identifier (`…1.15`) and the Owner Identifier (`…1.17`) are the numeric IDs of this repository and of the organization `altnovatrail`, 344507087. The Build Config URI (`…1.18`) is `https://github.com/altnovatrail/<repository>/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`;
  - on what branch and where. The Source Repository Ref (`…1.14`) is `refs/heads/main`, the Runner Environment (`…1.11`) is `github-hosted`;
  - from what commit. The Source Repository Digest (`…1.13`) and the Build Config Digest (`…1.19`) are the commit of the tag T of the same repository. The shared release signs only the commit of its run (R18 .github), so this is also the commit from which the files are built.

  Not checked are the Build Trigger (`…1.20`) — a release lawfully goes both by `workflow_run` and by the button, `workflow_dispatch` —, the Run Invocation URI (`…1.21`) and the Source Repository Visibility At Signing (`…1.22`): they say nothing about trust. Nor are the deprecated fields `…1.1`–`…1.6` checked: Fulcio still issues them, but has declared them deprecated.
- **A file of `spec`** is signed by the own `release.yml` of `spec` (R64). The same is checked, except the caller and the commit:
  - the SAN, the Build Signer URI and the Build Config URI are `https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`;
  - the Source Repository URI, the Source Repository Owner URI and both IDs are `spec`; the branch and the environment are the same.

  The Build Signer Digest, the Source Repository Digest and the Build Config Digest are not checked: they name the tip of `main` at the start of the run.

  The Source Repository Digest names the tip of `main` at the start of the run, and `spec` also releases a commit that is no longer the tip (the second 2026-10-29 amendment to R37). So the file is bound to the tag T by its content:
  - `format-<version>.tar.gz` — the commit that `git archive` writes into the archive's header, and `git get-tar-commit-id` reads, is the commit of the tag T;
  - `altnovatrail-spec-<version>.tgz` — the `version` in its `package.json` is T without `v`.

  A new kind of file of `spec` names its binding in the task that introduces it.
- **The list of releases of `.github`** the check reads from GitHub at the moment of the check, through git, without the REST API and without a token: the tags `v*` by `git ls-remote`, the history of `main` from the same repository. A new release of `.github` is good at once, without a release of `spec` and without a move of the consumers to a tag.
- **The minimum is v0.1.7:**
  - from v0.1.6 on, the shared release requires the caller's submodule `spec` to stand on a tag, and checks the sum of the script of `spec` (the 2026-10-22 amendment to R18 .github, T25 .github);
  - from v0.1.7 on, the recipes of `spec` run in a copy of the checkout, and their containers do not change the `.git` that the runner reads (the amendments to R10 and R18 .github, T28 .github; В24 `.github`).

  Releases below the minimum do not pass. `module-kit` `v0.1.0`, signed by v0.1.4, the rule rejects: nobody takes its CLI template, and the first release of `module-kit` with code will come out on a shared release no lower than the minimum. Only an amendment to this entry can raise the minimum. It names what to do with the files already released that the new minimum cuts off, and with the cumulative index of `modules`, whose previous index is signed below the new minimum (R63).
- **The condition of the check** is immutable releases and a ruleset of the tags `v*` with the rules `update`, `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`, without bypass. They are needed at `.github`, at `spec` and at each releasing repository: a repository turns them on before its first release (R31; R04 .github; architecture 3.3 .github).
  - Checked 2026-11-01 by the GitHub API. `immutable-releases` is `enabled: true` at `.github`, `spec` and `module-kit`, and their rulesets are 25452244, 25426896 and 25559103. All releases of `.github`, v0.1.0–v0.1.11, are immutable, and the tags v0.1.4–v0.1.11 lie on the history of its `main`.
  - The check does not read these settings: it is a standing condition, like the ruleset in R31, and it is checked by the task that changes the settings.
  - The ruleset does not restrict the creation of tags. A tag of `.github` on a commit outside `main` the rule rejects by the history of `main`. A tag of the caller, set by hand on an already released commit, carries the same signature of the same bytes. That only the release sets tags is held by R31 and R04 .github, not by a setting.
- **The check trusts the tags of `spec` too** (Т-27, added to 2026-10-22; В23 `.github`). The SHA of the release of `.github` does not pin all the code that ran with the right to sign: the script `spec/tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` comes from the caller's submodule, on a tag of `spec`, which the shared release checks since v0.1.6. The script is NovaTrail's code on an immutable tag, and it is pinned by the caller's commit — the Source Repository Digest —, like an action by SHA. The condition is immutable releases and a ruleset of the tags of `spec`, and it is met since T20 (R31).
- **Where it is checked** — where the file enters NovaTrail. From then on it is held by the digest that whoever checked pinned:
  - CI of `modules` and `canvas` — the CLI binary of `module-kit` from the release, by exact tag and before the first run, not `go install` (R25; В7 `module-kit`);
  - CI of `tutor` — the archive of the synthetic data of `canvas` (R38);
  - `app` and `canvas` — npm packages, in CI of the pull request that changes the version in the lock file. The archive from the registry is checked against the bundle of the release file with the same name — these are the same bytes (R37) —, and the `integrity` of the lock file against the checked bytes. From then on the version is held by `integrity`;
  - the release of `modules` — the index of the previous release, before the new one is built (R63), in the step that gets it (Т-35);
  - CI of the pull request of `api` that pins a release of `modules` and its index — this index. The pull request is the anchor of trust, and from then on trust goes by the chain of digests: index → inventory → parts → files (R62, R63);
  - code not in Go that takes the format as the file `format-<version>.tar.gz` (the 2026-10-28 amendment to R21) — on download;
  - the rollout of `infra` — the rule and the recipe for the release files it installs. What the rollout checks and with what is decided by `infra` together with Т-19.
- **One implementation** — the recipe `release-verify`, written by RUN.md, T52. Everyone takes it by the tag of the submodule `spec/`, like `release-version` (R31). With what the recipe checks a bundle — cosign or sigstore-js — is decided by T52.
- **`module-kit`** does not check signatures: its library does not go to the network (architecture 3.7). It checks a package by the chain of digests from the index that the pull request of `api` pinned (the 2026-11-01 amendment to R17).
- **The rerun path of the shared `release.yml`** checks the SAN by this same rule: only `@<SHA>` of a release of `.github` no lower than the minimum, without branches and tags. It is fixed by `.github` in a task of its own (RUN.md, Д54).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-01 in planning T37 — eight, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T37, «Решено автором»). The rest is the plan's proposal, which the author approved. The certificates were read 2026-11-01 from the bundles of the files of the releases `module-kit` `v0.1.0` and `spec` v0.5.5.
- **Both — the recommendation of Т-27.** The shared workflow is public. The SAN alone would let through a signature of someone else's call, and the caller's details alone a signature not of the shared workflow. The SAN names `job_workflow_ref`, and the caller's workflow is named by the Build Config URI ([Fulcio, OIDC usage](https://github.com/sigstore/fulcio/blob/a699382/docs/oidc.md) and [OID information](https://github.com/sigstore/fulcio/blob/a699382/docs/oid-info.md), commit a699382, read 2026-10-20). For `module-kit` `v0.1.0`, the bundle `module-kit_v0.1.0_linux_amd64.sigstore.json`:
  - the SAN and the Build Signer URI — `https://github.com/altnovatrail/.github/.github/workflows/release.yml@11435dbe61d3d4885c9a8dd30686e8111e26cabb`, that is, the release v0.1.4;
  - the Build Config URI — `https://github.com/altnovatrail/module-kit/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/main`;
  - the Source Repository Digest and the Build Config Digest — 7e0144a, the tag's commit;
  - the Source Repository Ref — `refs/heads/main`, the Source Repository Identifier — 1425817249, the Owner Identifier — 344507087, the Runner Environment — `github-hosted`, the Build Trigger — `workflow_run`.

  For `spec` v0.5.5 the SAN, the Build Signer URI and the Build Config URI are its `release.yml` on `refs/heads/main`, and the Source Repository Identifier is 1424771727.
- **The caller's branch and file.** The trial #33 of `.github` on a pull request signed files, and its entry lies in Rekor in the open: the SAN — `…/release.yml@refs/pull/33/merge`, the Build Config URI — the trial workflow, the Build Trigger — `pull_request` (architecture 4 .github). The rule rejects a signature of a run not on `main` or not from the caller's `release.yml`.
- **Its own parsing of the certificate.** cosign's flags `--certificate-github-workflow-*` compare deprecated fields: `--certificate-github-workflow-sha` — `1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.3`, and `--certificate-github-workflow-ref` — `…1.6` ([cosign v3.1.4, `pkg/cosign/certextensions.go`](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign/blob/v3.1.4/pkg/cosign/certextensions.go), read 2026-11-01). And Fulcio writes: "GitHub Workflow specific OID extensions have been deprecated in favor of provider generic extensions starting from 1.3.6.1.4.1.57264.1.8" ([OID information](https://github.com/sigstore/fulcio/blob/a699382/docs/oid-info.md), read 2026-11-01). The Build Config URI and the numeric IDs cannot be compared by flags at all. So they are compared by a parsing of the certificate — the one checked together with the bundle.
- **Numeric IDs.** A repository's address changes with a renaming, and its ID does not: the ID also tells apart a repository created anew under the former name.
- **The release's SHA, not the tag.** The caller pins the shared workflow by SHA (R04 .github), and the SAN ends in `@<sha>`. Any SHA would let through a commit of `.github` that did not come out as a release. A list from GitHub at the moment of the check does not require a release of `spec` for each release of `.github`, and Dependabot raises the pin in the callers by itself.
- **The history of `main`, not the release flag.** Through git the list is read without a token and without the REST API's limit: "The primary rate limit for unauthenticated requests is 60 requests per hour", and it is counted by the address the request came from ([GitHub Docs, Rate limits for the REST API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api), read 2026-11-01). And the flag of an immutable release would not close the gap of tag creation: a release on a commit of a branch without review is immutable too.
- **The minimum.** Т-27 allowed the checker not to compare the submodule itself, since the shared release compares it (added 2026-10-22). But only the shared release from v0.1.6 does so, and the runner's `.git` is protected from containers only from v0.1.7.
- **The content of a `spec` file.** The attestation of an immutable release links the bytes with the release, not with the commit: a release created by hand may carry the real bytes of another version. And it needs `gh` with a token, and tokens do not go into the container of the stage `toolchain` (R18 .github).
- **A recipe of `spec`, not of `module-kit`.** A CLI will not check its own binary before it runs, and `canvas`, `tutor` and `app` would install `module-kit` for the sake of one check. A signature also in the library would be a second implementation, and the two would diverge (В19 `canvas`). And `api` does not need the signature at work: the anchor of trust is the pull request that pins the index (R63).
- **Now, by `v0.1.0`.** The signature of a release of `module-kit` with code is built the same way: the same shared `release.yml`, the same fields. The rule and the recipe come out before the repositories move to line 0.6, and each takes them by the same single move (R76).

— *Rejected:*
- the SAN only; the caller only — the options of Т-27;
- cosign's flags only, without the Build Config URI and the numeric IDs;
- a list of the releases of `.github` in a file of `spec`: each release of `.github` would wait for a release of `spec` and for the consumers' move;
- the immutability of a release of `.github` by the REST API at each check, alone or together with the history of `main`: it needs a token, anonymous requests have a limit, and it does not close the gap of tag creation;
- any release of `.github`, without a minimum;
- the attestation of a GitHub release for `spec`'s files;
- a signature also in the library `module-kit`; a command of the CLI `module-kit`; a check of its own at each consumer;
- waiting for the first release of `module-kit` with code, as R76 put it: the recipe would come out after `modules` moved to line 0.6, and a second move would be needed.

— *Consequence:*
- amendments to R17, R37, R63, R64, R73 and R76;
- architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.6, 3.7, 3.10, 3.11 and 3.12; repositories 8 — Т-27 is closed, an addition to Т-35; [the format text](../format/README.md), sections 25 and 26;
- COORDINATION.md — rows 1.1, 1.3, 2.2, 3.3 and 3.6;

— *Amendment 2026-11-01:* the recipe `release-verify` is written (RUN.md, T52). The author's answers in planning T52 decide what R77 left to it — all by the plan's recommendations; the rest is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **The tool is sigstore-js** in `tools/`, by exact versions: `@sigstore/verify` 4.1.2, `@sigstore/bundle` 5.0.0, `@sigstore/tuf` 5.0.0 and `@sigstore/protobuf-specs` 0.5.2. To the other repositories the packages come with `tools/` of the submodule `spec/`, and Node 24.21.0, which they need (`engines` — `^24.15.0`), is in the stage `toolchain` of all thirteen. The recipe reads the certificate's fields from `identity.oids`, which `Verifier.verify` returns for a certificate checked together with the bundle. The licenses — Apache-2.0, MIT, and BlueOak-1.0.0 of `minimatch` — are in the list of R12, and there are no exceptions. Rejected — cosign in the stage `toolchain` of each repository: an edit of every Dockerfile with a sum for each architecture, its own parsing of DER for the fields, and `--trusted-root` for tests without the network.
- **The timestamp** — at least one RFC 3161 timestamp: by default the check also counts the time of the Rekor entry as a timestamp, and R77 names the timestamp separately. The rest is by Sigstore's default: the certificate's chain to Fulcio and its SCT, a Rekor entry with an inclusion proof, each timestamp and the signature of the bytes, at least one of each.
- **The root of trust** the recipe reads by TUF from `https://tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev` on each run, into a new cache, from the root that comes with `@sigstore/tuf`. If the network or Sigstore does not answer, the file is rejected: the recipe has neither a former cache nor a copy of the root.
- **Numeric IDs** — the table `tools/release/repositories.mjs`: the organization and thirteen repositories, by `gh api` 2026-11-01. A new repository is entered in it by the task of `spec` that sets it up (repositories 2.2). Rejected: reading from GitHub at the check — a repository created anew under the former name would return its new ID, and without a token the REST API gives 60 requests an hour; the ID as an argument — each consumer would have a copy of its own.
- **Git.** The recipe calls git without the caller's `GIT_*` variables, without its global and system settings, and in an empty folder of its own. Otherwise `insteadOf` would divert the address, and the checkout's `.git/config` carries a token in `http.extraheader`. From the output of `ls-remote` only references with the exact name are taken: the pattern is matched against the end of the name, and a branch `x/refs/tags/v1` would pass for a tag. An annotated tag is unwrapped by the pattern `^{}`. The history of `main` of `.github` is a clone without trees, `--filter=tree:0`, and a commit that is not in it is not fetched (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`).
- **Arguments.** `just release-verify <repository> <tag> <file> [<bundle>]`: the bundle by default is `<file>.sigstore.json`, and paths are from the caller's folder. The npm mode is `just release-verify-npm <lock-file>`, the whole lock file of version 2 or 3. Each package `@altnovatrail/*`, under its own name or under an alias, is taken by `resolved` — the registry's address for this version; any other is rejected. The recipe takes the bundle from the release of the package's repository by its tag and checks the archive as the file `altnovatrail-<repository>-<version>.tgz`, and then `integrity` by the checked bytes. A link to a folder, `link`, is never a release file: the recipe names it and skips it. Rejected — a package per call: a new package is easy to miss.
- **The tests** run without the network, on real files with their bundles — `spec` v0.5.6 and `LICENSE` of `module-kit` v0.1.0 — and on a copy of the root of trust. The check compares the validity periods of the certificates and keys with the bundle's timestamps, not with today, and the copy does not age. There is no bundle of the shared release v0.1.7 or newer yet. So acceptance is checked on `module-kit` v0.1.0 with a minimum that the test sets, and a real bundle will come into the tests by Д55.

Sources, read 2026-11-01: the npm registry — the packages' versions, licenses and `engines`; the source code of `@sigstore/verify` 4.1.2 (`dist/verifier.js`, `dist/key/index.js`) and of `@sigstore/tuf` 5.0.0 (`dist/index.js`, `dist/client.js`). — RUN.md, T52, Д55; repositories 2.2; architecture 3.12.

## Interface icons

**R78. The icons of the UI packages are one set of the Iconify catalog, Material Symbols, in the style Rounded: outlined, and what is selected — filled. Each UI package takes the set's package `@iconify-json/material-symbols` itself, by exact version, and builds in at build time only its own icons: the device does not call the Iconify API. Which icon has which value is said by the table of architecture 6.** The author's answers in planning T47 (RUN.md), 2026-11-02.
- **The set** — Material Symbols, the prefix `material-symbols`, the author Google, the license Apache-2.0 from the list of R12. The set is one, without a fallback. A button for a value that the set lacks holds by its caption alone until an amendment to this entry names an icon; a second set also comes only by an amendment. So it is now with the protractor (architecture 1 canvas): it is in none of the four candidates of T47.
- **The style** — Rounded. A button's icon is the outline, `<base>-outline-rounded`. The selected option of a choice — "Pen" or "Eraser" — and a mode turned on are the same icon with a fill, `<base>-rounded`. The fill does not replace the state: a screen reader is still told it by ARIA — `aria-checked` on "Pen" and "Eraser", `aria-expanded` on "Demo" (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R36; R42 canvas). For line icons — arrows, "Undo" — the outline and the fill are the same.
- **How the icons get into the build:**
  - the set's package `@iconify-json/material-symbols` a UI package takes by exact version. In a package that comes out in npm — `canvas` and `skill-map` — it stands in `devDependencies`: the consumer does not need the set's data, since the icons are already built in. In `app` — where the answer to Т-36 says. Dependabot and the license check see the set as any dependency;
  - each package raises its version of the set itself, and a new version may draw an icon differently. So that one value looks the same on one screen, `app` keeps the same version of the set as the versions of `canvas` and `skill-map` in its lock file have; how it compares this is decided by its T01 (RUN.md, Д61);
  - the build builds in only the icons that the package takes. By what — the package decides: by a plugin of its bundler, for example unplugin-icons, or by a script on `@iconify/utils` if there is no bundler, as with `canvas`, which only `tsc` builds (R12 canvas). The package does not turn on unplugin-icons' auto-install of sets, `autoInstall`: the set comes from the lock file, not by an import;
  - at run time — not one request to `api.iconify.design` or to another Iconify API. Iconify's components that go there for icons — `@iconify/react`, `iconify-icon` and the like — the packages do not take.
- **The license.** The check of the lock file by `spec`'s list (R39) reads the license of the set's package — `Apache-2.0`, from the list. The set's icons go into the build even when the set's package stands in `devDependencies`. So no exception is written for it in `licenses-check-repo`, not even under `dev`: the boundary `dev` of the 2026-10-22 amendment to R39 is for tools that never ship anywhere (R12). If a new version of the set changes the license to one not from the list, the check will reject it, while an exception under `dev` the check would let through: this rule is held by review, not by code. What is built in from `devDependencies` in general is decided by Т-36.
- **The notice:**
  - Apache-2.0 requires giving the recipient a copy of the license: "You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License" ([the set's LICENSE](https://github.com/google/material-design-icons/blob/10ecc14/LICENSE), section 4(a)), as in R46. It is carried by the `LICENSE` of the NovaTrail package itself: it is the same text of Apache-2.0 (R20). The set has no `NOTICE` file, so there are no notices from it to carry, and there is no copyright line of Google in the license text either;
  - beyond that, the package names the set in its `NOTICE`: Material Symbols, Google, Apache-2.0, the address `google/material-design-icons` and the version of the set's package. The packages `@iconify-json/*` have neither `LICENSE` nor `NOTICE`, and without this line one cannot learn from the build where the icons come from. `NOTICE` goes into the package's npm archive, and in `app` into its build, together with the notices of everything else built into it.
- **Accessibility:**
  - an icon's SVG is with `aria-hidden="true"` and without `<title>`. The button's name is the caption from the package's table of captions (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R36): if the caption beside the icon is visible, it is the button's text; if only the icon is visible, the caption goes into `aria-label`;
  - an icon's color is `currentColor`: in forced colors mode it takes the system color of the button (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R36);
  - whether the caption beside an icon is visible is decided by the accessibility standard of T07 of `app` (О-24), and the translations of captions go by its shared scheme (О-2). Until then a button's caption is visible.
- **The table of values** — architecture 6:
  - one value is one icon, and one icon is one value, like a term in concepts 15. Buttons with one value in different packages look the same, and an icon from the table does not stand on a button with another value;
  - the first rows are the buttons of the row of `canvas` (`src/element/labels.ts` of `canvas`, `main` e90e210): the task screen of `app` shows them. "Next" will be taken by the lesson player of `app` too (R42 canvas);
  - a value that a second package needs enters the table as a row «в реестр spec» (RULES.md, Across repositories). An icon for a value that only it has a package chooses from the set itself — not from those in the table — and records it in its `docs/architecture.md`. If it already stands at another package for another value, both values enter the table by the same route;
  - an icon whose direction goes along the line — "Next", "Undo", the hidden "Demo" — is mirrored in a right-to-left line. Which icons are so, the table says.
- **What the entry does not concern:** the pictures of content — these are the module's media files, and their rule is the module format; the icons of widgets — a widget is foreign code in the iframe sandbox (architecture 3.4).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-02 in planning T47: the set and the style — by their look in the catalog, the rest — by the plan's recommendations. The line in `NOTICE`, the visible caption until the standard of T07 of `app`, and the rule of direction are the plan's proposal, which the author approved. All read 2026-11-02.
- **The author's request of 2026-10-28.** The set is shared: otherwise one button would look different in `app` and in the canvas, and each package would decide the license and the way of delivery itself.
- **No requests at run time.** "Iconify icon components do not bundle icon data. They load only data for icons used on currently viewed page at run time", "Component requests data for icons from Iconify API", and among the drawbacks — "Requires access to Iconify API, making it unusable for offline applications" ([Iconify, Icons on Demand](https://iconify.design/docs/icon-components/)). A request from the learner's device would give its IP address to a third party that is not in architecture 3.12, and an IP address is personal information under COPPA ([16 CFR 312.2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/312.2); privacy 10). The UI packages themselves are not loaded at run time either (R16).
- **Building in without the network.** "Not using any frameworks, but want to automate the build process? Iconify Utils offers easy to use functions that generate SVG", and "All icons in Iconify packages pass very strict validation, so they do not contain any potentially harmful content, such as scripts and external resources" ([Iconify, SVG](https://iconify.design/docs/usage/svg/)). unplugin-icons has "On-demand - Only bundle the icons you really use, while having all the options", and the auto-install is "Option C: Auto Install (Experimental)", by default `autoInstall: false` ([README](https://github.com/unplugin/unplugin-icons/blob/v24.0.0/README.md), tag v24.0.0). The licenses of unplugin-icons 24.0.0 and `@iconify/utils` 3.1.7 are MIT (the npm registry).
- **The set and its license.** `@iconify-json/material-symbols` 1.2.97 of 2026-10-28 has `license` — `Apache-2.0`, and `info.json` names 15,761 icons, the author — Google — and the license. There are nine files in the package, and neither `LICENSE` nor `NOTICE` is among them (the npm registry and jsDelivr). `google/material-design-icons`, commit 10ecc14, has at its root a `LICENSE` with Apache-2.0 and no `NOTICE`, and the README says: "We have made these icons available for you to incorporate into your products under the Apache License Version 2.0" and "We'd love attribution in your app's *about* screen, but it's not required".
- **Coverage.** The set has icons for the canvas tools (architecture 1 canvas) — the pen `ink-pen`, the eraser `ink-eraser`, the ruler `straighten`, the calculator `calculate`, the keyboard `keyboard`, the microphone `mic` — and for all the buttons of the row of `canvas`, each in all six styles. A protractor is in no candidate — neither in Material Symbols nor in Lucide, Tabler and Phosphor. The catalog's search finds this tool only in small sets: iconoven, iconmind, matita and energy-icons (`api.iconify.design/search?query=protractor`).
- **Each package — itself.** The set's package gives data, not code, and a copy of its own in each package ties nothing. A shared package of icons would require a new repository, and a new icon its release and the consumers' move to a version. The table in `spec` gives the same unity without this.
- **The set's package, not copies of SVG.** Its version is raised by Dependabot, and its license compared by the check of the lock file; neither of them sees copies of SVG.

— *Rejected:*
- Lucide (ISC), Tabler (MIT) and Phosphor (MIT) — the other candidates of T47; the choice is by look;
- the styles Outlined and Sharp; always the outline; always the fill;
- a main set with a fallback;
- Iconify's components and its API at run time, including an instance of the API of our own;
- SVG copied into the package's repository together with the set's license;
- a shared package `@altnovatrail/icons` — a new repository, an amendment to R18 and a release of its own;
- an export `./icons` in `@altnovatrail/spec`: the package would stop carrying declarations alone (R73), and a new icon would wait for a release of `spec` and for the packages' move to a tag;
- only the set and the rules, without the table of values: the packages would draw one button with different icons;
- a guard in the code of `licenses-check-repo` that would reject an exception for `@iconify-json/*`: it would close one set of icons, and the general case would stay without a record. It is now Т-36.

— *Consequence:*
- architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.12 and 6; concepts 15 — "icon" and "icon set"; repositories 8 — Т-36;
- RUN.md — T47 and Д61. `canvas` by its move to a tag puts icons on the buttons of the row and revisits the "badges" in R28 and R33 canvas, `app` chooses in T01 what to build icons in with, and `skill-map` takes the set with its first code.

— architecture 3.1–3.3, 3.12, 6; concepts 15; repositories 8; RUN.md, T47, Д61; О-2, О-24, Т-36.
