## The template's kind `typescript`

**R79. The template's kind `typescript` carries a stage with a browser for tests and the Biome extension. A copy of this kind gets, at the end of the stage `toolchain`, Chrome Headless Shell from the Playwright image by tag and digest and its system libraries from a snapshot of Ubuntu, and in VS Code the extension `biomejs.biome` and Biome as the default TypeScript formatter.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В4 (RUN.md of `app`, commit 0849269), by its recommendation. Д17 is closed.
- **How it is built:**
  - a kind in `repo-template/kinds.json` is an object with three keys: `extensions` — VS Code extensions, `settings` — VS Code settings, `toolchain` — a file in `repo-template/kinds/` whose lines go at the end of the stage `toolchain` of the Dockerfile, before the heading of the stage `devcontainer` and its `FROM`. The recipe stops at a key it does not know, at a value of the wrong type, at a file outside `kinds/`, at a setting that `spec`'s devcontainer already has, and at a place in `spec`'s devcontainer that it did not find exactly once (repositories 2.2). A kind written as a list of extensions, as before this entry, the recipe still reads: `just new-repo` builds a copy from the template of the latest tag, and at `v0.6.2` the kind is still a list;
  - the kind `typescript` has `biomejs.biome@3.8.1`, the setting `"[typescript]": { "editor.defaultFormatter": "biomejs.biome" }` and the file `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`. The kinds `go` and `docs` have no stage, and `go` still has the Go extension;
  - the file's lines are the same as R13 canvas on `main` of `canvas` e90e210: Chrome Headless Shell of revision 1248 from `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble` by digest `sha256:7852dc5a7d72f5fe458a597d690f6c42fbc8e9e26ddfa95f8e6ef552558d9bbf`, `ENV PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright`, 24 `apt` packages — Chromium's libraries for Ubuntu 24.04 and fonts — from the snapshot `20261021T000000Z` (R40). The image's version is the same as `playwright` in `canvas` and in the plan of `app`: 1.64.1 (architecture 3.1 app). The stage of a copy of the kind `typescript` matches the stage of `canvas` line for line, and only the comments differ;
  - the decisions the file cites are `spec`'s decisions, and the recipe adds the suffix to them, as to the whole Dockerfile: `(R79 spec)`, `(R40 spec)`.
- **Who raises the versions.** `spec` raises the image, the revision and the snapshot in the template, and a copy gets them by its move to a tag. Dependabot does not see them: the image stands in `COPY --from`, not in a `FROM` line (R13 canvas). A repository that needs a new `playwright` sooner raises all three in its Dockerfile — in the pull request that raises the package, as R13 canvas does — and writes a row «в реестр spec». Until its move to a tag with the new template, its Dockerfile is no longer the recipe's output, and its decision names this.
- **The browser's terms.** Chrome Headless Shell is a build of Google Chrome for Testing under Google's free terms. This entry is the decision that brings it into a copy of the kind `typescript`, and so names it an exception within the two bounds of the 2026-10-22 amendment to R12: NovaTrail does not distribute the browser — the stage `toolchain` is built on each run and is published nowhere — and the platform is built, run and deployed without it. A repository of the kind `typescript` names it, citing this entry (Д16).
- **The default formatter** is the executor's proposal. The formatter setting exists in `canvas` and in the plan of `app` ("the stage `devcontainer` — the extension `biomejs.biome` and the default TypeScript formatter", architecture 3.1 app). Without it in the template, each repository would again add it by hand.

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-11-02, by the recommendation of `app` in В4. Д17 said to return "when a second repository on TypeScript takes up tests in the browser". `app` is the second: its screens with the element `<novatrail-canvas>` run in Chromium (R03 app), and the canvas element does not work in DOM emulators. Without a shared stage the same lines — the image, the revision, 24 `apt` packages and the snapshot — would live in two copies, and each move to a tag would carry the recipe's edits into the Dockerfile by hand: in `canvas` it is already so (R13 canvas). Biome was chosen by both repositories on TypeScript that have a decision on the linter: `canvas` (R12 canvas) and `app` (R03 app). The extension's version is the latest stable, 3.8.1 of 2026-10-24: `canvas` has 3.7.1, and `app` in its plan 3.8.1. Later versions in the gallery are pre-releases, with numbers of the form `2026.10.241124` (the VS Code Marketplace gallery API, `extensionquery` for `biomejs.biome`, read 2026-11-02). The image's digest was compared with the registry 2026-11-02: `https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/playwright/manifests/sha256:7852dc5a…` answers with an image index. Microsoft has since re-published the tag `v1.64.1-noble` itself, and it now points to the index `sha256:2f05f8a7…`. The template takes the digest of `canvas`: its CI has already built this stage.

— *Cost:* the stage with the browser also goes to a copy that does not test in a browser. The step "Toolchain image" of `canvas` took 57–67 seconds in each of five jobs, and without the browser 18 (R13 canvas). All the required checks of such a copy also depend on MCR and on `snapshot.ubuntu.com`. `skill-map` gets Biome before its decision on the linter, as Д17 warned. If it chooses another linter, its decision will remove the extension and the setting and name this a difference from the recipe.

— *Rejected:*
- each repository keeps its own copy of the stage, like `canvas` (option (b) of В4): two copies and two raises by hand;
- only the Biome extension, and the stage when a third repository takes up the browser (option (c) of В4): Д17 waited for the second;
- a shared image with the browser for all repositories: it would have to be published, and NovaTrail does not publish an image with Chrome for Testing (the 2026-10-22 amendment to R12; Д17);
- the image by the new digest of the tag `v1.64.1-noble`: a copy's stage would diverge from the stage of `canvas` that its CI built, while the Playwright version and the browser's revision are the same in both indexes.

— *Consequence:*
- `repo-template/kinds.json`, `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile` and the recipe `new-repo` — `tools/new-repo/devcontainer.mjs`, its functions `readKind` and `editDevcontainer`, with tests in `just new-repo-test`; repositories 2.2, the template's README and the list of what is raised by hand, in `.github/dependabot.yml`;
- `canvas` and `app` take the stage from the recipe by their move to a tag, and the Dockerfile of `canvas` becomes the recipe's output again: R13 canvas then says that the lines came from the template. `skill-map` gets the stage and Biome by the same route, at its move to a tag (RUN.md, Д63).

— repositories 2.2; `repo-template/`; RUN.md, Д17, Д63; R12, R40; R13 canvas, R03 app.

Verified 2026-11-11: `https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/playwright/manifests/v1.65.0-noble` answers with an image index with `Docker-Content-Digest` `sha256:9beb5460…`; `packages/playwright-core/browsers.json` at the tag v1.65.0 names for `chromium-headless-shell` `"revision": "1254"`; the list `chromium` for `ubuntu24.04-x64` in `packages/playwright-core/src/server/registry/nativeDeps.ts` at the tags v1.64.1 and v1.65.0 is one and the same, 21 packages. — *Why:* without this each copy of the kind `typescript` keeps Dependabot's pull request for `playwright` 1.65.0 red until it raises the image itself: Dependabot reads only `FROM` lines, and this image is not in such a line. — *Rejected:* waiting until `spec` itself or another copy needs a new `playwright` (option (b) of В8): `canvas` and `app` have the same kind and the same Dependabot. — *Consequence:* `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`; `canvas`, `app` and `skill-map` take it by their move to a tag, and `skill-map` drops its difference (Д9 skill-map).

## The learner model on the server

**R80. The learner model lives in the platform's database — the database of `api`. What is stored is an append-only log of evidence, and it is the source of truth, while the skills' state is a cache marked with the version of `learner-model` and the release of `modules`. The engine choice also stores the release of `modules` and the number of the log's last evidence by which it was made. П-7 and Т-22 are closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В4 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` d563af3), by its recommendation: to close both questions now. What `api` decided is R06 api, the details are architecture 3.2 api.
- **Where the model lives** — in the database of `api` (П-7). Several devices and several learners of the account and a subscription work with it, and the engine computes on the server, as Т-10 recommends. The export is in an open format (R09); its format is decided by epic E4 (R76).
- **What is stored** (Т-22):
  - evidence — one per finished attempt (concepts 11); an attempt of a task with a rubric gives none in the first slice (О-17). What is in it and how much it weighs is decided by `learner-model` (architecture 3.8), and `api` stores it as it is;
  - the log is only appended to. The recomputation cuts off evidence on a version that the index marked `wrong_key` (R63), and the rows remain. The log is deleted only whole — with the profile or by the time limit (П-9);
  - the skills' state is a cache marked with the version of `learner-model` and the release of `modules`. It is recomputed from the log when one of them changes or a version is withdrawn because of `wrong_key`. New evidence is appended to the cache without recomputing the whole log.
- **The condition for `learner-model`** is one: the state appended by new evidence matches the one recomputed from the log. If it does not match, the cache is recomputed whole. If T04 of `learner-model` decides otherwise, Т-22 returns.
- **The engine choice** stores what architecture 1 names, and also the release of `modules` and the number of the log's last evidence. Without them a repetition from the log does not know which prefix of the log to take and which withdrawal marks were in force then.

— *Why:* the author's answer by the recommendation of `api`; the recommendations of П-7 and Т-22 are the same. A change of algorithm recomputes the state from the log rather than carrying over the old one. The engine choice is repeated from the log (architecture 1), and by it too the model is recomputed without the evidence of `wrong_key` (R63). The cache is needed so that the engine choice after each attempt does not recompute the whole log.

— *Rejected:*
- a family's file — for example, in Google Drive, as in standalone. There the file was the truth, but writes went without a condition — "Whoever uploads last wins, silently" — and an emptied Drive trash erased a profile without a copy (`05-storage.md` of standalone, by architecture 4 api);
- the device: the engine computes on the server (Т-10), and each device would have a model of its own;
- closing only П-7, and Т-22 after T04 of `learner-model`: the condition for `learner-model` is one, and with another decision of T04 the question returns anyway.

— privacy 4, 9; architecture 1; repositories 8; RUN.md, Д67; R06 api.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **the boundary of the transfer of progress between `api` and `learner-model`.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В8 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` c0b4dc5), by its recommendation, with a refinement about the anchor skill. `api` cuts off the evidence of `wrong_key` and gives the profile's log and the graphs of the current versions of the log's modules with `retired_skills`, in the types of `learner-model` (R28), and `learner-model` does the transfer (R08 api). To the appending condition of T04 of `learner-model` the conditions of the transfer are added (architecture 3.8):
- a module's skill that is neither in `skills` nor in `retired_skills` of the current version goes to no skill, without an error;
- an anchor skill `core.<name>` goes as it is if the vocabulary of some format version in the window of `api` knows it, and otherwise to no skill; the trap's skills, if the evidence carries them, go by the same rules;
- in the cache there is only what the log, the graphs of the log's modules and the version of `learner-model` set. The starting point of skills without evidence and the mastery of an anchor skill by the learner's module skills `learner-model` computes on reading, without writing to the cache;
- evidence carries everything the recomputation reads — the task's band and difficulty, the number of options, the key's provenance, the trap's skills — and the recomputation opens no packages of former versions: with a change of the window they leave the image (R07 api);
- a snapshot of the state, if there is one, is valid only under the same mark of the cache, and the transfer does not apply to it.
- *Rejected:* leaving the boundary to T04 of `learner-model`, with `api` adjusting, — `api` builds the log and the graphs earlier, in its own tasks, and without a boundary the recomputation might need packages of former versions that are no longer in the image; `api` does the transfer, translating the IDs in the evidence, — the skills' IDs are part of the evidence type, and the type is set by `learner-model`, while `api` stores it as it is (above).

— architecture 3.5 and 3.8; RUN.md, Д70.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **an attempt that the learner left or abandoned gives no evidence if there were no wrong answers in it.** This is the second exception from "one per finished attempt", beside an attempt of a task with a rubric (О-17). With wrong answers its outcome is "left unfinished" (R82; concepts 11). The attempt itself remains a row with a close reason, and an adult sees it in the progress (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R06 api). — R82; RUN.md, Д73.

— *Third amendment 2026-11-02:* **an attempt of a lesson that the end of its run "not suitable" closed is, for evidence, like a left one:** with wrong answers its outcome is "left unfinished", without them there is no evidence. A run ends "not suitable" when the lesson or its task stopped suiting the profile, and its open attempt is closed with the same reason (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R10 api; R13 api). Not "unchecked": if `learner-model` gave it zero weight, the wrong answers before the end of the lesson would be lost — the same argument as for leaving (R82). Whether the weight needs the fact "a segment of a lesson" — the attempt knows its run and the segment place — is decided by `learner-model` (architecture 3.8). The author's answer to the addendum of T12 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В11 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` d896943), by its recommendation. — concepts 11 and 15; architecture 3.8; RUN.md, Д83.

— *Fourth amendment 2026-11-02:* **the mark of the state cache is also the window of format versions of `api`: the version of `learner-model`, the pinned release of `modules` and the window. The cache is recomputed when any of the three changes or a version is withdrawn because of `wrong_key`.** The window moves even with the same release of `modules` — with a new version of `api` —, and the current versions of the log's modules, their graphs and the transfer by `retired_skills` depend on the release and the window (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R80 above; R07 api; the 2026-11-02 amendment to R06 api). Without the window the mark would not change, while the graphs under it would, and the appended state would silently diverge from the recomputed one. The author's answer to the addendum of T03 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В4, which came as the row В20 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` 916b2d5), by its recommendation. The time of the choice from the same row is already recorded in architecture 1 (Д82, Д83). Rejected: the window is a detailing of `api`, and R80 names the mark without it, — R80 would diverge from its own first amendment, where an anchor skill goes by the vocabulary of a format version in the window of `api`. — repositories 8, Т-22; RUN.md, Д89.

## The inbox of `spec`

**R81. The session of `spec` finds the rows «в реестр spec» of the other repositories itself: before each task the recipe `just inbox` reads on GitHub the tables 3 of their RUN.md and compares them with table 5 of the RUN.md of `spec` — which rows are already recorded and where. A row counts as arrived when it is on `main` of its repository, while the rows of open pull requests are "on the way", and they are recorded only on the author's word. There is no new channel, and the author no longer carries rows.** The author's decision of 2026-11-02 in planning T66 (RUN.md), both answers by the plan's recommendations.
- **How it works.**
  - A repository's session writes a row as it did — into table 3 of its RUN.md — and its question opens with the mark «В реестр spec» (RULES.md, Across repositories). The recipe recognizes the mark regardless of case and only at the start of the question: the same words further in the text are not the mark.
  - `just inbox` reads through `gh` the RUN.md of each repository from `tools/release/repositories.mjs` except `spec`: on the commit of `main` and in each open pull request. It prints three lists: new rows on `main`; "on the way" — rows that a pull request adds to its base; rows of table 5 that the source no longer carries — they may leave it.
  - The session of `spec` triages the new rows before the task by rule 13 of RUN.md: what the author has already decided it records, and the rest it brings to the author with options and a recommendation. A recorded row goes into table 5.
  - The answer reaches the repository, as before, with its move to a tag (the «Д» rows of table 4).
  - What is not a question needs no route of its own: what a repository took by a move to a tag is seen by its submodule (rule 3 of COORDINATION.md), and its tasks by its RUN.md.
- **The first run**, 2026-11-02. 12 repositories were read: 40 rows on `main`, 0 on the way. 29 of them had been recorded, and they went into table 5 — by the «Д» rows and the start of table 3. There were 11 new: `api` В6–В9, `app` В11–В16, `canvas` В58. While the task ran, one more came to `main` of `.github`, В35, and the next run found it. The errors of the trials that the recipe no longer makes:
  - without the condition "at the start of the question" it took the row `module-kit` В1 — a question about the order of its tasks, where «в реестр spec» stands in the recommendation;
  - without comparison with the pull request's base — 38 rows from old branches of Dependabot, recorded long ago. The base is the common ancestor of the branch with `main`, not the pull request's `base.sha`: otherwise an old branch would bring back rows that `main` has closed since;
  - a row recorded from a pull request on the author's word it does not name as gone while the pull request is open; a failure of one repository or pull request does not stop the run, and it reads the lists page by page.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-02 in planning T66. The rows already lie in the tables 3 of the other repositories (RULES.md, Across repositories), and the coordinator already reads their RUN.md on GitHub (R76): all that was missing was that the session of `spec` read them itself. Nothing changes for the other repositories — neither rule 4 nor the order of their move to a tag — and the recipe works at once, on any tag of theirs. The record is one, in the repository's file, as the rule "Project context lives in the repository's files" requires. A row on `main` the author has already reviewed, while before the merge it may change, so the rows of pull requests are only "on the way".

— *Rejected:*
- issues in `spec` that the sessions of other repositories open: the rule would reach them only with a move to a tag, the row's text would live in two places, rule 4 would need an exception, and issues are public. The inbox would be only the issues of the author's account, and the author's answer by that account cannot be told apart from a session's record;
- Discussions in `spec`: the same, and the `gh` commands for them in version 2.101 are in preview, and a pull request does not close a discussion;
- messages between sessions of Claude Code: two sessions are needed at once, a message is not kept and does not get into files, and an exchange between different devcontainers is not verified. On 2026-11-02 `ListAgents` did not see other sessions;
- an inbox file in `spec` that the other repositories add to by pull requests: a session would change `spec` not from within it (RULES.md, Across repositories);
- only `main`, without the rows of pull requests: the author would wait for the merge where the answer can be prepared earlier, as with the `.github` rows В32 and В33 (Д64);
- `main` and pull requests on an equal footing: a row recorded from a branch could diverge from the one that gets merged.

— *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/` and the recipes `just inbox` and `just inbox-test`; rule 13 and table 5 of RUN.md; rule 3 of COORDINATION.md; RULES.md, Across repositories; the template of RUN.md, `repo-template/files/RUN.md`; CLAUDE.md, Environment; repositories 5. The edit of RULES.md reaches the other repositories with their move to a tag, but the recipe does not wait for it.

— RUN.md, T66; R19, R76.

— *Amendment 2026-11-04:* **table 5 keeps a fingerprint of the rows it names, and `just inbox` also prints the rows of table 5 whose rows on `main` of the source have changed since.** The author's answer of 2026-11-04 to the question В28 of RUN.md, by its recommendation. The recipe compared rows only by their numbers and did not see additions to recorded ones: so the addenda of T12 and T13 of `api` to its В3, В4, В11 and В14 and the edit of `modules` В3 in its T08 went through, and only the third inbox triage of 2026-11-02 found them, by reading the rows whole.
- **The fingerprint** is the first 12 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the rows of the source's table 3 in the order of their numbers: a row's cells, each with its whitespace collapsed, joined by " | ", and the rows joined by a line break (`fingerprintOf` in `tools/inbox/inbox.mjs`). An edit of any word of a row — the question, the options, the recommendation — changes it, while the row's place in the file and Markdown marks do not. The fingerprint is one per row of table 5, not per number: a row of table 5 names several rows of the source, and the column stays short.
- **What the recipe prints** — a row of table 5 at least one of whose rows is on `main` while their fingerprint is not the one recorded, or is not recorded at all, "—", — with the new fingerprint and the place of the rows at the source. The session rereads them, records what was added as a new row, and puts the fingerprint into table 5 (rule 13 of RUN.md). When some of the rows have left the source, the fingerprint of the remaining ones is different too, and the recipe names the row both among the changed and among the gone. A changed row is not an error, and the recipe ends with code 0; a fingerprint that is not 12 hexadecimal digits is an error of table 5, like an unread row. The rows "on the way" have no fingerprint: they go into table 5 only on the author's word.
- **The first fingerprints** were taken 2026-11-04 from `main` of the sources. Since the commits at which `spec` recorded the rows, `api` В15, В16 and В18, `module-kit` В15, and `modules` В3 and В12 have changed, and the same day they were compared: there are no new requests to `spec` in them.

— *Rejected:* a rule in RULES.md and in the template of RUN.md that an addition to a recorded row goes as a new row with its own number — it would be held by hand in twelve repositories, while the recipe sees the edit itself; changing nothing — the triage would reread each recorded row whole at each run.

— *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/` and its tests; rule 13, «Как устроен план» and table 5 of RUN.md; CLAUDE.md, Environment.

It reads the working tree, not GitHub.** The author's decision of 2026-11-12 in planning T126: the recipe runs before every task anyway. — *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/due.mjs`, `main.mjs` and tests; rule 13 of RUN.md. — R145; RUN.md, T126.

## Showing the solution and a hint on request

**R82. The solution is shown by a button: to a learner of the category `adult` from the start of the attempt, to a child from the fourth wrong answer, when the hint ladder has been passed, and with the adult's setting "ask before showing", on by default, by an adult action. Showing closes the attempt with the outcome "solution shown". The request "Hint" before the first wrong answer gives "givens and unknown" and the task's technique, after it the words of the current rung once more, without AI, and "explain differently" gives the same rung in other words, one AI call per rung, without the work. An attempt that the learner left or abandoned gives, with wrong answers, the outcome "left unfinished". О-7 and О-21 are closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `api` В10 and В11 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` d409351), by their recommendations, with the triage's refinements about the facts of evidence. What `api` decided is R09 and R10 api, the details are architecture 3.5 api.
- **The ladder** (concepts 10):
  - a wrong answer is a submission in which at least one answer slot got "not yet". "Unreadable" and "unchecked" give no rung: this is not the learner's mistake (R04);
  - the k-th wrong answer gives rung k while k is no more than three. From the fourth there is no new rung, and the AI is not called for new words: to a child the program offers to call an adult or to show the solution, to an adult learner to show the solution. "Call an adult" is the interface of `app`: `api` notifies no one (architecture 7);
  - the rung's answer slot is the first "not yet" slot in order in the submission that gave the rung: items by place, slots by order in the item. The program chooses it (R03), and the rung's words, "explain differently" and the fallback text speak of it (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R57). From the fourth wrong answer the slot stays the one rung 3 speaks of;
  - the ladder is per task, not per item. So on a page of a workbook four submissions with a mistake offer to show the solution of the whole page.
- **Showing the solution** (О-7):
  - a child is a learner of any age category except `adult` (concepts 13). To them showing is only from the fourth wrong answer, whatever kind of action the request came by;
  - the setting "ask before showing" belongs to the child's profile, is on by default, and an adult changes it. When on, showing goes by an adult action, behind the PIN of the section for adults, and a learning request for showing `api` rejects with the reason "an adult is needed". When off, showing becomes a learning action. The server tells apart kinds of actions, not people (R04 api), so the refusal is not a security boundary but one place where the setting is enforced for all the account's devices;
  - a learner of the category `adult` shows the solution from the start of the attempt, and has no setting;
  - showing closes the attempt with the outcome "solution shown". Showing adds no trap of its own — this is what "without a trap" in the recommendation of О-7 means — while the traps that the program found earlier the evidence carries (below);
  - the key and the task's solution go to the device only when the attempt is closed by a correct answer or by showing the solution. An attempt that was left, an abandoned one and one closed "unchecked" do not give the key (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R05).
- **A hint on request** (О-21). The request sends no work (R69), and the rung grows only with wrong answers (R03):
  - before the first wrong answer — "givens and unknown" and the task's technique, without AI (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R57). "Givens and unknown" `app` shows from the task's open view, and the technique is given by `api`;
  - after a wrong answer — once more the words of the current rung, which the attempt keeps, without AI; if there are none, the rung's fallback text;
  - "explain differently" — the same rung in other words: one AI call per rung, within the quota. The model gets the same as for the rung's words (architecture 4.1), except the work. Words that did not come or did not pass the leak check and the form check (R70) are replaced by the rung's fallback text. In the mode without AI (О-5) "differently" is not offered;
  - each call for the attempt's words — both of a rung and of "differently" — gets the previous questions of the same task, so as not to repeat them (privacy 4);
  - in the mode "self" the request gives the same: a hint exists in both modes, from the start of the task (concepts 10).
- **Evidence** (concepts 11). The outcome is by wrong answers, and the request and "explain differently" do not change it. The new outcome "left unfinished" is that of an attempt that the learner left by beginning another, or abandoned, when there were wrong answers in it. Without wrong answers such an attempt gives no evidence (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R80). Beyond the outcome, evidence carries:
  - the traps that the program found by the trap values, not the candidate traps of reading (R57);
  - the items correct to the end, with their verdict;
  - the task's technique — at a step or on request;
  - how many times the learner asked "explain differently";
  - whether the solution of this task went to the profile's device earlier — after a correct answer or showing. A task template has no such fact: a new attempt gives new numbers (R60).

  That the learner saw "givens and unknown" is not recorded: they are open, because they do not hint at the way (R57), and in the mode "by steps" `app` shows them at a step without a request to `api`, so the record would mean something other than what it says. The weights of the outcome and of each fact are decided by `learner-model` (architecture 3.8).
- **The engine** does not give again at once a task — not a template — whose solution has already gone to the learner's device: the learner has already seen its key. After how long it can be given again is decided by `engine` (architecture 3.8).

— *Why:* the author's answer by the recommendations of `api`, and they repeat the recommendations of О-7 and О-21. Beyond them:
- the threshold is the fourth wrong answer, as in canvas-api, where the ladder came from: there the analysis went on while there were no more than three wrong answers (R39 canvas-api), and from the fourth came an offer of help (by R09 api). So the child first tries the simpler case of the third rung;
- the setting is on by default: in MathTrail a child did not see the solution before a correct answer at all (R39 canvas-api), and this way an adult sees it first, and can also turn the setting off;
- showing closes the attempt: an answer after the shown solution would check nothing, and "solution shown" is an unsolved task, like the answer "I don't know" in standalone (R93 standalone, by R09 api);
- "differently" — once per rung and without the work: so beyond the rungs' words there are no more than three calls per attempt, and of what is kept privacy 4 lets only the previous questions go to the AI;
- the outcome "left unfinished" is not "not solved": that is what О-7 calls "solution shown", and one term means one thing. Leaving without wrong answers does not move the model, like skipping in R98 standalone, where punishing a skip would punish an accidental tap;
- the triage's refinements. The technique in evidence — at a step or on request: for the sake of this distinction the contract `app` ↔ `api` keeps two requests (RUN.md, «Что `app` нужно от контракта в E3»). The learner sees the solution after a correct answer too (concepts 6), so the fact about it is both after a correct answer and after showing. "Givens and unknown" are not recorded, as was also decided the same day by the `app` row В12.

— *Rejected:*
- never showing the solution to a child, as R39 canvas-api, and "skipped, the rating does not change", as in the prototype: О-7 does not recommend them;
- offering the showing already from the third rung: the child would skip the simpler case;
- showing without closing the attempt: the key would be on the device while the attempt is open (R05);
- every request raises the rung, as in the author's analysis (О-21): the learner would reach the solution without trying themselves (R03);
- "explain differently" without a limit and with the work of the last submission: the account's quota would go on presses, and the work would have to be kept on the device and sent once more;
- closing only О-7, and О-21 after a measurement of "differently" in `tutor`: the measurement is an eval of the hint of `tutor`, not a condition of the decision;
- a left and an abandoned attempt with the outcome "unchecked", as the attempts of R07 api: if `learner-model` gives "unchecked" zero weight, the incorrect answers before leaving would be lost to the model;
- leaving without incorrect answers is "left unfinished" too: R98 standalone rejected the same;
- recording that the learner saw the "givens and unknown", or that they asked for a hint before the first incorrect answer: the first is wrong in the "by steps" mode, and the second has no reader until `learner-model` asks for it.

— *Consequence:* О-7 and О-21 are closed (product 13); the 2026-11-02 amendments to R05, R57 and R80; concepts 6, 10, 11 and 15; architecture 3.5, 3.8 and 4.1; privacy 1 and 4; [the format text](../format/README.md), section 19 — by an editorial change: it changes no modules, verdicts, open view, leak or numbers; RUN.md, «Что `app` нужно от контракта в E3» and T62. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д73.

— product 13; concepts 10 and 11; architecture 3.5, 3.8 and 4.1; privacy 4; RUN.md, Д73; R09 and R10 api.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **beyond the facts above, the evidence carries for each item whether it was submitted, the reasons for its submissions without a verdict, the first verdict and the number of incorrect answers before the submission that gave it, the verdict at the end and the number of incorrect answers before the first "correct"; items correct to the end, too. Beyond them, everything the model reads; the evidence does not carry the lesson's segment.** What is in the evidence is decided by `learner-model` (R80), and it decided: these are facts of the attempt, not conclusions of the model. A conclusion "the item is blank" or "not solved" would be read by only one version of the weight rule, while submissions, verdicts and the number of incorrect answers will be read by the next one too (R08 learner-model). Without the first verdicts the model would not tell a page where nine items of ten are correct from the first submission from a page where all are correct only after hints (R06 learner-model). The verdicts of the slots and of the item, the traps and the number of incorrect answers are stored by the attempt of `api` anyway (architecture 3.2 api), so there are no new data of the learner. The series that weighs less than the sum is all the items of one attempt, not only those of one type (concepts 11; R06 learner-model). The lesson's segment does not change the weights, and it has no reader (R06, R08 learner-model). What else the evidence carries, in which form and by which operations `api` builds it, is architecture 3.8. The author's answer to the rows «в реестр spec» `learner-model` В9 and В16 (RUN.md of `learner-model`, `main` d5d17b0), by their recommendations; for В9, "whether the item was submitted" instead of "which items were blank", as R08 learner-model decided. — concepts 11 and 15; architecture 3.8; privacy 4; RUN.md, Д86.

— *Amendment 2026-11-07:* **"again at once" means "not as the next task"** (В8 `engine`; R107). How long until the engine gives again a task whose solution went to the device was decided by `engine`: for 24 hours it is not a candidate, and when the choice gave nothing, a second pass gives it too, after the others, but not the task of the last closed attempt (R03 engine, the 2026-11-07 amendment). — R107; architecture 3.8.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **before the first incorrect answer, "Hint" also gives the task's leading question, when it has one, from format 0.4. The evidence carries that the learner got it, as it carries the technique (R108).** The `modules` row В31 (RUN.md of `modules`, `main` 997e281). The question suggests the way to solve, so it is closed and recorded (R57). How to weigh it is decided by `learner-model` (architecture 3.8). It changes neither the rungs nor the fallback texts. — R108; concepts 10 and 11.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **"as it carries the technique" of the 2026-11-08 amendment above is about the fact being recorded, not about the field: the evidence carries the leading question in its own field of the schema of `learner-model`, separately from the technique on request (R21 learner-model), and `api` writes it only in this field — after the release of `learner-model` that introduces this field, and not earlier.** The row «в реестр spec» `learner-model` В27 (RUN.md of `learner-model`, `main` 763ce10), by the row's recommendation. With the same release the model gets the check kind `time`, a value of `CheckKind` with guessing 0 (R19 learner-model): an item of a kind it does not know it counts as an item without an answer. Both are a change after the baseline, through the gate of `sim` (R103). — *Why:* the log is append-only (R80): a question recorded in the field of the technique before this release would forever mix two facts, and recomputation would no longer separate them. — *Rejected:* a field of the leading question in the contract of `spec`: the evidence is not a contract of `spec` (architecture 3.8); writing the question in the field of the technique before the release of `learner-model`. — R108; concepts 10; architecture 3.8; RUN.md, Д138.

## Contracts: protobuf, buf and Connect

**R83. `spec`'s contracts are proto3 files in `contracts/`, packages `novatrail.<part>.v1`, by buf's rules `STANDARD`, `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC` and with the compatibility `FILE` against the previous release of `spec`. A field's name in JSON is its proto name, snake_case. A contract's version is the package's suffix and the tag of `spec`, and a breaking change is a new package and a new line of `spec`. The code from the contracts is generated by `spec`: in Go, the nested module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts`, in TypeScript, the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`. `app` and `api` talk over Connect.** The author's answers of 2026-11-02 in the planning of T54 (RUN.md), all by the plan's recommendations. The primary sources were read the same day.
- **Layout.**
  - The folder `contracts/` at the root of `spec`, as `format/`. The normative text is `contracts/README.md`, in English, as are the comments in the `.proto` files (R14, R42).
  - A file is `contracts/novatrail/<part>/v1/<name>.proto`, its package `novatrail.<part>.v1`: the path from `contracts/` repeats the package's name, as buf's rule `PACKAGE_DIRECTORY_MATCH` requires. The prefix `novatrail` makes the packages' names unique in the world, and the Go FAQ requires that of every declaration that gets into a Go binary.
  - `buf.yaml` of version 2 is at the root of `spec`, with one module, `contracts`, and without `deps`: buf takes dependencies only from the Buf Schema Registry, and the build must not depend on a service outside the repository.
- **buf's rules.**
  - `buf lint`: the categories `STANDARD`, `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC`, without `except` and with `disallow_comment_ignores: true`, so a comment in a file does not lift a rule. `COMMENTS` requires a comment on every element, as R45 requires a `description` on every property of a schema. `UNARY_RPC` forbids streams: the tutor's words go whole (R54), and there is no real-time channel in the first slice (Т-25). The rule `PROTOVALIDATE` is empty: protovalidate's constraints need the module `buf.validate` from the BSR, and the contracts do not take them.
  - `buf breaking`: the category `FILE`, against the previous release of `spec`; the first release with a package has nothing to compare with. How buf takes the previous release — by a git tag or by a release file checked by `release-verify` (R77) — is decided by T55.
- **Fields.**
  - Names are the terms of concepts 15 in English, in snake_case, and a repeated field is in the plural (protobuf's style).
  - Integer places and crops are `int32` (R53): an `int64` is a string in JSON and a `bigint` in TypeScript. There are no unsigned ones. `int64` is only for a value that can be greater than 2³¹ − 1, the greatest `int32`.
  - An enum's zero value is `<NAME>_UNSPECIFIED`, and it has no meaning. A field and an enum value are not removed from a package (version, below): what is not needed stays, with a comment saying so, and the next major package does not take it.
  - The values and IDs of the module format — `handwriting_sheet`, a task's ID — stay `string`, not a proto enum: otherwise one value would have two spellings.
  - `optional` is on a simple field where "none" and zero differ, as absence in R72. "One of" is `oneof`. PNG is `bytes`, and in JSON it is a base64 string.
  - How the format's open view, a JSON Schema value, goes into protobuf is decided by T64.
- **Names in JSON.** A field's name in JSON is its proto name, snake_case, as in the format (R45).
  - A JSON writer — of a sample file, of a file of `spec`, of the Connect codec — turns on `UseProtoNames` in Go (`protojson`) or `useProtoFieldName` in TypeScript (protobuf-es).
  - The option `json_name` is forbidden in the contracts. A reader accepts both spellings, as ProtoJSON requires.
- **Syntax** is `syntax = "proto3"`, and simple fields where presence matters are `optional`. The Go code is the Open API, the default for proto3. Moving to editions is possible later, by a decision of its own: the wire and JSON do not change by it.
- **Version.**
  - A contract has no MAJOR.MINOR version of its own. The version is the package's suffix, `v1`, and the tag of `spec` in which the file came out. buf's rule `PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX` does not let a package `v0` through.
  - Within a package a change only adds, and `buf breaking` `FILE` holds this. Such a change comes out in any release of the line.
  - A breaking change is a new package, `v2`, beside `v1`. A package `vN` with N from 2, beside `v(N−1)`, opens a new line of `spec`, and `release-version` holds this, as with the format (R44); the code of the check is T55. The first package `v1` of a new part does not open a line.
  - `api` keeps two major packages, the current and the previous, as the window of R44, and `app` reads the package of its build. Within a major package an old build of `app` works with a new `api`: both sides of Connect skip unknown fields. This is the answer to the question of RUN.md, Д20: which versions of the contract `api` and `app` read when the build of `app` is older than the service.
- **The Go code** is the nested module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts`, with its own `go.mod` in `contracts/`.
  - The generated `.pb.go` and `.connect.go` lie in the repository beside their `.proto`. Whether they match what buf generates is checked by T55, as `just types-check` checks the format's types (R72).
  - The module's tag is `contracts/vX.Y.Z`, with the number of the tag of `spec`. The module requires `google.golang.org/protobuf` and `connectrpc.com/connect/v2` at exact versions.
  - The root module of `spec` still requires nothing (R64): with the `go.mod` in `contracts/` that T55 brings, the nested module is not in its zip. Until then `contracts/README.md` lies in the root's zip, as the repository's other texts do.
- **The TypeScript code** is the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`: JavaScript code and declarations, `target=js+dts`, and JSON types, `json_types=true`.
  - Its dependency is `@bufbuild/protobuf` at an exact version.
  - The package comes out as a release file of its own, with a trusted publisher in npm, and a consumer checks it with `release-verify-npm`, as `@altnovatrail/spec` (R73, R77). The path is T57, and setting up the publisher is the author's step.
  - `@altnovatrail/spec` stays declarations only (R73). The mark's type in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` is written by hand, as the element's types are, and `tools/types/canvas.check.ts` compares it with the mark's type of the contract (R74; RUN.md, T62).
- **The transport** `app` ↔ `api` is Connect, and the contract chooses it: the services' stubs are born in `spec`, and the client must match the server.
  - The server is connect-go v2 in `api`, the client connect-es in `app`.
  - Calls are unary only.
  - JSON or binary protobuf on the wire is a choice of the transport, and T07 `api` decides it. A Connect server accepts both, and gRPC and gRPC-Web too.
- **The plugins** of buf are local, at exact versions; there are no remote BSR plugins, whose version may be "latest". How the devcontainer installs them is decided by T55:
  - `protoc-gen-go` and `protoc-gen-connect-go` by the `tool` directive of the Go module in `tools/`;
  - `protoc-gen-es` at an exact version in `tools/package.json`;
  - `buf` itself as an `ARG` of the Dockerfile, with a checksum for each architecture from its release's `sha256.txt` (R34).

  As of 2026-11-02 the newest versions are: buf v1.75.0 (Apache-2.0), `google.golang.org/protobuf` v1.36.12 (BSD-3-Clause), `connectrpc.com/connect/v2` v2.0.2 (Apache-2.0), `@bufbuild/protobuf` and `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` 2.16.0 (Apache-2.0 and BSD-3-Clause), `@connectrpc/connect` 2.3.0 (Apache-2.0). All the licenses are of category A (R12).

— *Why:*
- **One type per process.** `tutor`, `module-kit` and `api` exchange the observation in one process (R15), and it must have one type. The Go FAQ: "When a single .proto file is generated into two or more Go packages and linked into the same Go binary, it conflicts on every Protobuf declaration in the generated Go packages", and "Starting with v1.26.0 of the google.golang.org/protobuf module, a hard error will be reported when a Go program starts up that has multiple conflicting Protobuf names linked into it" (protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq, read 2026-11-02). Code generated at each consumer would not start this binary. `api` too expects the contract "as generated packages from the releases of `spec`" (architecture 1 api).
- **A nested module.** The generated code imports the protobuf runtime (`protoreflect`, `protoimpl`), and the root module of `spec` requires nothing (R64). The nested module's tag: "each tag name must be prefixed with the module subdirectory, followed by a slash" (go.dev/ref/mod, read 2026-11-02). R64 has two arguments against a subfolder: a second kind of tags — its cost is accepted — and a copy of `format/` inside; here nothing needs copying: the `.proto` files lie in the module itself.
- **An npm package of its own.** protobuf-es code takes a runtime too: `import { fileDesc, messageDesc } from "@bufbuild/protobuf/codegenv2"` (`packages/protobuf-example/src/gen/example_pb.ts` @v2.16.0). And `@altnovatrail/spec` is declarations only, without dependencies (R73). connect-es does not work without the descriptors, so types alone are not enough.
- **The rules.** The version suffix: "The last component of a package must be a version of the form v\d+ … where the numeric parts are at least 1" (buf.build/docs/lint/rules, read 2026-11-02). Compatibility: "If you don't know which to pick, start with FILE (the default)", and "you should use FILE to protect all generated languages" (buf.build/docs/breaking/rules, read 2026-11-02): the contracts generate code in two languages.
- **Names in JSON.** "Parsers accept both the lowerCamelCase name (or the one specified by the json_name option) and the original proto field name. This allows for a serializer option to choose to print using the original field name … and have the resulting output still be parsed back by all spec parsers" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json, read 2026-11-02). So a field has one spelling — in the format, in `.proto` and in JSON —, and a sample file is of the same style as the module (RUN.md, Д21).
- **`optional`.** "We recommend adding the optional label for proto3 basic types by default" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/field_presence, read 2026-11-02).
- **Integers.** "ProtoJSON serializers emit int64s as strings to ensure no precision loss will occur on large int64s by any implementation" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json). The fractions 0–1000 and the integer crops (R53) fit in `int32`, and in JSON they are numbers.
- **Connect.** "Connect also offers direct support for the gRPC-Web protocol used by grpc/grpc-web, without relying on a translating proxy like Envoy", and Connect's own protocol "works over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3" (connectrpc.com/docs/introduction, read 2026-11-02). Both sides skip unknown fields: connect-go v2.0.2 — `DiscardUnknown: true, // Ensure difference schema versions unmarshal.` (`connectproto/connectproto.go`), connect-es 2.3.0 — "In connect-es, unknown JSON fields are ignored by default" (`packages/connect/src/protocol/serialization.ts`).

— *Rejected:*
- a folder `proto/`: a name by the technology, not by the role; the contracts inside `format/`: two normative parts with different versions in one folder and one archive;
- `STANDARD` without `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC`, and the soft `BASIC`, `WIRE_JSON` and `PACKAGE`: without a version in the package's name, without `_UNSPECIFIED`, and `WIRE_JSON` does not protect the generated code;
- lowerCamelCase names in JSON, ProtoJSON's default: a field has two spellings; `json_name` on every field: a duplicate of the name, easy to forget;
- Edition 2023 and 2024: 2024 gives the Opaque API in Go by default, while publishers of generated Go code are advised the Hybrid one (go.dev/blog/protobuf-opaque, 16.12.2024), protoc-gen-go v1.36.12 goes no further than 2024, and every generator knows proto3;
- a MAJOR.MINOR version of its own, as the format has: a new line for each task of E3, and STANDARD does not let a package `v0` through; `v1alpha1` until the first app: buf would not catch the renaming of a field, and sample files are kept long;
- the code in the root module of `spec`: it breaks R64 and R72, and every consumer of `spec` in Go would get the protobuf runtime; the code at each consumer: a conflict of the protobuf registry in the binary of `api`; a generator of our own without a runtime, as `tools/types`: our own implementation of ProtoJSON and no Connect stubs, while connect-go requires `proto.Message`;
- the TypeScript code in `@altnovatrail/spec`: it breaks R73; generation at `app` and `canvas`: two generators whose versions may diverge; declarations only: connect-es does not work without descriptors;
- gRPC-Web: the browser needs a proxy, Envoy by default; HTTP of our own with protobuf bodies, as R67 canvas-api: there are no stubs, and the contract does not check the transport; choosing the transport in the detailing of `api`: the stubs are born in `spec`, and the client must match the server.

## Own key

**R84. An own key lies on the device only if the key's owner decided so on this device — in the database of their profile —, and otherwise only in the tab's memory while their profile is open; on the server, only in the request's memory. The key and its provider come with every request of the owner profile that calls AI, and `api` accepts them only with a profile of the category `adult`. The owner profile on an account that has a profile of another category is opened by the same PIN as the section for adults. The providers' terms allow giving the key to `api`. Т-9 and П-17 are closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `app` В20–В23 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 14f5a54): В20–В22 by their recommendations, and В23 not by its recommendation. What `app` and `api` decided is R08 app and R04 api.
- **Where the key lies** (Т-9). On the device, only by the key's owner's mark "Keep on this device", separate for each device: only they know whether the device is shared. Without the mark the key lives in the tab's memory while the owner profile is open. There is no encryption in the browser: whoever holds the device can get at a key saved on the device, and `app` says so plainly, and the damage is held by the key's limit and lifetime at the provider (R55 tutor; concepts 14). On the server, only in the request's memory, not in the database and not in the logs (privacy 5.2). The key is not in the export: the export is the learners' data, and the key is a secret of the key's owner (architecture 4.5).
- **With which request.** With every request of the owner profile that calls AI: with the work for reading, with the rung's words and with "explain differently", which sends no work (R82). `app` names the provider without the key at the start of the attempt (RUN.md, Д66). With a request of a profile of a category other than `adult`, `api` does not accept a key, and checks this itself (R04 api; О-4). A provider's refusal by a limit is the outcome "limit reached" with a cause (R55 tutor), a refusal of the key itself — wrong or revoked — is an outcome of its own, and neither moves the call to platform AI without an action of the key's owner (R08 app).
- **Connecting.** `api` checks the key through `tutor` — it does not go to providers bypassing `tutor` (architecture 3.5) — by a request without the learner's content, on behalf of the owner profile: the key is accepted, wrong, the key has no rights, or the provider is closed for the profile. The providers open to an own key for the profile are named by `api` by the admission function (Т-20), and `app` does not build them in.
- **The owner profile on a shared device** (П-17) is behind the same PIN as the section for adults, at every opening, if the account holds a profile of a category other than `adult`. It closes by itself: by "Switch learner", on reload and after 5 minutes of a hidden page. Without such profiles, without a PIN (R08 app). The PIN is a barrier of the interface, and `api` holds its hash and counter (R04 api).
- **The providers' terms** (В23). They allow giving an own key to `api`: so the author decided, without a lawyer. At Anthropic, API keys of individuals too go by the Commercial Terms, there is no clause about passing a key in them, and the help page directly describes a key in third-party tools: "when you upload your API key to third-party tools … you are giving the developer of that tool access to your Claude Console account". At OpenAI, the Services Agreement is a contract "between the organization agreeing to these terms", §3.1 says "Customer will not share Account access credentials or individual login credentials between multiple users", by §3.3(g) one may not "buy, sell, or transfer API keys from, to, or with a third party", and an End User is also the one "who accesses the Services under Customer’s Account". There is no direct ban on a key in a third-party service in it. The sources and dates are privacy 10.

— *Why:* the author's answer. The providers advise keeping a key on the server: OpenAI, "Don’t share it with others or expose it in any client-side code such as browsers or apps", Anthropic's SDK for the browser, "Any user with access to the browser can potentially inspect, extract, and misuse these credentials" (architecture 4 app; checked 2026-11-02). But there are no own keys on the server (architecture 7), so the key is on the device, by default only in memory, and in the database where an adult learns alone and decided so themselves. The key comes with every AI call: otherwise "explain differently" of the key's owner would go through platform AI, at its quota and under its contracts, not under the terms the key's owner accepted with the provider (privacy 5.1, 5.2). The check at connecting is so that a typo in the key is found on the page where the key is entered, not at the first hint. Both sides decided П-17, while О-4 and П-4 decide who gets an own key, not how it lies on a shared device: a key is only ever on a profile `adult` anyway.

— *Rejected:*
- the key always on the device, as Т-9 recommended: on a shared tablet it would always lie there, against the providers' advice;
- the key on the server, encrypted: the server would hold a secret of every key's owner, and architecture 7 does not allow it;
- the key only with the work, as architecture 3.9 tutor and T07 `api` wrote: "explain differently" of the key's owner would go through platform AI;
- no check of the key: a wrong key would be found at the first call;
- П-17 open until О-4: О-4 decides who gets a key;
- the providers' terms as a question to a lawyer in epic E4 before the code of the own key, as `app` recommended, as a question of its own or an addition to П-4; the own OpenAI key closed until the lawyer answers. The author chose to count the passing as allowed: Anthropic directly describes such a path, and OpenAI does not directly forbid it.

— *Does not decide:* for whom the own key is, О-4 and П-4; the admission table, Т-20 (RUN.md, T61); how `tutor` checks the key.

— *Consequence:* Т-9 and П-17 are closed; privacy 2, 4, 5.2 and 10; architecture 3.1, 3.5, 3.6, 4.3, 4.5, 5 and 7; concepts 14; product 12; RUN.md: «Свой ключ в контракте `app` ↔ `api`» at table 1 and T62–T64. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д78.
