## Observation

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **at the root of the build archive of `app` there are also `NOTICE` and `LICENSE`, beside `index.html`, `assets/`, `deployment.schema.json` and `csp.json`, and there is still no `deployment.json`; the site serves them at `/NOTICE` and `/LICENSE`.** The author's answer of 2026-11-11 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В49 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 77ccf50), option (a): the Vite bundle does not keep the packages' license comments, and without `NOTICE` the archive and the site would distribute the code of React, Firebase, `canvas` and others without the notices that Apache-2.0 §4(d), MIT and ISC require; a copy of the archive taken on its own carries them itself. Nothing changes for the rollout of `infra`: it does not reject extra files and deploys them all (`tools/deploy-check/check.mjs`, `main` 01c4d91 `infra`), and it can check that they are there at its move to a tag (RUN.md, Д208). Rejected: beside the archive in the release: a copy of the archive without them; only on the legal pages of `app`: an archive without them.

**R86. The observation is the contract `novatrail.observation.v1`. For each answer slot whose answer AI reads, it carries the value as written, or why there is no value, and for a slot `anywhere` also the box of the final answer. `module-kit` joins two readings into one, by the slot check, and gives the verdict by the joined observation. The module format does not change by this. The reading request and the analysis response are types of `tutor`, and a change of the contract's meaning is a new package.** The author's answers of 2026-11-02 in the planning of T56 (RUN.md), all by the plan's recommendations. Normatively, [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, and `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto`.
- **What is in the observation.** The message `Observation` is the slots whose answer AI reads, each once, in the task's order. On a handwriting sheet these are the slots `anywhere`, `zone` and `sheet`, on a workbook every box. `tutor` takes the boxes from the open view, and gives an empty one as empty without calling the model: the work holds only the filled ones (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R53). A slot has its place, `{ item, slot }` from 1, and one of two: `value`, as written, or `unreadable`: blank, illegible, ambiguous, no final answer, several final answers. AI does not read a tapped choice, and it is not in the observation: `api` gives `module-kit` the option the learner chose beside the observation.
- **What the reader gives.**
  - A value only if it is visible in the writing itself (R62 canvas-api), and as written: the check kind normalizes it (R56). A vertical fraction is written in a line.
  - "Ambiguous" is a mirrored digit (the 2026-10-29 amendment to R56), a value of which the reader sees another reading, and a value that it cannot show in the writing.
  - The reader knows nothing of the slot check: neither the kind nor the options of a handwritten choice. This is the answer to the question Д37. The answer's form is named by the task statement ([the format text](../format/README.md), section 15), and options among which the key stands would hint at the answer, as the key would (R67).
- **The place** is the answer to "how the observation chooses a place" (R53):
  - for a slot `anywhere`, the box of the final answer on the crop in whole thousandths, `CropBox`, if the reader named it and it is valid;
  - for a zone and a box, the slot itself;
  - a group label only if group boxes go with the work (Т-31).
- **Joining.** Slots with a verdict have two readers (R68), and `tutor` gives the observations of both or a call outcome, never one. `module-kit` joins them slot by slot:
  - values agree when the slot check compares them as equal, as a value with a trap, and gives them one verdict; then the value is that of the pair's first reader. A predicate compares the integers read;
  - equal reasons give the same reason, and everything else gives "ambiguous";
  - a value that the check kind normalizes to empty is joined as "blank", and a joined reason has no box;
  - an invalid observation is as an AI failure: there is no joined one, and every slot that AI reads is "unchecked". A reason that the release of `module-kit` reading the observation does not know is invalid too.

  An essay is read by one reader, and there is nothing to join (the second 2026-11-01 amendment to R68).
- **The verdict** is by the joined observation as a whole (the 2026-10-28 amendment to R54).
  - A value gets the format's verdict, with a reason and a trap ([the format text](../format/README.md), section 15).
  - A reason without a value gives `unreadable` with the reason of its name: `blank`, `illegible`, `ambiguous`, `no_final_answer` or `several_final_answers`. The reason `notation` remains the format's.
- **The call outcomes are not an observation.** An AI failure, a limit, "not admitted" and a refusal of the own key (R84) give the slots that AI reads "unchecked". If one reader failed, there is no observation at all.
- **What `api` stores** is the joined observation and the tapped choice: by them the same release of `module-kit` repeats the verdict (R03). The readers' observations, the writing parts and other readings are not stored, and what is stored for an essay is П-19.
- **The format does not change.** It judges the read value, and what makes a slot "unreadable" before the check kind its text already assigns to the observation. [The format text](../format/README.md), section 15, now refers to the contract: this is an editorial change. So too the rules about a vertical fraction and about a mirrored digit did not change the format's version: they are rules about the reader (the 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29 amendments to R56).
- **The reading request and the analysis response are types of `tutor`.** Only `api` and `tutor` exchange them, and `api` calls its library anyway.
  - The open view in the request is the format's type `open.Task` (R72), and how it goes into protobuf is decided by T64.
  - The analysis gives the box of the first error or nothing, and a trap from the block or nothing. The box is the same message `CropBox`, and in T62 `api` gives it as a mark without conversion.
  - The candidate trap and the place of the first error were put by concepts 9.1 in the observation, but this is the response of the analysis, which sees the key (R67).
- **The version of the meaning.**
  - A new value of a reason or a new field is an addition to `v1`.
  - A change of the meaning of a field, a value or a rule of [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10 — whatever gives another result on the same message — breaks the package: a `v2` and a new line are needed, as with a major change of the format (R44).
  - `buf breaking` does not see this, and review holds it (the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R83).
- **The vectors** of the joining and of the verdict by the observation are a separate task, T68: with the code of `tools/`, T56 would be more than one check (rule 11 of RUN.md).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-02 while T56 was planned, all by the plan's recommendations.
- **The join is `module-kit`'s.** Normalization is its own (R56), and comparing by verdict is possible only with the key. In `tutor`, the reading path would get the slot checks together with the keys, and R67 keeps reading without the key. The join is a rule, not perception, and its place is in the deterministic core (R03). The eval of `tutor` compares the same way: "their values, read as the check of the kind number reads them, and their verdicts are one" (`internal/report/reading.go` of `tutor`, `main` be607e5, read 2026-11-02).
- **Comparing by the check, not by the text.** "0.5" and "1/2" under `number` are one value, and "3 / 4" and "3/4" are one notation: by the text they would go to "unreadable" with no gain. One verdict is needed because the check compares "2/4" and "1/2" equal, while under `form: reduced` their verdicts differ.
- **Without the writing parts and the other readings.** The check needs only the values, and the analysis does not get the observation (architecture 3.10 tutor). With the parts, `api` would keep the learner's writing of the solution whole, "while the profile lives" (architecture 3.2 api), and minimization does not allow this (privacy 1). The other readings are already expressed by the reason "ambiguous" (R34 tutor).
- **The format is not touched.** The type of the observation is described once — in `.proto`, while in the format's vectors it would have to be described by JSON Schema as well. A new format version would require a new line and a move of all the components, though not one module changes.
- **The types of `tutor`.** A contract is needed where a type is shared by two repositories that do not call each other: the observation goes from `tutor` to `module-kit` (R83). The reading request and the analysis response go only between `api` and the library of `tutor`, and the place in them is from the contract.
- **A version of the meaning.** The verdict is repeated from the observation kept (R03), and an edit of the join rule would change it on the same messages with no sign in the package.

— *Rejected:*
- format 0.3, where the format's verdict is given from the observation, and the verdict vectors carry the reasons and two readings. That is a new line 0.7, ~140 files of `module_format_version`, new digests of the vectors of packages and indexes, and the type of the observation would be described twice;
- a rule in the format text without a new version: new reasons for "unreadable" are a new value of the list, and in v0 that is the next 0.y;
- the join in `tutor`, as architecture 3.7 tutor proposes: normalization and the key are `module-kit`'s;
- the join by the text after normalization — stricter with no gain;
- the writing parts in the observation, as architecture 3.10 tutor proposes, and the other readings, which architecture 3.2 api wants to keep;
- the reading request and the analysis response in the contract: the open view in protobuf would be decided before T64, and the analysis response before T62;
- the vectors in the same task: with the code of `tools/`, T56 would become two checks;
- an edit of the meaning within `v1`: an old observation in the database would be read by the new rule with no sign of the version.

— *Consequence:*
- [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) — sections 1, 2, 7 and the new section 10;
- `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto` and buf's code: the module `contracts` carries a Go package for the first time, and the recipes `ci-` check it;
- [format text](../format/README.md), section 15, — an editorial change: a link to the contract;
- the 2026-11-02 amendments to R53, R56 and R68 and the second amendment of the same day to R83;
- concepts 9.1 and 15; architecture 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 and 4.1; privacy 4; repositories 5;
- RUN.md — T68, «Вход» of T60 and T62, Д37 and Д81; rows 1.6 and 3.3 of COORDINATION.md;
- the components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д81.

— RUN.md, T56; R03, R15, R44, R53, R54, R56, R67, R68, R75, R83, R84.

— *Amendment 2026-11-03:* **the observation vectors are JSON files `contracts/vectors/observation/v1/<case>.json` without a schema of their own. They hold the task's items, the readers' observations with a validity flag, the taps and the joined observation with verdicts, and for an essay the outcome of the submission. `spec` reads the observations by the descriptors of buf's image and computes the result by a second implementation in `just contracts-check`. `module-kit` takes the vectors as `contracts.Vectors` of the Go module of the contracts. The [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, is refined by an editorial change: where it could be read two ways, the vectors pin one reading.** The author's answers of 2026-11-03 while T68 was planned (RUN.md), all by the plan's recommendations.
- **JSON, not YAML.** An observation in a vector is proto3 JSON with proto names, and with it the whole file. The [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 6, already names "a file of `spec`" as a writer of the contract's JSON. `module-kit` reads a vector through `encoding/json` and `protojson`, without YAML. JSON has none of YAML's type traps: `8.` and `0.5` stay strings. An observation is written as `toJson` with `useProtoFieldName` and `alwaysEmitImplicit` or `protojson` with `UseProtoNames` and `EmitDefaultValues` writes it — with every field, zeros too. A reason that the package does not have is written as a number. Rejected: YAML, like the format's vectors — rules of the format's YAML would be needed, and the observation would have to be rewritten in YAML.
- **No schema of its own.**
  - The type of the observation is described once — in `.proto` (the argument of R86). It is held by a strict `fromJson`, and the writing by a comparison with `toJson`.
  - The canvas and the items are held by the format's schema, `task.schema.json`: `#/properties/canvas` and `#/$defs/item`. The task's rules that are seen by the slot check are held by `slotBreaches` of `format-check`.
  - The keys of the file and of a case are held by the check's code, and the file is described by the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, "Test vectors".
  - Rejected: a JSON Schema of a wrapper in which the observation is just `object`. Under `contracts/` second schemas with their own conventions would appear, and the reference to the format version would have to be raised with each of its versions.
- **`contracts.Vectors`.**
  - The vectors lie in `contracts/`, so they are carried by the Go module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts` at the tag `contracts/vX.Y.Z`. `tools/gomod` already requires every file of `contracts/` in its zip.
  - The package `contracts` at the root of the module — `contracts/vectors.go`, written by hand, — embeds `vectors/` with the directive `//go:embed all:vectors`, like `spec.Format` (R64), and requires nothing beyond the standard library.
  - Its test checks that what is embedded matches the files on disk. It also reads each observation of each vector with `protojson` and compares the writing back: this shows that Go takes the vectors the same way as protobuf-es.
  - Rejected:
    - reading from the submodule `spec/` — it diverges from R64: code takes the files of `spec` from a release;
    - a release file of its own, `observation-vectors-<version>.tar.gz` — the contracts have no version of their own beyond the package ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 2), and a new kind of release file is a new line.
- **The descriptors of buf's image.**
  - The code `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation_pb.js` imports `@bufbuild/protobuf/codegenv2` by a bare name, and from `contracts/`, where there is no `node_modules`, this import does not resolve.
  - So the registry is built from the image of `buf build`, which `contracts-check` builds anyway. For this the image is read with `fromJson(FileDescriptorSetSchema, …, { ignoreUnknownFields: true })`, since the image file has a field of buf beyond `FileDescriptorProto`. The well-known types, which an image without imports omits, are taken from the runtime.
  - The descriptor is the same as the one embedded in the code, and the same recipe compares the code. The check runs in its own process and is part of the coverage.
  - Rejected: running the vectors in a trial project, like `tools/contracts/typescript.mjs`. Then they would wait for the build of the npm package and would run in a child process.
- **What the check computes** — `tools/contracts/observation.mjs`:
  - the validity of an observation by the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10. An invalid observation of a vector breaks one condition, so that it is seen which;
  - the join. Values join by the new `readingOf` of `tools/format-check/verdicts.mjs`: it gives "blank", the normal form outside the notation, or what the check compares by, with the verdict. It is separate from `comparableOf`: a value outside the notation may, after normalization, match its notation's writing, as `1/100000000000000` matches `0.00000000000001`;
  - the verdicts of the slots and of the item and the outcome of an essay. The verdict of a predicate on a value in the notation is taken from the vector, as with the format's verdict vectors (R56), while the join of predicates is computed in full: a predicate compares integers;
  - that the vectors together give each reason of the table of the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, in a joined observation, each check kind, an invalid observation and a tap. A reason that is not in the table the check refuses until a task adds it.
- **The refinements of the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, are an editorial change.** Each says what the text already implied, and the vectors hold it to one reading until `module-kit` has come out with the join; later an edit would be a new meaning and `v2` ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 2):
  - an extra slot — `choice` or a place that the task does not have — makes the observation invalid: "and no other";
  - white space is the Unicode property White_Space of the raw value, as in step 4 of the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15: U+0085 is white space, U+FEFF is not;
  - a value that the kind normalizes to empty is `UNREADABLE_BLANK` even before the join: with `UNREADABLE_BLANK` and with such a value it gives `UNREADABLE_BLANK`, and with a value or another reason — `UNREADABLE_AMBIGUOUS`;
  - "the same once normalized" is steps 1–7 for a number, with units, and a choice's normal form in lowercase. So `7²` and `7³` join: both are 7 and U+FFFD;
  - an invalid observation does not touch the taps: a slot `choice` gets the verdict of the option, and the item is made of all its slots.
- **Found in planning.**
  - `fromJson` refuses an unknown field and an unknown name of a reason, but accepts `answerSlot` in lowerCamelCase. So the proto names are held by the comparison with `toJson`.
  - `{"value": "x", "unreadable": null}` protobuf-es refuses, while Go accepts. The comparison with the writing does not let such a vector through.
  - The format's verdict vectors `module-kit` reads with Go types generated from the schemas (R72). The observation vectors have no schema, so `module-kit` writes its own structure: the items in `formatv0`, the observations through `protojson`. The module `contracts` cannot give this type: it would require the module `spec`, and `go-check` lets in only protobuf and Connect.
- **Not included:** the outcomes of a call are not observations (R84). There is no comparison of the vectors with the previous release: an edit of their meaning is still held by review (the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R83), since a byte-for-byte comparison would not let through even a new format version that changes the form of an item.

— *Consequence:* [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) — sections 3, 7, 8 and 10; the amendments of the same day to R64 and R83; concepts 15; architecture 3.7; repositories 5; README and CLAUDE.md of `spec`; RUN.md — T68 and Д93; row 3.3 of COORDINATION.md. — RUN.md, T68; R56, R64, R72, R83.

## A task with a rubric

**R87. A submission of a task with a rubric ends with feedback, "unreadable" or "unchecked" — not with a verdict, and the attempt is closed by the learner's "Done", and then the task is solved. Of such an attempt the server keeps how each submission ended, and for feedback the mark of each criterion, "met", "not met" or "not assessed", and the source of the words; it keeps neither the text of the essay, nor the justifications, nor the words of the feedback. П-19 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `api` В17 and В19 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` d896943), by their recommendations. What `api` decided is R14 and R15 api, the details are architecture 3.8 api.
- **The submission end** (R75; R14 api):
  - feedback — the assessment returned at least one criterion with a mark;
  - "unreadable" — the sheet is empty or the essay cannot be read as a whole, and it does not reach the assessment;
  - "unchecked" — an AI failure, an exhausted quota, "not admitted", a refusal of the provider by a limit, a refusal of the own key (R84), or an assessment without a single criterion with a mark.

  "Unreadable" and "unchecked" mean the same as the verdicts of the same name: this is not the learner's error (R04). But they stand at the submission, not at the answer slot and the item: an item with a rubric has no verdict (concepts 9.1). The three ends have no common name: "result" in concepts 15 already means both feedback and the end of an attempt. Normative for the observation is the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10.
- **"Unreadable" — only for the essay as a whole.** One illegible word does not send the whole essay to rewriting — the same argument as for the second 2026-11-01 amendment to R68. How a reader gives such a word is Т-37: the reading prompt of `tutor` has not yet measured the outcome "unreadable", and the synthetic data are all legible (architecture 3.5 tutor).
- **Feedback that did not pass** the leak check or the feedback rule (R70) is replaced by the phrase of `app` "no feedback this time", without a repeated call. This is not the neutral phrase of R04: there was an assessment, only the words did not pass. The marks are recorded then. A criterion that is not in the model's answer or that is named twice is "not assessed", and the call is not repeated either: this is the answer to the question that `tutor` left to `api` (architecture 3.5 tutor).
- **"Done"** is a learning action of the learner, after at least one submission, however it ended; before that — the refusal "no submission". Until "Done", the attempt is open for rewriting: the learner edits the same sheet and submits it again, and each submission is again two calls and its own quota (R11 api). "Done" after "unreadable" or "unchecked" is the way out for a learner whose essay cannot be read, and for one whose quota ran out. An attempt closed by "Done" gives no evidence (О-17), and the lesson's segment ends with it (R13 api).
- **The task is solved** when its attempt is closed by "Done" (the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R05). Then its criteria and its solution, if the task has one, are open. The adult sees the marks in the progress, and the learner sees feedback, not an assessment (concepts 9.1). Feedback does not go to the learner model (О-17), and "what to develop" for tasks with a rubric the progress reads from the marks, not from the model (concepts 11).
- **What is kept** — П-19, the second option:
  - for a submission — the time and how it ended;
  - for feedback — the mark of each criterion by its number in the rubric, and the source of the words: the model or the phrase "no feedback";
  - the crop of the sheet, the text read, the justifications and the words of the feedback are neither in the database, nor in the caches, nor in the logs: they live in the memory of the request, and what was read and the feedback also on the device, with the essay (R04 app). The server has no observation of an essay;
  - the text of the essay — only as an artifact at the account owner's choice (П-8).
- **The words of the marks** are "met", "not met", "not assessed", as in R75 and R71, not "yes" and "not yet", as П-19 proposed: "not yet" is a value of a verdict.

— *Why:* the recommendation of П-19 and of `api`. The assessment by criteria is needed by the progress — what to develop (product 3) —, and the text and the words are not. Repeating feedback from the observation is not needed: R03 repeats a verdict, and feedback has none. Otherwise the server would hold the essay without the owner's choice, contrary to П-8 and to the promise of privacy 7. "Done", not the first feedback: rewriting is a part of writing, and a rubric has no showing of the solution, with which an attempt of a task with a key ends. To the adult the marks say what to work on, and the criteria the author can name in the task statement anyway (R56).

— *Rejected:*
- keeping everything, as for any attempt: the text read, the words of the feedback and the assessment; keeping only the fact of the attempt;
- closing the attempt with the first feedback: in a lesson it would then be impossible to rewrite, and feedback lost in the network or that did not pass the rule could not be returned;
- repeating the assessment when the feedback did not pass the rule, and the neutral phrase of R04 instead of "no feedback";
- the rubric's criteria are always closed, and the marks are only in the export: the progress would have nothing to show;
- after "Done", the criteria with marks to the learner: that is an assessment, not feedback.

The arguments — R14 and R15 api.

— *Consequence:*
- privacy 4 and 9: П-19 is closed, П-20 and П-9 are added to;
- concepts 6, 9.1, 9.2, 11 and 15; architecture 3.5, 3.6 and 4.1; [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10; [format text](../format/README.md), section 21, — an editorial change;
- the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R05; the question Т-37;
- RUN.md — T62; the components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д83.

— R04, R05, R56, R68, R70, R71, R75; П-8, П-19, О-17; R11, R13, R14 and R15 api.

## The format's Starlark

**R88. All of the format's Starlark — the predicate of a check, the template expressions and the solver — runs in one dialect: go.starlark.net at version `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d` with the options `syntax.FileOptions` of standalone's solvers, and the built-in names are the 33 names of its `starlark.Universe`, by a list. The steps of the limits of the predicate and of the solver are counted by this version, and the computation stops when the count reaches the limit. The version of go.starlark.net is a part of the format: raising it is a new format version. Text — format 0.3, RUN.md, T69.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `module-kit` В10 and В11 (RUN.md of `module-kit`, `main` 78727cf), by the triage's recommendations: they are the recommendations of `module-kit`, and the triage refined the limit — "the count reaches N" — and gave the built-in names a list. What `module-kit` decided is R11 module-kit.
- **The version** is `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d`, commit 4f4267fb140d of 2026-10-21: on 2026-11-02 it is the latest, and go.starlark.net has no tags (google/starlark-go, read 2026-11-02). It is pinned by `module-kit` and excluded from Dependabot (R11 module-kit). Raising the version is a new format version: while the format is v0, the next 0.y and a new line of `spec` (R44).
- **The step count** of this version is by 10 on entering a function, after each call, on each back edge and after `load` (`starlark/interp.go`, lines 72–78, 289–293, 390–393, 536–540, 614–617 and 696), not by 1 per instruction, as in standalone's version, 89a6a09411d5 (the same file, line 109). The limits are as before: 1,000,000 for the predicate (R56) and 100,000,000 per template for the solver (R61). On standalone's solvers the median ratio of steps, new count / old, is 0.96, the heaviest is 2,725,355 steps against 2,413,617, and an iteration of an empty loop is 10 steps against 6 (the measurement of R11 module-kit, 2026-11-02).
- **The limit** — a thread with `Thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps(1000000)` for the predicate and `Thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps(100000000)` for the solver: the computation stops when the count reaches the limit. This is how go.starlark.net of both versions compares — `thread.Steps >= thread.maxSteps` (`starlark/interp.go`, lines 702–705 at 4f4267fb140d and 109–110 at 89a6a09411d5) —, while "more than 1 000 000" and "at most 100 000 000" of the text of format 0.2 diverge from it by a step.
- **The dialect** is one for all of the format's Starlark: `Set`, `While`, `TopLevelControl` and `GlobalReassign` are on, `Recursion` is off, `load` is forbidden, `print` writes nothing. The predicate and the template expressions run in it too, and for an expression only `Set` and `Recursion` of the options matter. The built-in names are the `starlark.Universe` of this version, 33 names, by a list in the format text: `None`, `True`, `False`, `abs`, `all`, `any`, `bool`, `bytes`, `chr`, `dict`, `dir`, `enumerate`, `fail`, `float`, `getattr`, `hasattr`, `hash`, `int`, `len`, `list`, `max`, `min`, `ord`, `print`, `range`, `repr`, `reversed`, `set`, `sorted`, `str`, `tuple`, `type` and `zip` (`starlark/library.go`, lines 39–73). The rule `task.predicate-expression` names the built-in names of the dialect, not "Starlark's built-in names".
- **The vector** `task.template-solver/past-the-budget-of-the-template` is a loop of 2,000,000 iterations: on this version a call of `solve` takes about 20,000,000 steps, a share of the budget, and 64 instances together go far beyond it. With 10,000,000 iterations one call took 100,000,040 steps, the whole budget, and the vector no longer showed that the budget is the template's (the measurement of R11 module-kit). How many steps a call takes is computed by the CI of `module-kit`: the CI of `spec` has no Starlark.
- **Template expressions.** The format text's "It takes no more steps than it has tokens" is wrong under both counts: the expression `a` has one token but two instructions, a load and `RETURN`, and under the new count any expression takes 10 steps on entering a function. The conclusion stays: an expression calls no functions and holds no loops, its steps are bounded by its length, and it has no step limit (R60).
- **The clock and concurrency** are still not the format: the clock is `module-kit`'s, and how many computations run at once `module-kit` leaves to the caller (architecture 3.5 and 3.7; R11 module-kit). The format text will say this by an editorial change.

Normative — format 0.3: [format text](../format/README.md), sections 2, 15, 23 and 24, the rule `task.predicate-expression` and the vector `past-the-budget-of-the-template` — RUN.md, T69. Until it comes out, the format is 0.2, and `module-kit` pins the same version of go.starlark.net (R11 module-kit).

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-11-02 by the triage's recommendations on the rows В10 and В11; the primary sources were read the same day.
- The format's limits are set "as go.starlark.net counts them", and the count changed on 2026-10-05, pull request #663, commit de228787c8fb: "We only need to increment the step counter and check for cancellation in loops (back edges) and calls" and "Clients may need to adjust their SetMaxSteps parameter to taste. (Let us know if you think our scale factor is way off.)". Without a version, two implementations of the format would diverge on one module, and a template near the boundary of the budget would pass in one and get a refusal in the other. So the version is a part of the format: the step limit and the dialect are a major edit ([format text](../format/README.md), section 2).
- The latest version, not standalone's: on standalone's solvers, by which the budget was calibrated (R61), there is almost no difference, for predicates the new count is no more expensive — a simple predicate is 20 steps against 19 —, and the panic of `set([1]).difference()` is fixed in it (#672, commit 4f4267fb140d). R56 chose the predicate's limit by judgement, not by a measurement: "an expression of one number does not need 25,000,000 steps".
- One dialect: for an expression it coincides with the Starlark specification that the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15, refers to. In it `set` is a built-in function, and "It is a dynamic error for a function to call itself or another function value with the same declaration" (bazelbuild/starlark, commit c0af0ea03d, `spec.md`, lines 3595 and 1419, read 2026-11-02). With `Recursion: false`, go.starlark.net catches recursion through `lambda` too: "We look for the same function code, not function value, otherwise the user could defeat the check by writing the Y combinator" (`starlark/interp.go`, lines 37–45). With `Recursion: true` the depth is bounded too — 100,000 frames (#619, the same file, lines 25–34) —, but the README promises of it only "enough in most cases": recursion turned off is an argument of one dialect and of the specification, not of a single protection of the stack.
- The list of names: the format text's "Starlark's built-in names" is the bazelbuild specification, which has no `chr` and `ord`, while go.starlark.net has "The `chr` and `ord` built-in functions are supported" (`doc/spec.md`, line 4349). The list of `Universe` with them needs no filter in `module-kit`, and standalone's solvers ran with these names. None of the 33 names brings in randomness or reads the clock (R03).
- The limit "reaches": this is how go.starlark.net itself stops a thread, and `module-kit` passes it the format's number as it is.

— *Rejected:*
- standalone's version, 89a6a09411d5, by an editorial change in 0.2 — the budget and the vector are calibrated on its count: the format would pin an old interpreter with the panic of the methods of `set`, and raising it would become a new format version anyway;
- a version without a name, like the Unicode version of normalization ([format text](../format/README.md), section 15): there the vectors hold characters that all versions since 15.0 normalize the same way, while steps have no such common core — an iteration of a loop costs 6 steps on one version and 10 on another;
- describing the step count in words of the format text: it is set by the bytecode of the compiler of go.starlark.net, and the text would repeat `internal/compile/compile.go`;
- zero options for the predicate: two dialects for one format, and the predicate would not know `set`, which the specification calls built-in;
- the built-in names of the specification, without `chr` and `ord`: a filter in `module-kit` for the sake of two harmless names;
- the limit "more than N", as in the text of format 0.2: `module-kit` would set `N + 1`, and a second implementation would be off by a step.

— *Consequence:*
- format 0.3 — RUN.md, T69: [format text](../format/README.md), sections 2, 15, 23 and 24, the rule `task.predicate-expression`, the vector `past-the-budget-of-the-template`; the 2026-11-02 amendments to R44, R56, R60 and R61;
- architecture 3.5 and 3.7; the memory of third-party Starlark from stage 4 — an addition to О-9 and architecture 3.13 (В12 `module-kit`);
- the components get the answer with their move to a tag of line 0.7 — RUN.md, Д85.

— R03, R44, R56, R60, R61; R11 module-kit; RUN.md, T43, T69, Д43, Д85.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **the components get the answer with their move to a tag of line 0.8, not 0.7: line 0.7 was opened by T57** (the third 2026-11-02 amendment to R44). — RUN.md, Д85.

— *Amendment 2026-11-04:* **format 0.3 came out in line 0.9, not 0.8: line 0.8 was opened by T61** (the 2026-11-04 amendment to R44), **and the components get the answer with their move to a tag of line 0.9.** Text — [format text](../format/README.md), sections 15, 23 and 24: the version of go.starlark.net is the same, `v0.0.0-20261021141710-4f4267fb140d`, on 2026-11-04 it is still the latest, without tags (google/starlark-go, the GitHub API, read 2026-11-04). The text does not repeat the count in words, but says by an example that the versions count differently. The predicate runs on its own thread with `Thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps(1000000)`, and the names that an expression binds itself — the variable of a list comprehension — do not hinder the rule `task.predicate-expression`. The vectors at the boundary are the measurement of T69 on this version (R101). — R101; RUN.md, T69, Д85, Д107.

## Versions of a module

**R89. The rules of the version comparison of a module are in the module format, from version 0.3. The version part is found by the comparison of the new version with each version published below it by semver, the withdrawn ones too, and the author may raise it higher but not lower. Major — when something of what the learner of the previous version had is gone or means something else; in 0.y.z the major is played by y. A new meaning of an entry is a new ID. Seven comparison rules and the index rule `module-index.version-above` refuse a new version, and the comparison vectors are a new kind, `vectors/versions/`, which `spec` computes by a second implementation. The places of the package that the comparison reads, the format holds in all versions, and `diff` compares across a move of the format too. Text — format 0.3, RUN.md, T69.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `module-kit` В14 and В15 (RUN.md of `module-kit`, `main` 78727cf), by their recommendations. What `module-kit` decided is R13 module-kit, the details are architecture 3.5 module-kit.
- **The version parts:**
  - major — an entry with a full ID is removed — a skill, a task, a lesson, a trap or a technique —, the audience is narrowed, a skill no longer teaches an anchor skill, the check of a task that stayed has changed, and while the format is v0 — also a move to a new format version;
  - minor — everything as before is in place and means the same, and the module gives more or leads differently;
  - patch — the same entries, checks and path, other words or pictures.

  The table "what changes — part" by the fields of the schemas is normative, in the format text. The rows where the principle leaves a judgement — the mark «Выбор» ("Choice") in `module-kit` — are decided by the planning of T69.
- **What is compared** is packages: the canonical view and the list of the device part (R62), not the author's YAML, so comments, the order of keys and `eval/` do not change the version. A slot check is compared by meaning, as its check kind reads it, and a predicate as a string. The instances of a template are matched by the values of the parameters.
- **0.y.z:** the major is played by y, and the minor and the patch by z; in 0.0.z each version is its own major. "The same major" of `diff` and of `api` is one.
- **A new meaning is a new ID:** a published ID of a skill, a task, a lesson, a trap or a technique does not name another entry of its kind. For a skill, R49 says so, for a trap the [format text](../format/README.md), section 16, and for a task, a lesson and a technique — now too.
- **The comparison rules** with the IDs that `module-kit` proposed: the new version is above each published one; it is the next by one of the parts after the newest and not below the part found; each skill of each published version below is in `skills` or in `retired_skills`; the entries of `retired_skills` of the newest stand in the new one too, and `replaced_by` only expands; a new entry of `retired_skills` names a skill of a published version; an ID that is not in the newest does not come back; `languages` are the same. The ID prefix — by parts, as `module-kit` proposed, or its own, as with the index rules — is decided by the planning of T69. The format text will say that these rules refuse a new version, not a module, as the index rules do ([format text](../format/README.md), section 7).
- **The index rule** `module-index.version-above`: a version that is not in the previous index is above each version of its module in it. It catches a release where CI did not run `diff`.
- **The vectors** are `vectors/versions/<case>/`: the packages of the published versions, the new version as a module folder, and the part found or a refusal by a rule. `format-check` computes them by a second implementation, and the CI of `module-kit` passes them all.
- **The places in all versions:** in the inventory — `id`, `version` and `server_part` beside `module_format_version`; the names `inventory.json` and `server.json` of a package as files; a digest — `sha256:` and 64 hexadecimal digits, and the package digest is the digest of the bytes of `inventory.json`; in the canonical view — `manifest.languages`, `skill_graph` with the keys `skills` and `retired_skills` with their `replaced_by`, and the keys `tasks`, `lessons`, `traps.traps` and `techniques.techniques`. The format holds them in all versions, v0 too, like the members of the index (R63), and a reader reads them in a package of any version by the places. All of them are in the schemas of 0.2.
- **All published versions:** `diff` takes the package of each published version of the module, the withdrawn ones too. The rules about skills, `retired_skills` and IDs go over all of them, and the part found and the immutability of `retired_skills` — over the newest; across a move of the format — by the places above. The packages are given by the CI of `modules` (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R03 modules).
- **Not decided here** — until the planning of T69: a wrong entry of `retired_skills` cannot be corrected, the rule lets through only an expansion. ## Accessibility

**R90. All UI packages — `app`, `canvas` and `skill-map` — have one accessibility standard: WCAG 2.2 level AA and beyond it two AAA criteria — 2.5.5, targets no smaller than 44 × 44 CSS px, and 2.3.3, motion by `prefers-reduced-motion`. What a package does not meet yet it declares itself, and `app` names it on its page "Accessibility". The caption beside an icon is always visible. О-24 is resolved.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В30 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 375a09b), by its recommendation. The standard is R11 app, how `app` arranges it is architecture 3.9 app, and the sources are architecture 4 app, read by `app` 2026-11-02.
- **The standard** — [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), W3C Recommendation 12 December 2024, level AA. Beyond it:
  - 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) — "at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels". `canvas` already has such targets (R36), and children of 6–12 hit with a finger worse than adults (R11 app);
  - 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions — "Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled, unless the animation is essential to the functionality or the information being conveyed": motion that an action starts is turned off by `prefers-reduced-motion`.

  AAA as a whole — no: "It is not recommended that Level AAA conformance be required as a general policy for entire sites because it is not possible to satisfy all Level AAA success criteria for some content". WCAG 3 is a Working Draft, and the standard does not look at it until it is a Recommendation.
- **Declared nonconformances.** What a package does not meet yet it names in its documents — the criterion, what there is instead and when it goes away —, and `app` gathers them on the page "Accessibility", among its legal pages (architecture 3.13). `app` has three of them now (R11 app): the answer in handwriting — 2.1.1, 2.5.1 and 2.5.7, until a second way of answering (О-25); the printed text of the workbook's lines, which does not grow with the page zoom beyond fitting to the width — 1.4.4, until the sheet of `canvas` zooms; submitting the answer on "Check" without confirmation and undo — 3.3.4.
- **What follows from the standard for `canvas`:**
  - zoom of the sheet up to 200 % with scrolling in two directions — 1.4.10 allows the sheet a two-dimensional layout —, and with it the nonconformance 1.4.4 of the workbook's lines goes away;
  - the workbook's lines and boxes in the accessibility tree;
  - the keyboard enters the sheet and leaves it (2.1.2);
  - the row of buttons does not stick when the window is low (1.4.10, 2.4.11);
  - the frames of `exportWork()` do not change with the theme and forced colors;
  - its own axe-core in CI: the CI of `app` does not check the subtree of the canvas element (R11 app).
- **What follows for `skill-map`:** a text alternative to the graph, `lang` on a skill's name, mastery not only by color (1.4.1), the keyboard, and moving the map without dragging (2.5.7).
- **For all packages:**
  - the caption beside an icon is always visible, and a button's name is its text (2.5.3; the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R78);
  - an own scroll container — only with `tabindex="0"`, the role `region` and a name: in Safari a container without focusable content cannot be scrolled from the keyboard (WebKit bug [277290](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=277290); О-24).
- **Scrolling the sheet with a single pointer** — by the buttons "Up" and "Down" of the row of `canvas`, as О-24 recorded on 2026-10-27 (R33 canvas): with them the sheet meets 2.5.1 and 2.5.7 on a narrow tablet too.

— *Why:* the author's answer by the recommendation of `app`. The task screen is put together by `app` and `canvas`, and the screen has one level. `app` cannot oblige another repository (RULES.md, Across repositories), and `spec` can. The standard is chosen by the learners, not by the law: the markets of the beta are not chosen (П-2), and what the accessibility laws mean for NovaTrail is П-25. WCAG 2.2 AA covers WCAG 2.1 AA, which the laws name where they name a level, except 4.1.1 Parsing — in 2.2 it is "Obsolete and removed" (architecture 4 app). This standard was awaited by the row of buttons of `canvas` (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R36) and by the caption beside an icon (R78).

— *Rejected:*
- each package has its own level, and `app` answers for the screen as a whole: `app` would learn of a package's nonconformance last;
- WCAG 2.2 AA without AAA: targets could become 24 × 24 CSS px — 2.5.8, "at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels", — too small for a child's finger.

— *Consequence:*
- О-24 is resolved and moves to product 13.1; a second way of answering is the question О-25;
- the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R78;
- architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 6;
- the components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д87.

— R11 app; R33 canvas; R36, R78; О-24, О-25, П-2, П-25.

The item on the zoom of the sheet in "What follows from the standard for `canvas`" is fulfilled by this. The element declares two nonconformances, in architecture 3.10 canvas (R74 canvas), and `app` takes them onto the same page: 1.4.12 — the printing of the workbook's lines does not take the user's text spacing, and the page rule `format/page.yaml` gives no margin for it; 3.1.2 — the value of the demo step `fill` is voiced in the language of the captions, until epic E12 of `canvas`. ## Translations of the UI packages

**R91. The rules of translations of the UI packages — `app`, `canvas` and `skill-map` — are shared, and each package has its own tables of translations. The words that more than one package shows are the table of words in architecture 6, and `spec` keeps it. The names of anchor skills stay English for now, with their own `lang="en"`.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В32 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 375a09b), by its recommendation with two changes: the shared words are in the table of `spec`, not in the glossary of `app`, and the names of anchor skills are not translated. How `app` arranges translations is R10 app and architecture 3.8 app.
- **The shared rules:**
  - the language of a package's captions is the attribute `lang` on the element itself, and the element does not read the language of an ancestor (R36);
  - the language in the package's table is looked up by truncating the tag, as in [RFC 4647](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647), section 3.4, and one not found is English, and the fallback caption has its own `lang`;
  - placeholders are by name, not by concatenating strings: the order of words differs between languages. "Part 2 of 4." is one string with two placeholders, not "Part", a number, "of" and a number;
  - the plural forms are the categories of CLDR, and `other` is always there;
  - a string does not give away the learner's gender (R70) and does not speak in the first person of AI (П-15);
  - each package carries each interface language — now `en` and `ru` (R92).
- **The table of words** — architecture 6: the value, its words in `en` and `ru`, and the packages that show it. The first rows are the captions of the buttons of the row of `canvas`: the strings of `app` speak of them too (architecture 3.8 app). A word that a second package needed enters the table as a row «в реестр spec» (RULES.md, Across repositories), like a value of the table of icons (R78), and the words of one package go in its documents.
- **The names of anchor skills** are the English text of the schema `shared-taxonomy.schema.json` (R50). A package sets them with their own `lang="en"`, as `app` does (R10 app). Whether to translate them into the interface languages and where the translations lie is a question of its own, when it is needed: it touches R50 and the format.
- **The examples of `spec`** write what the learner sees, without the first person of AI and without gender: «Прочитано: 6» ("Read:" and the number), not «Я прочитал 6» ("I read" and the number) (the third 2026-11-02 amendment to R05).

— *Why:* the author's answer. A screen that several packages put together must speak the same way, and the table of captions of `canvas` waited for a shared scheme (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R36). A package cannot take code from `app`, and `@altnovatrail/spec` lies in a consumer's `devDependencies` (R73), so only the rules can be shared. The table of words is `spec`'s, not in the glossary of `app`: a document of another repository does not oblige the packages (RULES.md, Across repositories), and the shared choice of the UI packages is already held by the table of values of icons (R78). The names of anchor skills are a part of the format, and an anchor skill has no explanation language (R50): their translation would require a place for translations in the format.

— *Rejected:*
- a shared package of the code of translations — one more package with its own release;
- the packages' captions are given by `app` — R36 rejected this: each consumer would translate the captions, and the samples page too;
- the shared words — by the glossary of `app`, as the row proposed: a glossary of another repository would oblige the packages;
- the names of anchor skills are translated into the interface languages already now, as the row proposed: that is an edit of R50 and of the format without a question of its own.

— *Consequence:*
- the third 2026-11-02 amendment to R05; product 7, concepts 9.1 and the diagram of architecture 4.1;
- architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 6 — the table of words;
- the components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д87.

— R10 app; R05, R36, R50, R70, R73, R78; П-15.

## Interface language

**R92. The interface languages are `en` and `ru`. A learner's interface language is a field of their profile, which an adult sets, and the screens before a learner is chosen and the section for adults are in the device's language. The contract carries any valid BCP 47 tag, without a list of languages, and texts from `api` `app` requests by naming the language in the request. The interface language does not go into an AI call.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В33 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 375a09b), by its recommendation; О-2 is added to. How `app` arranges it is R10 app and architecture 3.8 app.
- **The languages** are `en` and `ru`, by the recommendation of О-2. A new interface language is stage 5 (product 11), and each UI package carries it (R91).
- **The profile field** "interface language" is set and changed by an adult in the section for adults, and the learner has no switch: an accidental tap would take a child into a language they do not read. No field — the device's language. A tag that the build of `app` does not know it looks up by truncation, then takes the device's language, then English, and does not overwrite the field (R10 app).
- **The device's language** is for the screens before a learner is chosen — sign-in, choosing the learner, getting started, the failure screens — and for the section for adults: the sign-in screen is seen before the account, and an adult may read in another language than the child. It is the adult's choice on this device, and without a choice the browser's language (R10 app).
- **The contract** carries the language as a BCP 47 tag, without a list: which languages the build knows is its property, not `api`'s, and a new language does not change the contract. Texts from `api` — the legal texts and the consent — `app` requests by naming the language in the request, not by the header `Accept-Language`; the legal texts themselves are only in English for now (privacy 7). This is RUN.md, T63.
- **To AI** the interface language does not go: the tutor speaks in the module's explanation language (concepts 10 and 13; R46). privacy 4 names the purpose of the field so: in which language the screen speaks with the learner.
- **Before the first attempt** `app` gets the name and the explanation language of the connected modules: the module's card names the explanation language if it is not the screen's language. This is RUN.md, T64.

— *Why:* the author's answer by the recommendation of `app`. The language is in the learner's profile: the learner learns on other devices too, and on a shared tablet each child may have their own (R10 app). The explanation languages are a question of content, which `modules` writes, so О-2 is resolved only in its part about the interface.

— *Rejected:*
- О-2 is closed whole, and the explanations in the slice are only English: a Russian-speaking child of 6–12 would get tasks in English;
- the interface language is on the device, and `spec` does not know it: all children of a shared tablet would have one language, and on another device the learner would see another one.

— *Does not decide:* the explanation languages of the slice's modules and the decimal comma — the format reads `1,5` as two numbers ([format text](../format/README.md), sections 15 and 20). They stay in О-2, with `modules` and product.

— *Consequence:*
- О-2 is added to; concepts 13; privacy 4 — the row "Learner profile";
- RUN.md — T63 and T64;
- the components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д87.

— R10 app; R46, R91; О-2.

— *Amendment 2026-11-03:* **the request for texts from `api` — the legal texts and the consent — will come into the contract together with the texts themselves, their versions and the consent, in epic E4, while the rule of the request — the language as a field of the message, not the header `Accept-Language` — is already in the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15.** The author's answer of 2026-11-03 while T63 was planned, by the plan's recommendation: there are no texts yet, their form, versions and who approves them are decided by E4 together with a lawyer, and the first app does not need them (R76). The item "The contract" and "Consequence" above are read with this amendment. Rejected: the method now — the format of a text and its versions would be decided before the lawyer. — R98; RUN.md, T63.

## The sample file

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the method of the texts, which the 2026-11-03 amendment put off until E4, has come into the contract — `LegalService.GetLegalTexts` (R130). The language is still a field of the request, not a header.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T96 was planned (RUN.md): the method now, not with the contract of consent of T103. — R130; [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15.

**R93. The sample file is the message `Sample` of the package `novatrail.eval.v1`, the first message of the eval protocol: one JSON to a sample, without the task's key. Its contents are set by the purpose and by who wrote it, as in R09 canvas, but without pressure, and a sample of an eval set names its license. A reader reads the file strictly: an unknown field is a refusal. The PNG of the crops have not a single ancillary chunk. A sample is checked by the code of `spec`, and the other repositories call the same code.** The author's answers of 2026-11-03 while T58 was planned (RUN.md), all seven by the plan's recommendations; the seventh is about a step of the release, the second 2026-11-03 amendment to R37. Normative — the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 11.
- **The version** is the suffix of the package `v1` and the tag of `spec`, as for any contract (R83; the 2026-11-02 amendment to R44). The file names it by its first field, `protocol: "novatrail.eval.v1"`, and the reader chooses the type by it before it reads the file strictly, like the header `format` and `version` of the files of `tutor` (architecture 3.1 tutor). The protocol has no version MAJOR.MINOR of its own.
- **The contents.** The purpose is a measurement or an eval set, who wrote it is an adult in their own hand, an adult imitating a child's, or a child, and the origin is a person or synthetic data with a seed (R09 canvas):
  - an eval set — only an adult: the final geometry of the visible strokes, without a writer code, with `license: "Apache-2.0"`;
  - a measurement by an adult — the writing history and the writer code;
  - a measurement by a child — the final geometry and the writer code;
  - synthetic data — in each of the three; its sample ID is derived from the seed, a person's is random. The ID is fit to be a file name: 1–64 lowercase Latin letters, digits and hyphens.

  There is no name, email, account, device, browser, screen, language, date, age or grade in the file, and strict reading does not let them in as an extra field.
- **The writing history** is the events `write`, `erase`, `clear` and `undo` by the sheet's clock, as the element gives them (R22 canvas); the points are in units of the sheet to a precision of 0.1. **There is no pressure**: not one kind of input of a model takes it — «сырые штрихи с временем и нажимом не идут никуда» ("raw strokes with time and pressure go nowhere") (R11 tutor; T08 tutor) —, and minimization does not allow a record without a reader (privacy 1). `canvas` stops writing it: R09 canvas, *Revisit*, moves the contents to the protocol.
- **The final geometry** is the visible strokes, numbered by their place from 1, the points along the stroke; without time, the pointer type, the order and what was erased. The groups and the table of boxes move to the new numbers.
- **A sheet and a workbook.** A sheet is the size, the module's digit height, the groups with labels by place, and the crops. A workbook is the page size, all the boxes with their place and rectangle, the filled boxes with the IDs of strokes and the crops; there are no groups, and the geometry holds only the strokes of the boxes (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R53). The crops are at the eval heights 16, 24, 32 and 48 px and at the module's height, each with its own D, D′, size, margins, `s`, line, `sheet_box`, frames of groups and PNG, and the shared ones are the box of the points and h_med in tenths of a unit.
- **The reference to the task** is without the key: the source is a release of `modules` (the tag, the module, the version, the package digest), the file of open tasks of a release of `tutor` (the tag, the file's digest, the bank and its digest; R64 tutor), or a file of tasks outside a release; the task's ID, the seed of the template's instance, and the digest of the open view — `sha256:` and the SHA-256 of the canonical text of RFC 8785, for an instance with the numbers substituted (the row В67 of `tutor`; the row В17 of `module-kit`).
- **Strict reading, canonical text.** A writer writes every field, zeros too, by proto names (`UseProtoNames` and `EmitDefaultValues`, `useProtoFieldName` and `alwaysEmitImplicit`), like the observation vectors (the 2026-11-03 amendment to R86). A reader refuses an unknown field — this is the default of `protojson.Unmarshal` and `fromJson` —, and skipping the unknown is left to the transport (R83). The check compares the file with the text that the writer writes.
- **PNG** — grey, 8 bits, colour type 0, not interlaced, of the crop's size; the chunks are only IHDR, IDAT and IEND. Not a single ancillary one: neither tEXt, iTXt, zTXt, eXIf and tIME, nor others, private ones too. This is how the encoder of `canvas` writes (R25 canvas).
- **The license** is the field `license` of a sample of an eval set, `"Apache-2.0"` (R20): item (a) of the DCO, "the open source license indicated in the file", is read literally. A measurement and a child's sample have no field: they are not published. Whether this is enough is still a question for a lawyer in П-18.
- **Privacy.** A sample of a measurement by an adult goes to the measurement's organizer, outside git and the platform's server, and from them to the measurement's AI providers (П-18). A sample of an eval set goes to the eval-set organizer, into `modules`, under Apache-2.0, without withdrawal (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R25; П-16). A child sample is outside the repositories, with a separate consent (П-10), and the runner does not send it to AI until the agreement with the provider admits children (R24; П-3). A sample does not go to the platform's server (R09).
- **The check** is `tools/contracts/sample.mjs` in `just contracts-check`: strict reading by buf's image, the contents, the history, the sheet and the workbook, the crops and the PNG. The examples are `contracts/examples/eval/v1/`: three synthetic samples, one per contents, and the strokes, groups, crops and PNG come from the vectors and the code of `canvas`. Together they show each purpose, "who wrote", the history and the geometry, the sheet and the workbook, and each event of the history. A value that the package adds the check refuses until the text names it.
- **A command without a key** for the CI of `modules`, `canvas` and `tutor` is a recipe of `spec` through the submodule, `just -f spec/justfile sample-check <files>`, like `docs-check-repo`: the same code. The recipe for another repository and its tests are T72.

— *Why:*
- the version is as for a contract: the contracts have no version of their own beyond the package (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R44), and the field `protocol` gives the reader a clear refusal on a file of another package, not a list of foreign fields;
- no kind of input takes pressure, and the protocol had better not require it — so the record «Протокол eval и формат образцов в E3» beside table 1 of RUN.md put the question;
- a decoder may skip an ancillary chunk, and text, metadata and time hide precisely in them (the row В8 of `modules`), so a crop does not need them: `canvas` does not write them anyway;
- strict reading is what the closed schema of the row В8 of `modules` asks for: «имя не спрячется в лишнем поле» ("a name will not hide in an extra field"); `tutor` reads its files the same way (architecture 3.1 tutor);
- the license in the file — item (a) of the DCO speaks of a license "indicated in the file": the field costs nothing, and the question for a lawyer becomes narrower;
- one check for all repositories: the validity rules are written once, and the page of `canvas`, the runner of `tutor` and the CI of `modules` compare a file by one code (R38).

— *Rejected:*
- a version MAJOR.MINOR of the protocol's own, as the format has: the contracts have none (the 2026-11-02 amendment to R44);
- a file without the field `protocol`: a file of another package the reader would refuse with a list of foreign fields;
- pressure as an optional field, or as a required one in a measurement's history: the record has no reader;
- ancillary colour chunks without text — gAMA, sRGB, cHRM, pHYs: `canvas` does not write them, and another encoder will omit them; and forbidding only tEXt, iTXt, zTXt, eXIf and tIME: a new or private chunk would pass;
- reading without a canon — an unknown field is a refusal, while the check lets through omitted zeros and lowerCamelCase: the sample file would not be one text; and reading as Connect does, skipping the unknown: a name would lie in an extra field for a reader without a check;
- a file without a license field, with the license named by the module's `LICENSE`: then only a lawyer would decide the meaning of item (a);
- a command of the eval runner of `tutor` — the recommendation of `modules`: the CI of `modules` would wait for a release of `tutor` with the command, and `tutor` would write the validity rules too; the CLI of `module-kit` — the sample file would enter the format version, though it is a contract (R44);
- a JSON Schema of the sample file beside `.proto`: a second description of the same type, as in the 2026-11-03 amendment to R86;
- one field "kind of sample" instead of the purpose, "who wrote" and the origin: it would mix three independent features (R09 canvas).

— *Found in planning:*
- `canvas` on `main` (602945b) has neither code, nor a schema, nor an example of the sample file — only R09, R22, R24–R27, R34, R37–R39 canvas and architecture 3.5 canvas; its T17 waits for the protocol;
- the reader of `tutor` is strict: an unknown field and a foreign case are an error (architecture 3.1 tutor);
- T08 of `tutor` was done on 2026-10-21, and no kind of input of a model takes pressure;
- the format's seed is an unsigned 64-bit one, written in decimal digits ([format text](../format/README.md), section 22), — so in the contract it is `string`.

— *Consequence:*
- [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), sections 1, 3, 7, 8 and 11; `tools/contracts/sample.mjs`; `contracts/examples/eval/v1/`; the 2026-11-03 amendments to R38 and the third amendment of the same day to R83;
- concepts 15; architecture 3.2, 3.6, 3.7 and 3.10; privacy 9 — П-10, П-16 and П-18; repositories 5;
- RUN.md — T58, T72; the components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д94.

— R09, R15, R20, R24, R25, R38, R83, R86; R09, R22, R25 canvas; R11, R64 tutor; П-3, П-10, П-16, П-18.

## The rules of the device and the runner

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the value of `text_set_version` in a sample file is the ID of the text set and its version joined by a hyphen, for example `child-sample-1` ([the `legal/` part](../legal/README.md), section 4): by it the organizer finds exactly the set the person saw.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T96 (RUN.md). The rule of the field — from 1 to 32 Latin letters, digits, dots and hyphens — does not change. — R130; [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 11.

**R94. The rules that are the same for the device and the runner — the folding of the writing history, the stroke groups, the crop, the snapping of a model's box and the boxes of a workbook — the eval protocol wrote down as `canvas` wrote them: [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 12. Their test vectors are four files of `contracts/vectors/eval/v1/`, in messages of the package `novatrail.eval.v1`. `spec` computes them by a second implementation, and they come out in `contracts.Vectors` and in the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`. A sample's crops are drawn from the strokes the file holds, and the sample check recomputes their numbers, and for a history also the groups and the table of boxes. A rule changes only in `spec`, and a change of its result is a new package.** The author's answers of 2026-11-03 in planning T59 (RUN.md): of five, three by the recommendations of the plan, and the form of the vectors and the place of the sample check not. The rest is a proposal of the plan that the author approved. Normative — [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 12.
- **The rules** — those that R22, R24–R26, R34 and R37 canvas wrote down and that the author's records at table 1 of RUN.md accepted: «Правила `canvas` в протоколе eval», «Окошки рабочей тетради в протоколе eval» and «Свободная запись и строчные буквы в протоколе eval». The count is in whole numbers: places in tenths of a unit, time in whole milliseconds, a half rounded up. Beyond the rules of `canvas`, [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 12, writes what `canvas` does not compute:
  - the groups of an erased stroke. Erased is any stroke written that the sheet does not show at the end: erased by the eraser, by a clear or taken off by an undo. It belongs to the groups of those visible strokes that would be its neighbours — to none or to two. The action log of `tutor`'s runner waits for them (R11 tutor);
  - the time of the event "stroke" is no earlier than its last point (R22 canvas; the 2026-11-03 amendment to R93);
  - how the history of the element `<novatrail-canvas>` becomes a sample's history: `t` is `t_ms`, the kind of an event is its field, a stroke's `kind` is `pointer`, and the pressure does not go in (R93).
- **The vectors are messages of the protocol.** The input and the result of a rule are the JSON of the package `novatrail.eval.v1`, as [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 6, writes it: `History`, `FinalStroke`, `Group`, `TenthsBox`, `CropSet` with an empty PNG, `PageBox` and `FilledBox`, and the places are the observation's `CropBox` and `AnswerSlotPlace`. What the messages do not hold — the visible strokes, the pairs of neighbours, the bundles, each stroke's box, the strokes a box takes — lies in keys of the wrapper. There is no schema of its own, as with the observation vectors (the 2026-11-03 amendment to R86): the check holds the form.
  - The cases are those of `canvas`'s vectors at the tag v0.1.2, commit 8e9c6f6: the files are the same as on `main` 602945b and at v0.1.0. The history in them is without pressure and in whole milliseconds, so the case `rounding` lost its rounding of fractions of a millisecond: a sample's time is whole by its type. `spec`'s second implementation repeated all of `canvas`'s results: 11 cases of groups, 34 of crops, 14 of snapping with 597 boxes of a model and 20 of boxes.
  - `groups.json` adds to each case the groups of the erased strokes, and five more cases of its own: an erased stroke without neighbours, between two groups, inside a group, taken off by an undo and after a clear.
- **Where from and who changes them.** The vectors came into `spec` by its pull request from a tag of `canvas`: the files of `canvas`'s release do not carry them, so `release-verify` (R77) has nothing to check. From then on `spec` holds them. A change of a rule or of the vectors is brought by `canvas` and `tutor` as a row «в реестр spec», and a task of `spec` changes the text, the vectors and the second implementation together. A change that gives another result for the same input is a change of what the package means and a new package ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 2), and so is one of the margin and the threshold of snapping, though they are parameters of eval. A case that pins what is already written only adds.
- **The second implementation** is `tools/contracts/strokes.mjs` in `just contracts-check`, by the text that [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 12, gives, like `observation.mjs` for the observation. Each case is recomputed, and a mismatch is named by its file and line. Together the four files show each event that takes strokes off, an erased stroke in no group and in two, a crop without bundles, above the cap and below the height asked, a box of a model that takes strokes and one that does not, scratch work and a filled box.
- **The way to code.** Go takes the vectors as `contracts.Vectors`, as the folder `eval/v1/`, like the observation vectors (the 2026-11-03 amendment to R64): `tutor` — instead of its own copies of `crops.json` and `groups.json`. Code in TypeScript takes them from the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`, which carries them by their path, `@altnovatrail/contracts/vectors/eval/v1/groups.json` (the fourth 2026-11-03 amendment to R83). The observation vectors are not in the package, and no new line is needed: what the package holds follows the tree.
- **The types of the history** in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` stay the element's types — the 2026-11-03 amendment to R74.
- **A sample by the rules** ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 11; the 2026-11-03 amendment to R93):
  - a sample's crops are drawn from the strokes the file holds — those visible from the history or the final geometry —, with the sheet's groups, and a box's from its strokes. So any reader repeats their numbers, for the samples of an eval set in CI of `modules` too. T17 `canvas` draws a crop from the geometry it writes — RUN.md, Д96;
  - for a history, the sheet's groups and the table of boxes are those that the rules give for its visible strokes. For the final geometry they are the device's: there is no time in it, and the points along a stroke may be other than those that came (R26 canvas; T17 canvas);
  - `tools/contracts/sample.mjs` checks it, when the form of the sheet or the page is whole, and by the same code `sample-check` of the other repositories (R93).

— *Why:*
- messages of the protocol — the author's answer: the input and the result of a rule are the same messages that lie in a sample file, and the reader of the vectors reads them by the same code as the samples;
- the npm package — the author's answer by the recommendation: `canvas` runs the rules in TypeScript, and the submodule `spec/` for code was rejected by R64 and by the 2026-11-03 amendment to R86 — code takes `spec`'s files from a release. The argument "TypeScript gives no verdicts" holds for the observation, not for these rules;
- the element's types — the author's answer by the recommendation: this is the agreement of `canvas` and `app` (R74), and the element's history needs pressure to draw;
- the sample check by the rules — the author's answer: `strokes.mjs` already runs the rules, and «Открыто» of T58 named that only the form holds the numbers of a crop;
- the crop from the file's strokes — the author's answer by the recommendation: so any reader repeats the numbers of a crop to the bit, for a sample without a history too. Otherwise only the form would hold them, until T17 `canvas` decides how the points of the geometry are taken;
- the second implementation — as for the verdicts, the generator and the comparison of format versions and for the observation (R56; R86; R89): without an implementation that computes them, the vectors do not catch a typo in a case.

— *Rejected:*
- the vectors as they are — byte for byte with `canvas` or with rewritten headers. The headers cite `canvas`'s decisions without a suffix, the history is in the element's form and with pressure, and `tutor` would read it by its own structures, not by the protocol's type;
- the vectors as they are, with JSON Schema schemas and without an implementation of their own: that is a second description of the same thing (R93), and a case with a typo would pass the schema. A schema of the wrapper was rejected by the 2026-11-03 amendment to R86 too;
- `canvas` reads the vectors from the submodule `spec/`, like the sample's examples: code takes `spec`'s files from a release (R64; the 2026-11-03 amendment to R86);
- a release file of its own for the vectors: the protocol has no version of its own (R93), and a new kind of file would open a line;
- the vectors from a release of `canvas` checked by `release-verify`: a release of `canvas` does not carry them, `spec` would wait for a task of `canvas`, and would hold them itself after all from then on;
- the element's types in the protocol's form — `t_ms`, `oneof` and without pressure: `canvas` and `app` would rewrite code, and the pen's line would lose its width;
- the sample check by the rules as a separate task T73 — the recommendation of the plan: T59 is more than one check (rule 11 of RUN.md); and a check by the form alone, without the rules;
- for a sample without a history, only the form of the crops, with the device drawing them from raw strokes: nobody would check the numbers of the eval-set samples that `modules` publishes.

— *Found in planning:*
- `canvas`'s vectors have neither schemas nor a README, and the headers cite its decisions without a suffix. The vectors are written by `canvas`'s tests as snapshots, `toMatchFileSnapshot`, and the releases of `canvas` carry only the package;
- erased strokes are only in the case `staircase`, and no vector of `canvas` writes the groups of an erased stroke;
- in `boxes.json` the names of cases repeat — with a different density of points; in `spec` the second name has `-every-2`;
- `CropSet.bundle_median` is h_med before the cap of 100 units, and the scale takes H = min(h_med, 1000);
- the copies of `crops.json` and `groups.json` in `tutor` are byte for byte (`internal/render/testdata/`, `internal/lines/testdata/`), and its tests pin 34 and 11 cases;
- whether samples without a history will take the points "along the stroke, not as they came", `canvas` has not decided yet (R26 canvas; T17 canvas);
- "T59" in the documents of `canvas` is its own task, not this one.

— *Consequence:*
- [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), sections 1, 3, 7, 8, 11 and 12; `tools/contracts/strokes.mjs`, `sample.mjs`, `main.mjs`, `npm.mjs`, `typescript.mjs` and `contracts.check.mjs`; `contracts/vectors/eval/v1/`; `contracts/vectors_test.go`; the 2026-11-03 amendments to R74 and R93 and the fourth amendment of the same day to R83;
- concepts 15; architecture 3.2 and 3.6; repositories 5; the comment of `types/canvas/index.d.ts`; README.md and CLAUDE.md;
- RUN.md — T59 and Д96: `canvas` and `tutor` get the answer with their move to a tag.

— R22, R24–R26, R34, R37 canvas; R11 tutor; R42, R56, R64, R74, R77, R83, R86, R89, R93.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **snapping takes the strokes as they came: on the device, the strokes of the submission; in eval, those the writing history shows. A sample's final geometry is no input of it. Eval chooses the margin and the threshold of snapping, and measures snapping only on samples with a history. This does not change the result of a rule on the same input, and the package is the same.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В61 (RUN.md of `canvas`, `main` 3e7847a) — an inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, by the row's recommendation, with the triage's clarification about choosing the margin and the threshold. The "Found in planning" above waited for T17 `canvas`, and it decided: samples without a history take the points along the stroke — every 0.25 units, with the ends and the points on which the stroke's box rests (R48 canvas). The boxes of the strokes, the bundles, h_med and the numbers of the crop of such a sample are the same as those of the strokes written. But the share of points that a box of a model holds is another: on a sheet that was written on, the points stand as the pointer went.
- *Why:* there is no snapping in a sample, and `tutor`'s runner does not do it (R24 tutor), so there is nothing to drift apart now. But the margin and the threshold are parameters of eval, and eval may choose them anew by its own data ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 12). The samples of an eval set are all without a history (there too, section 11), and by them the parameters would come out for another share of points than the one the device computes. `tutor` already has the code of snapping: `protocol.Snap` passes the vectors of `snaps.json` (R67 tutor).
- *Rejected:* counting the share by the length of the stroke, not by the points. The rule would then stop depending on the density of the points, but that is a change of what the package means and a new package, and the vectors and the code of `canvas`, `tutor` and `spec` would change for the sake of a measure that does not exist. Also rejected: samples without a history taking the points as they came: their density gives away the speed of writing (R09 canvas; R48 canvas).
- *Revisit:* when a measurement of snapping takes its place on the device (the «Пересмотреть» of R26 canvas) — the share by the length of the stroke, by a row «в реестр spec» of its own.
