## The engine's inputs

**R104. The engine chooses a lesson or a task, not an item. Beyond the learner model its input is a summary of issues from `api`, which `api` gathers from its records of choices and attempts, and `Read` of `learner-model` gives for a module whether its trial series has ended and whether the last evidence was still in it. For a skill that the skill map opened, the engine gives a lesson or a task on it.** The author's answers of 2026-11-07 to the rows «в реестр spec» `engine` В2–В4 (RUN.md `engine`, `main` 479d0b7) and `skill-map` В2 (RUN.md `skill-map`, `main` 7f7043b) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, all by the rows' recommendations.
- **Not an item** (В2 `engine`): "item" leaves the list of concepts 12. Items are a part of a task, and the check, the evidence and the solution belong to the task as a whole; the choice is a lesson, a task or "nothing to give", as `ChoiceKind` (R99).
- **The summary of issues** (В3 `engine`): for a skill, the time of the last issue and, if the last closed attempt of the skill was a probe, whether it was correct; for a module, the number of tasks issued; for a task, when its solution last went to the device (R82). By it the rule keeps the queue "not issued for the longest", the turn of a probe — once in six tasks —, the return of a skill from a pause by a correct answer of a probe and the pause before a task with a seen solution. The types of the summary are its own and simple, like the types of the graph — T04 `engine`, and the repeat of a choice by it — T03 `engine`: the repeat gathers the summary anew from the records before the choice, which do not change (architecture 1).
- **The trial series** (В4 `engine`): in a module's trial series the engine does not work through an error and gives no probes (SPEC 3.2 standalone, step 1), and the series — the first five answers in the module — is a state of the model (R03 learner-model). So `Read` gives two marks for a module: whether the trial series has ended, and whether the module's last evidence was still in it — the second is needed so that an error in the series' last answer is not worked through.
- **A skill from the map** (В2 `skill-map`): the detailing of `engine` takes the rule "open" of the skill map (R03 skill-map) as an input. For a skill that the map opened and the learner chose, `ChooseNext` gives a lesson or a task on it with the code "the learner chose the skill", if the pool and the lessons hold at least one, and the reachability for "My subjects" may be its own. Such a choice is empty only when `api` has limited the pool to tasks without AI (concepts 12).

— *Why:*
- the time of practice from the model is not the time of issue: a task issued without evidence gives no practice, and the rule needs both. `api` keeps the records of choices and attempts anyway (R99; architecture 1), so the summary adds no learner's data, it only hands them to the engine (privacy 1);
- the model counts the series, and the engine does not repeat its rules: were it to count by itself by the number of evidence of the module's skills, evidence with several skills would be counted more than once;
- the map's rule rests on the definition of the code "new skill" in the contract, no new field is needed, and the learner's choice always gives something.

— *Rejected:*
- giving `ChoiceKind` the kind "item" — an amendment of the contract `app` ↔ `api` and of `api` for a choice the rule does not make;
- a summary only from the model, and in the input only the tasks with a seen solution: a task issued without evidence would not move the queue; a log of the last N issues, like standalone's window `recent` — more learner's data in the call than the rule reads (privacy 1);
- the engine counts the series by itself; a rule without a trial series;
- `engine` decides the reachability by itself, and the map moves to its rule by a field of `GetSkillMap` — the map would wait for the detailing of `engine`, and a field in `v1` cannot be removed afterwards; the map chooses any skill — the author of `skill-map` rejected this while planning T01 `skill-map`.

— *Consequence:* concepts 12 — the choice, the summary of issues among the inputs; architecture 1 — the repeat of a choice; architecture 3.5 and 3.8 — the summary from `api`, the marks of the series in `Read`, a skill from the map; Д112 — what `api`, `engine` and `learner-model` take; the rows `engine` В2–В4 and `skill-map` В2 are in table 5 of RUN.md.

— R03, R23, R82, R99, R100; R03 learner-model; R03 engine; R03 skill-map; SPEC 3.2 standalone; RUN.md, Д112.

— *Amendment 2026-11-07:* **the summary of issues comes with additions this answer did not see** (В12 `engine`; R107). The issue of a lesson is the issue of each of its skills; for a module, the number of choices, of a task and of a lesson one each, not of tasks issued; for a skill, the result of the last closed attempt if it is a probe or a repetition, not only a probe; and the result comes as facts — how many items where the skill is primary got a first verdict, at how many of them it is "correct" and whether the solution was shown — not as a mark "correct": the engine computes "failure". A skill from the map holds until the learner asks for something else, and the record of the choice carries it into the next one (В6 `engine`). — R107; concepts 12; architecture 3.8.

## Production images

**R105. An image that runs in production is a static Go binary on `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13` by the tag `nonroot` and digest: without a shell and a package manager, and not as root. NovaTrail does not use Docker Hardened Images.** The author's answer of 2026-11-07, outside an epic: «DHI - не используем. избыточен». The author had the rule recorded at once, by the recommendation of the analysis of the same day.
- **Which images.** The image that production runs — a Cloud Run service and its jobs:
  - for now only `api` will have such an image: it is one Go process, and its jobs run on the same image (architecture 3.5, 3.12);
  - later — `tutor`, when it becomes a service (R15), the services of stage 4 and the self-hosting of `infra` (architecture 3.11).

  The `toolchain` stage and the devcontainer are not part of this: they are built on every run and published nowhere (R30). The builds of `app` and `site` are static files of the hosting, they have no image.
- **The build** — in two stages, like the `Dockerfile` of canvas-api (commit 0901af0):
  - the build stage is the official `golang` image by exact tag and digest, with the Go version that `go.mod` names and on which the tests run;
  - the binary is built with `CGO_ENABLED=0` and `-trimpath`: it is static, without libc and without the paths of whoever built it.
- **The run** — on `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot@sha256:…`:
  - the base holds only "ca-certificates", "A /etc/passwd entry for a root user", "A /tmp directory" and "tzdata", without a shell and a package manager;
  - the tag `nonroot` runs as the user with uid 65532 (`NONROOT = 65532` in `common/variables.bzl`);
  - distroless tags carry no version — "latest, nonroot, debug, debug-nonroot" — so the image is held by its digest, and the tag names the variant taken. This is what "by tag and digest" in RULES.md means;
  - Dependabot raises the digest: it sees the base image (R30), and the registry is open and asks for no credentials.
- **In the image** — the binary and what its repository put into the image: for `api` these are the module packages (R07 api). Nothing else — no debugging tools, no `debug` variant.
- **Not static Go** — another runtime, cgo, a browser — this decision does not cover. Such an image comes by an amendment to it, to the same bar: without a shell and a package manager, not as root, by tag and digest.
- **Not decided here:** where the image is built, who signs it and what the deployment checks — that is Т-19 and the shared release of `.github` (architecture 3.11).

— *Why:*
- A static Go binary needs only the certificates and tzdata from the base. `static-debian13` gives exactly those: "The smallest distroless image, `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13`, is around 2 MiB". The vulnerabilities that remain are in Go and the dependencies, and govulncheck catches them: `just ci-vuln` and "Go / vuln" (R30).
- This path has already gone through production: on this base canvas-api rolled out and rolled back a signed release on Cloud Run on 2026-10-14 (R11).
- The base needs no login, and its signature is keyless: "All distroless images are signed by cosign with ephemeral keys (keyless)". The check is `cosign verify $IMAGE_NAME --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com --certificate-identity keyless@distroless.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. This is the same Sigstore model as that of `release-verify` (R77). The project's license is Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`).
- The source is the README, `base/README.md` and the sources of [GoogleContainerTools/distroless](https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/distroless), commit c3bf6a1 of 2026-11-02, read 2026-11-07.

— *Rejected:*
- **Docker Hardened Images** — by the author's word: excessive. All read 2026-11-07:
  - on static Go DHI give the same surface: `dhi.io/static` — "A very minimal image that is most useful in the context of running binary executables, such as those built from Rust and Golang" ([the DHI catalog](https://hub.docker.com/hardened-images/catalog/dhi/static)). Beyond it there are only the base's attestations: SBOM, VEX and SLSA Build Level 3 provenance ([the DHI documentation](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/));
  - since 2025-12-17 they are free under Apache 2.0 ([Docker's blog](https://www.docker.com/blog/docker-hardened-images-for-every-developer/)), but the guarantees are paid. "Critical CVE fixes < 7 days with SLA-backed continuous patching" is given by the Select level, "Starting at $5k/repo", and the free one gets "Upstream cadence for Docker-released patches" ([Hardened Images](https://www.docker.com/products/hardened-images/));
  - they can be pulled only after `docker login dhi.io`, and in CI — "authenticate using an organization access token (OAT)" ([Use a Docker Hardened Image](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/how-to/use/)). That would be the first secret in NovaTrail's CI, which a pull request from a fork would not get, and a Docker account for everyone who builds the platform themselves;
  - their signature is checked by Docker's key, without a transparency log: "DHI attestations may not be recorded in the public Rekor transparency log", hence the flag `--insecure-ignore-tlog=true` ([Verify a Docker Hardened Image](https://docs.docker.com/dhi/how-to/verify/)). That is a second model of trust beside R77.
- **`scratch` with certificates from the build stage:** such a base has neither a signature nor a list of packages of its own, and the certificates and tzdata are whatever happened to be in the build image. Besides, canvas-api has not gone this path.
- **`base-debian13` or `cc-debian13`:** a static binary needs no glibc and libssl — "Statically compiled applications (Go) that do not require libc can use the `gcr.io/distroless/static` image" (`base/README.md`).
- **An Alpine or Debian image without distroless** — that is a shell and a package manager in a production image.

— *Consequence:*
- In RULES.md, the section Hard rules, the rule "Production images", so that the session of every repository sees it when it takes a new tag of `spec`.
- If NovaTrail begins to publish an image — for example, for self-hosting — the base's packages will begin to ship with it. Then the rule of R12 about the licenses of what ships with the code is read anew for them, as in the 2026-10-22 amendment to R12 about npm.
- `api` takes the rule into the epic of its code, where it writes the `Dockerfile` and decides where the image is built (Т-19).

— R11, R12, R15, R30, R77; R07 api; Т-19.

— *Amendment 2026-11-07:* **NovaTrail publishes no images: a service's release puts out a signed binary and the `Dockerfile`, and whoever deploys builds the image and keeps it in their own private registry.** This is the author's answer to the item "Consequence" above about the licenses of the base's packages, by the executor's recommendation.
- **What is in the base.** The image `gcr.io/distroless/static-debian13:nonroot` (index `sha256:25ac8f0c3b2334a9eb05452266bd4697864a8c8ef0ef71e5e6480d7f92868329`, the amd64 variant) was pulled from the registry and taken apart on 2026-11-07. The packages are taken from `/var/lib/dpkg/status.d/`, the licenses from `/usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright`:
  - `base-files` 13.8+deb13u7 — "License: GPL-2+": `/usr/lib/os-release`, `/etc/issue` and the texts of `/usr/share/common-licenses/`;
  - `netbase` 6.5 — "License: GPL-2": `/etc/services`, `/etc/protocols`, `/etc/rpc` and `/etc/ethertypes`;
  - `ca-certificates` 20250419+deb13u1: the certificates are made from `mozilla/certdata.txt` — "License: MPL-2.0", and `debian/*` with the script `update-ca-certificates`, which also lies in the image, — "License: GPL-2+";
  - `tzdata` and `tzdata-legacy` 2026f-0+deb13u1 — "This database is in the public domain";
  - `media-types` 13.0.0 — "Copyright: public-domain".
- **What this means by R12.** R12 admits the ASF's category A in what ships with NovaTrail's code and packages. A published image would carry both GPL and MPL-2.0 ([ASF 3rd Party License Policy](https://www.apache.org/legal/resolved.html), read 2026-11-07):
  - GPL is the ASF's category X: "Apache projects may not distribute Category X licensed components, in source or binary form; in ASF source code or in convenience binaries";
  - MPL 2.0 is category B: "Any Category B licensed works may be included in binary-only form in Apache Software Foundation convenience binaries", and with a notice.
- **Now:**
  - **A service's release** puts out the binary as a release file, with a signature, and the `Dockerfile` by which the image is built.
  - **NovaTrail's deployment** builds the image around the binary that `release-verify` accepted (R77), on the base by digest, and puts it into its own private registry — the Artifact Registry of `infra` (architecture 3.11).
  - **Self-hosting** builds the same image on its own side, from the same binary and by the same `Dockerfile`.
  - **The example is canvas-api.** Its deployment takes the server from the release, having checked the signature, builds "an image around it" and puts it into its own Artifact Registry (`docs/self-hosting.md` of canvas-api; R45, R58 canvas-api).
  - **NovaTrail's image registry is private:** only the deployment and the platform's own Cloud Run read it. A public registry or an image among the release files is already publication, and it is possible only by a new decision, with a list of the base's packages and their licenses for each digest.
  - **The binary's licenses** are already checked by the license checks: "Go / licenses" and `ci-licenses` (R30, R39). The base is not part of them: NovaTrail does not distribute it.
  - **Т-19 still decides** where the image is built — in the release of `api` or in the deployment of `infra`. The rule above holds in either variant, as long as the image stays in the private registry.

*Why:*
- an image together with its base is a distribution of files under GPL-2 and MPL-2.0, which R12 does not admit, and a binary under Apache-2.0 with already checked dependencies is not;
- self-hosting loses only `docker pull`: instead of it, `docker build` with the same `Dockerfile`;
- it costs the platform itself nothing: canvas-api has checked this path in prod (R11).

*Rejected:*
- **Publishing images with an exception in R12, counting the base's packages as "the platform".** The ASF calls a platform what a product works with, not what it distributes: "It does not matter, unless the terms for that platform affect the Apache product's licensing". The ASF does not distribute category X in "convenience binaries" either. Besides, a list of packages and licenses for each new digest would be needed, that is, a new check in CI, and Debian's sources, as GPL-2 requires on distribution in the form of object code: "Accompany it with the complete corresponding machine-readable source code" or a written offer to give them (`/usr/share/common-licenses/GPL-2` in the same image).
- **A base of our own without GPL** — `scratch`, our own `/etc/passwd`, tzdata in the binary. R105 above rejected it, and the Mozilla certificates in it would still remain under MPL-2.0.

*Consequence:* the item "Consequence" above about the licenses of the base's packages is settled by this. RULES.md, the rule "Production images", says that NovaTrail publishes no images.

— *Amendment 2026-11-07:* where the image is built, R106 decided: in the deployment of `infra`, from the binary and the `Dockerfile` of the service's release. The item "Not decided here" and the words "Т-19 still decides" in the amendment above no longer hold: Т-19 is closed. Whether anyone signs the image itself R106 does not ask — the image does not leave the private registry, and the release files it is built from are signed. — R106.

It is still not part of the entry: it is not in production, and NovaTrail does not publish it.** The mismatch was found during the amendment to R30. — R31; R143; RUN.md, T131.

## Deployment

**R106. `infra` rolls out the services and the build of `app`, by one list of exact versions and digests. The deployment of `infra` builds a service's image from the files of its release. Т-19 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-07, outside an epic, by the recommendation of Т-19 and of the executor.
- **Who rolls out.** `infra`, by a list of exact versions and digests — of both the services and the build of `app` (repositories 3; Т-19). A component's repository rolls out nothing itself and has no access to production: the projects and Workload Identity Federation for CI are with `infra` (architecture 3.11).
- **A service's image** is built by the deployment of `infra`:
  1. it takes from the release of the service that the list names the binary and the `Dockerfile` — files of the release (the 2026-11-07 amendment to R105) — and checks them with `release-verify` (R77);
  2. it builds the image by this `Dockerfile`, on the base by digest (R105). What the service puts into the image beyond the binary, its own code does at the build stage. For `api` these are the module packages by `modules.json`, embedded in the binary, — by the same command with which the first app puts them into a folder (R07 api). The deployment does not repeat the logic of the packages;
  3. it puts the image into the private Artifact Registry of `infra` and rolls out a Cloud Run revision by the image's digest (R105).

  This is how canvas-api rolled out: the server from the release with a checked signature, "an image around it", a push and a revision by digest (`docs/self-hosting.md` of canvas-api; R45, R58 canvas-api).
- **The build of `app`** is rolled out by the same list, as Т-19 has already been extended. The rollout checks the archive's signature, writes `/deployment.json` and releases the build, the file and the CSP header in one release of the hosting (R85; R09 app).
- **A rollback** — as Т-19 was extended: `api`, and while the module format is v0 also a build of `app` that has moved to a new format version, roll back only forward. Everything else rolls back by a revert of the list.
- **Self-hosting** takes the same list and the same path of deployment in its own project (architecture 3.11).
- **Left to `infra`, to task T02:**
  - the format and place of the list and who edits it;
  - what the rollout checks before the deployment;
  - whether to reject a release of `api` lower than the one rolled out (Т-19).

— *Why:*
- Access to production stays in one repository. `infra` already has the projects and WIF for CI, and a service's release comes out of a public repository by the shared workflow of `.github` (architecture 3.11).
- The build path is one — for the platform and for self-hosting. Self-hosting cannot take NovaTrail's private image (R105), and both go through the build in the deployment the same way.
- One place shows what is running — this is the recommendation of Т-19. `api` and `app` come out in one list when the open view changes (repositories 4).
- The image's logic stays with the service — in its `Dockerfile` and code — and the deployment only executes what the release signed.

— *Rejected:*
- **The service's release builds the image** and puts it into the private registry, and `infra` rolls it out by digest. Then each service repository needs access to the production registry, and self-hosting builds its own image anyway — there would be two build paths.
- **Each repository rolls itself out by its release, like canvas-api.** In NovaTrail the releases come out of different repositories (R10), and what is running would be seen only by all of them at once.
- **The code of the deployment of `infra` puts the module packages into the image** — then the logic of `api` (R07 api) would live in two repositories.

— *Consequence:*
- repositories 8 — Т-19 is closed;
- architecture 3.11 — the card of `infra`;
- R105 — its item "Not decided here" about the place of the build is settled by this decision;
- `infra` takes the decision as an input to T02 when it moves to a new tag of `spec`.

— R10, R45 canvas-api, R58 canvas-api, R77, R85, R105; R07 api; R09 app; Т-19.

## The outcome of the detailing of `engine`

**R107. The detailing of `engine` is decided, and `spec` records its outcome. The age category is a filter of `api`, not an input of the engine, and there is no daily goal among the inputs. A skill chosen on the skill map holds until the learner asks for something else, and the record of the choice carries it into the next one. "At once" of R82 means "not as the next task". `ReasonCode` has a ninth value, `REASON_CODE_ROTATION`, "in rotation". The record of the choice also keeps the skill from the map, the age category and the mark of the engine's modules, and the seed in it is empty: the engine takes no randomness. The summary of issues comes with additions that R104 did not see. Т-10 is extended with the engine's side and stays open. The checks of identical bits are an option of the shared `go.yml`, and the test of the code rules a shared tool of `.github`.** The author's answers of 2026-11-07 to the rows «в реестр spec» `engine` В5–В15 (RUN.md `engine`, `main` b962ff4) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, all by the rows' recommendations. В5 and В14 the author decided in this triage. The other rows the author decided while planning T02–T06 and T09–T10 of `engine`, and the executor carries them here; the name `REASON_CODE_ROTATION` from В10 the author also confirmed in this triage. In detail — R03–R10 engine and architecture 3 engine.
- **The age category** (В5): the modules, the lessons and the pool of tasks `api` already selects by `age_categories` — a module by its audience, a lesson only as a whole, a task only for a learner of its categories (R07 api; [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15), — and the engine gets only what suits the learner. So the category leaves the engine's constraints in concepts 12, and `api` keeps it for the pool too, as for lessons. In the record of the choice it stays — for the repeat (below).
- **A skill from the map** (В6): a choice from the map holds until the learner asks for something else. `ChooseNext` without a skill returns "My subjects". The record of the choice keeps the chosen skill and carries it into the next one, and `api` calls the engine with it both for `next` and at the end of a run — whatever code the choice came out with, `REASON_CODE_OPEN_RUN` too (R04 engine). Without the field the skill cannot be restored: the lesson of an open run goes with `REASON_CODE_OPEN_RUN`, and only an item has a primary skill (concepts 6).
- **A lesson's band** (В7): the proposal of `modules` (Д90 of RUN.md; architecture 3.8) is accepted, with an answer to what it left to the engine. A lesson's band is the set of the bands of its tasks: a lesson with a verdict suits a skill when the band of its recommended task is in this set; a lesson without tasks suits any band; a lesson of another band does not hold the order (R05 engine).
- **"At once"** (В8): R82 says not to give "again at once" a task whose solution went to the device, and after how long — `engine` decides. The engine has 24 hours, and when the choice has given nothing, a second pass gives such a task too, after the others, but not the task of the last closed attempt (R03 engine, the 2026-11-07 amendment). So "at once" means "not as the next task", and the rest is the engine's pause.
- **The daily goal** (В9): it is neither in the profile nor in the contract ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15) — only in the prototype ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)), — and the engine's rule does not read it (R06 engine). It leaves the engine's constraints in concepts 12 until the product says what it means and where it is kept.
- **"In rotation"** (В10): three places of the rule had no exact code — branch 8 (all the reachable ones are mastered, no dates have come), the queue at "the bottom of the ladder" (no skill is reachable) and a skill "mastered" by the model whose recommended task went above the mastery band: `REASON_CODE_QUEUE` requires "within reach" and "not mastered". They get one value, `REASON_CODE_ROTATION` = 9: "Rotation: a skill given before comes round again, the one not given for longest first, though it does not fit the queue of `REASON_CODE_QUEUE`: it is mastered, or no skill is within reach". Two comments are made more precise, and the meaning of their values is as before ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 2): for `REASON_CODE_QUEUE` "not given for longest" is within its module (R04 engine), and for `REASON_CODE_NEW_SKILL` — "whose prerequisites the engine's rule counts as met, or which has none". The rule opens a skill with a prerequisite counted as met, not mastered, too: an anchor "unknown", a cycle, a prerequisite there is nothing to teach with, a prerequisite with `rubric` or `none` counted by a lesson (R03–R05 engine). The words of the code for an adult are written by `app` (R100).
- **The record of the choice** (В11): to repeat a choice without AI, it lacked three fields, and one was superfluous. (1) The field "seed" is empty as long as the engine takes no randomness, and it takes none (R07 engine): that this is so is seen by the version of `engine` in the same record. (2) The record also keeps the skill from the map (В6), the profile's age category at the time of the choice, and a mark of which of the digests are the engine's modules, connected and suiting the learner. The category changes at the yearly refinement and at a change of country (concepts 13), the connections at any time, and the digests also name the modules of the log, which only `learner-model` gets. (3) The last attempt and its outcome the repeat derives from the records of choices and attempts before the time of the choice, as it does the summary of issues (R104). This adds no learner's data: the category and the connections are already with `api` (privacy 1, 4).
- **The summary of issues** (В12): R104 recorded the row В3 `engine` in the revision of `main` 479d0b7, and it did not see the additions that T10 and T02 of `engine` and the author's decision while planning T04 made afterwards. They are: (1) the issue of a lesson is the issue of each of its skills: so a lesson moves the queue "not issued for the longest" and the module's time of issue (R05 engine); (2) for a module, the number of choices, of a task and of a lesson one each, not of tasks issued: the tasks of a lesson do not move the counter of the probe's turn, and the turn does not skip (R04 engine, the 2026-11-07 amendment); (3) for a skill, the outcome of the last closed attempt if it is a probe or a repetition: a correct repetition of an unreachable skill returns it from a pause, like a correct probe (R06 engine); (4) the result on the skill comes as facts, not as a mark "correct": how many items where the skill is primary got a first verdict, at how many of them it is "correct" and whether the solution was shown. The engine computes "failure" by its own rule (R03, R09 engine), and the rule does not live in `api` as well.
- **Т-10** (В13): extended with the engine's side and stays open. The recommendation is as before — compute on the server. `engine`, like `learner-model`, gives the same choice and the same code on any build of one version, WebAssembly too, is built for the device as it is and checks this in CI from the first code (R10 engine). How it works offline — a computation on the device or a queue the server has chosen in advance — stage 5 decides.
- **The checks of identical bits** (В14): Д86 promised that the shared `go.yml` would take the runs of arm64 and js/wasm as an option if `engine` takes them too. Now both libraries take them (R09 learner-model; R10 engine). So as an option of `go.yml` go the runs on the targets — amd64 with GOAMD64 v3, with v1 with `GODEBUG=cpu.all=off`, 386, js/wasm through Node and the wasip1 build, — the differential check of the assembler `fma-diff` and the job on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. Then the test of the code rules on `go/types` also becomes a shared tool of `.github` with lists per repository, instead of two copies of `rules_test.go`. Until `.github` answers, `engine` has its own port, as the author decided in T05 `engine`.
- **Card 3.8** (В15): the engine's items in "To decide when detailed" are decided, and the items beyond the card are written into its text. The rule of repetition — R06 engine, the anchor skill — R04 engine, a task with a seen solution — R03 engine and В8, lessons — R05 engine, the build for the device — R10 engine; the corridor, the prerequisites and the queue — R03 engine, several modules, the modes and the constraints — R04 engine, the reason codes, the seed and the repeat of a choice — R07 engine, the types — R09 engine. There is no consolidation in a lesson and no early end in the first slice, and `api` does not call the engine at the end of a segment (R05 engine), so the card's paragraph about them is removed. At the input are runs without the places of the finished segments, and of the attempts with a rubric only those closed by "Done" (R09 engine). The items' traps are with the engine's candidate, and the row of T04 to `learner-model` was not needed: the graph and the task description cover everything (R09 engine).

— *Why:*
- the category is a filter of `api`: `api` already keeps this rule, and for the engine the category decides nothing. There is as much learner's data in the call as the rule reads (privacy 1);
- a skill from the map holds — so a topic chosen by a person held in standalone: `lesson_topic` in the profile, until it is reset (SPEC 3.6 standalone). A field of the record, not of the profile: the repeat of a choice sees only the record;
- the band is a set of bands: a lesson has no band field, and `modules` rejected it; the band of the recommended task leads the lesson after the learner as they grow;
- "not as the next" — the key goes to the device after a correct answer too (R82), and the lessons of the first slice hold all the tasks of a skill and band: without the second pass the learner would hear "nothing to give" with a non-empty pool;
- without a daily goal — the rule cannot read it, and the day's goal is what an adult sees;
- one value, not three: the three places have one essence for an adult — the skill came again in rotation, not because it is being worked on. A new value is new words in `app` in all the interface languages, and three values would distinguish what an adult does not need to know. Branch 8 stays: without it, with one module the learner would hear "nothing to give" with a non-empty pool;
- three fields of the record — without them the repeat will not restore the input, and a snapshot of the whole input would keep twice as much learner's data as the rule reads;
- the result as facts — the rule "failure" is one, for the model and for the engine (R06 learner-model), and a mark from `api` would be its second copy;
- Т-10 is open — offline has a path without computation on the device at all, and stage 5 chooses it (product 11);
- shared checks — the two libraries have the same checks, and two copies of the rules test can diverge;
- the card is a summary, and it must not say what has been decided otherwise (RULES.md, Across repositories).

— *Rejected:*
- a filter by age in the engine — `age_categories` in the task description of `learner-model` and the category in the input;
- a skill from the map as a field of the profile — the repeat does not see it; a choice from the map for one choice;
- a lesson of only one band; a field `band` of a lesson;
- "at once" as 24 hours without exceptions; more tasks in the pool from `modules` instead of a second pass;
- a daily goal as a field of the profile and an input of the engine — an amendment of the contract, of `api` and of privacy 4, and one more rule;
- three values "all mastered", "the bottom of the ladder", "a new band of the mastered"; removing branch 8;
- a snapshot of the whole input in the record; only the skill from the map in the record — an old choice will not repeat after a change of the category or the connections;
- the summary as R104 recorded it: a lesson does not move the queue, the turn of the probe after a lesson shifts by the number of its tasks, a correct repetition does not return from a pause, and "correct" is decided by `api`; the engine computes the summary by itself — it has no input "records of choices";
- closing Т-10 now;
- only options of `go.yml`, and each library has its own rules test; everything its own for each library;
- amending only the items "To decide when detailed", and the rest when the code comes; not touching the card.

— *Consequence:*
- `contracts/novatrail/api/v1/cause.proto` — `REASON_CODE_ROTATION` and the refined comments of `REASON_CODE_NEW_SKILL` and `REASON_CODE_QUEUE`, buf's code; [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15, — the new code, a skill from the map in `ChooseNext`, consolidation in a lesson and "early" not in the first slice;
- concepts 12 and 15; architecture 1, 3.5 and 3.8; privacy 4; repositories 8 — Т-10;
- the 2026-11-07 amendments to R82, R100 and R104;
- RUN.md — Д114: what `engine`, `api`, `app`, `sim` and `.github` take; Д90 is closed; the rows `engine` В5–В15 are in table 5.

## Requests of `modules` to the format from the rest of the port

**R108. The requests of `modules` to the format from the rest of the port go into format 0.4, in epic E6, beside the rules of R102. A handwritten choice gets an optional mark: with it a word not among the options gets "not yet". A check kind `time` appears — a time `H:MM`, equal by minutes. In the path of a template's picture there are placeholders. A task gets an optional closed leading question: `api` gives it on "Hint" before the first incorrect answer, and the evidence carries it.** The author's answers of 2026-11-08 to the rows «в реестр spec» `modules` В28–В31 (RUN.md `modules`, `main` 997e281) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, all by the triage's recommendations. В30 — by the row's recommendation, В28 and В31 — with the triage's refinements, and В29 is decided otherwise than `modules` recommended. The rows' claims were checked during the triage. The numbers of В28 and В29 are by the tasks of `olympiad-math` 0.1.1 at commit 73c79af of `modules`, counted 2026-11-08: a handwritten choice — in 74 tasks, of them 30 times and 44 words; by tapping — 18 days of the week, 2 months, 6 dates and 3 times in a phrase. The numbers of В31 are by `content/examples/` of [mathtrail-standalone at commit 42b4408](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/tree/42b4408), read 2026-11-08: a hint `hint` is in 311 tasks of 753, and in band 5–6 in each of 272. Normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 15, 19, 20 and 23, and the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), when E6 amends them.

- **В28 — a mark on a handwritten choice.** The mark is optional, and without it a handwritten choice stays as it was. With the mark each option is one word of letters, and this is a new rule. The value first loses `.`, `!` and `?` at the end. One word of letters that is not among the options gets "not yet" and gives a rung, like an incorrect number. Everything else, as now, is "not in notation" and "unreadable". Traps stay values from the options. T38 gives the mark's name.
- **В29 — the check kind `time`.** The key is a time `"H:MM"`. A value is in notation when after steps 1–5 of the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15, it is `H:MM` or `HH:MM`: hours 0–23, minutes 00–59. It is compared with the key by minutes, so `07:30` is correct with the key `7:30`. The trap values are times in the same notation. The leak search finds the key with a leading zero too. Whether to read `7:30` and `19:30` as one time T38 decides by a parameter of the kind. Dates, days of the week and months stay a tapped choice.
- **В30 — an instance's picture.** In the path of the picture of a template's statement and solution there are placeholders of parameters and derived numbers — `pictures/split-{total}-{parts}.png`. There are no placeholders of the solver's result there: the path is open, and the result stands only in closed fields ([format text](../format/README.md), section 24). An instance has numbers in its path, and its file is held by `task.known-pictures`: the task's rule is checked on every instance anyway ([format text](../format/README.md), section 23). Outside a template there are no braces in a path (`task.placeholders`). The path of each picture of an instance is among the texts in which `task.no-leaks` looks for the task's keys.
- **В31 — the leading question.** The optional field of a task `leading_question` is the author's question that breaks the task down, in the module's explanation language. The field is closed. `api` gives it on "Hint" before the first incorrect answer, together with the task's techniques, and records it as a technique (the 2026-11-08 amendment to R82). `task.no-leaks` looks for the task's keys in it, as in `givens`, and in a template there are placeholders in it. It does not change the ladder and the fallback texts.

— *Why:*
- all this is new rules, not a refinement of the text, so, as with R102, they go into 0.4 and E6: the format changes once, and `module-kit` moves once. Each change, by the [format text](../format/README.md), section 2, only adds;
- В28: an incorrect word is an ordinary error, not an unreadable answer. The word of the answer stands in the question (R20 modules), and the learner copies it. The mark is only for options that are words, and a full stop at the end is removed: otherwise `Kim.` and `07:30` would get "not yet" for a correct answer, and a false alarm is worse than the absence of a check (R04);
- В29: all 30 handwritten times are tasks of the skill `time-clocks`, where the time is computed, like "It is 7 o'clock. What time will it be in half an hour?". A choice compares text, and time is computed in minutes. The subject that the recommendation of `modules` waited for already exists;
- В30: the number of instances is finite, `module-kit` already enumerates them and holds the rule of pictures on each, and the file may be any picture (R51);
- В31: before the first error band 5–6 now has only "givens and unknown" and the techniques, and standalone's hints are already written and checked. The field is closed because it hints at the method more strongly than a technique (R57). Its name is different: "hint" in concepts 15 is the tutor's words, and one term means one thing.

— *Rejected:*
- В28: a mark for any value not among the options, as in the row — `Kim.` and `07:30` would get "not yet" for a correct answer (R04); a new kind "word" without options — traps have nothing to bind to; leaving it as it is — 44 tasks without rungs for an incorrect answer;
- В29: time under the mark of В28, as `modules` recommended — "not yet" for `07:30`; time by tapping — guessing 1/5 (concepts 11; R05 modules); leaving it — 30 tasks of `time-clocks` without rungs;
- В30: a picture that `canvas` draws by the instance's data — R51 rejected it: 13 schemes and drawers for one module; leaving it — 6 templates are not carried over (R22 modules), and 4 have no picture;
- В31: the field `hint` — the name is taken by the tutor's words; an open field, like `givens`, — it hints at the method (R57); the text of rung 2 — it would change the order of the fallback texts of R82, and before the first error the learner will not see it; merging into `simpler_case` — a simpler case is something else; leaving it — 311 written hints would be lost;
- an amendment to R102 instead of a new decision: R102 is about the code of `module-kit`, and these are requests of content;
- a 0.y of its own before E6: the format and `module-kit` would change twice.

— *Consequence:*
- RUN.md: the row E6 of table 2 — four requests; Д121; the rows `modules` В28–В31 are in table 5;
- the 2026-11-08 amendment to R82;
- with E6, when 0.4 comes out: the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 15, 19, 20 and 23; concepts 10, 11 and 15 — the term "leading question"; architecture 3.5 and 3.8; the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md) and `novatrail.api.v1` — the leading question in the answer to "Hint".

— R04, R44, R51, R57, R82, R83, R102; concepts 11 and 15; R05, R07, R12, R20 and R22 modules; RUN.md, E6, Д121.

The content of `modules` at `main` ea2a2ba diverged from them: options that are phrases — in 29 tasks with a handwritten word of 44, traps with minutes from 60 — in 14 of 30.
