## The data region

**R109. The platform's data region is the United States, one place for all learners: Cloud Run and everything `infra` keeps in a region — `us-east4` (Ashburn, Virginia), Neon — `aws-us-east-1` (N. Virginia). П-11 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-08 to the row «в реестр spec» `infra` В3 (RUN.md `infra`, `main` 9e857a3) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, option (a), by the row's recommendation; the author also chose it while planning T01 `infra`. The sources are architecture 2.1 and 4 `infra` (`main` 9e857a3), read by `infra` 2026-11-08.
- **The region of each resource** (architecture 2.1 infra):
  - the Cloud Run services and jobs and the Artifact Registry repository — `us-east4`, regional;
  - the Secret Manager secrets — with user-managed replication, at the place `us-east4`, not regional: a regional secret is accessible only from its own region — "Regional secrets can only be accessed by applications or services running within the same location" ([Regional secrets and data residency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/regional-secrets/data-residency), updated 2026-10-26), — and the eval key under Т-28 would be read by CI on GitHub;
  - the log bucket — `us-east4`, and the sink `_Default` is directed into it; `_Required` — in `global`, as long as there is no Google Cloud organization: "Logging automatically creates two log buckets: _Required and _Default, which are in the global location. You can't change the location of existing buckets" ([Regionalize your logs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/regionalized-logs), updated 2026-10-16), and the place of new buckets is set only by an organization setting (Д3 infra; О-16);
  - the trace bucket `_Trace` — created in `us-east4` before the first trace: observability buckets have no `global` ([Observability bucket locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/observability/observability-bucket-locations), updated 2026-11-06);
  - Neon — `aws-us-east-1`; Firebase Auth processes data only in the United States in any region, and Firebase Hosting, if T03 `infra` chooses it, is a global service ([Privacy and Security in Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy), read 2026-11-08).
- **What does not change after creation:** the place of the log bucket, of the Artifact Registry repository — "settings that cannot be changed after the repository is created: … Repository location" ([Create standard repositories](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/repositories/create-repos), updated 2026-11-07), — of a secret with user-managed replication and of the Neon project. The place of `_Trace` only a reprovision changes: "You can't modify the location" ([Update observability buckets](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/update-observability-buckets), updated 2026-11-06), and "Reprovisioning is a destructive operation" ([Cloud Trace release notes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/trace/docs/release-notes), 2026-11-06): the traces are lost in a move.
- **The region of AI calls** is not part of R109: `tutor` and privacy 5 decide it, if the author wants (R96). Anthropic has inference only in the United States — `inference_geo: "us"` at a price of 1.1x — and OpenAI has data residency by approval (architecture 4 infra).
- **The price of the EU later** is a new project, a new Neon project and new buckets with a transfer of the data.

— *Why:*
- the EU gives the first slice nothing: the account owner's sign-in goes through the United States in any region (Firebase Auth), and the slice does not accept learners from the EU and the United Kingdom before the DPIA (П-2);
- one place gives the admission function no new input: the region is not its input (R96);
- `us-east4` has Tier 1 prices, and `europe-west3`, near Neon in Frankfurt, Tier 2 ([Cloud Run locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/locations), updated 2026-10-30); `us-east4` and `aws-us-east-1` are both in Northern Virginia, and R54 canvas-api decided the same way.

— *Rejected:*
- **The EU, one place** — Cloud Run `europe-west3` and Neon `aws-eu-central-1`, both in Frankfurt: Tier 2 and no Cloud Run domain mapping, and `europe-west1` and `europe-west4`, with Tier 1 and domain mapping, are not near Neon; Neon `aws-eu-west-2` (London) — without some of the functions ([Regions](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/regions), "Last updated: 2026-10-14"). Domain mapping itself is Preview and not recommended for production, so it does not decide the choice;
- **by learner, both places** — two projects, two Neon databases, two sets of buckets, and the admission function gets a new input, that is, a major version of the admission table (R96).

— *Consequence:*
- privacy 9 — П-11 is closed; privacy 5.1 — the region is named;
- architecture 1, card 3.11 and table 3.12 — the region instead of "П-11";
- row 6.9 of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md) — the region is decided;
- Д126 — what `infra` takes, Д127 — what `api` takes; the row `infra` В3 is in table 5 of RUN.md.

— R54 canvas-api, R57 canvas-api, R96; R03 and R05 api; П-2, Т-28, О-16; Д3 infra.

## Synthetic data and viewing a module's samples

**R110. Synthetic data for a module's tasks is the generator of `canvas` on the module package of the commit where the samples go, and a sample is viewed before a push on the samples page of `canvas`, in the mode "open a file".** The author's answers of 2026-11-08 to the rows «в реестр spec» `modules` В32 and В33 (RUN.md `modules`, `main` 0d2655f) — the inbox triage by rule 13 of RUN.md, by the rows' recommendations.
- **Synthetic data** (В32): `synthetic` of `canvas` (`src/eval/synthetic.ts`, the recipe `just synthetic`; R49 canvas) takes the open views of tasks from the module package, as `module-kit build` writes it, at the commit where the samples go — the call gives the package — and writes samples with the source `modules`: the module ID, the version and digest of this package and the tag of the newest release of `modules`, since the tag is not checked ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 13); `PURPOSE_EVAL_SET`, Apache-2.0, an ID from the seed, markup. The call names the tasks and seeds, and the seeds are those not yet in the module's eval set, and `modules` puts the files as `eval/<id>.json` (R25 modules). The kinds are those the generator draws: sheets and the workbook; essays — when `canvas` begins to draw them. The code of a sample from a seed stays with `canvas` (R38).
- **Viewing** (В33): the samples page of `canvas` opens a sample file in the same build, without a network: it shows the strokes of the final geometry, the crops and the texts of the markup, changing nothing, saving nothing and calling no AI. So the eval-set organizer and the module's author look in a sample for a name, a signature and contacts before a push, and neither an AI nor an agent looks at it (П-12; [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 11; R26 modules).

— *Why:* a pull request that changes the open view of a task remakes its samples in the same pull request (the 2026-11-06 amendment to R04 modules), and the runner of stage 2 will check the task on synthetic data at the same time as it changes. `canvas` already reads a sample file with its `src/eval/` and draws these strokes and crops (R48 canvas), the page works without a network and calls no AI, and the implementation is one for everyone who contributes samples.

— *Rejected:* synthetic data on the package of a release of `modules` — the synthetic data of a changed task would be lost until the next release; the generator as a library of `canvas`, and the script of the call in `modules` — the code of a sample would split across two repositories; without synthetic data — the module's eval set would hold only people's samples, by the form and with a manual check (R04 modules); viewing by a recipe of `spec` that writes an HTML page, or by a recipe of `modules`' own — a second implementation of what the page of `canvas` already draws.

— *Consequence:* the cards architecture 3.2 and 3.10 — a new link of `canvas` with the module package at stage 1 and the mode "open a file"; Д128 — what `canvas` and `modules` take; the rows `modules` В32 and В33 are in table 5 of RUN.md.

— R25, R38, R93, R95; R04, R25 and R26 modules; R48 and R49 canvas; П-12.

## The contents of format 0.4

**R111. The contents of format 0.4 are decided before the first change. The word mark on a handwritten choice is `notation: options | word`: with `word` the key and the read value are one word of letters, and the options stay phrases. The kind `time` admits into notation minutes from 60 too, compares hours and minutes as numbers and knows no 12-hour dial. A worked example on the workbook is in 0.4, with its own leak rule. A list of steps in a lesson's explanation is the part `numbered_list`.** The author's answers while planning RUN.md, T38, 2026-11-08, all by the plan's recommendations. The numbers are by `modules` at `main` ea2a2ba, `canvas` at `main` 73807f2 and `module-kit` at `main` aa7686c, read 2026-11-08. Normatively — the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 15, 20 and 21, when T82, T83, T87 and T89 amend them.

- **The word mark (В28 `modules`; T82).** The check field `notation` of a handwritten choice, `options` or `word`, by default `options` — as it was. With `word` the key is one word of letters, and the value first loses `.`, `!` and `?` at the end (R108). A value that is one word of letters not among the options is "not yet" and a rung, like an incorrect number. A phrase not among the options is "not in notation", as now. Traps stay values from the options, and an option may be a phrase.
- **The kind `time` (В29; T83).** A value is in notation when it is `H:MM` or `HH:MM` after steps 1–5 of the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15, with minutes of two or three digits. The key has hours 0–23, minutes 00–59. A value is correct when its hours and minutes as numbers equal the hours and minutes of the key: `07:30` is correct with the key `7:30`. The kind does not compute the sum of minutes, and minutes from 60 are "not yet", while a trap value may have them. There is no parameter of 12 or 24 hours: `7:30` and `19:30` are different times.
- **A worked example on the workbook (В19 `modules`; T89).** The `workbook` canvas of an example is the example's lines with boxes, and the demo fills the boxes step by step, on the page rule of T88. `lesson.no-leaks` finds a leak when a line of the example with its values equals a line of a task of the lesson with its keys: the example solves the lesson's task. The search for numbers does not see separate numbers of the example's lines.
- **A list of steps (В21 `modules`; T87).** The part of a lesson's explanation `numbered_list` is texts in order, and the app draws the numbers, and the search for numbers does not see them. The term of concepts 15 is "numbered list" («нумерованный список»).
- **What before v1** — in the row of epic E8 of table 2 of RUN.md, not in table 4: what to remove at v1.0 because no module of the first slice uses it, and the questions at the version's boundary (R44).

— *Why:*
- the mark: of the 44 tasks with a handwritten word, the options are one word in 15, and in 29 they are phrases, almost always traps: "It is impossible to tell" — in 27, "Ben and Kim", "red or blue". `modules` rejected rewriting them (the amendment to R20 modules): a child writes "It is impossible to tell" by hand without trouble. An incorrect word of an answer is a name from the statement that is not among the options: "Maya", "Amy", and where the statement writes "Alice (A)" — "A". The name `notation` is the term of concepts 15 "notation" («допустимая запись»): the mark changes exactly what is in notation. There are no boolean fields in the format, and switches are enumerations with a default value, like `form: any | reduced`;
- `time`: 14 tasks of `time-clocks` have the trap `time-unit-mixup` — "an hour has 100 minutes": `5:60`, `7:70`, `10:100`. By the letter of R108 they would be "unreadable" and lose the trap text, and with a comparison by the sum of minutes 7 of them would equal the key or another trap: `5:60` = `6:00`, `7:95` = `8:35`. The module writes time by 24 hours, "at 18:40… go out?" — `21:10`, and in two tasks of time zones `9:00` and `21:00` are different answers. No trap equals its key modulo 12 hours;
- the example on the workbook: in the lessons of `grade-3-math` there is not a single digit. `lesson.no-leaks` looks in each text of a lesson for the keys of the tasks of its pages, and for division with a remainder the keys are 0–8, for the multiplication table 4–64. With the search for numbers as now, "17 ÷ 5 = 3 r 2" would be a leak, and no example could be made. An example's leak is a task of the lesson solved in it, not a number in it;
- the list of steps: in all 41 lessons of `olympiad-math` the explanation ends with "How to solve: …" and three steps without numbers (R14 modules): the search for numbers would read "3." as a number. `steps` are the solving steps of a task, and one term means one thing.

— *Rejected:*
- the mark by the letter of R108 — it would work in 15 tasks of 44; asking `modules` to rewrite the options — `modules` rejected this; `form: any | word` — it would extend the "form rule" of a fraction; a boolean field — the first in the format, and R45 is silent about booleans;
- `time` by the letter of R108 — 14 traps "unreadable"; a comparison by the sum of minutes — `5:60` is correct with the key `6:00`; a parameter of 12 or 24 hours now — no task needs it. Where a learner answers by the 12-hour dial, `modules` sets a trap, `9:10` for `21:10`, and the parameter will come by a minor change when the content asks for it;
- an example on the workbook with the search for numbers as now — no example could be made; putting the example off until after 0.4 — one more move of all the repositories, and `canvas` cannot do the demo yet and will make it as a task of its own, with 0.4 too;
- `method_steps` — two kinds of steps beside `steps`.

— *Consequence:*
- the 2026-11-08 amendment to R108;
- RUN.md: the bodies of T82, T83, T84, T87, T89 and T90; the row E8 of table 2; Д121;
- with E6, when 0.4 comes out: the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 15, 20 and 21; concepts 15 — "numbered list"; a row of table 4 with T90 — what `canvas` (the demo of an example on the workbook), `modules` (`notation`, `time`, the traps of 12 hours) and `module-kit` take.

— R04, R14, R20 and R22 modules, R44, R45, R51, R57, R58, R102, R108; concepts 15; RUN.md, E6, T38.

## Legal analysis and the data before the first child

**R112. The platform has no lawyer: legal questions are decided by the author on Claude's analysis. Claude reads the primary sources — the text of a law, a rule or guidance of a regulator, a provider's terms — and gives for each question a quote with the date read, the risks, the options and a recommendation, and the author takes the decision. The analysis is not legal advice, and the risk of an error, in children's law among others, is the author's. So it is everywhere, and at the public launch too.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning epic E4 (RUN.md, epic E4, «Решено автором»), not by the plan's recommendation.
- **What the analysis gives:** for each claim about a law or terms — the primary source, a quote and the date read (RULES.md, The bar). What was not confirmed, or where the primary source is silent, is not claimed, but stays an open question with options (RULES.md, How we work). Where sources diverge or the text of a law allows two readings, the analysis names both and which one the recommendation chooses.
- **What the author decides:** each question of the registers «П» and «О» that earlier waited for a lawyer — with options and a recommendation, as any open question. The decision is recorded in the log, as the others are.
- **How to read the earlier entries:** «решает юрист», «вопрос юристу», «после ответа юриста», «проверка юристом» in the entries before this decision and in the archives `docs/plan/` read as the author's decision on Claude's analysis. The entries of the log are not rewritten; the documents where this sounds like a rule in force are corrected (RUN.md, T92), and the rows of the register privacy 9 — when the tasks of E4 T93–T95 close their question. The deployment fact `minor_safeguards`, which the operator declares "only once a lawyer has said the safeguards are enough", is in T94, together with the admission table (R96).
- **The risk** is named plainly: in the law of children's data an error is costly — COPPA, GDPR and the Age Appropriate Design Code punish the operator, not whoever analysed. Claude's analysis may misread a law, may not know a decision of a court or a regulator that is not in open sources, and does not replace the responsibility of a licensed lawyer to a client.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-11-09. The «П» questions waited for a lawyer for weeks by the calendar, while their primary sources are open, and an analysis of them with quotes and dates is the same work that the documents already do for the providers' terms (privacy 5.3).

— *Rejected:* Claude's analysis up to and including the closed beta, and a licensed lawyer before the public launch — the plan's recommendation: the closed beta with the children of families we know is already under COPPA and GDPR, but the risk in it is smaller than at the public launch; a licensed lawyer before the first child.

— privacy 9; product 10; RUN.md, epic E4, T92.

**R113. A learner's artifacts — essays, drawings, recordings — are stored on the server only if the account owner turned this on for the profile; by default storage is off. Storage once on is turned off in one step, and turning it off erases the copies on the server, and the artifacts themselves go into the export. П-8 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T92 (RUN.md), by the register's recommendation, with the default "off" — by the plan's recommendation.
- **When.** Storing essays on the server comes with the essays module, before the first child (the 2026-11-02 addition to П-8; В9 `app`): otherwise the only copy of a work depends on the browser's rules. Until then, and in a profile where storage is not turned on, the page "This device" in the section for adults and the sign-out warn of the loss (R04 app).
- **What is stored:** the artifact itself, as the device holds it — the strokes and the picture of the work —, not the read text and not the words of the feedback. The server does not read the artifact and does not give it to an AI provider: an essay is assessed by the picture of the work from the device (privacy 5.1). R87 stays: of an essay's attempt the server stores only the marks of the criteria, and the read text and the words of the feedback are nowhere on the server ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15); the stored artifact is not part of the attempt, but a work that the adult asked to keep.
- **What changes in the promises:** "what the learner writes by hand stays on the device" (privacy 7) is true while storage is not turned on, and the privacy policy (RUN.md, T97) speaks of this choice. With storage on, a child's admission in an essay of harm to themselves or from others lies on the server, but nobody reads it — this is question П-20, the analysis of T95.
- **Who turns it on:** the account owner, for each profile separately. A child neither turns storage on nor turns it off.

— *Why:* we collect a minimum of data (privacy 1), and storage on the server is an adult's choice, not a default. An adult to whom it matters not to lose works turns it on with one tap.

— *Rejected:* storage on by default, with the adult turning it off — more children's data on the server without an adult's choice; never — the only copy depends on the browser; always.

— privacy 1, 4, 6, 9; R41, R87; R04 app; П-8.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **what the storage switch says and on what basis what an essay discloses about health is stored — R127.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T95 (RUN.md).

— *Second amendment 2026-11-09:* **a learner who gives consent themselves — above the age of digital consent of their country — turns storage of their works on and off themselves, in their own profile, and this is their explicit consent; the account owner does not turn storage on for them.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in carrying out T98 (RUN.md), by the recommendation. — R116, R127, R132.

— *Amendment 2026-11-10:* **the storage switch is the method `SetWorkStorage`: turning it on is a consent by the text `storage-consent` with its version, by an adult action, and for a learner who gives consent themselves, by their learning request; the storage consent record lives while the profile lives, and turning it off writes its date.** The author's answer of 2026-11-10 in planning T103 (RUN.md), by the recommendation: after the profile is deleted the works are gone already, and the child consent is proved by the minimal record of R117. Rejected: keeping the record for 5 years after as well — without the profile ID there is nothing to link it to the works, which are gone already. In detail — R136.

**R114. Development agents — Claude Code, Codex and any others — get no learners' works, no eval samples that lie outside the repositories, no signed volunteers' forms and no records of them. The provider's training on the agent's data is turned off, and where this depends on the plan, the agent works on a plan where the provider does not train on the data. П-12 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T92 — the plan approved whole (RUN.md, T92, «Решено автором»), by the register's recommendation.
- **What is in the repositories:** synthetic samples and samples that adult volunteers and authors made for eval lie openly in the modules, as the modules themselves do (R02), and the agents see them. There are no learners' works in the repositories (RULES.md, Hard rules).
- **Anthropic, Claude Code** ([Data usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage), read 2026-11-09): "Commercial users: (Team and Enterprise plans, API, 3rd-party platforms, and Claude Gov) maintain existing policies: Anthropic does not train generative models using code or prompts sent to Claude Code under commercial terms, unless the customer has chosen to provide their data to us for model improvement"; for the plans Free, Pro, Max and Ultra — "We will train new models using data from Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra accounts when this setting is on", and the setting is [claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls](https://claude.ai/settings/data-privacy-controls). So: on commercial terms there is no training; on a plan for individuals the setting is turned off, and `/feedback` and consent to show a session in a quality survey are not given — they pass on the whole session.
- **OpenAI, Codex** ([How your data is used to improve model performance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5722486-how-your-data-is-used-to-improve-model-performance); on 2026-11-09 the page answers 403, and its copy in the Wayback Machine of 2026-11-01 was read — whether it has changed since was not checked, and the decision turns off both settings anyway): "By default, we don’t use inputs or outputs from ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Edu, or our API to improve our models"; for the plans for individuals — "turn off Improve the model for everyone under Settings > Data controls in ChatGPT, or select Do not train on my content in our Privacy Portal. Either option is sufficient for ChatGPT conversations and Codex tasks", and "Codex has a separate Include environments setting in Codex settings for allowing training on full environments. Changing your settings in ChatGPT or the Privacy Portal does not change that setting". So: on a plan for individuals both settings are turned off.

— *Why:* an agent reads everything it was given and gives it to the model's provider; it needs no learners' data to write the platform's code.

— *Rejected:* no restrictions; only a ban on training, without a ban on access — the data would go to the provider with training turned off as well, with its retention periods.

— privacy 9; R02; R04 modules; П-11 canvas-api; П-12.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **development agents get no scans of signed parental consent forms either: the operator keeps them outside the repositories and outside the database of `api` (R116).** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to a finding of the review of T93 (RUN.md), by the recommendation. — R116, R117.

**R115. A self-hosted copy shows the texts of its own operator: the policy, the consents and its name are given by the copy's `api` without a token, and `app` shows them as its own pages, without external links. The platform gives the texts of the part `legal/` of `spec`, and a copy's operator gives their own. Who is the controller of a copy's learners' data the author decides on the analysis of T93 (R112). П-24 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T92 — the plan approved whole (RUN.md, T92, «Решено автором»), by the register's recommendation — the recommendation of `app` (В29 `app`).
- The [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15, says so already: `app` asks `api` for the texts, naming the language in a field of the request, and the texts themselves are in English only (privacy 7).
- The texts change without a rollout of the build: the build of `app` is one for the platform and for the copies (R09 app), and the platform's texts in it would name the wrong one as the operator.

— *Why:* the text that an adult accepts names whoever is responsible for the data — the operator of this copy; and the build is one for all and signed, so the texts must come not from it but from the `api` of the copy whose operator wrote them.

— *Rejected:* the operator's name and contact in `deployment.json`, and the texts in the build — the build would carry texts that do not suit another copy; the texts in the build, and a copy rebuilds `app` — a copy would take not the same signed build as the platform.

— privacy 7, 9; R85, R98; R03 api, R09 app; П-24.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the controller of a self-hosted copy's learners' data is its operator, and the platform's author is neither a controller nor a processor, as long as the copy sends them no data and they do not set its purposes: no telemetry from the copies, no hosted service that the copies call.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T93 (RUN.md), by the conclusion of the analysis (R112). GDPR Art. 4(7): the controller is whoever "alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data". EDPB [07/2020](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/2023-10/EDPB_guidelines_202007_controllerprocessor_final_en.pdf), v2.1, read 2026-11-09: para. 67 — choosing another's tool "for its own purposes" may be a joint decision on the means, and footnote 29 — "The provider of the system can be a joint controller if the criteria mentioned above are met, i.e. if the provider participates in the determination of purposes and means"; para. 68 — there is no joint control "where the processing they carry out is separable and could be performed by one party without intervention from the other". So the platform's code sends a copy's data neither to the author nor to the platform. — R115; architecture 3.11.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-09:* **a copy keeps the texts of its own operator as a folder in the layout of [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md) — `VERSION`, `legal.yaml` and `texts/` — and checks it with `spec`'s recipe `legal-check-dir`; the copy's `api` reads it by the path from its configuration and does not start if the folder breaks the part's rules, and without a path gives the platform's texts from `spec.Legal`. There are no placeholders in the texts.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T96 (RUN.md), by the recommendation. — R130.

**R116. The lawful basis under GDPR: an adult's own learning data — contract, Art. 6(1)(b), and the data of a learner under 18 — consent, Art. 6(1)(a): below the age of digital consent of the country it is given by a parent (Art. 8), and under 13 also the verifiable parental consent under COPPA; above this age — by the learner themselves. Verifiable parental consent is now a signed form whose scan the operator checks, and before the public launch a card transaction with a notice to the holder is added to it. Consent is withdrawn as easily as it is given. What is mandatory in a consent is given briefly in the interface language, and the full text, the one in force, in English. П-1 is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 in planning T93 (RUN.md), all by the recommendations of the analysis (R112). Read 2026-11-09: GDPR — [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32016R0679); the EDPB guidelines [05/2020 on consent](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/system/files/documents/files/file1/edpb_guidelines_202005_consent_en.pdf), v1.1, and [2/2019 on Art. 6(1)(b)](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/sites/default/files/files/file1/edpb_guidelines-art_6-1-b-adopted_after_public_consultation_en.pdf), v2.0; WP260 rev.01 on transparency, endorsed by the EDPB; COPPA — 16 CFR 312 as amended by the FTC's 2025 rule ([90 FR 16918](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-04-22/html/2025-05904.htm), published 2025-04-22, in effect from 2025-06-23, compliance from 2026-04-22; the text of the part by the eCFR API as of 2026-11-05, the eCFR page answers with a bot check); ICO — the pages on children and UK GDPR by copies of the Wayback Machine of 2026-04-28, the site answers 403.
- **An adult's basis is contract.** Art. 6(1)(b): "processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party". An adult's learning is exactly what they ordered: the learner model, the choice of tasks and the checking do not work without them (EDPB 2/2019, para. 26 — the contract, its validity and necessity). Improving the service cannot be justified so (para. 49), and the platform does nothing of the kind on this basis.
- **The basis under 18 is consent.** A contract on behalf of a child is not taken: Art. 6(1)(b) requires a contract to which the data subject themselves is a party, EDPB 2/2019 para. 13 refers to national law on children's legal capacity, and the ICO writes of a parent's contract on behalf of a child: "you should again take legal advice". Legitimate interest is rejected: Art. 6(1)(f) — "in particular where the data subject is a child". Art. 8(1) applies, "Where point (a) of Article 6(1) applies, in relation to the offer of information society services directly to a child", and a service for all ages with children's profiles the ICO considers offered to children directly: "when any age restrictions in place allow users under the age of 18". The age of digital consent is by country, by the table of T100: GDPR — 16, a country may lower it to 13 (Art. 8(1)); UK GDPR — 13 ([Art. 8](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2016/679/article/8), read 2026-11-09). EDPB 05/2020 paras. 147–149: the learner confirms, changes or withdraws the parent's consent on reaching the age of digital consent, and the platform tells them of it. **A learner above this age gives their own consent themselves, in their own profile in `app`, before the first work, and withdraws it there too;** the profile is created by the account owner, but they do not give consent on behalf of a learner older than the age of digital consent. In the same way a child who has reached this age confirms the parent's consent or withdraws it at the yearly update of the category (privacy 3.3). The methods — RUN.md, T103. The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to a finding of the review of T93, by the recommendation.
- **The method of verifiable consent.** COPPA §312.5(b)(1): the method "must be reasonably calculated, in light of available technology, to ensure that the person providing consent is the child's parent". From the list of §312.5(b)(2) — (i) "a consent form to be signed by the parent and returned to the operator by postal mail, facsimile, or electronic scan" now, as in R26 canvas-api, and (ii) "in connection with a transaction, to use a credit card, debit card, or other online payment system that provides notification of each discrete transaction to the primary account holder" — before the public launch; EDPB 05/2020 gives the same argument for Art. 8(2) — "a payment of €0,01 … via a bank transaction" (footnote 68), and para. 137: "In low-risk cases, verification of parental responsibility via email may be sufficient. Conversely, in high-risk cases, it may be appropriate to ask for more proof". A child's work goes to an AI provider, so the risk is not low.
- **The scan of the signed form** is kept by the operator — outside the repositories and outside the database of `api`, in their own storage, with access only for themselves —, while the consent is in force and 5 years after the deletion, as the record of R117, and then erased. The form does not ask for the child's name — only the ID of the consent record. Development agents do not get the scan (R114). COPPA: what was obtained from the parent at consent the operator keeps confidential (FAQ, A.8, a copy of the Wayback Machine of 2026-10-13); GDPR: the proof of consent — no longer than needed (EDPB 05/2020 para. 107). The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to a finding of the review of T93, by the recommendation.
- **Email plus and text plus** (§312.5(b)(2)(viii), (ix)) — only for an operator to whom "discloses" of §312.2 does not apply. An AI provider that only reads the work for the platform's service and for nothing else is "support for the internal operations", not a third party (§312.2, the definitions "Disclose" and "Third party") — Claude's reading, the rule does not name AI providers expressly. A provider that trains models on the data is a third party, and a disclosure to it requires a separate consent: the FTC in its commentary to the rule — "Disclosures of a child's personal information to third parties … to train or otherwise develop artificial intelligence technologies, are not integral … and would require consent". So email plus would hold only while no provider has crossed this line — and it is rejected.
- **Withdrawal.** Art. 7(3): "It shall be as easy to withdraw as to give consent"; EDPB 05/2020 para. 114 — by the same interface, without a fee and without losing the service. How this fits into the contract — RUN.md, T103.
- **The notice to the parent** (§312.4(c), (d)): what is collected and why, to whom it is disclosed and why, the retention policy (§312.10), how to give consent and how to withdraw it, the parent's rights — this is written by the texts of T97 and T98.
- **The language — an amendment to the author's decision of 2026-11-02 in privacy 7.** The new argument is WP260 rev.01, para. 13: "A translation in one or more other languages should be provided where the controller targets data subjects speaking those languages", and the interface of `app` is in Russian too (footnote 15: "where the controller operates a website in the language in question"). Art. 12(1) — "clear and plain language", EDPB 05/2020 para. 70 — "A controller must assess what kind of audience it is". What is mandatory in a consent — who the operator is, which data and why, to whom they go, how to withdraw — `app` shows briefly in the language of the screen, as the "bite-sized" explanations of AADC std 4, and the full text, the one that is accepted and that is in force, in English. The translation is a text of the set `legal/` (RUN.md, T96), not the interface dictionary.

— *Why:* one basis per age that holds under both GDPR and COPPA: parental consent under COPPA is needed under 13 on any basis, and a contract with a child rests only on the country's law.

— *Rejected:* consent for all — withdrawing an adult's consent would mean the end of the service, and consent suits poorly what the service cannot exist without; legitimate interest; email plus; a verification service — knowledge questions or a document with a face (§312.5(b)(2)(vi), (vii)) — it collects more data than needed (EDPB 05/2020 para. 145), and costs money; for the language — full translations of the policy and the consent — they would have to be kept in step in all languages; English only — the consent of a parent who reads Russian may be deemed uninformed.

— privacy 3, 4, 7, 9; R26 canvas-api; R98; RUN.md, T93, T96–T98, T100, T103; П-1.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **"in their own storage" for the scan of the signed form is the operator's private Cloud Storage bucket in the project `infra`, `us-east4`, under its own prefix, with access only for the operator (R125).** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T95 (RUN.md). — R125; architecture 3.11.

— *Amendment 2026-11-10:* **the form names not the ID of the consent record but the request code — 10 characters of Crockford base32 in two groups, `ABCDE-FGHJK`, which `api` gives, unique among the waiting ones; the parent uploads the scan in `app` (`SendConsentForm`), and `api` puts it into the private bucket of this record, where the operator checks it against the code with their command of `api` and confirms the consent or does not accept the form; the scan of a withdrawn waiting consent is erased with it. A card transaction by the public launch is the open question П-28.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 in planning T103 (RUN.md), by the recommendations. *Why:* a UUID of 36 characters copied by hand onto paper is copied with errors, and the upload in `app` is one path to the bucket, without the operator's mailbox. *Rejected:* a letter to the operator — one more processor and retention period, which are hard to keep; paper by post — slow, and the operator's address is needed (П-27); choosing a payment provider now — the public launch is far off. In detail — R136.

**R117. The minimal record of a child consent — the record's ID, the date, the method of verification and the date of deletion, without the account and profile IDs, the pseudonym, the age category and the country — is kept for 5 years after the deletion of the account or the profile and erases itself. An adult's consent and a consent "waiting" are deleted whole. The period is in the written retention policy and in the privacy policy. П-14 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T93 (RUN.md), by the recommendation of the analysis (R112).
- GDPR Art. 7(1): "the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented"; Art. 5(2) — accountability; Art. 17(3)(e) — erasure does not apply while the processing is needed "for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims". EDPB 05/2020 para. 107: "After the processing activity ends, proof of consent should be kept no longer then strictly necessary for compliance with a legal obligation or for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims".
- COPPA sets no period for the consent record. §312.10 requires a written retention policy with the purposes, the need and the time of deletion, and a child's data "may not be retained indefinitely". The record holds no child's data, and what was obtained from the parent at consent the FTC tells to keep confidential (FAQ, A.8, a Wayback copy of 2026-10-13).
- The period is by the statute of limitations: 28 U.S.C. § 2462 ([Cornell LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/2462), read 2026-11-09) — "shall not be entertained unless commenced within five years from the date when the claim first accrued". That this general period holds the FTC's penalties under COPPA too is Claude's reading, not the text of the rule.
- The record can be linked to a family only through the export file held by the owner and the scan of the signed form held by the operator, which is kept for the same period (R116; П-14, the 2026-11-02 addition).

— *Why:* without the record the platform has nothing to prove the consent with after the deletion, and with a record longer than the statute of limitations it has nothing to justify the retention with.

— *Rejected:* 3 years — shorter than the statute of limitations; erasing it together with the account — nothing to prove the consent with; keeping it indefinitely — against §312.10 and Art. 5(1)(e).

— privacy 4, 9; R21 api; architecture 4.5; П-14.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the same minimal record also remains of the own consent of a learner under 18 who gave it themselves — after the withdrawal or the deletion of the profile, for 5 years.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in carrying out T98 (RUN.md): the withdrawal deletes the profile, and the learner's consent needs proving just as the parent's consent does (Art. 7(1)). — R132.

**R118. П-6, П-22 and П-23 are closed by the register's recommendations: the account owner's adulthood is their statement "I am 18" with a date, and for a child's profile the method of consent itself confirms it; voicing on Android and Linux is a choice of the system that the adult makes; the device's clock offset is not geolocation but account data, of which the policy speaks.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 in planning T93 (RUN.md), by the recommendations of the analysis (R112).
- **П-6.** EDPB 05/2020 para. 135: "In some low-risk situations, it may be appropriate to require a new subscriber to a service to disclose their year of birth or to fill out a form stating they are not a minor"; AADC std 3: "if you provide a logged-in or subscription based service, you may allow the main (confirmed adult) account holder to set up child profiles" (a Wayback copy of 2026-09-26). The signed form and the card transaction (R116) confirm also that the consent is given by an adult. A country where the law requires more than a statement `api` closes before the attempt (privacy 9, П-6).
- **П-22.** Chromium sets `is_local_service = !voices[i].remote` (`speech_synthesis_impl.cc`), and on Android and Linux gives a voice only `native = true` (`tts_android.cc`, `tts_linux.cc`; [chromium.googlesource.com](https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src), branch `main`, read 2026-11-09): every system voice there is given to the page with `localService` true, and the page cannot tell the network synthesis of the system's engine. Android lets only the app itself know this — `Voice.isNetworkConnectionRequired()` ([Android Developers](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/speech/tts/Voice), read 2026-11-09). The text is given to the synthesis engine by the browser by the adult's choice, as to their screen reader, and the platform has no agreement with the engine's provider.
- **П-23.** COPPA §312.2 names as personal information "Geolocation information sufficient to identify street name and name of a city or town"; an offset from UTC in minutes names a time zone, not a city. The ICO's code, std 10 — "data taken from a user's device which indicates the geographical location of that device, including GPS data or data about connection with local wifi equipment" — is silent on time zones (a Wayback copy of 2026-10-04). The offset is tied to the account, so it is account data (§312.2, para. 11), and the policy speaks of it.

— *Why:* none of the three questions required more than is decided already: the statement and the method of consent — the EDPB and the ICO allow them at low risk, and for children's profiles the confirmation is given by the method of consent; voicing and the offset the platform does not turn into geodata or a disclosure by its own actions.

— *Rejected:* П-6 — an age verification service; П-22 — no voicing on Android and Linux for children; П-23 — a time zone that the adult chooses (rejected by R11 api: an extra step).

— privacy 3.3, 6, 9; R04 api, R11 api, R07 app; П-6, П-22, П-23.

**R119. A DPIA — before the first child, wherever they live, and before the first learner from the EU or the United Kingdom, if one comes earlier — by the task of E4 T105, by the ICO's template. П-2 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T93 (RUN.md), by the recommendation of the analysis (R112). The ICO's code, std 2: "Undertake a DPIA to assess and mitigate risks to the rights and freedoms of children who are likely to access your service … Take into account differing ages, capacities and development needs", and the code applies to a service outside the EEA if "you offer your service to users in the UK … The code applies if that service is likely to be accessed by children" ("Services covered by this code"; copies of the Wayback Machine of 2026-09-26 and 2026-10-30, the site answers 403). GDPR Art. 35 requires an assessment when the processing is "likely to result in a high risk". The ICO: "A data protection impact assessment should help you to decide what steps you need to take to verify age and parental responsibility" — so the DPIA records too why the methods of consent and of age verification are proportionate to the risk (R116, R118).

— *Why:* the platform is open to children of any country, and a child's work goes to an AI provider; an assessment before the first child is cheaper than reworking after them, and the texts of T98 and T99, on children and on samples, rest on it.

— *Rejected:* a DPIA at stage 3, by the beta and the public launch — a closed beta with children of the United Kingdom would go outside std 2; only before the first learner from the EU or the United Kingdom — the recommendation of П-2 before the code; a DPIA inside T93 — it would not know the outcomes of T94 and T95.

## The eval key in CI

**R120. The platform's keys for eval (R24) lie in the Secret Manager of `infra` — a secret per AI provider, `eval-key-<provider code>`: `eval-key-anthropic` and `eval-key-openai` —, and the CI of `modules` and `tutor` reads them through Workload Identity Federation, by its own pool `github-eval`, with no long-lived copy in GitHub. The pool admits only the job of the GitHub environment `eval` of these two repositories and does not admit Dependabot; the pool of `bootstrap.sh` with the provider `github` and the deployment accounts stays only with `infra` (R13 infra). On a pull request from a fork and from Dependabot the eval job fails and names the reason, and a maintainer carries a Dependabot change over into their own branch and opens their own pull request from it. Т-28 is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 to Т-28 (RUN.md, T106), by the recommendations, and the own pool — by a finding of the review; the primary sources were read 2026-11-09.
- **The place.** The Secret Manager of the project `infra`, with user-managed replication, with the location `us-east4`, and not a regional secret (R109): "Regional secrets can only be accessed by applications or services running within the same location" ([Secret Manager, Regional secrets and data residency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/regional-secrets/data-residency), updated 2026-10-26), and a GitHub runner is not in this location. A secret with user-managed replication "has its payload data replicated to a user configured set of locations" ([Choosing a replication policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/choosing-replication)). The values are put in by the author — `gcloud secrets versions add` —, not by code (RULES.md, Hard rules); each key has its own spending limit at the provider, set by the author, and the price of a run is named before the first launch (R24, "Consequence"; rule 4 of RUN.md). A new eval provider is a new secret in the module of `infra`, by the provider code of the admission table (R96).
- **The own pool.** The pool `github-eval` and its provider `github` are described by the OpenTofu module of `infra` (T22), not by `bootstrap.sh`: the pool of `bootstrap.sh` admits only the tokens of `infra`, and `bootstrap.sh` at each run returns its provider's condition to its own (R13 infra), and in it are the production deployment accounts. In the pool `github-eval` there is nothing but access to the eval secrets. The mapping is `google.subject=assertion.sub`, and the provider's condition is `assertion.repository_owner_id=='344507087' && (assertion.repository_id=='1425775415' || assertion.repository_id=='1425813274') && assertion.environment=='eval' && assertion.actor!='dependabot[bot]'`: the numeric IDs of `altnovatrail`, `modules` and `tutor` (the GitHub API, read 2026-11-09), because "Using "name" fields like repository and repository_owner increases the chances of cybersquatting and typosquatting attacks … use the numeric *_id fields instead" ([Workload Identity Federation with deployment pipelines](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines), updated 2026-11-07), and "Always add an Attribute Condition to restrict entry into the Workload Identity Pool" ([google-github-actions/auth](https://github.com/google-github-actions/auth), README, branch `main`).
- **The sign-in.** Direct Workload Identity Federation, without an intermediary service account: "Without this input, the GitHub Action will use Direct Workload Identity Federation" (the README of `auth`; the latest release v3.0.0 of 2025-08-28, the tag on 7c6bc770dae815cd3e89ee6cdf493a5fab2cc093), and Google advises the same: "we recommend that you grant direct resource access to the principal" (ibid.); Secret Manager supports direct access — "No known limitations" ([Supported services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/federated-identity-supported-services)). Each eval secret gets `roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor` for two principals of the pool `github-eval`: `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/<project number>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/github-eval/subject/repo:altnovatrail@344507087/modules@1425775415:environment:eval` and the same with `tutor@1425813274`. The immutable `sub` is already turned on for `modules` and `tutor` (`use_immutable_subject: true`, the GitHub API `actions/oidc/customization/sub`, read 2026-11-09).
- **Who reads — the environment `eval`.** "The subject claim includes the environment name when the job references an environment" ([GitHub Docs, OpenID Connect reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc)), so the key goes only to a job with `environment: eval`, and other jobs of the same pull request do not get it. The environment's branch rule is "Selected branches and tags": `main` and `refs/pull/*/merge`, because "The deployment branch or tag rule is matched against the `GITHUB_REF` of the workflow run. … Adding another branch rule for `refs/pull/*/merge` would also allow workflows triggered by `pull_request` events to deploy to the environment" ([Deployments and environments](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments)); without it a pull request's job does not enter the environment. The environment has no reviewers: eval runs on every pull request, and the spending is held by the key's limit at the provider.
- **A fork.** `modules` and `tutor` are public. For a pull request from a fork "the permissions are adjusted to change any write permissions to read only" ([Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)), and `id-token` — "This requires `id-token: write`" (ibid.), so it has no OIDC token; the exception is the setting "Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests", and it exists only for "forks of private repositories" ([Managing GitHub Actions settings for a repository](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/enabling-features-for-your-repository/managing-github-actions-settings-for-a-repository)).
- **Dependabot can get an OIDC token:** "By default, GitHub Actions workflows triggered by Dependabot get a `GITHUB_TOKEN` with read-only permissions. You can use the `permissions` key in your workflow to increase the access for the token" ([Troubleshooting Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/troubleshooting-dependabot/troubleshooting-dependabot-on-github-actions)). So two places hold it back: the provider's condition refuses a token whose `actor` is `dependabot[bot]`, and the first step of the eval job fails and names the reason if the pull request is not from a branch of the repository itself (`github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.repository`) or was opened by Dependabot (`github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'`) — by the pull request's author, not by `github.actor`, which names whoever started the run (the 2026-10-20 amendment to R24; R05 .github).
- **A Dependabot change.** A maintainer reads it, puts Dependabot's commit into their own branch of the repository, opens their own pull request from it — the job runs in their name —, and closes Dependabot's pull request. There is no Dependabot secret with a copy of the key: "Secrets are populated from Dependabot secrets. GitHub Actions secrets are not available" ([Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-on-actions)), and it would be a second long-lived copy.
- **What each does:**
  - `infra` (T22): the pool `github-eval` and the provider `github` with the condition above; the secrets `eval-key-anthropic` and `eval-key-openai` without values, with user-managed replication in `us-east4`; the `secretAccessor` bindings to the two principals; tests. The pool of `bootstrap.sh` and R13 infra do not change;
  - `modules` and `tutor`: the environment `eval` with the branch rule `main` and `refs/pull/*/merge`, without reviewers; the eval job — `environment: eval`, `permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }`, the first step is the check of the fork and of the pull request's author, then `google-github-actions/auth` by SHA, with the `workload_identity_provider` of the pool `github-eval` and without `service_account`, and the reading of the secrets;
  - the author: the values of the keys, their spending limits at the providers, and before the first run — the price (rule 4).

— *Why:* the key is one per provider and lives in one place, and GitHub gets only a token for ten minutes — "the resulting token has a maximum lifetime of 10 minutes" (the README of `auth`); the own pool separates the pull requests of the two repositories from the production deployment accounts, and the environment separates the eval job from the other jobs of the same repositories.

— *Rejected:* an eval environment secret in each repository — a long-lived copy of the key in GitHub in two places; a Dependabot secret — one more copy; the shared pool of `bootstrap.sh` with a widened condition — the original recommendation, against R13 infra: the production pool with the deployment accounts would open to the pull request jobs of the two repositories, and only the precision of the bindings would separate them; a separate Google Cloud project for eval — a second project with a bootstrap, a state and a budget, while the own pool gives isolation too; a binding by `sub` without the environment — any job of any workflow would get the key; a condition by `job_workflow_ref` — the workflow file is edited in a branch, so the boundary is the same, and there is no setting visible in GitHub; one JSON secret with all the keys — changing one key would change them all; a maintainer's commit into Dependabot's branch — after it Dependabot stops rebasing the pull request, and the check by the pull request's author would not let the job in anyway.

— R05 .github, R11 and R13 infra; R24, R96, R109; architecture 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12; RUN.md, T106; Т-28.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the pool `github-eval` and its provider `github` are made by `bootstrap.sh` of `infra`, not by the OpenTofu module; the module makes the secrets `eval-key-…` and the rights to them. The provider's condition, the environment `eval` and what `modules` and `tutor` do — as above.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to the row «в реестр spec» `infra` В15 (RUN.md of `infra`, `main` e7516a0), by its recommendation; the author decided the same in planning T22 `infra`.
- A pool in the module would require for `infra-config` a role on the project's pools, and IAM conditions do not narrow pools: `iam.googleapis.com` is not among the services with resource attributes (Google Cloud, IAM Conditions, resource attributes, updated 2026-11-07; read by `infra`). With such a role `infra-config` could change the condition of the pool through which it enters itself, and it borrows the deployment accounts already — against R13 infra.
- "Are described by the OpenTofu module of `infra` (T22), not by `bootstrap.sh`" in the item "The own pool" reads so: the pool is its own, separate from the CI pool, and it is made by `bootstrap.sh`.
- *Why:* the boundary is the same, and `infra-config` gets no rights over its own door. *Rejected:* a role on the pools for `infra-config` with an amendment to R13 infra; a separate project for eval — R120 rejected it. — R13 infra; architecture 3.11; RUN.md, Д149.

## AI providers

**R121. The processor agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic enter their terms by themselves, and for OpenAI the author also signs a copy by a form; zero data retention the author asks of both now, and while the provider has approved neither it nor the exclusion of content from the abuse monitoring logs, the fact `minimal_retention` does not hold and platform AI is closed to all. `tutor` calls only the paths that zero data retention covers, and the models of Anthropic that need retention of 30 days are outside the list of models admitted for learners' works. What zero data retention does not lift the privacy policy names. The part of П-3 about agreements and retention is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T94 (RUN.md), by the recommendation of the analysis (R112). Read 2026-11-09.
- **OpenAI's DPA.** Services Agreement, §5.3: "If Customer uses the Services to process Personal Data, OpenAI and Customer will comply with the DPA, which is incorporated by this reference into the Agreement"; the DPA — "supplements, and is incorporated into, the OpenAI Services Agreement", "Updated: December 1, 2025", "Effective: January 1, 2026", and §1.1 — "OpenAI acts as a Data Processor on the Customer’s behalf". On the DPA's page there is the link "Execute Data Processing Agreement", an Ironclad form, for a signed copy. openai.com answers 403: copies of the Wayback Machine were read — the [Services Agreement](https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement) of 2026-11-07 and the [DPA](https://openai.com/policies/data-processing-addendum) of 2026-10-28. The DPA does not speak of children.
- **Anthropic's DPA.** The [Commercial Terms](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms), "Effective Jun 17, 2025", section C: "Data submitted through the Services will be processed in accordance with the Anthropic Data Processing Addendum ("DPA"), which is incorporated into these Terms by reference"; the [DPA](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum), "Effective Feb 24, 2025": "Customer is the controller and Anthropic is Customer's processor"; section B: "Anthropic may not train models on Customer Content from Services". Neither speaks of children.
- **OpenAI's zero data retention** ([Data controls in the OpenAI platform](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data), no date): "these controls are subject to prior approval by OpenAI and acceptance of additional requirements", the application — "Get in touch with our sales team". Covered are `/v1/responses` and `/v1/chat/completions`, where "the store parameter … will always be treated as false", and `/v1/files`, `/v1/conversations`, `/v1/assistants`, `/v1/vector_stores` and `/v1/batches` are not. It does not lift: "Image and file inputs are scanned for CSAM content upon submission. If the classifier detects potential CSAM content, the image will be retained for manual review", and "Safety Retention" — "we may retain and human review customer content when using these models that our classifiers detect as potentially violating our Usage Policies". Without zero data retention — "abuse monitoring logs are generated for all API feature usage and retained for up to 30 days", and Responses keeps the state for 30 days unless `store` is `false`.
- **Anthropic's zero data retention** ([API and data retention](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/api-and-data-retention), no date; [Zero data retention](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/8956058), updated 2026-10-15): "To request ZDR for your organization, contact the Anthropic sales team", "subject to Anthropic's approval"; covered are Messages and Token Counting, while Batch — "29-day retention", the Files API and the Console are not. It does not lift: "Anthropic still retains User Safety classifier results", and "if a chat or session is flagged, Anthropic may retain inputs and outputs for up to 2 years" and the classifiers' scores — "for up to 7 years" ([7996866](https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/7996866), updated 2026-07-01). The models "Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, and Claude Mythos 5: These models require 30-day data retention and are not available under ZDR unless expressly authorized by Anthropic" ([Covered Models](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15425695), updated 2026-09-01). The pages on default retention diverge — 30 days in 7996866 and "not retained by default" in API and data retention —, and the decision does not rest on this: the fact is held by an approved zero data retention.
- **What `tutor` does:** at OpenAI — Responses with `store: false` and the picture in the body of the request, without `/v1/files`; at Anthropic — Messages, without the Files API and Batch; the Covered Models are outside the list of models admitted for learners' works until Anthropic permits them under zero data retention.
- **Admission table 0.2** takes this into the descriptions of the facts: `data_processing_agreement` holds when the agreement is in force — signed or part of terms the platform accepted — and nothing in it excludes requests of learners of the declared categories; the cells refer to R121–R123 instead of the closed П-3, П-4 and П-15, and the date the terms were read is 2026-11-09 for each.
- **The author's step** (rule 4 of RUN.md): sign a copy of OpenAI's DPA by the Ironclad form and submit applications for zero data retention to the sales of OpenAI and Anthropic — the texts of the applications are written by Claude (RUN.md, T94). The price and the "additional requirements" are not published: before signing anything, the author names them.

— *Why:* without zero data retention a child's work lies at the provider for 30 days, and OpenAI requires it for under 13; the application is the only path, and it is worth submitting before it is needed.

— *Rejected:* an application to one provider first — without the second, two readers of different providers cannot be assembled (Т-33); the paths that zero data retention does not cover — the Files API and Batch.

— privacy 5.1, 5.3, 9; R07, R96; П-3.

**R122. An own key is only for a profile of the category `adult`; to a learner under 18 it is closed at all providers. П-4 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T94 (RUN.md), by the recommendation of the analysis (R112); `api` does so already (R04 api; О-4).
- The key's owner is the provider's "Customer". OpenAI: the Services Agreement is for "customers who are businesses and developers", and by §3.3(c) the Customer does not allow "minors to use OpenAI Services without consent from their parent or guardian"; zero data retention for under 13 (privacy 5.3) — only by the approval of sales, which a family's key does not have. Anthropic: "individuals and hobbyists are welcome to use the Claude API. However … use of the API is subject to our Commercial Terms of Service, regardless of whether you are an individual or representing a company" ([8987200](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8987200), updated 2026-03-16), and "Customer is responsible for all activity under its account" (Commercial Terms, D.5). With an own key a family would become an organization serving minors, with its measures (R123), which it will not carry out.

— *Why:* the obligations to the provider would fall on the family, and the platform cannot carry them out for it.

— *Rejected:* opening the own key to a learner of 13–18 above the age of digital consent, with the platform's measures — by the terms the key's owner is obliged to keep the measures anyway.

— privacy 5.2, 9; R84; R04 api; О-4; П-4.

**R123. The measures for minors that OpenAI and Anthropic require the platform keeps as a list per provider, with the status of each; to the provider's measures it adds its own — an adult's "report a problem" at the tutor's answer and an escalation path with the operator with a review period —, and it does not monitor the content of works itself. When all of a provider's measures are met, the author decides by analysis that they are sufficient (R112), and only then does the operator declare `minor_safeguards`. П-15 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T94 (RUN.md), by the recommendation of the analysis (R112).
- **OpenAI** ([Under-18 API guidance](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-checks/under-18-api-guidance), read 2026-11-09, no date): "Providing age-appropriate disclosures to minors about AI tools and how to use them responsibly", "Implementing age-appropriate content filters", "Implementing reasonable monitoring and reporting mechanisms, including escalation paths for high-risk interactions", "Where required or otherwise appropriate for your use case, using age assurance systems"; and "OpenAI reserves the right to audit organizations for compliance with this policy. Customers who fail to demonstrate compliance may receive warnings and, in cases of repeated or serious noncompliance, may be subject to suspension or termination of API access". The [Usage Policies](https://openai.com/policies/usage-policies), "Effective: November 20, 2026", a copy of the Wayback Machine of 2026-11-06: "Keep young people safe", and among the prohibitions — "inference regarding an individual’s emotions in the workplace and educational settings, except when necessary for medical or safety reasons" and "automation of high-stakes actions in sensitive areas without human review … education".
- **Anthropic** ([Guidelines for organizations serving minors](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9307344-responsible-use-of-anthropic-s-models-guidelines-for-organizations-serving-minors), updated 2026-03-16): "Age verification systems", "Content moderation and filtering", "Monitoring and reporting mechanisms to identify and address potential issues", "Educational resources and guidance for minors", "a child-safety system prompt, which organizations serving minors should implement", COPPA and a statement about it on the site, "Organizations must disclose to their users that they are interacting with an AI system rather than a human"; and "Anthropic will periodically audit organizations for compliance with these safeguards". The [Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup), "Effective Nov 12, 2026": "Products serving minors … must comply with the additional guidelines outlined in our Support article and all applicable laws", and "We define a minor or child to be any individual under the age of 18 years old, regardless of jurisdiction".
- **The list of measures and who keeps them:**
  - the disclosure that the learner is talking to an AI, and educational materials on safe use — `app`, to all learners (R54 tutor);
  - filters — the safety rules in all prompts of `tutor`, the safety system prompt for minors by Anthropic's article, and the safety item in the eval sets;
  - monitoring — at the provider, and at the platform — an adult's report at the tutor's answer and escalation: the report goes to the operator, who reviews it within the period the policy names and, if a child is threatened with harm, acts by the escalation path that the texts of T98 and П-20 (T95) will name;
  - age verification — the method of parental consent and the age category (R116, R118);
  - COPPA and a statement about it — the privacy policy (T97, T98);
  - zero data retention at OpenAI for under 13 or under the age of digital consent — the fact `zero_data_retention` (R121);
  - there is no inference of the learner's emotions anywhere: `tutor` does not call a model to judge the learner's feelings, and the verdict is given by a program, not by AI (R03), so the platform does not automate "high-stakes actions … without human review".
- **The providers' audits.** Both companies may check whether the platform carries out these measures, and suspend access: the list with the statuses is what the platform will show them.

— *Why:* both companies name "monitoring and reporting mechanisms", and OpenAI also "escalation paths for high-risk interactions": without its own report and escalation path the platform would have nothing to show at an audit, and nobody would see a child's admission of harm (П-20).

— *Rejected:* monitoring only at the provider, as R54 tutor; its own input filter and the platform reading the works — against the minimum of data (privacy 1).

— privacy 5.3, 9; R03, R96, R112, R116, R118, R121; R54 tutor; П-15, П-20.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **receiving an adult's report is a method of the contract `app` ↔ `api`, by the task of E4 T103, together with the consent: the attempt ID and the place of the tutor's answer, a word of a closed set and the adult's text. `api` stores the report in its database until the review and for a period after — the period is named by T103 by privacy 4 —, and the operator reads it with their command of `api`.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В43 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` 9f50a43), by its recommendation. *Rejected:* a letter to the operator at the address from the texts — the content of the work would go where the deletion of the account does not erase it (privacy 4), and a link outward would break privacy 7. — RUN.md, T103; Д155.
