## Samples, eval sets and essays

**R124. The writing history in a sample from the samples page — the time, the pressure and the course of the pen — is biometric data. It occurs only in measurement samples from adults, with explicit consent under Art. 9(2)(a) GDPR that names it, is never published and serves nobody to identify the writer. The final geometry is personal data, but not biometrics, and the make-up of the file by R09 canvas and the eval protocol (R93) does not change. There is no child's grade in the file: the band of grades is held by the record of the measurement organizer. An adult is one by the statement "I am 18 or older, and under the laws of where I live I may make this agreement". Item (c) of the DCO, when item (a) is certified in the form, and the field `license` are fit. П-18 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T95 (RUN.md), by the recommendations of the analysis (R112); the sources were read 2026-11-09 (privacy 10).
- **Biometrics:**
  - GDPR Art. 4(14): "'biometric data' means personal data resulting from specific technical processing relating to the physical, physiological or behavioural characteristics of a natural person, which allow or confirm the unique identification of that natural person". Art. 9(1) prohibits the processing of "biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person", and photographs, by recital 51, are biometrics "only when processed through a specific technical means allowing the unique identification or authentication of a natural person";
  - WP29, WP193, 27 April 2012, §4.4.6: "While traditional signature recognition relies on the analysis of static or geometric characteristics of the visual image of the signature (how the signature looks like), signature biometrics instead refer to the analysis of dynamic characteristics of the signature (how the signature was made)", and among these characteristics — "the amount of pressure, the angle of writing, velocity and acceleration of the pen";
  - the ICO, "Biometric recognition" — by a copy of the Wayback Machine of 2026-09-25, the site answers 403, and the page is marked "under review" after the Data (Use and Access) Act: "Behavioural characteristics can include a person's handwriting, how they type", and "specific technical processing" is an operation "which makes it possible to uniquely identify them";
  - EDPB 3/2019, v2.0, para. 74: "processing of raw data … must imply a measurement of this characteristics";
  - COPPA, §312.2, personal information (10): "A biometric identifier that can be used for the automated or semi-automated recognition of an individual, such as fingerprints; handprints; retina patterns; iris patterns; genetic data, including a DNA sequence; voiceprints; gait patterns; facial templates; or faceprints". Handwriting is not in the list, but the measure is "can be used for", not the use;
  - the CCPA, Cal. Civ. Code 1798.140(c), by the text of the California Privacy Protection Agency, names as biometrics also "keystroke patterns or rhythms". BIPA, 740 ILCS 14/10, excludes "writing samples, written signatures", but this was read by a copy at FindLaw: ilga.gov did not open, and it was not checked against the primary source.
- **Claude's reading.** The writing history carries the very dynamics that WP193 calls signature biometrics. The ban of Art. 9 depends on the purpose, and the purpose of another's copy cannot be held, so the history is treated as biometrics. The final geometry is "how the signature looks like". But for a child it is personal information by the measure of COPPA all the same, so it is not published and is kept for a period (R125).
- **What follows from this:**
  - the measurement notice and the measurement form name the writing history and take explicit consent for it;
  - the runner of `tutor` and the measurement organizer do not compare writers by handwriting and link samples only by the writer code (R09 canvas);
  - no agent gets the writing history (R114).
- **A child's grade.** The target for children's handwriting is measured by grades, and a first-grader's handwriting is different. There is no grade in the file, as by R09 canvas: the file goes to the runner, and with admission to the AI providers as well. The band of grades — 1–2, 3–4 or 5–6 — the measurement organizer writes into their own record by the writer code, and it lives as long as the sample (R125). Only they break the results down by bands.
- **"I am 18".** Majority does not come at 18 everywhere:
  - Alabama, §26-1-1(a) — at 19, but by (f) "an unemancipated minor who is 18 years old and of sound mind … may enter into a binding contract";
  - Nebraska, §43-2101(1) — at 19, but by (2)(a) from 18 one may "Enter into a binding contract";
  - Mississippi, §1-3-27 — at 21, but for contracts on personal property — at 18; this was read by a copy at FindLaw and was not checked;
  - in Scotland transactions are entered into from 16 (Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991, s.1).

  So the statement in the form and on the page is "I am 18 or older, and under the laws of where I live I may make this agreement". The weakness is not in the age, but in that the statement cannot be checked. A minor's contract can be disaffirmed: so by the sense of NY Gen. Oblig. Law §3-101(1), which forbids this only after 18. Against this the organizer accepts a form only from a person they have spoken with themselves.
- **DCO.**
  - Item (c) of DCO 1.1 — "The contribution was provided directly to me by some other person who certified (a), (b) or (c) and I have not modified it". It does not say where item (a) is certified, so a certification in the signed form holds it (R04 modules).
  - Item (a) — "under the open source license indicated in the file", and the field `license: "Apache-2.0"` of an eval-set sample (R93) is exactly this license in the file.
- **The order.** The form comes before the first sample, as it was (R11 canvas): the data appear after the consent.
- **A name on the sheet.** In measurement samples and child samples it is looked for by the measurement organizer — by hand, without AI and agents, before the file goes to the runner, as in eval-set samples the eval-set organizer does it (R04 modules). A sample with a name is erased, and the person writes it anew.
- **The measurement notice** names the period — 2 years from the session, as for children's samples (R125) — and what remains after withdrawal: the AI providers' logs by their periods (privacy 5.1) and the copy of the file on the device, which the person erases themselves. The runner's report that names the IDs of erased samples lies in the same place as they do (R95), and is erased together with them; conclusions recorded without IDs — thresholds and targets in decisions — remain.

— *Why:* the supervisory authorities call precisely the writing history behavioural biometrics, and the final geometry holds everything eval needs without it (R09 canvas). The grade is needed by the target, but not by the file, which goes further than the organizer.

— *Rejected:*
- **both records are biometrics.** Then the final geometry too would need explicit consent under Art. 9, and eval-set samples are published forever, and the purposes of others' copies cannot be held;
- **neither** — diverges from WP193 on the dynamics of writing;
- **no grade anywhere** — the target by grades cannot be checked;
- **the grade in the file** — requires a change to R09 canvas and R93, and the grade goes with the file;
- **the date of birth in the form** — extra data, and it cannot be checked anyway (П-6);
- **checking a document** — a copy of a document for the sake of a license on a sample.

— privacy 4, 9, 10; R04 modules; R09, R11 and R59 canvas; R93, R95, R112, R114, R125; П-6, П-18.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **an adult's withdrawal of measurement samples is by the writer code, and the organizer erases them within 30 days, as for children's samples (R125); the signed measurement form — with the name, the signature and the date — is kept for 5 years after all the samples under it are erased, as the scan of the parent's form.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 in carrying out T99 (RUN.md), by the recommendations: one withdrawal period for both purposes fits into the month of Art. 12(3) GDPR, and the form is the proof of explicit consent to the writing history (Arts. 7(1), 17(3)(e)). — R133.

**R125. Child samples. The consent is a separate signed form of the parent before the first session. The period is 2 years from the session: a withdrawal by the writer code erases earlier, within 30 days, and the period can be extended only by a new form. The sample file and the scan of the form go to the measurement organizer into the operator's private Cloud Storage bucket in the project `infra`, `us-east4`, by an upload link with an expiry, which the organizer gives. Only they see them. A child sample does not go to AI until the work of a child under 13 — the strictest category — is admitted to the provider: there is no category in the file (R124; R121; the admission table). П-10 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 in planning T95 (RUN.md), by the recommendations of the analysis (R112).
- **The consent.** It is a separate signed form of the parent or guardian with the child's code; the organizer accepts it before the first session (R59 canvas).
  - The form names:
    - what lies in the sample — the final geometry without the writing history (R124), the crops and the markup from the child's words;
    - what for — to check the target for children's handwriting and to recheck models;
    - who sees it, the period and how to withdraw;
    - Apple's cloud — if Safari saves downloads to iCloud Drive (В67 `canvas`; П-10);
    - and that the adult erases the file from the device once they have passed it to the organizer.
  - The basis is consent under Art. 6(1)(a) and Art. 8 GDPR, and for children under 13 also the verifiable parental consent under COPPA, by the same method as R116: a signed form.
- **The period.**
  - COPPA, §312.10: "Personal information collected online from a child may not be retained indefinitely", and the written retention policy names "a timeframe for deletion". 2 years from the session cover the target before the beta and the rechecking of models after it. It can be extended only by a new form, with a new period.
  - Withdrawal: the parent names the code or the form, and the organizer within 30 days erases the samples of this code, their copies and the runner's reports that name their IDs (R95).
  - The organizer's record with the band of grades is erased together with the samples of its code (R124). The scan of the parent's form — the proof of consent — lives 5 years after all the samples under it are erased, as the record of R117, and is erased then too.
  - Deletion by the period is done by the bucket's lifecycle rule, not by the organizer's memory. It counts from the upload, so the upload link is valid for a day from the session: the period from the upload is the same as from the session.
- **The channel and the place.** It is the operator's private Cloud Storage bucket in the project `infra`, `us-east4` (R109). Cloud Storage is a service of Google Cloud, and by the Cloud Data Processing Addendum, para. 4.1, "Google is a processor" ([Cloud DPA](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum), "Last modified October 30, 2026"; [Google Cloud Services Summary](https://cloud.google.com/terms/services) — Cloud Storage is in the list).
  - The adult uploads the file and the scan of the form by the upload link that the organizer gives for the session and that is valid for a day; how to sign it `infra` decides. Neither the platform's server nor GitHub sees the file (R04 modules).
  - Samples, forms and the organizer's records each lie under their own prefix. Access is only for the measurement organizer, without CI and agents (R114).
  - The same bucket holds the scans of the consents of R116, under their own prefix and with the operator's access (the 2026-11-09 amendment to R116), and the volunteers' forms (R126).
  - The organizer reads the file in the bucket or on their own device and puts no copies into other storage: the runner takes the file from the same place.
- **To AI** a child sample does not go until the admission table admits to the provider the work of a child under 13 — and before the approval of zero data retention it does not admit it (R121). The strictest category — because there is no child's category in the file, and the band of grades lies only in the organizer's record (R124). The runner holds this by the field "who wrote" (R93), by a refusal for each sample `WRITER_CHILD`, until the provider is admitted. A sample is never given to agents (R114).
- **Hosting.** The session is run by a build of the page from a file. When the page moves to Hosting (R128), the IP address of the session's device will go into the Hosting log for "a few months" — the notice and the form name this.

— *Why:* the period is what COPPA requires, and 2 years cover the target. A bucket under the Cloud DPA is the channel and the storage at once: a processor by agreement, the period set by code, and access with one person.

— *Rejected:*
- **until the end of the beta and 12 more months** — there is no date of the end of the beta, and the retention policy needs a period;
- **5 years** — longer than eval needs;
- **hand to hand** — does not suit a volunteer from far away;
- **email** — attachments lie with the mail services of both sides, and the platform has no processor agreement with them.

— privacy 4, 5, 9; R25, R59 canvas, R93, R109, R114, R116, R121, R124; П-10, П-12.

**R126. The volunteer's form of an eval set and its route. The form lives as long as at least one sample by it is in any published version of a module: it is the evidence of the license and of point (a) of the DCO. A form by which no sample was contributed is erased 12 months after it is signed. The files and the scan of the form come to the bucket of R125 by an upload link. A file that failed the check is erased at once. П-16 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T95 was planned (RUN.md), by the recommendations of the analysis (R112).
- **What is in the form** — to the list of R04 modules and П-16:
  - the text of DCO 1.1 word for word and the certification of point (a);
  - the statement "I am 18 or older, and under the laws of where I live I may make this agreement" (R124);
  - publication under Apache-2.0 without withdrawal: a sample in an eval set is public forever (concepts 3), and by point (d) of the DCO "a record of the contribution … is maintained indefinitely";
  - the runs of the sample at AI providers in CI of `modules` (R24), with the names of the providers (R06 tutor);
  - training of an own reading model — if the samples will be trained on (the 2026-10-28 amendment to R12);
  - samples without names and signatures, on made-up topics (R127);
  - how an essay is marked up and how people agree (П-16; R95);
  - the version of the text set and the form's retention period.
- **Where.** In the bucket of R125, under its own prefix, with access for the eval-set organizer. The record of the form names the SHA-256 digests of the samples contributed by it (R04 modules).
- **Retention period.**
  - The form and the record live as long as at least one sample by it is in a published version of a module — that is, indefinitely. The basis is GDPR Art. 17(3)(e): erasure does not apply while the data are needed "for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims" (R117). The form says so.
  - A form with no contributed samples is erased 12 months after it is signed.
- **Channel.** The volunteer uploads the files and the scan of the form by an upload link with an expiry, as in R125. The platform's server and GitHub do not see them (R04 modules).
- **A file that failed the check** is erased at once with all its copies. The record of the form marks only that it was rejected, and the date, and the volunteer writes the sample anew (R04 modules).

— *Why:* the license is not withdrawn, and a dispute about it is possible at any moment, and without the form there would be nothing to show point (a) with.

— *Rejected:* 5 years after the contribution — a dispute about the license is possible later too, and by then the form would be gone.

— privacy 9; R04 modules; R24, R93, R95, R117, R124, R125; concepts 3; П-16.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the form of version 1 takes no consent to training an own reading model: the samples are for checking AI, and training will require a new version of the text set; an essay is graded by two people, each on their own, and where they differed, a third decides, and one mark per criterion is published.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 while T99 was carried out (RUN.md), by the recommendations: consent to a purpose that does not exist is not "specific" (GDPR Art. 4(11)), and one mark does not catch an assessor's error. — R95, R133.

— *Amendment 2026-11-10:* **the volunteer withdraws an eval-set sample by the name and the date of the form, within 30 days: one not contributed to the module's repository is erased, and one contributed leaves the next version of the module and its tests; released versions keep it forever, as do others' copies under Apache-2.0. The platform does not train its own model on the samples, but anyone may take the published ones.** The author's answer of 2026-11-10 while T111 was carried out (RUN.md). In detail — R139.

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **the writer and the eval-set organizer may be one person — a module author writes their own samples by the volunteer's form, signs it themselves and accepts them themselves (the T61 amendment to R04 modules; architecture 3.4 modules, «Путь образца автора»). Then they sign the commit of the sample under point (a) of DCO 1.1, not (c), and their name in the commit is their own signature. The form of version 1 in force does not exclude this case and stays: "signing the commit … under point (c)" and "Nothing of you is in the commit" describe the organizer and a promise to another person, and an author who is the organizer knows this and accepts it.** The author's answer to the request of `modules` during E8 of `modules`, T62. Rejected: `volunteer-form` version 2 and the set `eval-set` version 2 with a phrase for this case — one more round of approval for a case the author knows themselves.

**R127. An essay is personal data of the learner and of those it names. A disclosure of self-harm is data about health. The platform does not look for such things. To a learner under 18, at work with a rubric and in `app`, where to turn is always shown: to an adult they trust, and to the helplines of their country. To an adult — "report a problem", and to the operator — the escalation path of R123, with a report under 18 U.S.C. §2258A if they learned of what this law names. The reminder not to write names is shown by the platform itself. Topics under 18 are made-up and general. П-20 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T95 was planned (RUN.md), by the recommendations of the analysis (R112).
- **Personal data.** CJEU, C-434/16 Nowak, 20 December 2017:
  - para. 37 — "the content of those answers reflects the extent of the candidate's knowledge and competence in a given field and, in some cases, his intellect, thought processes, and judgment. In the case of a handwritten script, the answers contain, in addition, information as to his handwriting";
  - para. 42 — the examiner's comments also relate to the candidate;
  - para. 45 — "The same information may relate to a number of individuals".

  Therefore an essay and the marks of a rubric are the learner's data, and a person named in an essay is one more data subject. A disclosure of self-harm is data about health: by Art. 4(15) it is "personal data related to the physical or mental health", and the ICO counts among them "details about an individual's mental health" (by a Wayback Machine copy of 2026-10-17).
- **Topics.** To a learner under 18 a module gives made-up and general topics, and marks a topic about the learner's life as not for their category (R51; privacy 9, П-20).
- **The reminder.** The platform itself shows "do not write your name or the real names of people you know" before each submission of work that goes to an AI provider whole — this is the proposal of `modules` (В18 `modules`; R16 modules). The essays module removes its own reminder from the statements with a new version once `app` already shows it itself. The platform does not look for others' names in an essay, and does not store the text of an essay (R87) — except for storing artifacts by choice (R113).
- **Disclosure of harm.**
  - **The platform has no duty to report.**
    - 18 U.S.C. §2258A tells a provider to report to NCMEC's CyberTipline "after obtaining actual knowledge" of child pornography, of child trafficking (§1591) and of enticement of a child (§2422(b)), and by (f) "Nothing in this section shall be construed to require a provider to— (1) monitor any user".
    - In 17 states and Puerto Rico "any person" is obliged to report (Child Welfare Information Gateway, "Current Through 05-31-2023"). That is a person who learned, not a program that nobody reads.
    - In England s.85 Crime and Policing Act 2026 is a duty of a person in a "relevant activity", and it is not in force yet ("Prospective"). When it will be brought in is not verified.
  - **The platform does not look for signs of harm.** That would be an inference about the learner's health and feelings (Art. 9; R123). The ICO counts under Art. 9 an inference too, when "you intend to treat someone differently on the basis of inferred information".
  - **To a learner under 18**, at work with a rubric and in the section "Help" of `app`, which is open to them from any screen, there is always shown: "if something is wrong — tell an adult you trust", and the helplines of their country.
    - The helplines come as a name and a number, without links, so the promise of privacy 7 "no external links" holds.
    - Samaritans: "At a minimum standard, all sites and platforms should provide basic signposting, including: Trusted helplines" and "All companies must review signposting regularly to ensure accuracy of contact numbers". Therefore the list by country that `app` keeps carries the date it was checked.
  - **To an adult** — "report a problem" at each answer of the tutor, and the operator handles the reports by the escalation path (R123).
    - If from a report or otherwise the operator gained actual knowledge of what §2258A names, they report to the CyberTipline.
    - The ICO: "Data protection law doesn't prevent you from doing this" (A 10 step guide to sharing information to safeguard children, a Wayback Machine copy of 2026-10-15), and under a threat to life the basis is Art. 6(1)(d) and 9(2)(c).
- **Storage on the server (R113).**
  - The text of the switch says that an essay may hold personal matters, including about health and about the family, and that nobody reads it.
  - Turning it on is explicit consent to what the essay discloses about health (Art. 9(2)(a)). It is given by whoever gives consent for this learner (R116).

— *Why:* nobody will read a child's disclosure, so it is proportionate not to look for it, but to tell the child where to turn — the minimum that Samaritans name — and to keep a path for what a person learned.

— *Rejected:*
- **detection and a report to an adult** — an inference about health and feelings (Art. 9; R123), and if the harm comes from the adult themselves, the report would do harm;
- **nothing beyond R123** — below the minimum of Samaritans.

— privacy 3.2, 6, 7, 9; R16 modules; R51, R87, R113, R116, R123; П-20.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **the words of the storage switch are the legal text `storage-consent` [of the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md), with a version and a gist in the language of the screen, not a string of `app`: the version the person saw is written by the consent record.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T97 was carried out (RUN.md). — R131.

**R128. Firebase Hosting is fit for the build of `app` and the samples page: by the Firebase Data Processing and Security Terms Google is a processor for Hosting, and IP addresses for serving the site and for protection are "support for the internal operations" under COPPA. The link of Hosting with Cloud Logging is off. The retention period of Hosting — "a few months" — and the retention period of the audit — 400 days — stand in the written retention policy and in the notice to the parent. П-9 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T95 was planned (RUN.md), by the recommendations of the analysis (R112); the sources were read 2026-11-09 (privacy 10).
- **The agreement.**
  - Hosting works under the Google APIs Terms of Service, the Firebase Data Processing and Security Terms and the Firebase Paid Services Agreement ([Firebase Terms](https://firebase.google.com/terms), "Terms last modified: September 24, 2026").
  - DPST, §5.1.1: "Google is a processor of that Customer Personal Data", and by §14.1, on a conflict with the rest of the agreement, "these Terms will prevail" ([DPST](https://firebase.google.com/terms/data-processing-terms), "Terms last modified: August 21, 2024").
  - The Google APIs Terms, §1(i), take in the Controller-Controller Terms only "To the extent required by data protection laws". The list of Controller Services is "Google Maps APIs, Google Play, NotebookLM Plus for Workspace Service Data, Subscribe with Google, Waze APIs and SDKs, Waze Carpool, Google Beam" ([Services](https://business.safety.google/services/), "Last update: 27 April 2026"): Hosting is not in it.
  - The suspicion of privacy 2 and T93 about "controller to controller" terms was not confirmed.
- **COPPA.**
  - An IP address is personal information, item (7) of §312.2.
  - Serving the site and protection from abuse are "support for the internal operations": "(ii) Perform network communications; … (v) Protect the security or integrity of the user, website, or online service". The condition is that the information does not go "to contact a specific individual … to amass a profile on a specific individual, or for any other purpose".
  - Whoever does only this is not a "third party" (§312.2), and there is no disclosure.
  - The written assurances of §312.8(c) are the DPST and its Appendix 2 on security measures.
  - The weak spot is §7(a) of the Google APIs Terms: "Google may use submitted information in accordance with our privacy policies". The DPST prevails (§14.1), but how the FTC will read this is not verified.
- **Measures:**
  - The link of Hosting with Cloud Logging is off. The request log of Hosting carries `remoteIp` and the full URL of the request ([Hosting logs](https://firebase.google.com/docs/hosting/web-request-logs-and-metrics), "Last updated 2026-11-05 UTC"), and the link itself is turned on only by choice: "You can link your Firebase project to Cloud Logging".
  - The retention period of Hosting cannot be configured — "Hosting retains IP data for a few months" — and it stands in the written retention policy (§312.10) and in the notice to the parent together with the internal operations for which the IP address is taken (§312.4(d)(3)).
- **The Admin Activity audit** — 400 days, the period cannot be configured (R07 infra). The callers are the operator and CI, and what `SignUp` writes the first code of `infra` will check (П-9). This period stands in the same retention policy.
- **The retention policy (§312.10)** is assembled from the periods of the additions of П-9, of decisions R113, R117, R125, R126 and of this one. It is written by the texts of T97 and T98 by privacy 4 and П-9.
- **The samples page** may move to Hosting as a separate site (the second 2026-11-08 amendment to R25). When, the author decides; the notice and the form name the retention period of the Hosting log (R125).

— *Why:* the agreement makes Google a processor, and the log that Google keeps itself serves only the internal operations that COPPA names.

— *Rejected:*
- **Cloud Storage with Cloud CDN or Cloud Run** under the Cloud DPA — the logs and periods there are in our own hands, but it is longer and more expensive, revises R06 infra, and Google stays a processor there too;
- **Hosting only for `app`** — an iPad with the samples page still does not work.

— privacy 2, 4, 9; R06 and R07 infra; R25, R113, R116, R117, R125, R126; П-9.

## DPIA

**R129. The platform's DPIA is [docs/dpia.md](dpia.md), in Russian, by the ICO's template. It is reviewed by a task that changes what it rests on, and besides — before the beta, before the public launch and at least once a year. Before the first child the author asks the parents of the first families of the beta. No DPO is appointed, and the DPIA records why. The measures and the residual risks are accepted by the author.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T105 was planned (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the sources were read 2026-11-09 ([DPIA](dpia.md), section 9).
- **Place and language.** It is an internal record, not a text shown to people, so it lies among the documents of `docs/` and is written in Russian (R14). The repository is public, so the DPIA is published: the ICO — "it is good practice to publish your DPIA", and WP248 — "controllers should consider publishing at least parts". A translation into English is given on request of the ICO, to which the DPIA itself is given at a consultation (Art. 36(3)(e)), or of an AI provider at a review of the measures (R123), with the date and the version of the original. It is cited by section, as `dpia 6`, and `just docs-check` checks such citations.
- **Review.**
  - GDPR Art. 35(11): "at least when there is a change of the risk represented by processing operations". The ICO adds outside changes: "if a new security flaw is identified, or a new public concern is raised".
  - Therefore the DPIA is reviewed by a task that changes what it rests on: a kind of data or a retention period, a provider or a processor, an AI capability or an AI route, opening an age, a country or a function to children. Its «Сделано» names the review, and the log at the start of the DPIA — the version.
  - Besides — before the beta, before the public launch and at least once a year. No source sets a period: the yearly review is the platform's own rule.
- **The views of parents and children.** Art. 35(9) — "Where appropriate, the controller shall seek the views of data subjects", and std 2 — "seek and document the views of children and parents". Before the first child the author gives the parents of the first families of the beta a short summary of the risks and measures and records their answers in the DPIA without names; the views of children — through the parents. Until then the first child waits ([DPIA](dpia.md), section 8).
- **A council of experts** on the rights and development of children, which std 2 advises, — before the public launch.
- **DPO.** Not appointed: by the ICO, "Under the UK GDPR, you must appoint a DPO if" the core activity is "large scale" monitoring or processing of special categories on a "large scale", and the platform has no scale before the beta. This is a retelling of the ICO, and the text of Art. 37 is not checked. The ICO: "If you decide that you don't need to appoint a DPO … it's a good idea to record this decision". The decision is reviewed before the public launch.
- **Sign-off.** The measures and the residual risks are accepted by the author (R112). If a high risk remains, the first child waits, and by Art. 36(1) the platform consults the ICO.

— *Why:* the DPIA is read first of all by the author, and by the ICO and providers on request. A review by event catches changes that the platform makes itself, and a yearly one those that come from outside.

— *Rejected:*
- **`legal/dpia.md` in English** — the part `legal/` does not exist yet (T96), and the author would have to read in English;
- **both languages** — the two texts will diverge;
- **a review by event only** — outside changes would not trigger it;
- **every half year** — twice the work without a new argument;
- **to record why the parents were not asked** — std 2 expects a consultation, and the first families exist;
- **a survey before the beta** — a study with its own data and texts.

— privacy 9; product 11; R112, R119, R123; [DPIA](dpia.md); RUN.md, T105; П-2, П-26.

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **parents and children are not asked — neither before the first child nor before the public launch: there will be no consultation of the parents of the first families, and the former "before the first child the author asks the parents of the first families of the beta" is removed. The council of experts on the rights and development of children before the public launch stays (dpia 4).** The author's answer during T113 (RUN.md). Art. 35(9) asks for the views of people "where appropriate", and the author judged that they are not needed here; they named no new argument — this is their decision under R112, not new evidence against the former "std 2 expects a consultation, and the first families exist". The ICO's code, std 2, Step 3, expects "seek and document the views of children and parents": the DPIA departs from it and records this in dpia 4 and 7 — by the formerly rejected option "to record why the parents were not asked", which the author now chooses. Problem reports and mails to the operator, where a family says that a measure does not work, become a reason for a review (dpia 1), but do not replace asking: whether a child understands what they are told, nobody checks — this is the new risk 19 of the DPIA, medium, accepted by the author. Rejected: a consultation before the first child — the former decision; a consultation before the public launch, together with the experts.

— *Amendment 2026-11-12:* **the DPIA is in English, as the other documents of `docs/` (R143), from version 14: "Place and language" above is replaced by this. It is given to the ICO at a consultation (Art. 36(3)(e)) and to an AI provider at a review of the measures (R123) as it is, with the date and the version; there is no translation on request any more, and the Russian text up to version 14 is in git's history.** The author's decision of 2026-11-11 — R143 and the 2026-11-11 amendment to R14; the translation — RUN.md, T136. — dpia, the header and the review log.

## Legal texts

**R130. The platform's legal texts are a normative part of `spec`, [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md): the policy, the terms, the consents, the text sets of the samples page and the volunteer's form. The part has a version of its own, an integer, and each text and set has its own versions 1, 2, 3…, each as a file of its own forever. A version's status is draft or in force, and a version in force does not change by a byte. A text is Markdown in English, and the passport `legal.yaml` carries the versions, statuses, dates and the gist in the languages of the screen. The texts for `app` are given by `api` with the method `LegalService.GetLegalTexts`, and `canvas` and the organizer take theirs from the release file `legal-<version>.tar.gz`.** The author's answer of 2026-11-09 while T96 was planned (RUN.md).
- **Versions.** `legal/VERSION` is the version of the layout, of the passport's schema and of the rules, as with the deployment configuration (R85). A text and a set have their own numbers. Consent must be demonstrable after the text changes too — GDPR Art. 7(1): "the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented", — and a sample names the version of the set forever (R93). Therefore each version is a file of its own `texts/<id>/<n>.md`, and it never leaves the part.
- **Status.** `draft` is edited freely and shown to nobody. `in_force` — with the date when the author approved the version (R112); from that release its file and the passport's record do not change by a byte — the rule `legal.in-force-unchanged` compares them with the part of the previous release, as published versions of modules are compared with the previous ones (R89). The current version is the version in force with the highest number.
- **Format.** A text version is Markdown, CommonMark with GFM tables, in English — the English text is in force (privacy 7), — without HTML, pictures and links: `app` shows the texts as its own pages, without external links (R115), and the form is printed. The gist of a version in `en` and `ru` (R92; R116) lies in the passport beside the version and is approved together with it: the gist and the text will not diverge, and a copy gives its own.
- **Rules** — [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md), section 5: `legal.files`, `legal.versions`, `legal.set-texts`, `legal.markdown` and `legal.in-force-unchanged`. They are checked by `just legal-check` together with the schemas, examples and reading vectors, and the folder of a self-hosting copy by `just -f spec/justfile legal-check-dir <folder>`, without the comparison with a release.
- **Who reads it.**
  - `api` — from the Go module of `spec`, `spec.Legal` (R64), and a copy — from its operator's folder (the second 2026-11-09 amendment to R115). It gives the texts with a place of `app` by the method `LegalService.GetLegalTexts`: Connect GET without a token, as the methods of `PackageService`, because the policy is read before sign-in ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15). Consent by text version — T103.
  - `canvas` puts the sets of its purposes into the build of the samples page from the release file of `spec` that `release-verify` accepted (R77) — the recommendation of the row `canvas` В24; a purpose is open only with the current set (R11 canvas).
  - The organizer of an eval set and of a measurement takes the form from the same place (R126).
- **The texts of T96 are drafts:** their words are written by T97–T99, and the author approves them.
- **Line.** The new part opens a line: `RELEASE_LINE` is 0.13, and version 1 of the part comes out with the release of E4 (T102).

— *Why:* a consent and a sample refer to a text forever, so a text must have a version that cannot be rewritten, and a place from which everyone who shows it takes it. The method of the contract is now: the author's answer, not the recommendation, which put it together with consent in T103.

— *Rejected:*
- **a date as the version** — two versions of one day could not be told apart;
- **git's history only** — `api` and the organizer would not show a former version from one release;
- **three statuses** with "superseded" — a replacement would edit the old file, and "superseded" can be derived anyway;
- **all in YAML** — long legal texts in YAML are harder to read and edit;
- **the gist in the translations of `app`** — it would not follow the text version, and a copy would show the gist of the platform's texts;
- **an npm package** — the types package would carry legal texts;
- **a method in `AccountService` with a token** — the policy must be shown before sign-in;
- **the method together with consent in T103** — the recommendation of the plan;
- **templates with the operator's name** for a copy — another operator would promise what the platform does.

— privacy 7; R11 canvas; R64, R77, R85, R89, R92, R93, R98, R112, R115, R116, R126; [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md); RUN.md, T96.

— *Amendment 2026-11-09:* **version 1 of the part comes out with the release `v0.13.0`, before the end of E4, with draft texts; the words of the texts and their approval come out in the line 0.13 with the next releases.** The author's decision of 2026-11-09 — the third amendment of that day to answer 5 of the epic E4 (RUN.md).

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **version 2 of the part — translations of versions.** A text version may name the languages of the interface, other than English, into which it has a translation, by the field `translations`, and a translation is a file `texts/<id>/<n>.<tag>.md`, without force: English is in force, and a consent names the version. The rules `legal.files`, `legal.markdown` and `legal.in-force-unchanged` hold translations too, `GetLegalTexts` gives the translation into the language of the screen, the types are `types/legalv2`, and the version of the part starts the line 0.15. The author's answer during T112: Connecticut's law requires a privacy notice in every language of the service (R141). Rejected: a translation as a separate text with its own ID — `app` would guess by the name whose translation it is.

**R131. The platform's operator is in the United States. Its name, postal address, telephone and email, and with them the law and court of the terms of use, the author writes into the texts at approval (П-27). The privacy policy is one for all learners: with the notice to the parent under COPPA §312.4(d) and the written retention policy of §312.10. Consent to storing works on the server is the legal text `storage-consent`. Representatives in the EU and in the United Kingdom under Art. 27 of the GDPR and of the UK GDPR the operator appoints before the first learner from there, and until then `api` accepts no learners from the countries of the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom. The laws of US states on children's data are analysed by the analysis task T107 — before the first child from the United States.** The author's answers of 2026-11-09 while T97 was carried out (RUN.md), all by the recommendations. The sources were read 2026-11-09 (privacy 10).
- **Where the operator is.** The GDPR covers learners from the EU with an operator in the United States too — Art. 3(2): "the processing of personal data of data subjects who are in the Union by a controller or processor not established in the Union, where the processing activities are related to: (a) the offering of goods or services, irrespective of whether a payment of the data subject is required". Then Art. 27(1): "Where Article 3(2) applies, the controller or the processor shall designate in writing a representative in the Union". The exception of 27(2)(a) is processing "which is occasional, does not include, on a large scale, processing of special categories of data … and is unlikely to result in a risk". The platform's processing is constant, the data are children's, and an essay may disclose health (R127), so the exception does not fit it — Claude's reading (R112). The UK GDPR has the same Arts. 3(2) and 27(1), with a representative "in the United Kingdom" ([legislation.gov.uk](https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2016/679/article/27), the revision of 2026-09-30).
- **Contacts.** COPPA §312.4(d)(1): "The name, address, telephone number, and email address of all operators collecting or maintaining personal information from children"; GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) — "the identity and the contact details of the controller". The repository is public, and these are the author's data, so they write them in themselves, when they move the version to `in_force`. The email is written as code: `legal.markdown` rejects a bare address, which GFM makes into a link ([the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md), section 5).
- **One policy.** §312.4(d) names what the notice on the website says, and §312.10 — "The operator must provide its written data retention policy addressing personal information collected from children in the notice on the website or online service provided in accordance with § 312.4(d)". Therefore version 1 of the policy already speaks of children, with the retention periods of all kinds of data, and of the samples of the samples page too (R125, R126), and a child's profile will not require a new version. The parental consent and the text for the child — T98.
- **Storage consent is a text of the part.** Turning storage on is explicit consent under Art. 9(2)(a) (R127), and consent must be demonstrable (Art. 7(1)): the version of the words the person saw is written into the consent record, as with the other consents (R130; RUN.md, T103). Who gives it for a teenager who gives consent themselves — T98: R113 gives the switch to the account owner, and R127 — to whoever gives consent for the learner.
- **Representatives.** Until they are appointed, the policy says that the platform does not accept learners from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom, and a version that names them will come as a new one. The appointment is the author's step: it costs money (rule 4 of RUN.md).
- **Transfer to the United States** — what each agreement says (Art. 13(1)(f)):
  - Google — [Cloud Data Processing Addendum](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum), "Last modified October 30, 2026", Appendix 3, §4.1: with an "Alternative Transfer Solution" the transfer goes by it, otherwise — by the SCCs; [Alternative Transfer Solution](https://cloud.google.com/terms/alternative-transfer-solution), "Last modified September 29, 2026": "Google LLC has certified to the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework" and "to the UK Extension to the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework". Firebase Auth goes under the terms of Google Cloud ([Firebase Terms](https://firebase.google.com/terms), "Terms last modified: September 24, 2026"), and Hosting — under the [DPST](https://firebase.google.com/terms/data-processing-terms), §10.6: "The Data Privacy Framework will apply to any Restricted European Transfer to a certified Google entity in the US". The fallback SCCs of both are Module 2 with the UK Addendum;
  - Neon — the Product Specific Schedule refers to the DPA of Databricks ([Databricks DPA v3](https://www.databricks.com/legal/dpa), 2023-07-21), §8.1: "such transfer shall be governed by the Standard Contractual Clauses", Annex B — Module 2 and the UK Addendum; by §8.2 an "alternative transfer mechanism" applies instead of them, and Databricks, Inc. with Neon, LLC is in the Data Privacy Framework list, EU and UK Extension, "Active" (the API of [dataprivacyframework.gov](https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list), read 2026-11-09);
  - OpenAI — [DPA](https://openai.com/policies/data-processing-addendum), "Updated: December 1, 2025", a Wayback Machine copy of 2026-10-28: §4.1 — the data of the EEA are processed by OpenAI Ireland Limited, which transfers them outside the EEA "on the basis of agreements containing SCCs"; §4.2 — the data of the United Kingdom "with the SCCs as amended by the UK Addendum";
  - Anthropic — [DPA](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum), "Effective Feb 24, 2025", §I.1: "the terms of the SCCs Module Two (controller to processor) and/or Module Three (processor to processor) … are hereby incorporated by reference", and Appendix 3 B is the UK Addendum.

  Neither OpenAI nor Anthropic is in the Data Privacy Framework list.
- **The United Kingdom's regulator.** In the UK GDPR since 2026-09-30 stands "the Commission" — an amendment under the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (Art. 27(4)), — and what the regulator is now called is not verified. Therefore the policy names the right to complain in the words of Art. 77(1) — "in particular in the Member State of his or her habitual residence, place of work or place of the alleged infringement" — without the regulator's name.
- **The laws of US states** are not analysed in the documents, and whether the laws on children have thresholds is not verified. The task T107 is before the first child from the United States, and the texts of T97 do not wait for it.

— *Why:* an operator in the United States makes COPPA its law, and the GDPR and the UK GDPR the laws for learners from there, with a representative; one policy, and the law calls it complete only when it has children and retention periods in it.

— *Rejected:*
- **the contacts now** — the author's data would land in a public repository earlier than they are needed;
- **the section on children as version 2 in T98** — the version in force would have to be replaced before the first child;
- **the words of the switch as a string of `app`** — nothing to demonstrate which version of the words the person saw;
- **representatives now** — paying before the first learner from there; **not opening the EU and the United Kingdom** — would close markets without a review;
- **the states — before the public launch** or **without an analysis**.

— *Consequence:* `privacy-policy`, `terms-of-use` and `storage-consent` in [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md); privacy 7.1, 9 (П-27) and 10; dpia 1, 3.5 and 8; the 2026-11-09 amendment to R127; RUN.md — T97, T107, Д165 and Д166.

The texts name both, and the move of the page does not require a new version of the set.
- **Retention periods** — by R124–R126 and the amendments to them: measurement samples and children's samples — 2 years from the session, withdrawal — 30 days, the measurement and parent's forms — 5 years after the samples, the volunteer's form — while its samples are published, and without them — 12 months.

— *Why:* the notice on the page and the form that the organizer accepts say one thing (R11 canvas), and the form names everything to which consent is given — and nothing beyond that.

**R134. The age of digital consent by country is a normative part, `consent-age/` (T100): by country — the age, the day from which it applies, the law and its provision, a quote in the original, the primary source and the date it was read; in the table — the 27 countries of the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, the United Kingdom and the United States; a country outside the table — 18; a record is not rewritten, and a new age is a new record; when a country's age went up, a learner who gave consent themselves states their age anew.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T100 was planned (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the 2026-11-10 amendment to R98.
- **A part of its own**, the way of `deployment/` and `legal/` (the author's answer 3 in E4; RUN.md, E4): a version of its own, a schema, rules, vectors, the check `just consent-age-check`, the release file `consent-age-<VERSION>.tar.gz` from the line 0.14, a Go module — `spec.ConsentAge` — and the types `consentagev1` ([the part's text](../consent-age/README.md)). Not a section of `admission/`: the admission table gets no country, and a new input would be its major (R96).
- **Countries** — the EU and the EEA, where the age is given by Art. 8(1) of the GDPR or by the country's law that lowered it; the United Kingdom — the UK GDPR, 13; the United States — COPPA, 16 CFR §312.2, "under the age of 13", and the laws of the states — T107 (R131). The analysis T93 named no other countries, and a market outside them is not chosen.
- **Outside the table — 18:** consent for a learner under 18 is given by a parent, and the category `from_consent_to_18` is empty. The platform does not know a law that nobody has read. An error in this direction is a parent's consent for a teenager who could have given their own, not a teenager's own consent where the law requires a parent's. The former "13, unless the country's law says otherwise" (privacy 3.1; concepts 13) a program cannot check.
- **Category** — by the age in years and the country on the day when the age is stated: under 13 — `under_13`, below the country's age — `from_13_to_consent`, below 18 — `from_consent_to_18`, otherwise — `adult` (R06, R46). An age in the table is from 13 to 18: under 13 consent is given by a parent everywhere (COPPA; Art. 8(1) of the GDPR).
- **History.** A country's record is not rewritten: it has `from` — the day from which the age applies, and a law passed with a deferred entry into force is a record with a day ahead, and a bill is not a record. The table starts with the ages in force on 2026-11-10, when it was read: what was before, the record's note names. The words of a record — the law, the provision, the quote, the source, the date read, the note — can be corrected, and the age and the day cannot: the rule `consent-age.ages-kept` holds them against the release before.
- **The age went up.** `api` stores the category, the day and the country's age by which the category was given — from 13 to 18, a property of the law, not of the learner, — and not the age in years (privacy 3.3). For a profile `from_consent_to_18` whose country now requires a higher age than that one, `api` asks before the next work to state the age anew. The age is stored, not only the day: a law found late — a record with a day in the past — would otherwise change what this day gave, and there would be no question. A lowered age waits for the yearly confirmation: the former category is stricter. Storing the country's age is a proposal of the plan, by a finding of the review of T100.
- **Country codes** — the 249 codes that ISO 3166-1 assigns officially, as an enumeration of the schema: a code that ISO only reserves — `UK`, `EL` — the schema rejects, and `api` and `app` take the same enumeration. The enumeration is by Debian's iso-codes project ([`data/iso_3166-1.json`](https://salsa.debian.org/iso-codes-team/iso-codes/-/blob/d055275324963c9bce5882eaaa93024cf2bf7ed0/data/iso_3166-1.json), commit d055275 of 2023-02-22, read 2026-11-10); a new code is a new version of the part.
- **To close a country** the table cannot: it is about the law, the same for all copies. A country is closed by the list of countries of the operator of `api` (R118, R131): the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom — until representatives there.

— *Why:* the category decides who gives consent (R116), and `api` must compute it by a program, from primary sources, with a date — the rule "unless the law says otherwise" cannot be computed.

— *Rejected:* a section of `admission/` — R96 rejected the country as an input of the admission function; more Russian-speaking countries — the market is not chosen, and Russia also has 242-FZ on storing citizens' data in Russia, and that is a question of whether one may go there at all; 13 outside the table — a teenager of 13–17 from a country whose law requires a parent would consent themselves; 16 — the same for countries where the boundary is above 16; a country outside the table closed to children — the refusal `CAUSE_COUNTRY_NOT_ACCEPTED` closes a country to everyone, and a new one would be needed; waiting for the yearly confirmation when the age went up — for up to a year a teenager would work on their own consent where the law already requires a parent.

— *Consequence:* [the part `consent-age/`](../consent-age/README.md) and `tools/consent-age/`; `spec.ConsentAge`, `types/consentagev1`; `RELEASE_LINE` — 0.14; the 2026-11-10 amendment to R98; privacy 3.1 and 3.3; concepts 13 and 15; dpia — risk 11 and section 8; RUN.md — T100, Д174.

— privacy 3, 9; R06, R46, R96, R98, R116, R118, R131; П-1, П-6; RUN.md, T93, T100, T103, T107.

**R135. The export format is a normative part, `export/` (T101): an export file is a ZIP of JSON files — the manifest of `app`, the part of `api` byte for byte, `api.zip`, and per profile a file of what the device holds; one form for the export of a profile and of an account; the evidence log, the model's state and the observation are the JSON of their protobuf messages, and their `.proto` files are in the export; records — by the part's JSON Schema.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T101 was planned (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the 2026-11-10 amendment to R09 and the second 2026-11-10 amendment to R98.
- **The container is a ZIP**: any system opens it without a program of its own, and `app` puts the part of `api` as a separate file, as the method gave it, without parsing it (R98). Inside `api.zip` — `account.json` in an account export, `profiles/<id>.json` and `proto/` ([the part's text](../export/README.md), section 3).
- **Protobuf is JSON of the same value**, by the protobuf JSON mapping with the field names as in `.proto`, — as `buf convert` does (R10 learner-model), — and the `.proto` of the version of `learner-model` that computed it and `novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto` lie in the export: the export says what each field means, and the same bytes can be assembled from it again. There are no bytes in the export.
- **Records** — the profile, consents, attempts, observations, submissions with a rubric, lesson runs, engine choices, evidence, the state, artifacts, counters and what the device holds — by the part's schemas, by the columns «в выгрузку» of architecture 3.2 api and 3.2 app; without secrets and service data (R21 api; R84), without the minimal consent record (R117) and the scan of the form (R116).
- **One form for two scopes**: a profile export is one profile without the account, an account export is the account and all its profiles; the rules of [the part's text](../export/README.md), section 5, hold this.
- **Version** — the integer `export/VERSION` and the field `format` of each JSON file of the export; `export_format_version` of the contract is the same integer as a string. A new field, a new kind of record or a new rule is a new version of the part and a new line of `spec`.
- **Work in two places.** When storage on the server is on (R113), a work may lie both at `api` and on the device; the export puts both, and a reader recognizes them by the attempt ID.

— *Why:* the export is the account owner's right (privacy 1, 7; GDPR Arts. 15 and 20), and any program must read it, without the platform's library (R09), and `api` and `app` must write it by one norm.

— *Rejected:* one JSON file into which `app` inserts the part of `api` — fragile, and the part of `api` would become a string inside a string; both bytes and JSON in the export — two forms of one value that would have to be kept in step; only bytes — not readable without a protobuf library (R09); a proto package `novatrail.export.v1` for the records — against the author's answer 3 in E4 («нормативными частями, путём `deployment/`»).

— *Consequence:* [the part `export/`](../export/README.md) and `tools/export/`; `spec.Export`, `types/exportv1`; the release file `export-1.tar.gz` from the line 0.14; the comment of `export_format_version` and [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15; privacy 4; concepts 15; architecture 4.5; RUN.md — T101.

— *Amendment 2026-11-10:* **version 1 comes out with the data of T103: a consent has who gave it (the owner, a parent, the learner), the request code and the state of the form, the text versions as a list; a profile has whether storage of works is on, the records of storage consent and the problem reports.** The author's answer of 2026-11-10 while T103 was planned (RUN.md), by the recommendation: version 1 has not come out yet — `v0.14.0` will release it together with T103, — so the number is not reused. *Rejected:* version 2 — the first release of the part at once with the second version, the first of which nobody saw. In detail — R136.

**R136. The consent contract (T103): confirmation of parental consent by a signed form, the scan of which `app` uploads by the request code; a learner's own consent and its withdrawal in their profile; cancelling a waiting one and the limit of "waiting" consents; age and country anew; storage of works as a consent; the text version in each consent record; "report a problem" with storage for a year after handling.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T103 was planned (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the 2026-11-10 amendments to R98, R113, R116, R123, R131, R132 and R135.
- **Who gives consent** — by the category (R116, R134): for a learner below the country's age of digital consent — a parent, at it and above — the learner themselves, for their own profile — the owner. `ChildConsent` and `ProfileConsent` name this by the field `giver`, and `ProfileConsent.need` names what the profile waits for before the next work: the learner's own consent, a parental consent or the age; while it waits, a learning request gets `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` or `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15).
- **Parental consent** is a signed form `parent-consent` with the request code: 10 characters of Crockford base32, `ABCDE-FGHJK`, unique among the waiting ones. A scan, a photo or a PDF up to 10 MiB the adult uploads in `app`, `SendConsentForm`; `api` puts it into the closed bucket of R116, and the operator checks it against the code with its command and confirms the consent or does not accept the form, and then a new one is sent. A card transaction — by the public launch (П-28).
- **A learner's own consent** — `GiveOwnConsent` by the text `teen-consent`, in their profile, before the first work: the profile of such a learner `CreateChildProfile` creates at once. With it too a learner who has grown to the age confirms the consent that a parent gave (R116).
- **Withdrawal** is deletion of the profile with everything in it, with the minimal record of R117 (R132): parental consent — `DeleteProfile`, one's own — `WithdrawOwnConsent`, by a learning request. A learner who gave consent themselves also exports before the withdrawal themselves: `ExportProfile` with `ACTION_LEARNING`. Neither `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` nor `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` refuses requests about the consent itself — `GiveOwnConsent`, `WithdrawOwnConsent`, the learner's export, turning storage off and `ReportProblem`. The profile of a learner who gave consent themselves is deleted by an adult's `DeleteProfile` too: the account is the owner's (R21 api), and `app` says so before that. Deletion leaves problem reports until their period, without an ID (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R123). `GetAccount` does not show what was withdrawn or cancelled: of them only the minimal record remains, without the account ID (R117).
- **Cancelling** — `CancelChildConsent`, at a consent without a profile: a waiting one is erased whole, with the scan (R117), and a confirmed one is cancelled as a withdrawal — with the minimal record and the scan for their period; neither counts toward the limit any more. The limit is `CAUSE_TOO_MANY_CONSENTS`, `resource_exhausted`, without data; the number is kept by `api` (R11 api), a retry with the same key gets the same consent even at the limit (the 2026-11-09 amendment to R98).
- **Age and country anew** — `RestateAge`, by an adult action: when the country raised the age of digital consent (`CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED`; R134), at the yearly confirmation, which `Profile.age_check_due` marks a year later, and with a change of country (privacy 3.3). A category that needs another consent leaves the profile waiting for it: the learner's own consent or a parental consent with a new code.
- **Storage of works** — `SetWorkStorage`: turning it on is a consent by `storage-consent` of whoever consents for the learner (R113, R127), and for a learner who gives consent themselves — by their own learning request; the wrong kind of action gets `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED` or the new cause `CAUSE_LEARNER_DECIDES`. The record lives as long as the profile lives.
- **Text version** — `LegalTextRef`, which the request that gives consent takes from `GetLegalTexts` (R130, R131); one not current — `CAUSE_TEXT_NOT_CURRENT`. `RequestChildConsent` and `RestateAge` always name `parent-consent` while the text has a version in force: who gives consent only `api` computes, and it writes the version only into a parental consent.
- **"Report a problem"** — `AttemptService.ReportProblem`, by a learning request from the task screen (to whom `app` shows the button — П-26): which answer and rung, the words as `app` showed them, a word of the closed set and a text; the answer is an ID and the review period, 3 days (R132). `api` stores it until the review and a year after (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R123).
- **The operator's commands** — to confirm or not accept a form, to read and close a report — are a decision of `api` (R34 api).
- **Export** — version 1 of the part `export/` carries all this (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R135).

— *Why:* without these methods the operator has nothing to confirm consent with, a teenager nothing to give their own with, and an adult nothing to withdraw and cancel a waiting one with; the first child waits for the consent contract (dpia 8), and `api` and `app` for one release of the epic E4 (Д144, Д169, Д174).

— *Rejected:* a mail to the operator with a scan, and paper by post (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R116); `consent_id` on the form; the repeated question of age as a task of its own — `api` would wait for it longer (Д174); version 2 of the export (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R135); only an adult exports (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R132); report periods of 90 days and 3 years (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R123); choosing a payment provider now.

— *Consequence:* `account.proto`, `attempt.proto`, `cause.proto`, `legal.proto` and [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15; [the part `export/`](../export/README.md); privacy 3.3, 4, 7.1 and 9 — П-28; [DPIA](dpia.md), version 6; the drafts of `privacy-policy` and `parent-consent`; RUN.md — T103 and rows of table 4.

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **a teenager who has grown to the age of digital consent under a parental consent also withdraws it: `WithdrawOwnConsent` is valid at a profile that waits for the learner's own consent, `CONSENT_NEED_OWN`, and deletes the profile, as `DeleteProfile` does; `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED` — only at a profile whose consent an adult gave and which does not wait for the learner's own consent. Storage of works turned on by an adult `app` offers to the teenager after the confirmation on a separate screen: the consent is the teenager's `SetWorkStorage`, which, for storage turned on by an adult, is not a repeat but a record of their own consent in place of the adult's; a refusal turns storage off and erases the copies, and `app` offers the export before that.** The author's answers during T112 (R141): R116 and the texts promise "confirm or withdraw", and New York's law requires a teenager's separate consent to what learning does not need (GBL §899-ff). Rejected: only confirm; leave storage on; turn it off at once.

**R137. The NovaTrail operator in the texts is ALT EdTech LLC, the author's company, formed in Texas: the address, telephone and email are the company's; the terms are governed by the law of Texas, and a dispute is heard by the courts of Bexar County, Texas, — without mandatory arbitration and without a waiver of class actions. П-27 is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T109 was planned (RUN.md); the 2026-11-10 amendment to R131.
- **The operator is the company**, not the author personally: the liability is on the company. Rejected: the author personally — they would be liable themselves, and changing the operator later means new versions of all texts and a transfer of data.
- **The data** — in the section "Who we are" of [the policy](../legal/texts/privacy-policy/1.md): ALT EdTech LLC, 12828 Willow Centre Dr, Ste D, Houston, TX 77066-3043, USA; +1 224 933 2890; `altedtech.info@gmail.com`, as code. This is asked for by COPPA — "The name, address, telephone number, and email address of all operators collecting or maintaining personal information from children through the website or online service" (16 CFR §312.4(d)(1), [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-312/section-312.4), read 2026-11-10) — and by GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) (R131). These are the data of a company, not of a person: in the public repository and in every release they stand by the author's choice. The email is a consumer Gmail, without a processor agreement with Google, — the open question П-29, before the policy is approved.
- **The address is the company's.** The rule does not name the kind of address, and the FTC's FAQ, C.2, repeats its words ([Complying with COPPA: FAQ](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions), the live page, read 2026-11-10; before, the site answered 403, privacy 10); where the FTC needs a kind, it names it — ""Valid physical postal address" means the sender's current street address, a Post Office box the sender has accurately registered with the United States Postal Service, or a private mailbox…" (16 CFR §316.2(p), CAN-SPAM, [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-316/section-316.2), read 2026-11-10). Whether a mailbox is fit for COPPA neither the rule nor the FAQ says — Claude's reading (R112), — and the company's address removes this question. Rejected: a mailbox — not confirmed; a home address — forever in a public repository.
- **Law and court** — in the section "Law and disputes" of [the terms](../legal/texts/terms-of-use/1.md): the law of the State of Texas; the state courts in Bexar County or the federal court of the Western District of Texas, San Antonio Division, which Bexar belongs to — "The San Antonio Division comprises the counties of Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, …" (28 U.S.C. §124(d)(4), [LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/124), read 2026-11-10), — unless the law of the user's country or state gives them the right to sue where they live; the consumer's rights under the law of their country the terms do not take away anyway. The court is by the author's choice, separate from the address: Houston is in Harris County, the Southern District of Texas. Rejected: mandatory arbitration with a waiver of class actions — a longer text and stricter to the family.
- **The state of formation** the author chose; T109 did not analyse it: it is a question of taxes and residence, not of learners' data. Which laws of Texas and other states concern the platform — T107.

— *Why:* without the operator and the law neither the policy nor the terms come into force (COPPA §312.4(d)(1); GDPR Art. 13(1)(a)), and `app` E3 — the first deployment with adults — waits for them.

— *Consequence:* the drafts of `privacy-policy` and `terms-of-use` of version 1 and their gist in [the passport](../legal/legal.yaml); privacy 2, 7.1, 9 — П-27 and П-29 — and 10; RUN.md — T109, T110, T111 and T107.

**R138. The texts for adults — `privacy-policy`, `terms-of-use` and `storage-consent` version 1 — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions they rest on; the operator's mail stays consumer Gmail, `altedtech.info@gmail.com`, and the policy names Google as its recipient under Google's own terms, without a processor agreement, and asks not to write a child's data in letters; people's letters to the operator are kept a year after the letter or the last answer to it. П-29 is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 in the planning of T110 (RUN.md); the approval is the author's, by R112.
- **The reconciliation.** The drafts were written before R136, the 2026-11-10 amendments and R137, and the reconciliation before the approval found 31 discrepancies — 21 of them such that the text in force would have said something other than what was decided —, all corrected before the approval: a version in force does not change by a byte (`legal.in-force-unchanged`):
  - parental consent — a form with the consent request code, the upload of a scan in `app`; a check by card is not promised, it is П-28 (R116, R136);
  - a teenager: the profile — at once, their own consent, they decide the storage of their work and the export themselves, withdrawal deletes the profile (R113, R116, R132, R136);
  - the age asked anew — every year, with a change of country and when the country raised the age; the country's age by which the category is given (R134, R136);
  - what remains after the withdrawal and the removal of consent, and the scan of a removed waiting consent (R117, R136);
  - disclosure — "to nobody, except as the law requires", and the basis when life is threatened, Arts. 6(1)(d) and 9(2)(c) (R123, R127);
  - the problem report and the letters to the operator — in what is collected, and in the retention periods (R123, R136);
  - the providers of the samples and who sees the IP address of the samples page (R125, R133); the volunteer's form — kept without a time limit while the samples are published (R126);
  - the terms name ALT EdTech LLC (R137) and do not accept learners from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom until there are representatives (R131); the storage consent — who stores, where and why, and the consent record (R113, R116).
- **The mail** is the company's consumer Gmail, and the policy says so plainly: in "Who receives data" — a separate table of the recipients not under a processor agreement, in "Who we are" and "Children" — a request not to write a child's data in letters, and to do the export, deletion and withdrawal in the app. There is no processor agreement for Gmail: the Cloud Data Processing Addendum covers "an Agreement for Google Workspace or Cloud Identity" ([Google](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum), read 2026-11-10), not Gmail. This is the author's answer: they are not ready to pay for Workspace yet. *Cost:* Google keeps people's letters as it decides itself, not under an agreement with the operator. For children this is not enough: before someone keeps a child's data for the operator, COPPA requires the operator to "obtain written assurances that such entities will employ reasonable measures to maintain the confidentiality, security, and integrity of the information" (16 CFR [§312.8(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-312/section-312.8), read 2026-11-10), and whether Google's consumer terms count as such assurances has not been checked; for learners from the EU and the United Kingdom, GDPR Art. 28 requires a processor under an agreement. Therefore **Gmail — only while adults learn**: before the first child, the mail moves to a service with a processor agreement, and the new address comes with a new version of the policy, with T112 (dpia 8). While there are no children, there must be no child's data in letters, and the policy asks not to write it anyway. *Rejected:* Google Workspace on the company's domain, under the Cloud Data Processing Addendum, — the recommendation, which has to be paid for; another mail service with an agreement — a new processor and money too.
- **The retention of letters** — a year after the letter or after the last answer to it, whichever is later: to show what the operator answered to a request about rights and when (GDPR Arts. 5(2), 12(3)) — the same year as for the problem report. Rejected: 30 days after the answer — there would be nothing to show that the request was fulfilled; 3 years — a child's data in letters would live longer.
- **The basis of letters and problem reports** — the legitimate interest in answering, in protecting learners from harm and in showing that an answer was given (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)); an answer to a request about rights is also an obligation under the GDPR (Art. 6(1)(c)). This is Claude's reading (R112): there was no decision about it, and the reconciliation found that Art. 13(1)(c) asks for the basis of each purpose.
- **The age boundary** — "from this age", not "above it": a learner exactly at the age of digital consent of their country consents themselves (R136).
- **The mail at Google** is in data centers of Google's choosing: the policy does not promise where Gmail keeps the letters.
- **The approval** — the author reads the final texts and writes «утверждаю» ("I approve"), and `in_force_since` is the day of this word.

— *Why:* `app` E3, the first deployment with adults, waits for the policy and the terms in force: while no version is in force, `GetLegalTexts` gives an empty list.

**R139. The text sets of the samples page `measure` and `eval-set` version 1 — the notices `measure-notice` and `eval-set-notice`, the forms `measure-form` and `volunteer-form` — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions; the controller of the samples and the forms is ALT EdTech LLC, and the organizer acts for it, on its instructions; an eval-set sample can always be withdrawn: before it is entered into the module's repository, it is erased, and after that it leaves the next version of the module and its tests, while the released versions and others' copies remain; the organizer takes no volunteers from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom until the representatives are named.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 in the execution of T111 (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the 2026-11-10 amendments to R126 and R131; the approval is the author's, by R112.
- **The controller** is the operator, ALT EdTech LLC (R137): each of the four texts names it and its contacts, as GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) requires (R131), while before they said only "the operator". The organizer — the maintainer of `modules` or of the measurement, now the author — acts for the operator, on its instructions: there is one controller. Rejected: the organizer on their own — a second recipient or a joint controller, whom the texts would have to name, and an agreement between them.
- **Withdrawal** — by a letter to both the organizer and the operator, by the writer code in the measurement (Art. 7(3); the 2026-11-09 amendment to R124); one who lost the code — by the name and the date of the form; for an eval-set sample — by the name and the date of the form, within 30 days: one not yet entered into the module's repository is erased, and one entered leaves the next version of the module and its tests, while the released versions and others' copies under Apache-2.0 remain; the form lives while the sample is in the repository or in a released version (R126). The basis stays consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), as in the policy in force, and a withdrawal under Art. 7(3) stops what the platform itself does. Rejected: withdrawing nothing after publication — against Art. 7(3); the basis being a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) — the policy in force says "consent", and its version 2 would have been needed before the sets.
- **Volunteers from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom** — as with learners (R131): until there are representatives under Art. 27, the organizer does not take their forms, and the form asks to declare this. Rejected: accepting them — Art. 27 requires a representative for them too.
- **Model training** — the platform trains no model of its own on eval-set samples (the 2026-11-09 amendment to R126), but after publication under Apache-2.0 anyone takes them, as the license allows, for training too: the former "not for training a model" promised what cannot be held to (R124).
- **The reconciliation** found other things too, now corrected: the writing history — with the pointer and with what was erased, which stays in it ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 11); the basis — Arts. 6(1)(a), 9(2)(a), 7(1) and 17(3)(e); the runner's reports are erased with the samples (R124); the scan of the form — by the same upload link (R125); iCloud Drive in the forms too; "runner" — "NovaTrail's program that measures the reading"; a link to the rights in the policy; the gist names the operator and the way to withdraw.
- **Discrepancies with the policy.** The policy in force says of the page's samples "never on our server or in a repository", while eval-set samples are published in the module's repository (R126), and of a sample given to a module "this cannot be withdrawn", while now a withdrawal takes it out of the next version. The version in force does not change: both phrases are corrected by version 2 of the policy, with T112.
- **The writer code** links the samples to each other, and only the measurement form at the operator links them to the name: the former "never to your name" was wrong.

— *Why:* the large measurement on the samples of adult volunteers waits for the approved sets, and without a named controller and a way to withdraw, consent on the page is not informed (Arts. 7, 13).
