**R140. The laws of the US states (T107): the platform knows the learner's country, not the state, so a requirement of a state law that concerns it is fulfilled for all learners from the US; what concerns it now — with no threshold or below one — is the small-business rules of Texas, the laws of New York, Connecticut, Colorado, Montana and Arkansas on minors, Rhode Island's rule on the controller and the biometrics laws of Colorado and Washington; the measurement takes no volunteers from Colorado and Washington.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 in the planning and the execution of T107 (RUN.md); read from the primary sources 2026-11-10 — privacy 3.4 and 10.
- **The scope** — all the states' children's laws, the biometric laws and those on educational data, the general privacy laws by their thresholds, and all the laws of Texas, the operator's state; the other general laws — as a list for "when the platform grows". Rejected: all the laws of all the states — longer, and most general laws do not concern a small operator; only Texas.
- **Fulfilled across the whole country.** The learner's state is a new kind of data, which `api` does not know and does not ask for (privacy 1). The exception is the measurement's volunteers: the form asks them to declare that they do not live in Colorado or Washington (below). Rejected: asking for the state and closing states — new data and a change of the contract; for now only Texas.
- **The operator is a small business by the SBA's standards** under any fitting code (13 CFR 121.201): Texas and Nebraska (§541.002, 87-1103) and Minnesota (325M.12) require of it only the ban on selling sensitive data without consent, and the platform sells nothing.
- **What concerns it now and what is missing** — privacy 3.4:
  - New York, GBL §899-ff: for a teenager of 13–17 — only what is strictly necessary for the service, or a separate consent with refusal as the most prominent choice and without asking again for a year; the storage of work is such a consent (Д201); a notice when the learner stops being a minor, and device signals (§899-hh, 899-ii; Д201); processor agreements with deletion within 30 days (§899-gg) — open question П-30;
  - Connecticut, Colorado, Montana: care for minors, no advertising, no selling, no features that stretch out use — this is already so: no notifications, no mailings (architecture 7), and for children no timers and no competitions (product 7, principle 9); the risk assessment for minors is the DPIA, version 10, and the learner model is profiling, which the DPIA assesses too; consumer rights with an appeal — in Connecticut, which applies the whole law to the processing of sensitive data, — version 2 of the policy (T112); in Colorado and Montana the general rights apply only above their thresholds;
  - Arkansas, Act 952: the right to correct data — by a request to the operator, by version 2 of the policy;
  - Texas, §521.053: the procedure in a breach — 60 days for people, 30 for the attorney general from 250 residents (Д200);
  - Rhode Island: the controller is named (R137).
- **The volunteers' biometrics.** Colorado, C.R.S. 6-1-1314, counts as biometrics also behavioral data that "can be processed" for identification, with no threshold; Washington, RCW 19.373, — "keystroke patterns or rhythms" and the like, with a private right of action. The measurement's writing history may fall under them, and it may not. The author's answer: while there is no public biometric policy, the organizer takes no volunteers from Colorado and Washington — from today on, asking them on their own (Д202) —, and the form asks to declare this, in a new version of the set `measure` (T112). Rejected: meeting their requirements now — a public policy, a protocol and a review once a year for the sake of a few volunteers; the measurement without the writing history — against R124.
- **Not checked against the primary source, and named so in privacy 3.4:** whether Montana applies to the invited; "commercial purposes" for a free service in Arkansas; Rhode Island's "commercial website"; whether Colorado and Washington apply to the writing history; part of the dates and signatures, read from copies in the Wayback Machine and from indexes.
- **To watch:** entering an app store — Texas SB 2420 is in effect, Utah and California AB 1043 will come; selling to schools — the laws on educational data; Vermont, the design code, from 2027-01-01, if the platform gets online revenue; the thresholds of "when the platform grows".

**R141. The texts for the family — `parent-consent`, `teen-consent`, `child-notice` and `teen-notice` version 1 — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions and the state laws; with them come version 2 of `privacy-policy`, with the US consumer rights, and its translation into Russian, for which the part `legal/` gets translations of versions, by its version 2; and version 2 of the set `measure`, where a volunteer declares that they do not live in Colorado or Washington. The operator's mail stays Gmail for families too, and a teenager who has reached the age of digital consent can also withdraw the parent's consent.** The author's answers of 2026-11-11 in the planning and the execution of T112 (RUN.md); the 2026-11-11 amendments to R130, R136 and R138; the approval is the author's, by R112.
- **The reconciliation.** The drafts were written before R136–R140, and the reconciliation found 24 discrepancies, 10 of them such that the text in force would have said something other than what was decided. All were corrected before the approval:
  - not one text for the family named the controller and its contacts — now there is the section "Who we are", as in the text sets of the samples page (R139), and in the texts for the learner the company's name;
  - not one named the basis — now there is the section "Why we may": Arts. 6(1)(a) and 8, the check under COPPA, the record after deletion — Arts. 7(1) and 17(3)(e);
  - what remains after withdrawal was incomplete: the scan of the form, the problem report and the letters to the operator remain too (R117, R123, R136, R138);
  - `child-notice` said "Nobody else can see it", while the operator reads a problem report with the tutor's words — now this is said too;
  - `teen-consent` did not say that an adult can delete the profile too (R136), did not name the recipients, and reduced "what remains" to the consent record;
  - the gist of `parent-consent` and of `teen-notice` said less than the text;
  - small things: the age asked anew — once a year, with a change of country and when the country raised the age (R134, R136); for an essay, the text read goes to the AI; deletion — after a new sign-in; the form — the consent of ALT EdTech LLC; the data — in the US.
- **The mail is Gmail for good, and for families with children too** — the author's answer, the 2026-11-11 amendment to R138: there will be no processor agreement for the mail. The texts for the family and the policy ask not to write a child's data in letters; what the app can do — in the app; the rest — by a letter from the address one signs in with, naming nothing about the child: by the sign-in address the operator finds the account. The risk is the new risk 18 of the DPIA, which the author accepted. *Rejected* — the services with a processor agreement, by their sites, read 2026-11-11: [Fastmail](https://www.fastmail.com/pricing/) — $5 a month when paid for a year, an address without a domain of one's own, [an agreement](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/dpa/) with erasure within 14 days after closing; [Proton Mail Plus](https://proton.me/mail/pricing) — $2.49 a month, but its [agreement](https://proton.me/legal/dpa) sets no erasure period; Zoho Mail Lite and Google Workspace — only with a domain of one's own, which there is not (О-16), and Google's Cloud Data Processing Addendum gives erasure within up to 180 days.
- **A teenager who has reached the age of digital consent under the parent's consent** confirms it by `GiveOwnConsent` or withdraws it by `WithdrawOwnConsent`, which until now refused them with `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED`, — the author's answer, the 2026-11-11 amendment to R136: the texts, the policy in force and R116 (EDPB 05/2020, paras. 147–149) promise "confirm or withdraw", and withdrawal is as easy as consent (Art. 7(3)). *Rejected:* only confirming, while an adult can delete the profile, — the promise would have to be taken back.
- **The storage of work turned on by the adult, after the teenager's confirmation** — `app` asks the teenager about it on a separate screen, a refusal turns storage off and erases the copies on the server, and `app` offers the export before that — the author's answer, the 2026-11-11 amendment to R136: the New York law requires a separate consent of a teenager to what learning does not need (GBL §899-ff; R140). *Rejected:* leaving it on — there is no consent of the teenager to it; turning it off at once — it erases what the teenager may have wanted.
- **At 18** the texts say only that `app` will tell the learner that the protection the law gives minors no longer applies to them (GBL §899-hh(2): "shall provide notice to such user that such user is no longer covered by the protections and rights provided under this article", [NY Senate](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-HH), read 2026-11-11). What then happens to the profile of an adult in someone else's account — a move to their own account or a new consent — is open question П-31. *Rejected:* deciding the move now — a change of the contract and the decisions, more than the task.
- **Requests about a child that the app cannot handle** — correction (Arkansas, A.C.A. §4-88-1503(b)(3)–(4)) and access beyond the export: by a letter from the sign-in address, without the child's data, and a method of its own for the request in the app is open question П-32, by the public launch. *Rejected:* a method now — a change of the contract before the first child, with no need for it.
- **The US consumer rights in version 2 of the policy.** The Connecticut law with amendment PA 25-113 has been in effect since 2026-07-01 also for whoever "control or process consumers' sensitive data" (CGS §42-516(2)), and the data of a known child are sensitive (§42-515(39)(D)), with no threshold and no small-business exemption ([2026 Supplement, ch. 743jj](https://www.cga.ct.gov/2026/sup/chap_743jj.htm), read 2026-11-11). By R140 this is fulfilled for everyone in the US:
  - the rights of §42-518(a): to know and to see — with inferences, that is with the learner model; to correct; to delete; a copy; to opt out of targeted advertising, of sale and of profiling with significant effects; to contest such profiling; the list of buyers — the platform does none of these things, and says so;
  - the answer — 45 days, and another 45 with a notice within the first 45 (§42-518(c)(1)); free of charge once in 12 months, (c)(3); the check that it is the owner who asks — by a letter from the sign-in address, (c)(4), and no new account is needed (§42-520(c)(1));
  - the appeal — by the same way, an answer in writing within 60 days, and with a refusal, how to complain to the attorney general of Connecticut (§42-518(d)) — by the form of that office, subject "Consumer Data Privacy" ([CT AG](https://portal.ct.gov/ag/common/complaint-form-landing-page), read 2026-11-11);
  - the notice of §42-520(b)(1): there are no sales and no targeted advertising; a statement on the training of large language models, (H); the month and year of the last change, (I);
  - Arkansas, Act 952 (from 2026-07-01): correction at the request of a parent or of a teenager of 13–16 ([Act 952](https://www.arkleg.state.ar.us/Home/FTPDocument?path=%2FACTS%2F2025R%2FPublic%2FACT952.pdf), read 2026-11-11);
  - Texas: a small business does not owe the rights of the TDPSA (Bus. & Com. Code §541.002(a)(3)) — the policy says so, and gives the rights anyway;
  - New York, §899-ff, -hh, -ii: a separate consent screen for what is optional, with refusal as the most prominent choice and without asking again for a year; a notice at 18; a device signal counts as a refusal ([NY Senate, §899-II](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-II), read 2026-11-11);
  - the heartbeat of the sign-in SDK (`app` row В48) — in the row "Signing in" and in the retention periods; the two phrases about samples — by R139.
- **The translation of the policy into Russian.** CGS §42-520(b)(2) requires the notice "in each language in which the controller … provides any product or service", and `app` speaks `en` and `ru` (R92). The author's answer — the translation in this task. The part `legal/` gets translations of versions, by its version 2 (the 2026-11-11 amendment to R130): the field `translations` of a text version and the file `texts/<id>/<n>.<tag>.md`, which the rules `legal.files`, `legal.markdown` and `legal.in-force-unchanged` hold too; `GetLegalTexts` gives the translation into the language of the screen, in the fields `translation` and `translation_language`; the types are `types/legalv2`, and the npm package from line 0.15 on has `./legalv2` instead of `./legalv1`; the part's version starts line 0.15. A translation has no force: the English is in force, and a consent names the version, not the translation. *Rejected:* the translation as a task of its own — without it the policy in force would not fulfill the Connecticut law for a Russian screen; a Russian interface not for the US — a change of `app` and О-2.
- **The set `measure` version 2** — `measure-notice` and `measure-form` version 2: the organizer takes no forms from those who live in Colorado or Washington, and the form asks to declare this (R140; Д202).
- **The set `child-sample`** is not here: the operator has no bucket for it yet (Д156), and texts in force would describe a storage that does not exist. T117 introduces it, when `infra` creates the bucket — the author's answer.
- **П-30 is checked** against GBL §899-gg by the primary sources 2026-11-11 ([§899-GG](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-GG)): the law requires an agreement with instructions, help with deletion, information and audits, notice of new processors, erasure on the operator's instruction with the instruction passed on, and a confirmation of erasure within 30 days of the request. All four — [OpenAI](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/openai-data-processing-addendum.pdf), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum), [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum) with Firebase and [Neon at Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/sites/default/files/legal/dpa-20230721.pdf) — lack the confirmation of erasure within 30 days and the passing of the instruction to their own processors; OpenAI and Anthropic lack erasure on instruction too, Google erases within up to 180 days, Neon only on a written request. П-30 stays open: the operator asks each of them for an addendum, before the first child (privacy 9).
- **Not checked against the primary source:** "commercial purposes" for a free service in Arkansas; whether a SOC 2 report is enough for §899-gg(5)(d); the web page of OpenAI's agreement gave 403, and the PDF on its CDN was read; the rules of the New York attorney general under the child data law are not final.

— *Why:* `app` E3 waits for the texts for the family, and the first child from the US waits for what the state laws require of the policy (R140; dpia 8).

— *Consequence:* [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md), version 2 — translations; four texts for the family, `privacy-policy` version 2 with a translation, `measure-notice` and `measure-form` version 2 and the set `measure` version 2; [contracts](../contracts/README.md), section 15 — the translation in `GetLegalTexts` and the teenager's withdrawal; `types/legalv2`; line 0.15; privacy 2, 3.4, 7.1, 9 — П-30, П-31 and П-32 — and 10; [DPIA](dpia.md), version 11 — risk 18; RUN.md — T112, T113, T117 and the rows Д203–Д206.

**R142. The measurement of E10 weighs the spending of Claude Code sessions by the prices of Anthropic's API, not by shares of the subscription's limit; once, on the trial T119, the weight is checked against the share of the limit that `/usage` shows.** The author's answer of 2026-11-11 to Т-39, by the recommendation (RUN.md, T118).
- NovaTrail's sessions run on the author's subscription, and Anthropic does not publish how the subscription counts spending: the help names the five-hour and the weekly limits and what spending depends on, but there is no formula that would turn cache reads, writes and output into a share of the limit (Т-39, repositories 8, with quotes and a date).
- The weight of a call is by the prices of repositories 9.2, which `tools/tokens/prices.mjs` holds; `just tokens-report` prints it in dollars.
- The check is on the trial T119: the share of the limit from `/usage` before and after each run, beside its weight by the prices. If the shares do not follow the weight, an amendment to this entry follows.

— *Why:* the prices are published by the primary source, and the measurement can be repeated in any repository without the author, while `/usage` is read only by a session that is signed in. *Rejected:* always measuring by the shares of `/usage` — they cannot be restored from the transcripts, and the line of repositories 9.3 could not be recomputed; only tokens, without weights, — they would add cache reads to output, which for Opus 5.5 is 100 times dearer: $0.20 against $20 per million.

*Amendment 2026-11-11 (T119), the author's answer at the trial:* `/usage` cannot be read from `claude -p` — neither by a field of its JSON nor by a command —, so the check was made not for each run but once, before and after the whole trial. The share of the limit over the window — +66 p.p. of the five-hour limit and +11 p.p. of the weekly one. The weight of all the sessions of this machine by API prices over the same window — ≈ $53–72 (repositories 9.4). So 1 p.p. of the five-hour limit of Max is no more than ≈ $0.8–1.1 at API prices, and of the weekly one ≈ $5–6.5. The weight by the prices stays, and the measurement of E10 converts it into shares of the limit by these numbers.

## Claude Code sessions

**R143. The token savings of E10 come from the order of the sessions' work and the structure of the documents, not from code-map tools: one task is one session, early compaction, a thin CLAUDE.md, no claude.ai connectors, the bodies of done tasks go to the archive at once, table 4 goes to a file of its own, "Sources" and the measurements go out of `docs/architecture.md`; `docs/` move to English; gopls is taken for the diagnostics of Go code.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-11 in the planning of T121, by the recommendations of repositories 9.4–9.6, except for the translation (RUN.md, T121).
- **One task is one session.** The planning, the execution and the inbox triage of one task are one session; the next task is a new session or `/clear`. The rule is in RULES.md, How we work, and in RUN.md, and the hook `UserPromptSubmit` in `.claude/settings.json` stops the phrase «Выполни задачу», «планируй» or «Разбери входящие» about another task in the same session and names `/clear`. By repositories 9.5 — −51% of the context of the main sessions of E4 and E9. The rule «в новой сессии» ("in a new session") was in RUN.md before too, but E4 and E9 each ran in one session, so the hook is needed.
- **Auto-compaction at 400 thousand tokens**, by the key `autoCompactWindow` in `.claude/settings.json` of `spec` and of the template, not by a variable of `containerEnv`: the project's settings hold in a cloud session too. The saving overlaps with one session per task (repositories 9.5).
- **A thin CLAUDE.md.** The paragraph Environment goes into the rules of `.claude/rules/`, with `paths` by parts, and CLAUDE.md names where they are: −5,090 tokens on each call, ≈ 2% (repositories 9.5). A part's rule is not loaded until the session reads or edits a file of the part, and it is dropped after compaction; CI holds all the checks.
- **The claude.ai connectors are turned off** in the project settings of NovaTrail's repositories: their tasks do not need them, and they carry ≈ 10 thousand tokens per call together with the list of skills (repositories 9.5). How much goes in fact the measurement shows: the connector setting does not turn off the skills of plugins.
- **The body of a done task goes to the epic's archive at once**, in all repositories; what stays in RUN.md is its row of table 1 and a sentence with the outcome and a link to the archive. ≤ 1.9% of "carried" across all 13 repositories (repositories 9.6).
- **Table 4 of `spec` becomes a file of its own, `DEBT.md`**, in the root, in Russian: ≤ 3.9% for `spec` (repositories 9.6). A task reads the debt in it by the «Д» number and by its own files.
- **"Sources" and the results of measurements go out of `docs/architecture.md` into files of their own**, and a claim cites the record of its source: ≤ 0.8%, most of all for `.github`, `infra`, `canvas` and `tutor` (repositories 9.6).
- **A decision that changes another puts an amendment on it** — a rule of RULES.md, How we work. The sample T128 found 6 entries of 15 whose text in force is set by another decision without an amendment to them: R37 reads 60 minutes, while R64 raised them to 85 (repositories 9.6). The ones found get amendments, the rest of the log a sweep, as a row of table 4.
- **The reader of `docs/` is a Claude Code session**, which acts for an engineer, a module author or a lawyer without asking what was meant. The four points of the bar of RULES.md stay: one term — one meaning, a source with a date, a gap — an open question, a decision with "why" and "rejected"; the structure is chosen for reading in parts. For people stay `legal/`, the normative texts for authors (R42), README, RUN.md, COORDINATION.md, the archives of `docs/plan/` and the reports. The edits are in RULES.md, "The bar", and in "Your role" of CLAUDE.md.
- **`docs/` move to English**, in all repositories (the 2026-11-11 amendment to R14). What stays in Russian is RUN.md, COORDINATION.md, `DEBT.md`, the archives of `docs/plan/` and the reports. A quote of a source stays in its own language; the prefixes О-, П-, Т-, «Д» and «В» are Cyrillic; the numbers of the entries and the sections are the same. A translation is not a rewrite of the decision: the meaning and all the citations are the same, which the check of the translation verifies against the Russian text, and the Russian text itself stays in the git history, at the last tag before the translation.
- **The plugin `gopls-lsp`** — in the repositories of Go code, by the kind `go` of the template, where gopls is already built (R102): for the diagnostics after an edit, not for savings. In a cloud session the plugin's language server does not start (repositories 9.4).
- The tasks of `spec` are T129–T139 and T126, part 2 of epic E10; what each repository takes is T123.

— *Why:* a session's spending is set by what it has gathered: the start of a session is 41–45 thousand tokens, and the average context of a call is 218–294 thousand (repositories 9.5). So the main thing is a short session, and restructuring the documents is of the second order, ≈ 4.4% of "carried" together (repositories 9.6). The translation is the author's word: `docs/` are written for the agent, and English is cheaper than Russian by 11.4% of tokens on seven sections (repositories 9.6). This is a new argument against "Rejected: everything in English" in R14. The argument for gopls is the quality of edits of Go code: the server's diagnostics go into the context after each edit. *Rejected:*
- code-map tools — Serena, graphify, claude-context, repomix, ast-grep, aider's map: on the trial T119 none is cheaper than `grep` and `Read`, LSP is +9%, graphify +25% on code and +32% on documents, and the graph of `spec`'s documents takes 69 minutes to build and costs ≈ $7–25 (repositories 9.4);

- leaving `docs/` in Russian, as T125 recommended: ≈ 0.8% in all, for ≈ $65 and an edit of every line of 13 repositories. The author decided to translate. — repositories 9.4–9.6; RUN.md, T121.

— *Amendment 2026-11-12:* **the plugin `gopls-lsp` comes to the Go repositories as a copy in `spec`, not from the marketplace `claude-plugins-official`: the folder `claude-plugins/` — the marketplace `novatrail` of the kind `directory` — holds the plugin's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `LICENSE` byte for byte from commit `e37d307` of Anthropic's marketplace. The kind `go` of the template adds to `.claude/settings.json` of a copy, by the new key `claude` in `repo-template/kinds.json`, the marketplace at the path `./spec/claude-plugins` and `"gopls-lsp@novatrail": true`; `new-repo` appends the keys to the template's file, and `new-repo-check` finds the marketplace and the plugin in the copy's submodule. The devcontainer of `spec` itself has neither gopls nor the plugin. The Go repositories — `api`, `engine`, `learner-model`, `module-kit`, `sim` and `tutor` — take the keys with their move to a tag, T122 (RUN.md, T123).** The author's decisions of 2026-11-12 in the planning of T134, by the recommendations. The plugin's license is Apache-2.0, like NovaTrail's, and it needs no exception under R12.
- **Found in planning** (sources 2.7): a marketplace's `ref` is only a branch or a tag, and `anthropics/claude-plugins-official` has no tags; the name `claude-plugins-official` is reserved, and Claude Code updates such a marketplace itself; `enabledPlugins` in the project's settings does not install a plugin from an external source, while a marketplace in one's own folder with a relative path needs no installation.
- **The trial of 2026-11-12** (RUN.md, T134): in a copy of the kind `go` with gopls 0.24.0 on `PATH`, a session `claude -p` of Claude Code 2.1.280 with these settings loaded the plugin from `spec/claude-plugins/gopls-lsp` in place, without installation, and after writing a file with a type error got "cannot use "x" (untyped string constant) as int value in return statement [IncompatibleAssign] (compiler)". In a folder that was not trusted, the same run did not load the plugin, silently, as the documentation says: in a repository the folder is trusted once, in the first session. The session writes the marketplace into `~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json` by an absolute path, and this directory is a volume shared by all NovaTrail containers: a second copy with another path rewrote the record to its own path and loaded its own plugin, so each session takes the plugin of its own copy.

— *Why:* the rule of exact versions (RULES.md, Exact versions) — the version is held by the tag of `spec`, not by the marketplace's choice; there is neither network nor installation for each clone, and the copy is one JSON file. *Rejected:*
- `gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official` as it is — it cannot be pinned: `ref` does not take a commit, and the marketplace updates itself; `"version": "1.0.0"` keeps the copy in the cache by Anthropic's choice, not ours;
- the built-in marketplace `settings` with `git-subdir` and `sha` — it pins the commit, but the plugin is fetched over the network, and each clone needs `claude plugin install --scope project`;
- gopls and the plugin in the devcontainer of `spec`: its Dockerfile is the base of the container of every kind, and gopls would come to the kinds `docs` and `typescript`, while `spec` has little Go code — `tools/gomod`, `tools/types/roundtrip` and the generated code of `contracts/` —, and `go vet` and `ci-lint` hold it;
- the plugin `typescript-lsp` for the kind `typescript` — R143 did not take it.

— *Consequence:* `claude-plugins/`; `repo-template/kinds.json`; `tools/new-repo/` — `claude.mjs`, the key `claude` and tests; repositories 2.2; the template's README; `.claude/rules/new-repo.md` and CLAUDE.md; sources 2.7; the 2026-11-12 amendment to R102; RUN.md, T123. — RUN.md, T134.


— *Third amendment 2026-11-12:* **a translation is checked by `translation-check` — `tools/translation/`, the recipes `just translation-check <ref> <file>…` and `just translation-anchors <ref> <file>…`, and in another repository the same through `-f spec/justfile`. A document is compared with its original at `<ref>` unit by unit — a heading of the same level and with the same number, a paragraph, a list item at the same depth, a table cell, a block of code —, and in each pair these match: the numbers of the registers and the tasks with their suffix, the citations of sections, the links, the numbers — as sequences of digits, so that "14 878" and "14,878" are one number —, the code in backticks, and for code with Russian words everything but the words, the quotes of an English text — word for word, the lines of code blocks without Russian — as they are, and the fixed words of the log and the cards — the vocabulary `tools/translation/vocabulary.mjs`: «Почему» — "Why", «Отвергнуто» — "Rejected", «Следствие» — "Consequence", «Поправка» — "Amendment", «Вторая поправка» — "Second amendment", «Заменено» — "Superseded", «Решить при детализации» — "To decide when detailed" and others. Russian in a translation is only in «…» whose words are in the original, in code and in the prefixes О-, П-, Т-, «Д» and «В». A citation or a number that went into another item in the translation is an error, and the message names where it went: they return to their place. Russian anchors are rewritten by `translation-anchors` in all the Markdown files of the repository, in the archives of `docs/plan/` too. The meaning is checked by a blind reading: the sample — pieces of ≈ 4 KB, until a tenth of the document's bytes and at least one piece are gathered — is chosen by `main.mjs sample` by the hash of the commit before the translation, not by whoever translated, and a fresh subagent that did not translate names every difference of meaning. The order of a translation is [tools/translation/README.md](../tools/translation/README.md): pieces of 15–30 KB, a subagent of Opus per batch of pieces of ≈ 100 KB, each piece checked by the command `pair`, the glossary — concepts 15, translated first, with the Russian term beside the English one.** The executor's decisions of 2026-11-12 in the planning of T135: the author charged the executor with doing T135–T139 itself and with choosing the decisions itself (RUN.md, T135). The pilot of T135: a piece of the log, 22.8 KB of entries R66–R70, Opus 5.5 translated in 110 s and 64 thousand tokens, Sonnet 5 in 328 s and 86 thousand, and both clean by `pair`, but Sonnet's terms are worse: the «подпись» of a workbook is "signature", not "caption", «ответ вводом» is "an answer given through input". The glossary, 99 KB, Opus translated in 7 minutes and 131 thousand tokens. — *Why:* a translation is an edit of every line, and without a check by a machine a lost link, number or condition goes unnoticed; unit by unit is the strictest comparison that the check holds without a model, and it also keeps the structure that citations of items rely on. *Rejected:* comparing by sections, not by units, — a link that went into another item would pass; accepting a link that went away — the translation would change the structure; a back-translation instead of a blind reading — twice as dear, and its own errors hide differences; the sample chosen by the translator — they would choose what they know; Sonnet 5 — slower and worse in terms. — *Consequence:* `tools/translation/` — `compare.mjs`, `main.mjs`, `pieces.mjs`, `vocabulary.mjs`, README and tests; `tools/docs-check/` — the third 2026-11-12 amendment to R32; justfile; `.claude/rules/tools.md`; RULES.md — Language; CLAUDE.md; rule 10 of RUN.md and of the template; the template's `docs/` — in English, its CLAUDE.md and README; repositories 2.2; the other repositories — by T123. — RUN.md, T135.

## Account deletion and the Google sign-in

**R144. Account deletion also removes the "Sign in with Google" connection in the owner's Google account: `app` revokes the Google access token that the fresh sign-in by the window before the deletion gives, and `api` does not get this token.** The author's answer of 2026-11-12 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В52 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` 77fbf21), its first option (the 2026-11-12 amendment to R21 api); the triage before T134.
- **What was found.** Deleting the user at the sign-in service does not remove the connection: after `DeleteAccount` the user is gone, but the dev project's connection stayed among the author's connected apps (T42 `api`). Google's help says nothing about this (sources 4.6).
- **How.** Deletion requires a fresh sign-in (R98; R20 api), and the sign-in by the window gives the Google access token. After the answer "deleted", `app` revokes it at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke`, and the revocation removes everything the owner granted the project (sources 4.6). The token lives only in the memory of `app`.
- **What `app` decides** (DEBT.md, Д221): how to send the request — Google's documentation prescribes a form, without CORS, while the trial of 2026-11-12 saw CORS in the response; what to add to `csp.json` (the third 2026-11-09 amendment to R85); what the screen says if the revocation failed.
- **The texts.** The policy of version 2 does not name the connection among what remains. With the revocation the connection is not there, and no new version is needed (R130). The DPIA does not change: the connection is data of the adult owner in their Google account, and dpia 3.1 and measure 6 of dpia 6.2 — "sign-in only through the Google window" — are the same (R129).

— *Why:* deletion requires a fresh sign-in anyway, the token is already in the memory of `app`, and a connection the policy is silent about would contradict the honest retention periods (privacy 1). *Rejected:* only writing down that the connection stays — version 3 of the policy would be needed; the revocation on the server — `api` would hold a Google token it does not need (privacy 1, minimization). — *Consequence:* architecture 3.12 and 4.5; sources 4.6; Д221.

## Keeping the token savings

**R145. What epic E10 saved is kept by three levels, from the cheapest: budgets of size in `docs-check` on every pull request, without a model; a measurement by `tokens-report --row` at each epic's archive and once a month; and a new analysis only by a threshold. The budgets are in bytes, in `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`, and a repository is checked by them once its root holds `docs-budgets.json`.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-12 in the planning of T126, all by the recommendations; that the savings are kept by a threshold and not by a weekly analysis, the author decided on 2026-11-11 with the epic (RUN.md, T126).
- **Budgets.** `docs-check` measures each whole file named, each rule of `.claude/rules/`, each entry of the decision log with its amendments, the own text under each heading of a document cited by name — to the next heading, numbered or not — and above its first heading, and each row of a table of the files named; a limit is in KB of 1,024 bytes, and a numbered section may have a limit of its own. Over the limit is an error that names the file, the size, the limit and the file the limit came from; raising a limit is an edit of that file, seen in review. A wrong file of budgets — an unknown key, a limit that is not a whole number of KB, a limit for a file or a section that does not exist — is an error, not a check turned off. Each limit is the largest of its kind on 2026-11-12 plus 10–20% (measurements 1.9). `format/`, `legal/` and the archives of `docs/plan/` have none.
- **Another repository.** The block `repository` of the same file holds its limits, read from its `spec/` submodule, and its `docs-budgets.json` names what differs, `{}` when nothing does. Without that file `docs-check-repo` does not measure, so a move to the tag of T122 does not turn red; the repository's task of T123 writes the file by its own numbers, and the template carries it from the start (repositories 2.2). Once every repository has it, the check without it goes, as the reading of table 4 in RUN.md does (the 2026-11-12 amendment to R32).
- **The measurement.** At the archive of an epic, the repository's session runs `tokens-report --since <the first day of the epic> --row` and adds the row to its measurements; once a month a session of `spec` measures the folders of transcripts of all 13 repositories on this machine, from the window of the last row, and adds a row for each to measurements 1.9. The transcripts are on the machine where the work ran, so the measurement is a session there, not a cloud task on a schedule. `just inbox`, which runs before every task, prints the date of the monthly measurement and of the quarterly check once it has come, from the lines of measurements 1.9 (the 2026-11-12 amendment to R81).
- **The threshold.** A task of analysis goes into «Задачи вне эпика» of RUN.md when the context of a main call is more than 25% above the repository's reference, over at least 300 main calls; or when a budget was raised three times since the last analysis, by `git log` of the file of budgets; or when a quarter has passed since the last check of Claude Code's changelog — what new means of saving it brings. Its planning decides whether an epic is needed. The reference of `spec` is part 2 of E10, 183.2 thousand, until the measurement after of T124, and of another repository its T124 (measurements 1.9).

— *Why:* an analysis reads the documents of 13 repositories, so a weekly one spends what it saves, and frequent restructuring breaks the citations of sections and the structure the sessions rely on; it is like the review of the DPIA, by occasion and at least once a year (R129). Bytes, since a check on every pull request runs in CI, which has no key, and the lower bound of bytes per token of measurements 1.6 keeps a limit in bytes from letting through more tokens than meant. A repository by its own file, since the other repositories have not restructured their documents yet (RUN.md, T123): their RUN.md is up to 228 KB and their `docs/architecture.md` up to 791 KB (measurements 1.6), and spec's limits on them would make the move to the tag red. *Rejected:*
- a weekly analysis with restructuring — the reasons above;
- counting tokens through the API — a key in CI and a call over the network on every run, and the check turns red by itself when the tokenizer changes; through `claude -p` — it costs money on every pull request;
- spec's limits in every repository at once, by the tag of T122;
- only `spec` measured monthly, and reminded by the rule alone — the rule rests on the session's memory, and the other repositories' "before" would be missing for T124;
- a check in `docs-check` of the rule "a decision that changes another puts an amendment on it" (RULES.md, How we work; R143): without a model it cannot tell an entry that changes another from one that cites it, and it would only add noise; review keeps the rule, and Д216 sweeps the log;
- a check that the consolidation of the decisions is lossless, and that tables of contents are fresh — T121 took neither (R143).

— *Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/` — `budgets.json`, `budgets.mjs`, `config.mjs`, `main.mjs` and tests (the fourth 2026-11-12 amendment to R32); `tools/tokens/` — `--row`, and a path the user may not look at is not a file (Д209 closed); `tools/inbox/due.mjs`; measurements 1.9; rule 13 and «Как устроен план: эпики» of RUN.md (the second 2026-11-12 amendment to R19); the template — `docs-budgets.json` and its RUN.md (repositories 2.2); CLAUDE.md, Environment; `.claude/rules/tools.md`; the fourth 2026-11-12 amendment to R143; RUN.md, T123. — RUN.md, T126.

— *Amendment 2026-11-12:* **`just inbox` no longer runs before every task, but on the author's word or once every task of the current epic is done (the second 2026-11-12 amendment to R81). It still prints the dates of measurements 1.9 when they have come, so the monthly measurement and the quarterly check go with that triage, and a monthly row may come later than its date; the measurement at each epic's archive does not depend on it.** The author's word of 2026-11-12, after T126. — *Consequence:* rule 13 and «Как устроен план: эпики» of RUN.md; measurements 1.9.
